description: An annual with dark green, toothed leaves. Small, summertime, daisy-like flowers bloom in white with yellow centers.

A showy annual flower with a mounding growth habit. Open-faced flowers are typically bicolored and come in a broad spectrum of cheerful colors. Dark green leaves stay bushy and low. Blooms in spring and summer.
A unique, tropical annual with plume-like flower clusters in brilliant colors.

High-performing, compact, mounding perennial grown for cool-season color, with silver-marked, heart-shaped leaves and prolific, large, upswept flowers in a wide mix of colors. Bloom is strongest from fall through spring. Our cyclamen are grown outdoors under shade, not in climate controlled greenhouses, so they are hardier and more durable in the landscape. Available in colors: white, lilac, rose eye, scarlet red, deep magenta, purple, and rose. We are taking bookings for the fall season now through October 30. Please note that inventory will display as 0 until our first crops become ready in fall.

A compact, showy annual with a mounding, cascading growth habit. Loose clusters of semi-tubular flowers are available in blue, dark-blue, pale sky-blue, lilac-pink, rose-pink, or white. Leaves are narrow, green, and sometimes tinged with bronze. Attracts butterflies and hummingbirds. Used for borders, hanging baskets and window boxes.
An herbaceous annual with soft green, heart-shaped leaves and flowers that resemble dense clusters of powdery puff balls in lavender-blue.
An annual that makes a bold statement in a cool season garden. Rounded plant with center leaves that grow more colorful in colder weather.

A short-lived perennial that is prized for its large, saucer-shaped flowers. Crinkled, papery petals come in white, pink, orange, or yellow. Fuzzy, blue-green foliage forms short basal clumps below the leafless flower stalks.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a vigorously spreading carpet. Silky flowers are lavender-blue with white throats and dark purple veins. Blooms in spring, cool summers, and fall. Beneficial for butterflies and birds. Leaves are heart-shaped, bronze-green, and tinged dark maroon in cool weather. Native to the U.S.

A showy garden flower with an upright or trailing growth habit. Stalks of leathery, rich green foliage bear open-faced flowers, which are available in a variety of colors with contrasting throats. Blooms in summer and fall. Attracts moths and butterflies.

A showy annual flower with a dwarf, compact habit. Flowers come in a variety of colors, in yellows, oranges, pinks, red, and white. Gray-green leaves are rounded or lance-shaped. Blooms from summer to early fall. Attracts birds and butterflies.

An annual with a compact, mounding growth habit. Large flower heads take on different forms, which include double, semi-double, globe-shaped, and anemone. Flowers bloom in shades of white, yellow, orange, and red. Toothed, gray-green leaflets stay low and bushy. Attracts beneficial insects.

An annual with a compact, mounding growth habit. Large flower heads take on different forms, which include double, semi-double, globe-shaped, and anemone. Flowers bloom in shades of white, yellow, orange, and red. Toothed, gray-green leaflets stay low and bushy. Attracts beneficial insects.
A classic annual in the flower bed. Flowers are available in a broad spectrum of color combinations and markings. Foliage stays low, green, and bushy. Most cultivars bloom throughout fall and spring.

A classic garden flower with a trailing growth habit. Showy funnel-shaped flowers are available in a broad specturm of color combinations and markings. Leaves are egg-shaped, green and slightly sticky. Blooms in spring, summer and fall.

An annual or biennial bulb that blooms with showy flower clusters amongst tufts of grassy foliage. Disk-shaped flowers feature petals with notched edges and white stamens. Colors range from white to shades of pink, red, or purple. Some cultivars are bicolored. Attracts bees and butterflies. Makes a good cut flower. Flowers are edible.

A classic garden flower with a clumping growth habit. Upright clusters of showy, open-faced flowers are available in a broad spectrum of color combinations and markings. Leaves resemble romaine lettuce. Blooms throughout spring.

A showy annual flower with a creeping habit. Flowers come in a variety of colors, and single or double forms. Gray-green leaves are rounded or lance-shaped. Blooms from summer to early fall. Attracts birds and butterflies.
Annual with beautiful, ruffled rose-like flowers. Trailing stems set with fleshy and narrow green leaves.

Many small, bright-faced flowers cover this compact, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial, often grown as a cool-season annual. Colors range from purple and blue to yellow, white, and mixed shades. Use it for edging, containers, or mass bedding. Sun or light shade, rich soil, and even moisture extend bloom; the flowers are edible.

A perennial grown as an annual. This hybrid series has resistance to mildew and tolerates more heat, sun, and humidity than other Impatiens. Plants grow 18 - 24 inches tall. Single, 3 inch wide flowers bloom from spring through fall and come in an array of color options.

A perennial grown as an annual. This hybrid series has resistance to mildew and tolerates more heat, sun, and humidity than other Impatiens. Plants grow 18 - 24 inches tall. Single, 3 inch wide flowers bloom from spring through fall and come in an array of color options.
A self-sowing, low, trailing annual with small leaves and tiny clusters of sweetly fragrant flowers. Does well in poor and rocky soil. Beneficial for pollinators.

A classic garden flower with a clumping growth habit. Showy spikes of complex flowers bloom in a variety of colors. Leaves are dark green and lance-shaped. Blooms in spring, summer and fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.

A classic annual in the flower bed. Silky flowers are available in a broad spectrum of bright color combinations with vivid markings. Green foliage is low and mounding. Most cultivars bloom throughout fall and spring.

A tender perennial often grown as an annual with a compact, mounding habit for bedding, edging, and containers. Rounded, waxy green or bronze foliage pairs with clusters of white, pink, or red flowers over a long warm season. It performs best in fertile, evenly moist soil and protected filtered light.

An evergreen, clumping bamboo with upright golden canes striped green and new shoots flushed pink. Fine-textured foliage creates a bright screen without the running habit of many bamboos. Effective for narrow privacy plantings, containers, and courtyards, especially with fertile soil and consistent water during establishment.
Running bamboo with young green culms that mature and turn black in the second year of growth, features rich green foliage.

50% mushroom compost and 50% ground and composted wood products. Excellent organic soil conditioner for planting trees, shrubs, and perennials. Use as top-dressing when seeding a lawn. Great for loosening clay soils. This product is available at our San Ramon store, for pickup or delivery to select cities in Contra Costa County.

Black dyed fir bark. Use as top-dressing to control weeds and conserve moisture as well as give the garden a finished look. This product is available at our San Ramon store, for pickup or delivery to select cities in Contra Costa County.

Redwood bark that has been shredded and dyed black. Use as top-dressing to control weeds and conserve moisture as well as give the garden a finished look. Will turn gray with age. WARNING: FLAMMABLE - DO NOT INSTALL IN HIGH FIRE DANGER AREAS This product is available at our San Ramon store, for pickup or delivery to select cities in Contra Costa County.

50% Brown sandy loam, 25% mushroom compost, and 25% composted organic material. Use to fill low spots in the ground or to increase volume in containers. Mix into existing soil when planting trees, shrubs, vegetables, and flower beds. Plant directly in the mix in pots or add to existing soil. This product is available at our San Ramon store, for pickup or delivery to select cities in Contra Costa County.

Very fine fir bark, 1/4-0. Use as top-dressing to control weeds and conserve moisture as well as give the garden a finished look. Great as a soil additive to increase drainage. This product is available at our San Ramon store, for pickup or delivery to select cities in Contra Costa County.

Combination of 1/3 sand, 1/3 fir bark, 1/3 fine fir bark. Use for planting in containers or for planting trees, shrubs, and perennials in the ground. Good for planting azaleas, camellias, and other acid-loving plants. This product is available for pickup in San Ramon or Clements. Local delivery available in Contra Costa County.

Redwood bark that has been shredded. Use as top-dressing to control weeds and conserve moisture as well as give the garden a finished look. Will turn gray with age. WARNING: FLAMMABLE - DO NOT INSTALL IN HIGH FIRE DANGER AREAS This product is available at our San Ramon store, for pickup or delivery to select cities in Contra Costa County.

Small fir bark, 3/16-5/16. Use as top-dressing to control weeds and conserve moisture as well as give the garden a finished look. This product is available at our San Ramon store, for pickup or delivery to select cities in Contra Costa County.

commonName: West Marin Compost Hi-Test Compost Bulk
description: All the benefits of Nicasio Blend but with higher nitrogen content from the inclusion of High-N Manure. Hi-Test Compost is great for new gardens and landscapes, especially where soils have been neglected or overworked. In addition to improving soil structure, our Hi-Test Compost will give new plants the nitrogen needed for a vibrant start. This product is available at our Petaluma store for pickup only.

commonName: West Marin Compost Nicasio/Sonoma Compost Bulk
description: This dark, rich, premium quality compost is made from recycled yard trimmings, dairy manure, and horse manure. Recommended for applications that do not require high nitrogen content such as trees, shrubs, grape vines, and natives. Provides valuable organic matter to soil, making it easier to work and more productive. Provides a wealth of slow release nutrients and beneficial microbes to your soil and plants. Screened to approximately 00. This product is available at our Petaluma store for pickup only.

commonName: West Marin Compost Vineyard Mulch Bulk
description: An affordable, organic alternative to expensive bark products. Screened Vineyard Mulch provides great background color and texture in landscaping applications. It suppresses weeds, conserves moisture, moderates soil temperatures, and controls erosion. Vineyard Mulch undergoes a brief composting process over 131Â°F that renders it virtually free of weed seeds and plant pathogens. It is particularly suited for use on steep hillsides, and when properly applied will reduce soil loss from erosion by up to 95%. This product is available at our Petaluma store for pickup only.

An evergreen, rosette-forming hybrid succulent perennial with a compact clumping habit. Tight rosettes carry thick pale blue-green leaves that develop pink tones at the tips and margins in bright conditions. Short, branching flower stalks carry yellow flowers with red spotting in late spring. Useful as a small-scale accent in containers, rock gardens, and mixed succulent plantings.
A multi-branching succulent with eye-catching rosettes. The striking color combination displays a high-contrast dark red against the pale green new growth.

A succulent that forms a ground-hugging mat of small, bright green rosettes. Clusters of yellow flowers bloom from mature rosettes. Likes partial shade inland, or full coastal sun. Drought tolerant once established.

A Mexican succulent that forms large rosettes of fleshy, cupped, paddle-shaped leaves in silvery lavender-pink with brighter pink margins. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in orange-red. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.
A succulent shrub with waxy, fin-shaped leaves that are velvety gray-blue-green. Leaves point in alternating directions from a central, upright stalk. Tall clusters of flowers bloom in red.

Broad rosettes give this evergreen, clumping succulent a bold, low form. Turquoise leaves may blush pink, while branched orange flower stalks draw hummingbirds in the cool season. It fits rock gardens, dry borders, and large pots. Bright light and gritty, fast-draining soil keep the rosettes clean; leaf sap may irritate skin.

A perennial succulent that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Bright yellow-green leaves are fleshy and needle-like. Foliage tinges orange in cool weather. Flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.
A sprawling succulent that forms rosettes of thick, fleshy, blue green leaves atop slow-growing stems. Leaves flush maroon in winter. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in orange-red.

A succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, velvety, narrow, pointed leaves in green with pink on the tips. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in bright red and yellow. Forms offsets.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

Groundcover succulent with striking, serrated and variegated foliage. Dark green leaves are arranged in rosettes, and heavily edged with lemon yellow. Inconspicuous summer flowers attract pollinators.

A perennial succulent that forms a spreading mound with stout, upright stems. Variegated gray-green, cream-edged leaves are fleshy, narrowly egg-shaped and toothed on the edges. Large, light pink to copper flower clusters bloom in late summer and fall, attracting bees and butterflies.

A perennial succulent that forms a spreading mound with stout, upright stems. Light blue-green leaves are fleshy, egg-shaped and toothed on the edges. Large, pink-red flower clusters bloom in late summer and fall, attracting bees and butterflies. A larger version of 'Autumn Joy' that holds its flowers into winter.

A perennial succulent that forms a spreading mound with stout, upright stems. Light blue-green leaves are fleshy, egg-shaped and toothed on the edges. Large, light pink to copper flower clusters bloom in late summer and fall, attracting bees and butterflies.

A true cactus that spreads to form a shrubby fence. Blue-green cladodes are flat, rounded and pad-like. Widely spaced areoles lack spines. Large flowers are followed by sweet, prickly-pear fruits. Fruit ripens in summer. The fruits ( tunas ) and the flesh of the cladodes ( nopales ) are edible.

A true cactus that spreads to form a low, shrubby fence. Gray-green cladodes are shaped like beaver tails. Barbed bristles poke out from widely spaced areoles. Showy, brilliant pink flowers in spring and summer are followed by prickly pear fruits. Native to North America, including California. Evergreen.

A cold-hardy evergreen succulent that usually forms one rosette per trunk. Gray-blue leaves are stiff, very narrow, and needle-pointed. Spent leaves skirt the trunk as it slowy grows upwards to 12 feet or more. Large clusters of white flowers rise up in early summer, followed by beak-like, capsule-type fruits.

A succulent that forms loose, lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, somewhat lance-shaped leaves in dull black with glowing green centers. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in red-orange.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, triangular leaves in blackish burgundy with blue-green centers. Offsets form colonies. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in red-orange. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with fleshy leaves arranged on branching stems. The bold foliage texture works well in containers, coastal plantings, and low-water accent beds, with seasonal flower stalks on mature rosettes. It benefits from excellent drainage and light irrigation during active growth.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, slightly cupped, pointed leaves in pale blue-green. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in yellow and pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Offsets form colonies.

An evergreen succulent that slowly forms a barrel-shaped rosette. Mauve-purple and gray-green leaves are drooping, sword-shaped, and needle-pointed. Large clusters of white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

An evergreen succulent that forms a semi-trailing mat of upright foliage. Cylindrical, finger-like leaves are chalky blue-green. Off-white disk flowers bloom in spring and summer. Attracts pollinators.

A Mexican succulent that forms large rosettes of fleshy, narrow, paddle-shaped leaves in cool blue green with blushing pink margins. Similar to E. 'Blue Waves' but with more blue in the foliage and more red on the margins. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

botanicalName: Agave x 'Blue Flame', Agave shawii x A. attenuata
description: An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, triangular leaves in greyish blue flushed with blush pink. Offsets form colonies. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in coral pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

A succulent that forms large rosettes of fleshy, rounded leaves in pale blue-green, flushed with pink. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in red and yellow. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Offsets form colonies.

This Mexican succulent forms a wide rosette of fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves. Foliage is powdery gray-blue with rosy pink edges, tips and undersides. Best color in bright light. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in orange-pink.

A perennial succulent that forms a tight ground cover. Blue-green, needle-like leaves are reminiscent of a conifer's. Foliage tinges purple in cool weather. Yellow flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.

A cold-hardy evergreen succulent that usually forms one rosette per trunk. Powdery blue-gray leaves are stiff, very narrow, gently arching, and needle-pointed. Spent leaves skirt the trunk as it slowly grows upwards to 12 feet or more. Large clusters of white flowers rise up in early summer, followed by beak-like, capsule-type fruits.

A California native succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy leaves, which are coated in a fine chalky blue-gray powder. Outer leaves become flushed with red. Stalks of white flowers appear in spring and attract hummingbirds. Spreads by offsets.

A hybrid, multi-branching succulent with tightly clustered rosettes. Bright green centers are complimented by blushing red leaf tips. Yellow flower clusters emerge from mature rosettes. Drought tolerant. Likes partial shade inland, full sun on the coast. Hardy to 25 - 30 degrees F.

A native southwestern perennial forming clumps of stiff and leathery, gray-green leaves with thread-like fringe along the margins. Branching inflorescences carry clusters of tubular, bright red flowers. Very abundant flower display over a long season.

A low-growing evergreen succulent that forms colonies of rosettes. Green leaves with variegated yellow margins are arching and sword-shaped. Large clusters of fragrant, white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

commonName: Bright Star Spanish Dagger, Soft-Tip Yucca
description: An evergreen succulent that slowly forms a short trunk. Gray-green leaves are curved downward, sword-shaped, and needle-pointed. Variegated bright yellow stripes run down the edges of each leaf. Large clusters of pink, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

A perennial succulent that forms a spreading mound with stout, upright stems. Gray-green leaves are fleshy, egg-shaped and toothed on the edges. Huge, pink flower clusters bloom in late summer and fall, attracting bees, and butterflies.

A succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy leaves which are coated in a fine chalky white powder. Stalks of yellow flowers appear in spring and summer, attracting hummingbirds. Spreads by offsets. Avoid overhead watering.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with a compact, rounded habit. Green leaves are edged and flushed burgundy-pink, with stronger color in brighter light. Well suited to containers, rock gardens, and succulent plantings with sun to part sun, excellent drainage, and moderate to low water.

A low-growing succulent that forms mounding colonies of rosettes, pupping densely around the central base. Long leaves are pale green with reddish tips. A cluster of yellow flowers blooms from each mature rosette in spring and summer. Full sun on the coast, or partial shade inland. Drought tolerant.

An evergreen, spreading succulent groundcover with branching stems and stacked, propeller-like leaves. Foliage emerges light green and develops vivid red to orange-red color in bright light and cool weather, with clusters of small white flowers in summer. Best color and growth occur in bright filtered sun to part sun with well-drained soil and low supplemental water.

A succulent that forms bushy colonies of curvy-leaved rosettes. Rosettes are comprised of waxy leaves in medium green. New growth comes in pale green; older growth displays red tips. A panicle of small yellow flowers emerges from each mature rosette. Full sun on the coast, partial shade inland.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

A large tree-like Euphorbia resembling E. candelabra. Over time it forms many four-sided stems with dark brown spines along the edges. Coloration is butter-yellow with bluish-green marbled variegation.
A slow growing, large tree-like Euphorbia resembling E. candelabra. Over time it forms many four-sided stems with dark brown spines along the edges. Coloration is cool bluish green.

A succulent that forms rosettes of fleshy, gray-green leaves with red-toothed margins. Large, extra showy, clusters of tubular flowers appear in bright orange-red. Forms a single trunk after about 10 years, with older leaves forming a "petticoat" under the rosettes.

A perennial succulent that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Chalky silver leaves are flattened, spoon-shaped, and arranged in tiny rosettes. Foliage tinges purple in cool weather. Flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies. Tolerates shade. Native to the California Bay Area and beyond.

botanicalName: Agave angustifolia 'Marginata', A. vivipara var. margiata
description: An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen succulent that forms spreading colonies of rosettes. Younger, smaller offsets crowd around older, larger rosettes. Fleshy leaves are pointed, spoon-shaped and bright green, tinged with shades of red and burgundy on the tips. Striking pink flower stalks bloom in summer.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.
