Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

A California native succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, flattened leaves. Gray-green leaves are somewhat translucent, and coated in a fine chalky white powder. Stalks of pale red flowers appear in spring and attracts hummingbirds. Spreads by offsets.
A succulent that forms low-branching colonies of large rosettes. Spoon-shaped leaves are waxy and reddish-brown.
An ornamental succulent with a palm-like appearance that forms clumps of broad, arching, blue-green leaves. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in coral red.

Fine white threads stretch across each green rosette on this evergreen, clumping succulent groundcover, giving the mound a webbed look. Pink flowers rise from mature rosettes before offsets replace them. Use it in troughs, rock walls, or alpine beds. Full sun, gritty soil, and quick drainage keep the threads clean and crowns firm.

A low-growing evergreen succulent that forms colonies of rosettes. Variegated green leaves are arching, sword-shaped, and display a thick yellow stripe running down the center of each leaf. Large clusters of fragrant, white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with fleshy leaves arranged on branching stems. The bold foliage texture works well in containers, coastal plantings, and low-water accent beds, with seasonal flower stalks on mature rosettes. It benefits from excellent drainage and light irrigation during active growth.

Long fleshy leaves shift from green to copper-orange on this evergreen, spreading succulent when grown in strong sun. White star flowers rise above trailing stems and attract small insects. Use it on dry slopes, in rock gardens, or spilling from large pots. Gritty soil and deep, spaced watering keep stems firm and color bright.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

A small, ornamental succulent with thick, variegated, green-and-yellow striped leaves. Margins are jaggedly toothed. Careful of the very sharp terminal spines. After several years it produces a tall, branched flower stalk. Cold hardy to 20 - 25 degrees F.

A small to mid-size succulent species, native to Mexico. Yellow-green leaves are lined with teeth, and imprinted with the teeth of other leaves. A scarlet-brown, needle-sharp spine punctuates the tip of each leaf. After several years, an astoundingly tall flower stalk arises, potentially reaching up to around 20 feet high. Does not form offsets.

Small, fleshy leaves pack tightly on this evergreen, rounded succulent shrub and often gain red edges in strong light. Starry white to pale pink flowers may open in winter. Use it for low accents, bonsai forms, or bright indoor containers. Fast-draining soil and deep, spaced watering keep stems firm; the foliage is toxic to pets.
A succulent that forms many rosettes of dark green and white-spotted leaves, flushed with bronzy-red in fall. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appera in orange-red.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, plump, oblong leaves in pale blue-green tinged with dark purple. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in yellow and pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Offsets form colonies.

A perennial succulent that forms rosettes of broad, yellow and dark green leaves that are heavily marked in a somewhat zig-zag pattern. Leaves have an unusually rough texture. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in orange-red.

A compact selection with a prolific flower display, this Southwestern perennial is cold hardy down to -20 degrees F. The leathery gray-green leaves are lined with threadlike fringe. Branching inflorescences are topped with clusters of tubular, coral-pink flowers. Attracts hummingbirds.

A grassy-looking evergreen shrub that forms clumps of long, stiff, gray-green leaves with distinctive spoon-shaped bases. Leaf margins are serrated and sharp. Develops a stout trunk over time. Eventually bears large flowers spikes that can reach up to 15 feet high.

A bold, evergreen succulent forming upright, clumping rosettes with a strong architectural presence. Fleshy, spiky leaves emerge green and develop deep red to copper tones under high light and dry conditions, adding dramatic contrast to drought-tolerant plantings. Thrives in sharply drained soils with low water once established, making it well-suited to xeriscapes and containers.

A Mexican succulent that forms loose rosettes of fleshy, ruffled leaves in powdery gray-green to purple with pink edges. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

This succulent forms a small rosette that spreads by numerous offsets. Velvety, pale green leaves are covered in fuzzy, white hairs. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in red-orange. Blooms spring to fall.

An evergreen, slow-growing succulent tree with a thick gray trunk and bold crowns of blue-green leaves. Mature plants branch into a broad, umbrella-like form and may bear greenish white flowers and orange fruit. Use it as a strong specimen or courtyard tree. The red sap may irritate skin, and plant parts are toxic if eaten.

commonName: Dragon's Blood Stonecrop, Two Row Stonecrop
description: A perennial succulent that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Green, red-tinged leaves are scalloped, flattened, and stacked in rows along short stems. Foliage flushes deep, dark red in cool weather. Red flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.
An evergreen succulent that forms a semi-trailing mat of upright foliage. Finger-like leaves are frosty blue-green with pink tips. White disk flowers bloom in summer. Attracts pollinators.

Tiny purple star flowers cover this evergreen, spreading succulent groundcover above a tight mat of fine green leaves. The low growth fills joints, slopes, and dry parkways without hiding stones. Bees visit the cool-season bloom. Full sun, fast drainage, and deep, spaced watering maintain a dense carpet that handles light foot traffic.

botanicalName: Agave potatorum 'Kichiokan Marginata', Agave potatorum 'Kissho Kan'
description: An evergreen, compact rosette-forming succulent with short gray-green leaves edged in creamy yellow. Red teeth add color and sharp texture. Its small size fits containers, rock gardens, entries, and tight accent beds. The parent species comes from highlands of southern Mexico.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, triangular leaves in gray-green with thick, ebony-red edges. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in red-orange. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Best color in full sun.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with a compact, symmetrical habit. Fleshy blue-green to gray-green leaves have pink to red margins and pointed tips, with slender stalks of bell-shaped yellow to coral flowers in season. Thrives in bright light, well-drained soil, and moderate to low water once established.

A succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, diamond-shaped leaves in frosty gray-green, finely edged in dark red. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in yellow. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

An upright succulent shrub with obovate leaves and thick, multi-branching stems - sometimes likened to a small-leafed jade plant. Bright emerald green foliage adorns the reddish-brown stems. Requires excellent drainage. Hardy to 25 - 30 degrees F. Does well indoors. Stays small in containers, excellent for bonsai. Occasional summer flowers. Native to South Africa.

An evergreen, low-growing succulent shrub with a dense, trailing to mounding habit. Small glossy green leaves are held on reddish-brown stems, creating fine texture for containers, bonsai work, and small succulent combinations. The compact form stays low and can be used as a small-scale groundcover in frost-protected dry gardens. Benefits from well-drained soil and is useful indoors where bright conditions are available.

A succulent shrub with oppositely arranged pairs of waxy, cupped leaves that have dark green upper sides and purple-pink undersides. Wiry stems hold clusters of small star-shaped flowers in pink to white. Does well as a spreading groundcover or hanging plant.
A multi-branched, shrub-like succulent that grows unusual fanlike rosettes of fleshy, flattened leaves. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in orange-red.

A succulent perennial that forms basal rosettes of foliage. Unusual leaves are fleshy, flattened, broad and circular. Color is gray-green with red margins and variegated cream markings. Terminal clusters of tubular, yellow flowers bloom in late winter or spring. Forms spreading colonies of offsets.

commonName: Felt Plant, Velvet Elephant Ear Kalanchoe
description: A succulent perennial that forms a tree-like shrub. Unusual leaves are fleshy, velvety, folded, triangular and wavy-edged. Color is silvery-olive-green. Terminal clusters of yellow-green flowers bloom in late winter or spring.
A multi-branching succulent shrub with plump, finger-like leaves, which are powdery blue-gray-green and sometimes tipped in dull red. Flower stalks carry drooping, bell-shaped flowers in orange.
A multi-branching succulent shrub with plump, finger-like leaves, which are powdery blue-gray-green and sometimes tipped in dull red. Flower stalks carry drooping, bell-shaped flowers in orange.

A Mexican succulent that forms rosettes of cupped, narrowly triangular leaves in pale silver-green and outlined in red. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in orange-pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.
An evergreen mat-forming succulent. Daisy-like flowers bloom from spring to fall. Multi-colored petals radiate from neon pink to goldfish orange. Leaves are chunky and frosty green.

An evergreen, low-growing succulent perennial with trailing stems and a cascading groundcover habit. Greenish-yellow fleshy leaves develop vivid red margins in bright light or cool temperatures. Star-shaped white flowers add contrast above the foliage. A compact, colorful selection for borders, pathways, containers, succulent walls, and waterwise landscape accents.

Large blue rosettes give this evergreen, clumping succulent a formal, layered shape. Powdery leaves may gain pink edges, and warm-colored flower stems rise above the mound for hummingbirds. Use it as a container centerpiece or a bright accent in dry beds. Sun, gritty soil, and room around the leaves preserve the clean finish.

An evergreen succulent with trailing, cascading stems. Fishhook-shaped leaves are blue-green. Off-white disk flowers bloom in fall and winter. Lightly fragrant. Attracts pollinators. Does well indoors.

This evergreen, trailing cactus grows flat green stems with deep zigzag cuts. Large cream-white flowers open at night and have a sweet scent. Edible fruit may follow. It comes from moist forests in Mexico and suits baskets or indoor pots. Filtered light, airy soil, and even water meet its needs better than dry desert care.

A succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of long, triangular leaves in salmon pink to light purple with pointed tips. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in vivid pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Best color in full sun.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent perennial with a bold, architectural habit. Broad paddle-shaped leaves are gray-green with red margins, often developing stronger red tones in cool, bright conditions. A tall flower stalk with pale yellow tubular flowers rises from mature rosettes in late winter to early spring. A strong accent for containers and dry garden compositions.

A succulent perennial that forms a trailing, mounding shrub. Frosty leaves are rounded, scalloped, and coated in waxy white hairs. Showy clusters of violet-pink flowers with yellow anthers bloom in winter and spring. Does well in a hanging pot.

commonName: Fox Tail Agave, Lion's Tail Agave, Swan's Neck Agave
botanicalName: Agave attenuata, A. cernua, A. glaucescens, A. pruinosa
description: An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

Foliage shifts through bronze, pink, purple, and green tones depending on season and exposure, giving it strong value in massed or mixed succulent designs. Yellow flowers appear on tall stalks. A durable, fast-growing selection for containers, slopes, and waterwise landscapes.

An evergreen, single-rosette succulent with broad, cupped, powder-blue leaves. Its bold shape makes a strong accent in rock gardens, dry beds, slopes, and large pots. The parent species grows in the high country of northeast Mexico. Mature plants send up a tall yellow-green flower stalk.

A succulent that forms a dense, mounding shrub. Rosettes are two-toned dark red on the edges, and light green at the centers. Best color emerges with exposure to bright light. Leaves are long, waxy. and spoon-shaped. Flowers bloom from mature rosettes. Cold hardy to 32 degrees F. Protect from frost.

This succulent forms colonies of low-growing rosettes. Gray-green leaves are triangular with neatly serrated edges. Color tinges purple in dry and cool conditions. Tall clusters of vivid orange flowers bloom in winter. Does well in sea-side conditions.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent perennial with a slow, compact habit. Symmetrical rosettes carry thick, spoon-shaped leaves with a powdery silver-gray finish and soft lilac to pink blush. Coral-pink flowers rise on short arching stems from late winter into early spring and provide food for pollinators. Benefits from excellent drainage and works well in containers, rock gardens, and small-scale succulent plantings.

A spreading, multi-branching succulent with rosettes of fleshy, pointed leaves. Leaves on the same plant display a palette of ghostly pale blues, purples, and pinks. White, star-shaped flowers in spring. Very hardy to 20 - 25 degrees F.

A Mexican succulent that forms large rosettes of fleshy, wavy-edged, paddle-shaped leaves in cool blue green with blushing pink margins. Similar to E. 'Blue Waves' but with more blue in the foliage and more red on the margins. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

A hybrid succulent that forms large, dramatic rosettes at the tips of tall, branched stems. Waxy rosettes are dark bronzy-red, surrounding high-contrast pale green centers. Yellow flower clusters bloom from mature rosettes in summer and fall. Provide partial shade inland, or full sun on the coast.

A succulent that forms mounding colonies of giant rosettes. Leaves are fuzzy, spoon-shaped and bright green with red tips. Abundant panicles of yellow flowers bloom from mature rosettes from winter to spring. Provide partial shade inland, or full sun on the coast. Drought tolerant.

An evergreen succulent that forms a tall, multi-branching tree. Powder-green leaves are flexible, sword-shaped, and pointed. Tan, spent leaves remain drooping downward below the rosettes. Large clusters of white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

A succulent that forms large rosettes of fleshy leaves in a variety of forms and colors. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in bright pink, orange, red, or yellow. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

A bold, evergreen succulent forming a broad, architectural rosette, Agave desmettiana ‘Gold Rush’ is prized for its bright variegation and relatively soft, user-friendly form. Smooth, spineless leaves feature a vibrant golden-yellow center with green margins, creating strong contrast and year-round color. This faster-growing agave performs well in full sun to partial sun, developing its best color with ample light, and thrives in well-drained soils with occasional deep watering once established. An excellent choice for containers, mass plantings, or as a focal point in low-water landscapes.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

A slow-growing Mexican cactus with a rounded to cylindrical, dark green body. Prominent vertical ribs are lined with needle-sharp yellow spines. Yellow flowers appear in summer. Produces offsets. Native to Mexico.

Golden green leaves turn orange and copper in strong light on this evergreen, spreading succulent. White star flowers may rise above the low stems, while broken pieces root easily. Use it to spill from pots, cover dry banks, or brighten rocks. Sun, gritty soil, and deep, spaced watering keep the color strong and stems compact.

A succulent shrub that forms a dense, upright bush. Chalky gray-green, pencil-like stems carry inconspicuous leaves that are remembered by their leaf scars. Small, yellow flower clusters bloom at branch tips in spring. Attracts butterflies.

A low-growing evergreen succulent that forms colonies of rosettes. Gray-green leaves are flexible, drooping, and sword-shaped. Variegated bright yellow streaks run down the center of each leaf. Large clusters of white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in spring, followed by brown capsule-type fruits.

A clumping perennial succulent that forms rosettes of fleshy, grass-like, green leaves with white, finely-toothed edges. Flushes to a bronze color in full sun. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in vermillion red.

A perennial succulent that forms a low, spreading ground cover of multiplying rosettes. Frosty blue-green leaves are fleshy, spoon-shaped, and notched on the tips. White flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.
A multi-branching succulent shrub with flat, rounded, cupped leaves, which are powdery yellow-green and outlined in crimson. Flower stalks carry drooping, bell-shaped flowers in salmon-red.
This evergreen succulent forms a showy, low-maintenance groundcover. Bright flowers bloom in neon magenta nearly year round from late spring to frost. The frosty green leaves are fleshy and slender.
An evergreen mat-forming succulent with a very dense growth habit. Golden daisy-like flowers bloom from spring to fall. Leaves are chunky, frosty green, and turn bronze in winter.

A succulent that forms rosettes of fleshy, diamond-shaped leaves in light green, tinged red. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in red and yellow. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

A succulent that forms rosettes of fleshy, diamond-shaped leaves in light green, tinged red. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in red and yellow. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

A multi-branched, tree-like succulent that forms rosettes of fleshy, broadly triangular, dark green leaves. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in salmon-orange. Grows faster and with a heavier trunk than A. barberae.

This succulent forms a dense rosette of slightly cupped, pointed leaves. Foliage is frosty blue green, outlined in pink. Best color in bright light. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers. Spreads by offsets.

A cold tolerant Sempervivum, hardy down to at least -30 degrees F. Silver-green rosettes are dramatically tipped in dark maroon-red. Offsets spread to form a dense, mounding groundcover. Reddish flowers.

Blue-green rosettes with red pointed tips spread into a low, evergreen succulent groundcover. Mature crowns lift pink flower stalks once, then nearby offsets fill the gap. Its precise pattern suits rock gardens, troughs, and cold dry slopes. Strong light, lean mineral soil, and fast drainage keep the rosettes tight and richly colored.

commonName: Hummel's Sunset Jade Plant, Golden Jade Tree
description: A succulent shrub with waxy, spoon-shaped leaves that are golden-green and outlined in fruity pink. Star-shaped flowers bloom in white to pale pink.

Dense burgundy spots cover the green leaves of this evergreen, rosette-form succulent and merge into a dark inked look in strong sun. The compact shape suits dry borders, rock gardens, and pots. Bright light, gritty soil, and deep, spaced watering preserve the pattern. Place the sharp leaf tips away from walks and play areas.

commonName: J. C. Raulston Hardy Century Plant
description: A handsome ornamental succulent that forms symmetrical rosettes of stiff, leathery, silvery-green leaves. Needle-sharp, brown to black spines arm the leaf margins and leaf tips. Especially adapted to winters in wet, humid climates. Spreads by suckering offshoots. Mature plants produce tall flower spikes.

A hybrid succulent that forms a showy mound of slightly cupped, brightly colored rosettes. Waxy, deep-red leaves surround highlighted green centers. Clusters of flowers bloom from mature rosettes. Cold hardy down to 25 degrees F.
A succulent shrub with waxy, tubular, jade green leaves that tint slightly maroon. Star-shaped flowers bloom in white to pale pink. Forms a stout, grayish stalks over time.
A succulent shrub with waxy, tubular, jade green leaves that tint slightly maroon. Star-shaped flowers bloom in white to pale pink. Forms a stout, grayish stalks over time.
A low-growing, spreading succulent that forms sprawling rosettes of broad, dark green leaves with bright golden teeth along the margins. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in orange-red.

Cream-striped leaves edged in green give this evergreen succulent a bright, architectural look. The open rosette stays tidy and works well as a container feature, entry accent, or contrast plant among darker foliage. Gray-green tones add year-round interest. Mature rosettes can send up tall flower stalks, while offsets help carry the planting forward.

commonName: John Creech Stonecrop, Two Row Stonecrop
description: A perennial succulent that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Small, cool green leaves are scalloped, rounded, and stacked in rows along short stems. Foliage flushes dark bugundy in cool weather. Pink flower clusters bloom in fall, attracting bees and butterflies. Tolerates part shade.
A small succulent that forms dense rosettes of narrow, fleshy, bright green leaves with white spots and small teeth. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in bright orange.
This succulent forms horizontally spreading colonies. Densely clustered rosettes display long, pointed leaves in cheerful green. Flower clusters bloom from mature rosettes.
A cultivated succulent with broad, spineless leaves. The suave, variegated leaves are chartreuse-yellow with glaucous-green edges. Slow growing.

A small, slow-growing succulent with chunky, triangular leaves. Coloration is silvery blue-green with white markings. Dark, spineless margins taper to sharp, terminal spines. After several years it produces a tall, branched flower stalk. Cold hardy to 10 - 15 degrees F.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with fleshy leaves arranged on branching stems. The bold foliage texture works well in containers, coastal plantings, and low-water accent beds, with seasonal flower stalks on mature rosettes. It benefits from excellent drainage and light irrigation during active growth.

A succulent with a balanced, well-branched form reminiscent of a miniature shrub. Attractively striped rosettes display cheerful green leaves with thick yellow margins, and yellow new growth. Yellow flower clusters bloom from mature rosettes in summer. Cold hardy to 25 - 30 degrees F.
An evergreen succulent that forms a spreading ground cover. Upward-pointing, fleshy, finger-like leaves are waxy blue-gray. Off-white disk flowers bloom in winter. Attracts pollinators.

An evergreen, clumping succulent forming tight rosettes. This cultivar features heavily ruffled, undulating leaves in powdery blue-green tones with pink to lavender margins under stress. Best color develops in bright light with cool temperatures. Performs best in fast-draining soil with a watering regimen that allows soil to dry between deep soakings.

A shrubby succulent with fleshy, upright stems and sparse leaves. Stems are bright green coated in a waxy, whitish film. Unusual, orange-red flowers bloom in spring and fall, attracting hummingbirds. Male flowers are showy and slipper-shaped. Female flowers have two bracts and an upper spur. Does well in containers. Drought tolerant. Native to Mexico.

This evergreen, rosette-form succulent spreads broad smoky lavender leaves. Fine purple spots grow darker in full sun. The soft color works well in modern pots, gravel beds, and mixed dry plantings. Give it bright light, fast-draining soil, and deep, spaced water. Set the sharp leaf tips back from paths and play areas.

A perennial succulent that forms a mounding, creeping cushion. Bright golden leaves are small, linear and needle-like. Bright yellow flower clusters bloom in late spring, attracting bees and butterflies.

A perennial succulent that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Bright chartreuse leaves are fleshy and needle-like. Foliage tinges red-orange in cool weather. Yellow flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.

An evergreen succulent that forms a pincushion rosette atop a stout trunk. Bluish-green leaves are flexible, very narrow, finely toothed, and pointed. Large clusters of white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, triangular leaves in apple green with crisp red margins. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in red-orange. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Best color in full sun.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

commonName: Liuzard's Tail, Watch Chain, Princess Pine
botanicalName: Crassula muscosa, C. lycopodioides, C. mucosa var. pseudolycopodioides
description: A succulent shrub with tightly formed, jade green rosettes that grow upright on stalks. Small flowers bloom in yellowish green.

A succulent that forms a rosette atop a stout trunk, which may eventually reach up to 20 feet high in ideal conditions. Leaves are dark gray-green, slender, sword-shaped and lined with teeth. Mature plants send up tall branched flower stalks. In the Agave family.

An evergreen succulent makes a sculptural rosette of broad blue-gray leaves marked with bold bud imprints and scalloped edges. It is native to rocky oak grasslands of western Mexico. Use it in dry borders, gravel gardens, and containers. Mature plants send up a tall flower stalk, set seed, and can continue through seedlings or offsets.

A hybrid succulent with outstanding tri-color variegation. Leaves are striped in bright green, yellow, and red. Best color when grown in bright light. Offsets form a spreading colony of large, showy rosettes. Flower stalks bloom from the centers of mature rosettes.

An ornamental succulent that forms rosettes of lengthy, spineless, outwardly arching leaves in green with a pale green midrib down the center of each leaf. Soft, finely-toothed margins taper to flimsy tips of glowing scarlet-brown. Mature plants produce tall flower spikes.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

A charming succulent that forms large rosettes of fleshy, cupped, paddle-shaped leaves in shades of silvery green and lavender. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in bright pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.
A slow-growing, tall, clumping cactus with ribbed, spiny, bluish green skin. Showy pinkish-red flowers.
A grassy-looking evergreen shrub that forms clumps of stiff, arching, olive green leaves. Develops a stout trunk over time. Eventually bears large spikes of creamy white flowers.

A succulent that forms short-stemmed rosettes of fleshy, ruffled leaves in glaucous blue-gray, sometimes with pink edges. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in pink-yellow. Fall to winter flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Offsets form colonies.

An evergreen, clumping succulent that forms tight rosettes and slowly spreads by offsets into a low mound. Spoon-shaped whitish-green to pale gray leaves create a clean, rounded texture, with pink and yellow-tinged flowers in late winter through spring. Performs well in full sun to light shade with well-drained soil and occasional deep watering.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with fleshy leaves arranged on branching stems. The bold foliage texture works well in containers, coastal plantings, and low-water accent beds, with seasonal flower stalks on mature rosettes. It benefits from excellent drainage and light irrigation during active growth.

Soft curtains of thin green stems hang from this evergreen, trailing cactus. Small white flowers may be followed by red berry-like fruit. It comes from moist forests in Brazil and makes a good basket or indoor plant. Give it filtered light, airy rich soil, even water, warmth, and shelter from frost for full growth.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, triangular leaves in apple green with blushing, pointed tips. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in red-orange. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Best color in full sun.
A succulent that forms a rosette of narrow, fleshy, prickly, green leaves. Tall clusters of tubular winter flowers appear in orange-red.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with a compact, powdery texture. Spoon-shaped blue-green to gray-green leaves are coated with farina and edged pink, with color becoming stronger in brighter light. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.
A shrubby evergreen succulent that forms mounding rosettes. Fleshy, rounded leaves are frosty blue-green. Bright red-orange disk flowers bloom in fall and winter. Attracts pollinators.

An evergreen succulent that forms a spiky, fountain-like rosette atop a slow-growing, palm-like trunk. Silvery-blue-green leaves are thin and stiff with coarse margins. A large flower stalk arises at maturity. Native to Mexico.

An evergreen, clumping succulent perennial with bold, ruffled rosettes. Blue-green to mauve foliage develops vivid purple-pink, crinkled margins, with color intensifying in bright conditions. Offsets form over time, making it useful for containers, accent plantings, and waterwise compositions. A hybrid noted for strong ornamental color and improved garden performance.

This blue-gray succulent forms a broad, rounded rosette. Leaves are edged with small, red spines and are tipped with long terminal spines. Produces a tall flower spike at a younger age than most Agaves. Does not form offsets.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

A perennial succulent that forms a creeping, small-scale ground cover. Golden leaves are tiny, fleshy and circular. Foliage sometimes tinges pink. Yellow flower clusters bloom in late spring, attracting bees and butterflies. Tolerates some shade.

An attractive succulent that forms tight rosettes of pale gray-blue to light pink leaves. Short branching inflorescences emerge in late spring, carrying yellow flowers with orange centers. Best color in full sun.

An evergreen, clumping succulent perennial with grass-like fleshy leaves and slender spikes of orange starry flowers. The long warm-season bloom supports bees and adds fine texture to low-water plantings. It performs best in well-drained soil and can be cut back to refresh growth.

An evergreen, clumping succulent perennial with grass-like fleshy leaves and slender spikes of orange starry flowers. The long warm-season bloom supports bees and adds fine texture to low-water plantings. It performs best in well-drained soil and can be cut back to refresh growth.

commonName: Our Lord's Candle, Spanish Bayonet, Chaparral Yucca
description: Evergreen shrub with rosettes of strappy and tooth-edged leaves in gray-green, tall spikes of creamy white bell-shaped flowers.

An evergreen succulent that forms spreading colonies of rosettes. Younger, smaller, vibrant pink offsets crowd around older, larger, deeper purple rosettes. Leaves are uniquely tubular and fleshy. Flower stalks bloom in summer.

A Mexican succulent that forms large, loose rosettes of fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves in dark gray-green with cabernet-red stripes and margins. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in orange-yellow. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

An evergreen succulent that stays low to the ground. Pale blue-gray leaves are flexible, sword-shaped, and pointed. Margins are light yellow and finely serrated. Large clusters of white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

A succulent perennial that forms a multi-branched shrub of rosettes. Fleshy, oval, gray-green leaves are coated in white fur and marked in brown-black along the edges. Terminal clusters of yellow-green flowers bloom in winter and spring. Rarely blooms indoors.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with a refined, symmetrical habit. Fleshy obovate leaves are gray to purplish-gray with pink highlights and a powdery surface, with coral to light red flowers on upright stems in warm weather. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.
A tall, clumping cactus with ribbed, spiny, blue-green skin. Large, white flowers open fully at night. Edible, apple-shaped fruits ripen from purple to red.
A succulent shrub featuring silver-green, flat, round leaves, arranged in opposite pairs. Showy, salmon-orange, bell-shaped flowers bloom from summer through fall.

A succulent that forms rosettes of fleshy, diamond-shaped leaves in purple-gray-green. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in orange-pink. Fall to winter flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Offsets form colonies.

A Southwestern perennial that forms clumps of stiff, leathery, bright green leaves with thread-like fringe along the margins. Tall branching inflorescences up to 6 - 8 feet tall carry clusters of tubular, pink flowers.

A succulent that forms a mounding colony of small, 3 - 4" rosettes. Variegated leaves are cool blue-green, outlined in rosy pink. Flower stalks bloom from mature rosettes in spring and summer. Flowers can be light yellow, white, or pinkish. Cold hardy down to 20 - 25 degrees F. Provide partial shade inland, or full sun on the coast.

A succulent that forms a small, multi-branching shrub of 10 inch wide rosettes. Spoon-shaped leaves are rich plum-purple, surrounding bright green centers. Yellow flower stalks bloom from mature rosettes.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with broad, softly cupped foliage and a compact architectural form. Powdery gray-blue to silvery leaves develop a pale pink blush at the margins in bright light, creating strong contrast in mixed succulent plantings.

A palm-like succulent with an unusual multi-branching form. The base is gray-brown, leathery and becomes swollen with age until it resembles the foot of an elephant. Recurved green leaves sprout like top-knot ponytails. Insignificant cream-white flowers are rarely seen. Native to Mexico. Typically kept as an indoor plant.

A perennial succulent that forms a sprawling, cascading ground cover with upright stems. Shiny, green leaves are fleshy, plump, and jellybean-like. Foliage tints bronze-red in summer. Flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.

An evergreen, upright rosette-forming succulent with a compact, highly architectural habit. Dark green leaves curl upward and inward into a narrow, artichoke-like form, with cinnamon-brown terminal spines and narrow reddish margins that define the rosette. This slow-growing selection is useful as a specimen, container accent, or focal point in modern, dry garden, and rock garden plantings. Best performance comes with fast drainage, lean to average soil, and low supplemental irrigation once established.

A succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, diamond-shaped leaves in frosty gray-green, finely edged in dark red. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in yellow. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

A multi-branching succulent with rosettes of dark, wine red leaves emerge from light green centers. Eventually forms a shrubby, tree-like structure. Blooms with large clusters of bright yellow flowers in summer. Hardy to 25 - 30 degrees F. Drought tolerant. Likes full sun on the coast, and partial shade inland.
A succulent that forms tight lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, triangular leaves in dusty dark green and rusty maroon. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in orange-red.

A succulent that forms robust rosettes of dense, purple-black leaves emerging from bright green centers. Rosettes resemble pinwheels at the tips of bare, branched stems. As each rosette reaches maturity, a panicle of yellow flowers blooms.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, slow-growing succulent shrub with a sprawling, easily pruned habit. Reddish-brown stems carry small glossy green leaves edged in cream, adding bright contrast to dry garden plantings and container combinations. This selection works well as a bonsai subject, hanging basket plant, or informal hedge in frost-free sites. Size is readily managed with pruning and container culture.

commonName: Ray of Light Fox Tail Agave
description: An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.
An evergreen succulent with gray-green leaves with deep red tips. Red intensifies in cool weather. Offsets spread to form a mounding groundcover. Pink flower spikes in summer.

A multi-branching succulent that forms rosettes of thick, super fuzzy leaves in light green, tinged red. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in orange and yellow. Offsets form colonies.

A Mexican succulent that forms large rosettes of cupped, wavy, triangular leaves in pale silver-green and outlined in red. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in orange-pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

An evergreen succulent that forms spreading colonies of lotus-like rosettes. Younger, smaller offsets crowd around older, larger rosettes. Fleshy leaves are pointed, narrowly spoon-shaped and deep wine red with bright green tips. Leaves will become almost fully red during winter. Flower stalks bloom in summer.

An evergreen mat-forming succulent. Daisy-like flowers bloom from spring to fall. Multi-colored petals radiate from yellow to white to hot pink to luminous orange-red. Leaves are chunky and frosty green.

A perennial succulent that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Chalky silver foliage heavily blushes purple-red. Leaves are flattened, spoon-shaped, and arranged in tiny rosettes. Yellow flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies. Tolerates part shade. Native to California and beyond.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves in cool apple green with blushing red edges and pointed tips. Offsets form colonies. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in red-orange. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Best color in full sun.
This succulent forms clusters of large, open rosettes. Waxy, maroon-red leaves are highlighted by pale green new growth. Stalks of yellow flowers emerge from mature rosettes.

A native southwestern perennial forming clumps of stiff and leathery, gray-green leaves with thread-like fringe along the margins. Tall branching inflorescences carry clusters of tubular, pink flowers.

commonName: Ripple Jade, Blue Waves Jade Plant
description: A succulent shrub that forms a stout trunk and dense foliage. Wavy-edged leaves are waxy, narrow, and bright green with fine red margins. Star-shaped flowers bloom in white to pale pink. Can be grown indoors.
A shrubby perennial succulent with a clumping growth habit. Leaves are fleshy and gray-green. Brilliant magenta flowers bloom year round atop tall, bare stalks. Native to Chile.

This succulent forms a spiny, pale blue-gray rosette. Leaves are the texture of sand paper. At maturity, each rosette produces a very tall flower stalk up to 20 feet high. Offsets form clumps. Cold hardy to 15 degrees F.

An evergreen, shrubby succulent with branching woody stems and softly hairy foliage. Green paddle-shaped leaves are densely arranged and tipped deep pink-red, with bright orange flowers rising above the foliage. Offsets form colonies over time.

A succulent that forms dense clumps of small rosettes with many offsets. Variegated leaves are green with a broad yellow stripe down the center. Reddish toothed margins taper to sharp terminal spines. Mature plants produce tall flower spikes.
A clustering succulent that forms rosettes of recurved, fleshy, gray-green leaves. Tall clusters of tubular winter flowers appear in salmon pink.
A clustering succulent that forms rosettes of recurved, fleshy, gray-green leaves. Tall clusters of tubular winter flowers appear in bright orange.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with medium-sized rosettes. Foliage is warm-toned, ranging from sandy apricot to muted copper with soft pink highlights, intensifying in bright light and dry conditions. Maintains a compact, uniform habit suited to mixed succulent plantings and container use. Prefers fast-draining soils and responds well to infrequent, deep irrigation.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with fleshy leaves arranged on branching stems. The bold foliage texture works well in containers, coastal plantings, and low-water accent beds, with seasonal flower stalks on mature rosettes. It benefits from excellent drainage and light irrigation during active growth.

Small glossy green leaves pack into a low, evergreen to semi-evergreen mat on this spreading succulent perennial. Yellow star flowers appear in summer and feed small insects. It fills pots, wall pockets, and shaded rock edges with soft texture. Sun or bright shade, open soil, and moderate drainage keep the mat full without coarse growth.

A cactus with a columnar growth habit, often with branching side arms. The body is deeply ribbed and lined with minute spines. The color is medium green to bluish-green. Flowers are large, white and nocturnal.

A succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, glaucous green leaves which are coated in a fine chalky white powder. Stalks of yellow flowers appear in spring and summer, attracting hummingbirds. Spreads by offsets. Avoid overhead watering.

A cold-hardy evergreen succulent that usually forms one rosette per trunk. Powder-blue leaves are shorter than the species, stiff, very narrow, and needle-pointed. Spent leaves skirt the trunk as it slowy grows upwards to 12 feet or more. Large clusters of white flowers rise up in early summer, followed by beak-like, capsule-type fruits.

This multi-branching succulent forms a dense shrub of broad, flattened rosettes. The rounded, waxy leaves are bright, true green. Clusters of yellow flowers emerge from mature rosettes. Provide partial shade inland, or full coastal sun. Drought tolerant once established.

A bright green succulent that forms a very large rosette up to 20" across, accompanied by a gigantic pyramidal flower stalk at maturity. The inflorescence can stand up to 3 feet high and wide above the rosette. Flowers are light pink and star-shaped.

A California native succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, finger-like leaves. Gray-green leaves are somewhat translucent, coated in a fine powder, and tipped in rosy-pink. Impressive pinkish red stalks bear orange flowers in spring and attract hummingbirds. Spreads by offsets.

A Mexican succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, somewhat lance-shaped leaves in dark olive-maroon with green centers. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in orange-pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.
A stout, ornamental succulent that forms rosettes of smooth, glaucous, dark gray-green leaves with dark, needle-sharp, terminal spines. Mature plants produce tall flowers stalks. Suckers freely.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

A low-growing evergreen succulent that forms colonies of rosettes. Bluish-green leaves are flexible, arching, sword-shaped, and pointed. 6 foot tall clusters of fragrant, ivory-white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.
A succulent shrub with waxy, rounded leaves that are stippled and silvery gray with fine red margins. Star-shaped flowers bloom in white to pale pink.

Powdery silver leaves stand upright on this evergreen, clumping succulent, creating a bright architectural mound. Tall stems carry pendent coral-orange bells that attract hummingbirds. It works well in dry borders, coastal gardens, and large pots. Sun and gritty soil deepen the leaf color. All parts are toxic if eaten by people or animals.

An upright succulent with robust, blue-green leaves providing a year-round show of color. Incredibly tolerant to heat and drought once established, this provides excellent structure and vertical interest to succulent gardens.
This succulent produces an abundance of offsets, forming clumps of smooth-edged, sharp-tipped rosettes. Foliage is light blue-green. Mature rosettes produce tall, branched flower spikes.

A succulent that forms tight rosettes of fleshy, maroon-green leaves, lined with small brown teeth. The leaves feature faint white spots that flush pink in hot weather. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in salmon-orange.
This succulent that forms a rounded rosette of pencil-thin, emerald green leaves garnished with curly, white threads on leaf edges. Mature plants produce tall spikes of paired, yellow flowers.

A perennial succulent that forms a creeping, small-scale ground cover. Blue-gray leaves are tiny, fleshy, and needle-like. Foliage tinges purple in cool weather. Pinkish-white flower clusters bloom in early spring and summer, attracting bees and butterflies.
An ornamental succulent that forms clumps of numerous, thin, prickly leaves in gray-green. Tall clusters of tubular flowers appear in red.

A true cactus that spreads to form a low, shrubby fence. Blue-green cladodes are flat, rounded and pad-like. Widely spaced areoles lack spines. Large flowers are followed by prickly-pear fruits. Fruit ripens in summer. Hardy to 0 deg F.

An evergreen succulent that forms spreading colonies of rosettes. Younger, smaller offsets crowd around older, larger rosettes. Leaves are uniquely fleshy and vibrant green with blushing pink tips. Flower stalks bloom in summer.

A slow growing evergreen succulent with intricate rosettes and showy clusters of pink and red flowers from spring into winter. Light grey to bluish green leaves are oppositely arranged on stiff upright stems. Attracts pollinators.

This succulent forms an unusual rosette of large, wavy leaves in bright metallic green. Rosettes perch above ground atop stout, unbranched stalks. A dark yellow flower cluster blooms as the rosette prepares to complete its life cycle. Provide partial shade for hot, inland climates.

commonName: Sticks on Fire Milkbush, Red Pencil Tree
description: A succulent shrub that forms an upright bush. Pencil-like stems carry tiny, inconspicuous leaves. Stems are bright coral-red to yellow-orange to golden-green. Non-showy flowers. Toxic to dogs, cats, other animals, and humans. All plant parts contain a caustic, milky sap that is known to cause burns and welts.

commonName: String of Pearls, String of Beads
description: An evergreen succulent with trailing, cascading stems. Pea-shaped leaves are bright green. Pinkish cottony disk flowers bloom in fall and winter. Lightly fragrant. Attracts pollinators.

A stemless, evergreen succulent forms loose clusters of green rosettes marked with pale spots and soft teeth. Branched flowers shift from coral to orange and attract hummingbirds. Native to rocky, sandy ground in Sudan, it suits dry beds and containers. Strong light, warm conditions, and quick drainage help it keep a compact form.
A perennial succulent that forms a vigorous, compact ground cover. Eye-catching cherry-red leaves are oval and flattened. Large, pink flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.
A perennial succulent that forms a vigorous, compact ground cover. Eye-catching blue-gray leaves are oval and flattened. Huge, pink flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.

A perennial succulent that forms a vigorous, compact ground cover. Powdery, purple-flushed leaves are oval and flattened. Huge, bright pink flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.

A perennial succulent that forms a compact ground cover. Variegated lime green, pink-edged leaves are rounded, flattened, and small. Light pink flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with open rosettes of long, arching leaves. Blue, lavender, purple, and burgundy tones deepen in bright light, and soft red teeth line each leaf. Branched stalks carry red tubular flowers that feed hummingbirds. Use in containers, rock gardens, or bold mass plantings. Provide porous soil with sharp drainage.

A shrubby succulent with upright stems, thicker and taller than P. macrocarpus. Stems are beset with oval, green leaves. Unusual, male and female flowers are enclosed in pinky-red bracts. Blooms in spring and summer. Good in containers. Drought tolerant. Native to Mexico. Hardy to at least 25 degrees F.

botanicalName: Aloe arborescens x ferox 'Tangerine', A. principis
description: An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.
A South African perennial succulent with fleshy, bright green, pencil-like leaves. Tangerine-orange flower clusters attract butterflies from spring through fall.

This iconic succulent species is used as the base ingredient for tequila production in Mexico. Main rosette produces abundant offsets. Blue-gray leaves are armed with sharp, dark brown marginal and terminal spines. Mature rosettes produce tall flower stalks. Hardy to 27 degrees F.

A grassy-looking evergreen shrub that forms clumps of stiff, light green leaf blades. Develops a stout trunk over time. Eventually bears large spikes of creamy white flowers, which can grow 9 - 15 feet high.

A succulent that forms large rosettes of fleshy, cupped, paddle-shaped leaves in silvery lavender with pointed tips in a cool pink. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in coral pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

A small, ornamental succulent. Dark green rosettes are adorned with white hair-like filaments along the margins. Sharp terminal spines. Mature plants produce tall, branched flower spikes. Super cold hardy to 0 degrees F.

A succulent that forms rosettes of fleshy, curved, tongue-shaped leaves in frosty gray-green. Slender flower stalks carry nodding, bell-shaped flowers in coral pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators. Offsets form colonies.
A dwarf, spreading succulent with fleshy, pointed leaves that taper to whip-like threads. Long, arching spikes of flower clusters appear in pinky-red. A cold hardy variety.

An evergreen, clumping succulent with fleshy leaves and upright flower spikes that are highly attractive to hummingbirds. The bold foliage provides year-round texture in low-water borders, rock gardens, and containers. It thrives in sharply drained soil and responds well to deep, infrequent irrigation.

A perennial succulent that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Variegated green, white-edged, pink-tinted leaves are small, rounded, and stacked in rows along short stems. Pink flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies. Tolerates part shade.

A true cactus that spreads to form a shrubby fence. Blue-gray, pad-like cladodes turn ornamental purple in winter. Needle-like spines poke out from widely spaced areoles. Large, yellow flowers in spring and summer are followed by prickly pear fruits. Evergreen.

An evergreen succulent with rosettes of fleshy, bright green leaves. Yellow-red flowers clusters are available from spring into summer, and attract butterflies and hummingbirds. Great selection for a rock wall, or container planting.

This succulent species forms a compact, rounded rosette of flexible, pencil-thin leaves. Foliage is dark green. The mature rosette produces a very tall spike of paired, yellow flowers. Typically solitary, not known for producing offsets. Hardy to 25 degrees F.

An evergreen succulent that forms a low fountain-like rosette. Bright green leaves are twisted and sword-shaped. Large clusters of white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

An ornamental succulent that forms a solitary rosette of curvy, cupped leaves in glaucous gray-green. Toothed margins taper to dark, needle-sharp terminal spines. Mature plants produce tall flower spikes. One of the hardiest Agaves.

A perennial succulent that looks much like yucca. A fountain-shaped rosette of variegated green and yellow leaves grows from an above-ground trunk. From the center of each rosette, a tall red stalk emerges to display bright pink and green bell-shaped flowers. Attracts hummingbirds.

commonName: Variegated Blue Glow Agave, Snow Glow Agave
botanicalName: Agave x 'Blue Glow', Agave x 'Snow Glow'
description: An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

A succulent that forms a large rosette, usually without a trunk. Variegated leaves are green with a thick white band down the center, sword-shaped, wavy, and not sharp. Mature plants send up tall branched flower stalks, up to 25 feet high. Flowers are strongly fragrant. In the Agave family.

An evergreen succulent that forms a single or multi-branching shrub. Gray-green leave are sword-shaped and sharp-tipped. Variegated creamy-yellow leaf margins tinge pink in cool weather. Large clusters of white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

This iconic succulent species is used as the base ingredient for tequila production in Mexico. Main rosette produces abundant offsets. Blue-gray leaves are armed with sharp, dark brown marginal and terminal spines. Mature rosettes produce tall flower stalks. Hardy to 27 degrees F.

A perennial succulent that forms a compact mound. Purple-gray, pink-tinted leaves are egg-shaped and arranged on purple stems. Large, flat-topped, rouge-pink flower clusters bloom in late summer and fall, attracting bees and butterflies.

A compact, evergreen rosette-forming succulent with a symmetrical, mounding habit. Thick, fleshy leaves are powdery blue-gray with a soft violet blush, forming tight rosettes that add refined structure to containers and rock gardens. Ideal for well-drained soils and bright light, this selection develops its best coloration with ample sun and deep, infrequent irrigation.

A succulent that forms lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, narrow leaves in frosty pale green with rosy tips and edges. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink and yellow. Forms offsets.

Burgundy and green rosettes form a tight, evergreen succulent groundcover that changes color with sun and cold. Older rosettes bloom pink once, then offsets continue the colony. Use it in stone joints, alpine beds, or shallow containers. Bright light, lean gritty soil, and fast drainage keep the rosettes compact through winter.

A perennial succulent that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Black-cherry red leaves are scallop-edged, flattened, and arranged in stacked rows. Bright pinkish-red flower clusters bloom in summer, attracting bees and butterflies.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

A succulent that forms larger, lotus-like rosettes of fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves in silver-white with a soft lavender-pink glow. Slender flower stalks carry nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink. Flowers provide nectar for pollinators.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

A Southwestern perennial that forms spiky clusters of extra wide leaves with thread-like fringe along the margins. Foliage is stiff, leathery, and unarmed. Branching inflorescences carry clusters of tubular, creamy-white flowers. Flowers stalks reach up to 8 - 12 feet high. Cold hardy to 10 degrees F.

An evergreen, clumping succulent perennial with narrow fleshy leaves and slender spikes of yellow starry flowers. The long bloom season and low profile suit dry borders, containers, and mass plantings. It thrives in heat, reflected light, and well-drained soil with occasional irrigation.

An evergreen, clumping, succulent perennial with arching, sword-like foliage and a clean, architectural form. Leathery gray-green leaves have narrow grooves and white thread-like margins, forming a durable accent for xeric, desert, poolside, and mass plantings. Tall, arching stalks carry yellow tubular flowers from late spring into summer, attracting hummingbirds. Performs well with good drainage and occasional summer irrigation in dry inland sites.

A native southwestern perennial forming clumps of stiff and leathery, gray-green leaves with thread-like fringe along the margins. Tall branching inflorescences carry clusters of tubular, yellow flowers.

An evergreen, rosette-forming succulent with thick architectural leaves and a strong sculptural presence. Mature plants produce a tall flowering stalk that attracts pollinators before the rosette completes its life cycle. It is an excellent low-water accent for well-drained soil, slopes, containers, and contemporary landscapes.

commonName: Yucca, Adam's Needle, Spanish Bayonet, Needle Palm
description: A low-growing evergreen succulent that forms colonies of rosettes. Dark blue-green leaves are arching, sword-shaped, needle-pointed. Curly, white threads line the margins. Large clusters of fragrant, white, bell-shaped flowers rise up in early summer, followed by capsule-type fruits.

A compact, evergreen shrub with dense green foliage and a rounded habit. Large white flowers with a pale green throat bloom in spring, bringing bright color to shaded borders, foundations, and containers. Performs best with acidic, well-drained organic soil, mulch, and regular moisture.

A slow-growing evergreen shrub with an upright, bushy habit. Medium-sized, double-white flowers show off early in the season. Each flower has over 100 petals. Leaves are medium green and extra glossy.

Rounded and evergreen, this shrub bears white flower heads with a light lilac wash. Thick leaves make a dense screen after bloom, and early insects visit the flowers. Use it as a tall backdrop, hedge, or woodland group. Filtered light, acid soil rich in leaf mold, and regular water support roots. All parts are toxic.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded habit. Mid to late spring bloom. Funnel-shaped flowers grow in globe-shaped trusses. Flowers are purple-pink with a red blotch. Attracts butterflies, bees and hummingbirds. Glossy green leaves are elliptic and leathery. Tolerates heat and sun. Does well in Northern California. Hardy to -15 degrees F. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a vigorous habit. Mid to late spring bloom. Large, funnel-shaped flowers grow in globe-shaped trusses. Flowers are deep pink, faintly spotted in brown. Attracts butterflies, bees and hummingbirds. Matte, olive-green leaves are elliptic and leathery. Dependable and widely adapted. Hardy to -5 degrees F. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

A graceful evergreen shrub with an upright, airy growth habit. Flowers are single and profuse. Petals are white with blushing pink edges. Stamens are golden yellow. Blooms from fall to winter in California. Foliage is dark green. Leaves are smaller than C. japonica. Sasanqua camellias are more tolerant of sun than japonicas. Needs acidic soil, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit. Showy, funnel-shaped flowers come in pinky purple with blooms from spring to fall. Foliage is glossy and pointed. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit. Showy, fragrant, funnel-shaped flowers come in crisp white. Blooms from spring to fall. Foliage is glossy and dark green. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit. Showy, semi-double, funnel-shaped flowers appear in scarlet red. Blooms from spring to fall. Glossy, dark green foliage turns bronze in winter. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit. Showy, semi-double, funnel-shaped flowers appear in rich pink. Blooms from spring to fall. Glossy, dark green foliage turns bronze in winter. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with a rounded, compact growth habit. Showy, semi-double, funnel-shaped flowers come in tomato red. Blooms from spring to fall. Foliage is leathery and dark green. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with a rounded, compact growth habit. Showy, semi-double, funnel-shaped flowers come in ruby red. Blooms from spring to fall. Foliage is deep green and glossy. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with a rounded, compact growth habit. Showy, funnel-shaped flowers come in ivory white. Blooms from spring to fall. Foliage is dark and glossy green. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit. Showy, semi-double, funnel-shaped flowers appear in white. Blooms from spring to fall. Glossy, dark green foliage turns bronze in winter. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a round form. Foliage is dark green and glossy. Showy, semi-double, funnel-shaped flowers come in deep rosy pink. Blooms from spring to fall. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit. Showy, ruffled, funnel-shaped flowers come in magenta pink. Blooms from spring to fall. Foliage is deep green and glossy. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Showy, ruffled, funnel-shaped flowers come in coral pink with white edges. Blooms from spring to fall. Foliage is dark green and glossy. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

A broadleaf evergreen shrub with ball-shaped trusses of striking dark red blooms that appear almost black, and an upright, spreading habit. Foliage is heavily veined. Needs acidic soil, 4.5 - 6.0. Hardy to -5 degrees F.

An understory evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Flowers are large, semi-double, and peony-form. Petals are deep red. Stamens are golden yellow. Blooms from January to March in California. Leaves are leathery, dark green, and have finely serrated edges. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit. Showy, funnel-shaped flowers come in an array of colors. Blooms in spring and re-blooms in late summer through fall. Foliage is dark green and glossy. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0. 'Double Pink' has double flowers in vibrant pink. 'Hot Pink' has hot pink flowers. 'Lavender' has lavender-pink flowers with dark pink markings. 'Red' has true red flowers. 'White' has crisp white flowers.

This evergreen, broad shrub bears round white spring flower heads like snowballs. Some blooms have small green or brown marks. Dense leaves make a year-round screen. Use it in woodland groups, shaded foundation beds, or loose hedges. Filtered light, acid soil rich in leaf mold, and steady water support roots. All parts are toxic.

An evergreen shrub with a dense, upright, spreading habit. Mid to late spring bloom. Funnel-shaped flowers grow in globe-shaped trusses. Flowers are light pinkish-purple with a pale brown blotch. Attracts butterflies, bees and hummingbirds. Mid-green leaves are elliptic and leathery. Tolerant of sun and heat. Hardy to -20 degrees F. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded habit. A pink-flowered sport of 'Unique.' Early to mid-spring bloom. Large, funnel-shaped flowers grow in dome-shaped trusses. Flowers are light pink with pale yellow throats. Attracts butterflies, bees and hummingbirds. Glossy, olive green leaves are oval-elliptic and leathery. Hardy to -5 degrees F. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0. Photo courtesy of Enjoy Rhododendrons.

A graceful evergreen shrub with a dense, mounding growth habit. Flowers are slightly fragrant, small, and semi-double or formal. Petals are pale creamy yellow. Stamens are golden yellow. Blooms between C. sasanqua and C. japonica, from late winter to spring. Leaves are leathery, light green, and have finely serrated margins. Needs acidic soil, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

An understory evergreen shrub with a compact growth habit. Flowers are midsize, semi-double, and formal or peony form. Petals are pale pink with dark pink stripes. Stamens are golden yellow. Blooms from October to May in California. Leaves are leathery, medium green, and have finely serrated edges. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a vigorous, rounded habit. Mid to late spring bloom. Large, funnel-shaped flowers grow in globe-shaped trusses. Flowers are light purple with a yellow-red blotch. Attracts butterflies, bees and hummingbirds. Glossy, dark green leaves are elliptic and leathery. Hardy to -15 degrees F. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

A graceful evergreen shrub with a low, arching growth habit. Flowers are double and profuse. Petals are bright pink. Stamens are golden yellow. Blooms from fall to winter in California. Foliage is dark green. Leaves are smaller than C. japonica. Sasanqua camellias are more tolerant of sun than japonicas. Needs acidic soil, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

With a rounded form, this shrub carries white flower heads, often with a pale yellow-green mark. Dense dark leaves give year-round cover, and early insects visit the bloom. Use it in foundation beds, woodland groups, or loose hedges. Filtered sun, acid soil rich in leaf mold, and water keep roots cool. All parts are toxic.

A graceful evergreen shrub with a compact, upright growth habit. Flowers are small to midsize, and semi-double to double. Petals are creamy rouge pink. Stamens are golden yellow. Blooms from fall to winter in California. Foliage is dark green. Leaves are smaller than C. japonica. Sasanqua camellias are more tolerant of sun than japonicas. Needs acidic soil, pH 5.1 - 6.0.
A broadleaf evergreen shrub with fuzzy, glossy leaves. Pink and white flowers emerge in spring. Attracts bees. Needs acidic soil, 4.5 - 6.0.
An evergreen shrub or small tree producing beautiful dark red, formal double blooms. Leathery, dark green leaves have finely toothed margins. Can tolerate full shade.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit. Abundant, showy, funnel-shaped flowers come in bright coral-pink with darker pink centers. Foliage is leathery and rich green. Kurume hybrid. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

An understory evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded growth habit. Flowers are small to midsize, and semi-double. Petals are rich coral pink. Stamens are bright yellow. Blooms from January to March in California. Leaves are glossy, dark green, and have finely serrated edges. Can tolerate full shade. Needs acidic soil, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

An evergreen shrub with a dense habit. Mid to late spring bloom. Funnel-shaped flowers grow in loose trusses. Flowers are white with light purple-brown markings. Attracts butterflies, bees and hummingbirds. Dark green leaves are elliptic and leathery. Hardy to -15 degrees F. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 6.0.

Technically a conifer, this evergreen tree is noted for being clean and relatively pest-free. Feathery foliage is narrow and longer than P. gracilior, in deep glossy green.

A large, evergreen conifer with a bold pyramidal to open architectural habit. Stiff, glossy, triangular dark green leaves densely cover thick branches, creating a strong specimen silhouette. Slow growth and striking texture suit large gardens, parks, and institutional landscapes. Performs best with well-drained soil and moderate summer irrigation in warm inland sites.
A wind-swept conifer native to the Monterey Peninsula in California. Deep green, overlapping scale-like leaves cloak outwardly spreading branches. Best grown along the coast where summers are cool.

commonName: Mops Mugo Pine, Swiss Mountain Pine
description: A dwarf evergreen conifer that forms a low, compact globe. Slow growing. Dark green needles tend to take on a golden hue in winter.

An evergreen conifer that forms a spreading shrub. Yellow-green foliage is overlapping and scale-like. New growth at branch tips emerges bright golden-yellow. Similar to J. x p. 'Aurea'. Typically, plants bear either catkin-like male cones, or berry-like female cones. Attracts birds.
Evergreen tree with rich, blue-green needles and shaggy, reddish-orange bark. Pom Pom is a sculpted form.
An evergreen, coniferous ground-cover shrub with chartreuse foliage on long, trailing branches. Juvenile leaves are needle-like and mature to scaly, overlapping leaves.
Low growing evergreen conifer with silvery blue needle-like foliage, and stiffly horizontal branches.
An evergreen conifer tree with a slow, low growth habit. Horizontally spreading branches display upright cones and blue-green needles arranged in fascicles.

An evergreen conifer that forms a shrubby ground cover. Sage-green foliage is needle-like when young and scale-like when mature. Typically, plants bear either catkin-like male cones, or berry-like female cones. Attracts birds.

An evergreen conifer that forms a compact, fountain-like shrub. Rich green foliage is needle-like when young and scale-like when mature. Typically, plants bear either catkin-like male cones, or berry-like female cones. Attracts birds.
Technically a conifer, this evergreen tree is noted for its dense and upright form. Feathery foliage is narrow and dark green. Takes well to shearing and makes a great screen or hedge.

An evergreen conifer that forms a very narrow, columnar tree. Blue-green foliage is held in sprays of overlapping, scale-like leaves. Typically, plants bear either catkin-like male cones, or berry-like female cones. Attracts birds.

A slow growing conifer that form an exceptionally dense mound of finely textured, rich emerald green foliage. Seldom needs pruning or maintenance, this is impactful as a specimen or as a mass planting.

An evergreen tree with a columnar trunk and a conical crown. Horizontal branches carry upturned branchlets of fine needles in forest green with blue-gray undersides. Fibrous bark is reddish-brown. Small brown cones form in winter. Native to the coast of California and southwest Oregon. Provides habitat for native wildlife.

An evergreen conifer that forms a symmetrical, columnar tree. Dark green foliage is scale-like and dense. Typically, plants bear either catkin-like male cones, or berry-like female cones. Attracts birds.
A columnar conifer with upright branches that are densely clothed in tiny, scale-like foliage. The leaves emerge bright golden green and retain good color throughout the seasons. Evergreen.

An evergreen conifer that forms a dense, spreading ground cover. Bluish-green foliage is held in feathery sprays of overlapping, needle-like leaves. Typically, plants bear either catkin-like male cones, or berry-like female cones. Attracts birds.
Dwarf evergreen tree with stiff, dark green needles. Good selection for bonsai.

A narrow, columnar conifer with upright branches that are finely textured with tiny, deep green, scale-like foliage. Foliage is more dense and even smaller than the species. Evergreen. Very slow growth; 8 feet high after 10 years.
A coniferous tree with an irregular, broad habit. Light gray-green long needles line branches, dark brown ovoid cones in winter. Native to Southern California.

commonName: Waterer's Scotch Pine, Blue Scots Pine
description: An evergreen, pyramidal conifer that becomes open and rounded with age. Blue-green needles grow in pairs, while orange-red upper bark adds year-round color. Small gray-brown cones feed wildlife. Native across Europe and northern Asia, it thrives in cool climates and well-drained soil. Use as a windbreak, screen, or bold specimen.
An evergreen conifer with a slow, weeping growth habit. Silvery-blue-green needles are arranged in fascicles.

An evergreen conifer that forms a broadly conical, upright tree. Silver-blue foliage is held in flattened sprays of overlapping, scale-like foliage. Typically, plants bear either catkin-like male cones, or berry-like female cones. Male selection. Attracts birds.
A dwarf conifer with a bushy, conical form. Scale-like foliage is golden-green, fragrant and tiny. Best grown along the coast where summers are cool. Native to Monterey, California.
An evergreen shrub with a very narrow, conical growth habit. Scale-like foliage is arranged in flattened sprays of bright gold. Holds color through winter.
Technically a conifer, this evergreen tree is noted for its narrow and pyramidal form. Feathery foliage is narrow and bright green. Takes well to shearing and makes a great screen or hedge.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Large, elongated flower clusters in white. Foliage turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Mophead flower clusters in pink if grown in alkaline soil, or blue if grown in acidic soil.
