botanicalName: Cytisus x praecox 'Allgold', C. multiflorus x C. purgans
description: A deciduous shrub with upright, slender green stems. Small leaves are inconspicuous amongst the abundant sprays of fragrant, bright yellow, sweet pea-like flowers. Spreads vigorously and tends to take over plant communities.

A deciduous shrub with a mounding growth habit. Leaves are lobed, bright green, and toothed on the edges. Inconspicuous, yellow-green flowers and red summer berries appear on female plants only. Native to Europe.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit. Green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In mid-spring, large conical flower clusters bloom at branch tips in pure white. Single flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Low chill Descanso hybrid. Good for mild winter climates.
A deciduous shrub with very large and rounded white flower clusters up to 12 inches across. Lush, gray-green foliage.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Foliage emerges burgundy and matures to bright green. Good fall color. Leaves are lance-shaped with toothed margins. Rosy-pink flowers bloom in flat-topped clusters in spring and summer. Attracts butterflies.

commonName: Arctic Fire Redtwid Dogwood, Red Osier Dogwood
description: A dwarf deciduous shrub with bare, bright red branches in winter. Green, oval leaves turn bright red in fall. Creamy white flower clusters in spring are followed by small berry-like fruits. Spreads by rhizomes. Can tolerate full shade.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Mophead flower clusters in mauve pink.

commonName: Bailey's Redtwig Dogwood, Red Osier Dogwood
description: A deciduous shrub with bare, bright red branches in winter. Green, oval leaves turn bright red in fall. Creamy white flower clusters in spring are followed by small berry-like fruits. Does not spread by rhizomes. Can tolerate full shade.
A spiny deciduous shrub with variegated leaves that are small, oval, and red with gold edges. Fall foliage turns red-orange. Bright red berries attract birds.

A deciduous shrub with a woody base that forms a compact mound. Leaves are slender, aromatic, glossy and dark green. Tiny, dark blue flowers grow in clusters on upright stems. Blooms from midsummer into fall. In the mint family. Attracts pollinators.

commonName: Black Knight Butterfly Bush, Summer Lilac
description: A deciduous, arching shrub with gray-green leaves and long, deep purple flower panicles from summer into fall. The fragrant blooms attract butterflies, bees, and hummingbirds, making it useful in habitat and cutting gardens. It benefits from well-drained soil and annual pruning to renew flowering wood.

commonName: Black Lace Black Elder, European Elder
description: A deciduous shrub with a suckering, multi-branching growth habit. Dark purple compound leaves are finely dissected. From late spring into summer, lacy pink lemon-scented flower clusters bloom, followed by heavy clusters of small glossy reddish black fruit in fall. The edible fruit is eaten dried, in herbal medicines, syrup, wine, pie, and jam. Eat raw fruit only when ripe. Not as tasty as S. canadensis. Flowers are also edible. Attracts birds, wildlife, and pollinators.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Rounded mophead flower clusters in pink if grown in alkaline soil, or blue if grown in acidic soil. Purple-black stems.
A loosely branched, deciduous shrub featuring profuse clusters of citrus-scented, pure white flowers. Broadly oval, light green leaves.

A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Mophead flower clusters in pink if grown in alkaline soil, or blue if grown in acidic soil. Repeat bloomer if spent flowers are removed.
Deciduous shrub with oval and pointed, finely serrated foliage and dainty lacecap flower clusters in sky blue. Foliage shifts to shades of beautifyl burgundy red in fall.

commonName: Blue Chip Dwarf Butterfly Bush, Summer Lilac
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in violet-blue and orange. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and elliptical. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies. A dwarf, sterile cultivar that does not reseed.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Mophead flower clusters in violet-blue.

botanicalName: Sambucus nigra ssp. caerulea, S. mexicana, S. cerulea
description: A deciduous shrub with a suckering, multi-branching growth habit. Green compound leaves are divided into toothed, oval-elliptic leaflets. From late spring into summer, lacy yellowish umbrella-shaped flower clusters bloom, followed by heavy clusters of small berries in fall. Fruit turns powdery blackish-blue when ripe. The edible nutrient-dense fruit is popularly eaten dried, in herbal medicines, syrup, wine, pie, and jam. Eat raw berries only when they're fully ripe. Flowers are also edible. Attracts birds, wildlife, and pollinators. Native to North America, including California.

A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Dark reddish black stems hoist large mophead flower clusters above foliage. Flower color ranges from pink if grown in alkaline soil, to blue if grown in acidic soil. Blooms age to creamy light green. Repeat bloomer if spent flowers are removed.

A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Mophead flower clusters in vibrant pink if grown in alkaline soil, or deep blue if grown in acidic soil. Repeat blooms throughout summer.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit. Green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In mid-spring, large conical flower clusters bloom at branch tips in lavender sky blue. Single flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Low chill Descanso hybrid. Good for mild winter climates.
A deciduous shrub with showy, hollyhock-like, double blush pink flowers. Coarsely-toothed, three-lobed, medium green leaves.
A compact deciduous shrub with rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Cone-shaped, panicle flower clusters in creamy yellowish-white to pale pink. One of the most winter-hardy hydrangeas.

commonName: Bridal Wreath Spirea, Shoe Button Spirea
description: A deciduous shrub with a spreading, rounded growth habit. Arching branches appear snow-covered when abundant white flower clusters bloom in spring. Flowers look like tiny double roses. Dark green leaves are rounded. Good red-orange fall color. Attracts butterflies.
Deciduous shrub with rich green, coarsely toothed foliage and large rounded mophead flowers in deep pink. Each petal is edged in white.

commonName: Buuzuz Series Butterfly Bush, Summer Lilac
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant flower clusters bloom in a variety of vivid colors. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and lance-shaped. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies. A dwarf cultivar. 'Buzz Violet' has violet blue flowers. 'Buzz Lavender' has lavender-purple and orange flowers. 'Buzz Ivory' has crisp ivory white flowers. 'Buzz Midnight' has dark purple and orange flowers. 'Buzz Purple' has purple flowers. 'Buzz Sky Blue' has pale blue and magenta flowers. 'Buzz Soft Pink' has true pink and orange flowers. 'Buzz Velvet' has rich pink flowers. 'Buzz Burgundy' has deep reddish-burgundy flowers.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit. Green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In mid-spring, large conical flower clusters bloom at branch tips in wine red. Double flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.

A deciduous shrub or small tree with a rounded to vase-shaped growth habit. Aromatic, gray-green leaves are palmately divided into finger-like lobes with fuzzy undersides. From summer to fall, fragrant, upright flower spikes bloom in purple, followed by small, dark berries. Attracts hummingbirds, butterflies, and honey bees. Can be deadheaded to proliferate blooms. Known for medicinal qualities.
A spiny deciduous shrub with small, rounded leaves that flush deep red-bronze when exposed to enough sunlight. Fall foliage turns red-orange. Bright red berries attract birds.

A deciduous shrub with a wiry-stemmed, airy growth habit. Late summer flowers are five-petaled and bright blue. Foliage is fresh green, narrowly diamond-shaped, and turns yellow-red in fall. Can be used as a groundcover.
Deciduous shrub with rich green coarsely toothed foliage and rounded mophead flower clusters in intense pink-red on sturdy stems. Excellent mildew resistance.

A vigorous deciduous shrub with an upright, vase-shaped growth habit. Aromatic leaves are lobed, fuzzy, green, and serrated on the edges. Good fall color. Extra showy, drooping clusters of spring flowers are bright, light pink. Berries are blackish blue with a waxy-powder coating. Attracts birds, especially hummingbirds. Native to California.

A deciduous shrub with upright, arching, suckering branches. Grow in thickets for erosion control. Leaves are egg-shaped and bluish-green. Bell-shaped pink flowers bloom in spring and summer. Clusters of pearly white berries form in fall and hang on into winter. Provides food and habitat for birds. Fruit is not palatable for humans. Native to North America, including California.
A spiny deciduous shrub with small, rounded, plum-purple leaves. Fall foliage turns red-orange. Bright red berries attract birds. Must have sun to develop intense foliage color.

commonName: Corkscrew Hauzelnut, Harry Lauder's Walking Stick
description: A deciduous shrub or small tree with spectacularly contorted branches and twigs. Oval, bright green leaves have saw-toothed edges and turn yellow in fall. Pendulous, yellow catkins appear in winter. This hybrid typically does not bear fruit.
A loosely branched, deciduous shrub featuring citrus-scented, pure white flowers. Broadly oval, light green leaves.

A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in berry pink. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and lance-shaped. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies.

A deciduous, compact rounded shrub with dense branching and small burgundy-red leaves. Yellow spring flowers are followed by small red berries, and foliage can deepen in fall. Useful for low barriers, color contrast, and formal edging; it develops best color with good light and well-drained soil.

A deciduous shrub with upright, arching branches and exfoliating, red bark. Aromatic leaves are fuzzy, lobed, gray green, and serrated on the edges. Foliage turns red in fall. Long, drooping clusters of winter flowers are white and deep pink. Flowers are larger than the species. Berries are blackish blue with a powdery-waxy outer coating. Attracts birds, especially hummingbirds. Native to California.
A low, mounding, deciduous shrub with a woody base and slender, aromatic, gray-green leaves. Tiny, smokey blue flowers grow in clusters on upright stems. In the mint family. Attracts pollinators.
A deciduous shrub with lobed foliage in deep reddish purple. Rounded clusters of creamy to pale pink flowers.
A deciduous shrub with showy, hollyhock-like flowers in pure white. Coarsely-toothed, three-lobed, medium green leaves.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Foliage emerges bright red and matures to vivid green. Good fall color. Leaves are lance-shaped with toothed margins. Deep rosy-pink flowers bloom in flat-topped clusters in spring and summer. Attracts butterflies.

A deciduous shrub with an open, suckering habit. Bright green leaves are egg-shaped and pointed with deep veins and coarse teeth. Foliage turns yellow in fall. In spring, double, pompom-like flowers bloom in golden-yellow. Stems are bare and bright yellow-green in winter.

commonName: Dwarf Blue Chip Butterfly Bush, Summer Lilac
botanicalName: Buddleja Lo & Behold 'Blue Chip Jr.' PP 26,581
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in violet-blue and orange. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and elliptical. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies. A dwarf, sterile cultivar that does not reseed. Even more compact than 'Blue Chip.'
A small spiny deciduous shrub with small, rounded, chartreuse leaves. Fall foliage turns red-orange. Bright red berries attract birds.
Dwarf deciduous shrub with glossy, bright green foliage and single red-orange flowers with ruffled petals. Flowers are followed by dry red fruits.
A deciduous shrub boasting showy and fragrant, double white flowers. Dark green, oval leaves.

A deciduous shrub or small tree with a dense, rounded, multi-stemmed habit. Leaves are oval with finely serrated edges and spectacular fall color. Autumn foliage turns strikingly brilliant red when grown in full sun, or more pink when grown in shady conditions.

A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Mophead flower clusters in pink if grown in alkaline soil, or blue if grown in acidic soil. Repeat bloomer if spent flowers are removed.

commonName: Endless Summer Blushing Bride Bigleaf Hydrangea
description: A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Large and rounded mophead flower clusters in white blushed with pink. Repeat bloomer if spent flowers are removed.

A deciduous shrub with a full, rounded form. Adaptable to pruning. Shiny red branchlets are ornamental in winter. Catkins form in spring. Slender, variegated leaves are dappled in pale green and cream. New growth is lovely pink. Prefers wetland and riparian habitats.

commonName: Flutterby Petite Butterflu Bush, Summer Lilac
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in rich pink and orange. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and elliptical. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies. A dwarf cultivar.

A drought-deciduous shrub with arching, sharply thorned branches. Leaves are lobed, glossy, and deep green. In early spring, drooping, fuchsia-like flowers bloom in red. Summer berries are orange and thorny. Provides habitat for many birds, especially hummingbirds. Native to California.
A deciduous shrub featuring abundant highly fragrant, creamy white, four-petaled flowers. Serrated oval, bright green leaves.
A spiny deciduous shrub with velvety, small, rounded, burgundy leaves. An improved selection of B. 'Crimson Pygmy.' Sparse berries. Fall foliage turns dark blackish red.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Large and rounded mophead flower clusters in deep reddish-pink.

A deciduous shrub with a dense, rounded growth habit. Foliage emerges bronze and matures to yellow-green. Good copper-orange fall color. Leaves are lance-shaped with toothed margins. Red-pink flowers bloom in flat-topped clusters in summer. Attracts butterflies.

A deciduous shrub with a suckering, multi-branching growth habit. Green compound leaves are divided into oval-elliptic leaflets. In summer, lacy white umbrella-shaped flower clusters bloom, followed by heavy clusters of small edible fruits that turn blackish purple when ripe. The nutrient-dense fruit is popularly eaten dried, in herbal medicines, syrup, wine, pie, and jam. Eat raw berries only when they're fully ripe. Flowers are also edible. Attracts birds, wildlife, and pollinators. Native to North America.

A deciduous shrub with sprawling branches. Leaves are glossy green and lobed. Foliage turns red in fall. Small spring flowers are yellow to red, and are followed by tasty, edible berries in summer. Attracts birds. Native to California. Ribes aureum yields some of the best berries for human consumption.

A deciduous shrub with sprawling branches. Leaves are glossy green and lobed. Foliage turns red in fall. Small spring flowers are yellow to red, and are followed by tasty, edible berries in summer. Attracts birds. Native to California. Ribes aureum yields some of the best berries for human consumption.
A dwarf spiny deciduous shrub with small, rounded, chartreuse leaves. Bright red berries in fall and winter attract birds.
A spiny deciduous shrub with coral-pink stems and small, rounded, bright chartreuese leaves. Bright red berries in fall and winter attract birds.

A round deciduous shrub known for pinkish sprays of spent flowers which create a smoke-like appearance in summer. Circular to egg-shaped leaves emerge copper-tinged lime green, mature to yellow, then turn pink and orange in fall.
Deciduous shrub with deep green, fine textured foliage and an abundance of golden yellow, buttercup-like flowers.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Golden-green leaves are lance-shaped with toothed margins. Good fall color. Pink flowers bloom in flat-topped clusters in spring and summer. Attracts butterflies.
A loosely branched, deciduous shrub featuring citrus-scented, creamy white double flowers. Broadly oval, deep green leaves.

A deciduous shrub known for pinkish sprays of spent flowers which create a smoke-like appearance in summer. Circular to egg-shaped leaves emerge bronzy purple, mature to blue-green, then put on a spectacular show of fall colors.

A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in rich magenta and white. Variegated leaves are gray-green and yellow, felt-textured and lance-shaped. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies. A compact cultivar.

commonName: Hedgerows Gold Redtwig Dogwood, Red Osier Dogwood
description: A graceful deciduous shrub with bare, bright red branches in winter. Variegated leaves are bright green and gold. Creamy white flower clusters in spring produce berry-like fruits. Spreads by rhizomes. Can tolerate full shade.
Tropical looking deciduous shrub with showy, funnel shaped single flowers and prominent stamens. Blooms are ruffled and white, with dark pink centers.
A spiny, columnar deciduous shrub with small, rounded, purple-green leaves. Bright red berries in fall and winter attract birds.
A deciduous shrub with fragrant and white flower clusters held in drooping, cylindrical racemes. Narrow, dark green leaves that turn bright red in the fall.
A deciduous shrub with showy, hollyhock-like flowers in lavender with deep rose centers. Coarsely-toothed, three-lobed, medium green leaves.

A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a spreading, fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in golden-yellow and orange. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and lance-shaped. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies.

A semi-evergreen shrub with neatly arranged rich green foliage. Golden cup-shaped flowers with prominent, showy stamens. Red fruits in the fall. Rust resistant foliage. Tolerates dry shade once established.
A deciduous shrub with very large and rounded white flower clusters up to 12 inches across. Lush, gray-green foliage.
A compact deciduous shrub with very large and rounded ruby red flower clusters that sit atop a clean mound of lush, gray-green foliage.

commonName: Kelsey's Dwarf Redtwig Dogwood, Red Osier Dogwood
description: A dwarf deciduous shrub with bare, bright red branches in the winter. Leaves are oval and bright green. Creamy white flower clusters in spring produce berry-like fruits. Spreads by rhizomes. Can tolerate full shade.

commonName: King Edward VII Red Flowering Currant
description: A deciduous shrub with upright, arching branches. Aromatic leaves are lobed, fuzzy, green, and serrated on the edges. Foliage turns yellow in fall. Extra showy, drooping clusters of spring flowers are vibrant crimson-pink. Summer berries are blackish blue. Attracts birds, especially hummingbirds. Native to California.

A deciduous shrub with a slow-growing, upright to spreading form. In spring, glossy pink buds bloom into rounded clusters of white flowers. The flowers are tubular, flare into a star-shape, and emit a spicy-sweet fragrance. Inconspicuous blackish-blue fruits attract birds. Dull green foliage turns reddish in fall. Leaves are elliptical, rounded at the base, and toothed on the edges.
Tropical-looking deciduous shrub with showy, funnel-shaped single flowers with central tufts of petals.

A deciduous shrub with a rounded growth habit. Mid-green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In spring, great big conical flower clusters bloom at branch tips in signature lilac-purple. Single flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Low-chill Descanso hybrid. Good for mild winter climates.

Long white flower spikes top this compact, deciduous, mounding shrub from summer into fall. Gray-green leaves form a tidy base, while fragrant blooms feed butterflies, bees, and hummingbirds. Its small size fits low hedges, containers, and pollinator borders. Full sun, good drainage, and spring pruning keep the plant dense and flowering near eye level.
A compact deciduous shrub with bright chartreuse, lobed foliage held on contrasting red stems. Rounded clusters of white flowers.

A deciduous to semi-evergreen, upright aromatic shrub grown for intensely lemon-scented foliage. Small white to pale lavender summer flowers add light pollinator value, while the leaves are useful for culinary and fragrance plantings. It responds well to pruning and appreciates well-drained soil.

A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Mophead flower clusters in pink if grown in alkaline soil, or blue if grown in acidic soil. Repeat bloomer if spent flowers are removed, blooms on old and new wood.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Foliage emerges yellow-green and matures to lime green. Good orange-red fall color. Leaves are lance-shaped with toothed margins. Pink flowers bloom in flat-topped clusters in spring and summer. Attracts butterflies.
A deciduous shrub with rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Cone-shaped, panicle flower clusters in white aging to chartreuse and eventually pink-beige.

A compact deciduous shrub with rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Cone-shaped, panicle flower clusters in white aging to chartreuse and eventually pink-beige. Longer blooming than 'Limelight'.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Cone-shaped flower clusters in white. Foliage emerges golden green and turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.
A deciduous shrub with rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Cone-shaped, panicle flower clusters in white aging to chartreuse and eventually pink to burgundy.

A deciduous shrub with a round, compact growth habit. Mid-green leaves are lance-shaped with toothed margins. Good fall color. Dainty blush-pink flowers bloom in flat-topped clusters in spring and summer. Attracts butterflies.
A deciduous shrub with rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Cone-shaped, panicle flower clusters in white aging to shades of pink and red as time progresses.

A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in light lavender-blue. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and elliptical. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, speading growth habit. Foliage emerges bright red and matures to golden green. Good fall color. Leaves are lance-shaped with toothed margins. Bright pink flowers bloom in flat-topped clusters in spring and summer. Attracts butterflies.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Rounded mophead flower clusters in dark pink if grown in alkaline soil, or violet-blue if grown in acidic soil.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Rounded mophead flower clusters in dark pink if grown in alkaline soil, or violet-blue if grown in acidic soil.
A deciduous shrub with white, flower-like bracts and rich green foliage that turns golden in fall. Bare, fiery orange branches stand out in the winter landscape.
A deciduous shrub with showy, hollyhock-like flowers in lavender-pink with red eyes. Coarsely-toothed, three-lobed, medium green leaves.

A deciduous shrub with a rounded, mounding growth habit. Arching branches light up in spring with prolific, rosy-pink, funnel-shaped flowers. Egg-shaped leaves are purplish-bronzy-green. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Dark green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In mid-spring, large conical flower clusters bloom in cool blue from purple buds. Single flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Low chill Descanso hybrid. Good for mild winter climates.

A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in deep fuchsia-pink and yellow. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and elliptical. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies.

commonName: Montrose Purple Chaste Tree, Monk's Pepper
description: A deciduous shrub or small tree with a rounded to vase-shaped growth habit. Aromatic, gray-green leaves are palmately divided into finger-like lobes with fuzzy undersides. From summer to fall, fragrant, upright flower spikes bloom in deep violet-blue, followed by small, dark berries. Attracts hummingbirds, butterflies, and honey bees. Can be deadheaded to proliferate blooms. Known for medicinal qualities.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Cone-shaped flower clusters in white and aging to pink. Foliage turns mahogany red in the fall.

A deciduous, compact arching shrub with narrow gray-green leaves and lavender-blue flower panicles in summer. Its smaller scale fits mixed borders and pollinator plantings where larger forms are too vigorous. Fragrant blooms attract butterflies and bees, especially with good drainage and seasonal pruning.

commonName: Nanho Purple Butterfly Bush, Summer Lilac
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in vivid lavender-purple and orange. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and lance-shaped. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies. A compact cultivar.
A deciduous shrub boasting prolific, showy and fragrant, double white flowers. Dark green, oval leaves.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Large and rounded mophead flower clusters in pink if grown in alkaline soil, or blue if grown in acidic soil, ocassionally purple.
A compact deciduous shrub. Arching stems are clothed in bright green, toothed leaves. Foliage turns burgundy in fall. Showy clusters of small white buds open to reveal fragrant double flowers.

A round deciduous shrub known for pinkish-tan sprays of spent flowers that create a smoke-like appearance in summer. Circular to egg-shaped leaves emerge with a pink tinge, mature to deep green, then turn pinkish red in fall. Petioles and veins are reddish-pink.

A deciduous, narrow upright shrub with bright coral-orange new growth maturing to red and burgundy tones. Small yellow spring flowers and red berries add seasonal interest on spiny stems. The tight vertical habit is useful for accents, low hedges, and containers with well-drained soil.

Peeling brown bark and arching branches shape this deciduous, rounded California native shrub. White spring flower clusters feed insects, then red-brown seed pods add summer detail and leaves turn yellow in fall. Use it for streambank repair, moist screens, and woodland edges. Sun or shade, organic soil, and regular moisture support a full canopy.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Cone-shaped flower clusters in white fading to pink. Foliage turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Rounded mophead clusters of double pale pink to white flowers. Blooms on new wood.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, arching growth habit. Green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In late spring, abundant conical flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Pale bluish-purple single flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.

A deciduous tree with an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, deep pinky-red flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to yellow in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Dwarf hybrid.

A deciduous tree with an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, bright purple-pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to yellow in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Dwarf hybrid.

A deciduous tree with an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, bright pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to yellow in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Dwarf hybrid.

A deciduous tree with an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, plum-pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to yellow in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Dwarf hybrid.

commonName: Petite Red Imp Dwarf Crape Myrtle
description: A deciduous tree with an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, crimson-red flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to yellow in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Dwarf hybrid.
A deciduous shrub with rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Cone-shaped, panicle flower clusters in yellow-white to pale pink.

A deciduous, rounded shrub with a dense habit and large mophead flower clusters. Broad, coarsely toothed green leaves create a full, lush backdrop for pink summer blooms, with flower color performing best in neutral to alkaline soils. Best suited to rich, well-drained soil with consistent moisture and protection from hot afternoon sun in warm inland sites. Useful for foundation plantings, shaded borders, containers, and cut flower gardens.

commonName: Pink Delight Butterfly Bush, Summer Lilac
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in rich, bright pink. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and elliptical. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies. A compact cultivar.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Mophead flower clusters in rich pink.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, vase-shaped growth habit. Aromatic leaves are lobed, fuzzy, deep green, and serrated on the edges. Good fall color. Showy, drooping clusters of early spring flowers bloom in shades of pink. Berries are blackish blue with a waxy-powder coating. Attracts birds, especially hummingbirds. Native to California. Can tolerate full shade.
A deciduous shrub with heavily textured, rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Cone-shaped, panicle flower clusters in pink and fading to white at the tips.
A deciduous shrub with interesting, rounded mophead flower clusters in pink, violet, and green. Rich green, coarsely toothed foliage.

Tropical deciduous native from Mexico and Panama. Rosy pink to red, large and highly fragrant flowers bloom throughout spring on terminal branches, often before foliage emerges. Leaves are elliptic and dark green, with undulate margins.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit. Bluish-green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In mid-spring, large conical flower clusters bloom in deep violet from burgundy buds. Single flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Typically blooms before S. vulgaris. Cold hardy.

A deciduous shrub with a tiered, upright branching habit. From mid-spring to summer, buds bloom into small, rounded clusters of white flowers. Showy dark red fruits attract birds. Dark green foliage turns burgundy in fall. Leaves are broadly elliptical, deeply veined, and toothed on the edges.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit. Bluish-green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In late spring, large conical flower clusters bloom in light lilac-blue from reddish buds. Double flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.

A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a dwarf, fountain-shaped form. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in deep blue. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and elliptical. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies.
Tropical looking deciduous shrub with an upright columnar form, that produces showy funnel-shaped single purple flowers with prominent stamens.

A dwarf spiny deciduous shrub with small, rounded, glossy leaves that flush with deep red when exposed to enough sunlight. Fall foliage turns brilliant red. Bright red berries in fall and winter attract birds.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Elongated, cone-shaped clusters of white flowers that mature to a deep rosy pink. Foliage turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.
A showy deciduous shrub with very large and rounded reddish violet mophead flowers that sit atop a clean mound of lush, medium green foliage.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, vase-shaped growth habit. Aromatic leaves are lobed, fuzzy, deep green, and serrated on the edges. Good fall color. Showy, drooping clusters of early spring flowers are pinky-red. Summer Berries are blackish blue with a waxy-powder coating. Attracts birds, especially hummingbirds. Native to the Pacific Northwest, including northern California.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, mounding growth habit. Branches light up in spring with prolific, rich red, funnel-shaped flowers. Egg-shaped leaves are dark green with serrated edges. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.
A spiny deciduous shrub with small, rounded leaves that flush deep bronze-red when exposed to enough sunlight. Fall foliage turns red-orange. Bright red berries attract birds.

A deciduous shrub with a spreading, rounded growth habit. Long, arching branches appear snow-covered when abundant double white flower clusters bloom in spring. Blue-green leaves are lance-shaped. Good red fall color. Attracts butterflies.

A low, dense deciduous shrub with small green leaves arranged in a herringbone pattern. Foliage turns shades of orange and red in fall. Small white flowers develop into bright red cranberry-like fruits. Attracts birds and bees.
Deciduous shrub with rich green coarsely toothed foliage and rounded mophead flower clusters in rosy red or blue, depending on soil conditions.

A deciduous, rounded shrub with arching, spiny stems and mottled rose, burgundy, and cream foliage. Small yellow spring flowers are followed by red berries, adding wildlife value and winter color. Effective as a colorful barrier, hedge, or accent where soil drains well.
Deciduous shrub with rich green, coarsely toothed foliage. Rounded mophead flower clusters in rich, dark purple throughout summer and into fall.

A deciduous shrub known for pink-purple sprays of spent flowers which create a smoke-like appearance in summer. Circular to egg-shaped leaves emerge wine red, mature to dark purple, then turn bright red and orange in fall.

commonName: Royal Red Butterfly Bush, Summer Lilac
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped growth habit. Sweetly fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in rich violet-red. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and elliptical. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Cone-shaped flower clusters that emerge white and age to deep pink. Foliage turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.

commonName: Seaside Serenade Bar Harbor Smooth Hydrangea
description: A deciduous shrub with very large and rounded pale yellow to white flower clusters up to 12 inches across. Lush, gray-green foliage.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit. Green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. In mid-spring, large conical flower clusters bloom at branch tips in reddish-purple with white-edged petals. Single flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Cone-shaped flower clusters in greenish-white aging to pink. Foliage turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.
A deciduous shrub with lush green, coarsely toothed foliage. Rounded mophead flower clusters in white.

commonName: Snow Mound Nippon Spirea, Bridal Wreath Spirea
description: A deciduous shrub with a spreading, rounded growth habit. Arching branches appear snow-covered when abundant white flower clusters bloom in spring. Dark green leaves are rounded. Attracts butterflies.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Elongated, cone-shaped flower clusters in snow white aging to pink. Foliage turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Cone-shaped flower clusters in creamy white age to shades of soft pink and green. Foliage turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.
A deciduous shrub with deeply lobed, oak-like leaves. Elongated, cone-shaped clusters of double white flowers. Foliage turns bright orange to scarlet in the fall.

A waterside deciduous shrub with a wine-like fragrance. Leaves are glossy, broad, oval, and bright green. Water lily-like, deep red flowers emerge at the tips of branchlets and are followed by pear-shaped seed capsules. Native to California, it is pollinated by native beetles.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, vase-shaped growth habit. Aromatic leaves are lobed, fuzzy, deep green, and serrated on the edges. Good fall color. Long, drooping clusters of early spring flowers are bright, light pink. Summer berries are blackish blue with a waxy-powder coating. Attracts birds, especially hummingbirds. Native to California.

commonName: Squawbush, Skunkbush, Three Leaf Sumac, Basket Bush
description: A deciduous shrub with a spreading habit and arching branches. Mid-green foliage divides into leaflets of three, with resemblance to poison oak. Foliage turns attractive yellow-red in fall. Yellow summer flowers are followed by showy red fruits in fall. Attracts birds. Unlike some of its relatives, R. trilobata is not toxic. Native to western North America, including California.

Raspberry-pink or deep purple flower heads cover this compact, deciduous, rounded shrub on both old and new stems. Broad green leaves make a dense mound around the repeat blooms. Use it in low hedges, shaded foundations, or large pots. Morning sun, rich soil, and regular moisture support color; every part is toxic if eaten.

A deciduous shrub with an upright, tiered branching habit. From spring to fall, buds bloom into flat-topped clusters of off-white, lacecap flowers. Showy bright red fruits attract birds. Medium green foliage turns red in fall. Leaves are broadly elliptical, deeply veined, and toothed on the edges.

commonName: Summer Wine Common Ninebark, Seward Common Ninebark
description: A deciduous shrub with lobed foliage in deep reddish burgundy. Rounded clusters of pale pink flowers. Similar to 'Diabolo' but smaller.
A compact spiny deciduous shrub with a columnar growth habit and small, rounded, bright chartreuse leaves. Bright red berries in fall and winter attract birds. Fall foliage turns red-orange.
A deciduous shrub with a profuse display of fragrant, sweet pea-like yellow flowers. Bright green branches and small rounded green leaves.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Lacecap flower clusters in pink if grown in alkaline soil, or blue if grown in acidic soil.

A deciduous shrub known for its very early spring blooms before leaf-out. Fiery red flowers bear edible, quince-like fruit that are best tasting when processed in preserves or jellies. Branches are often contorted and spiny. Glossy, finely toothed leaves are characteristic of the rose family.

A deciduous shrub with upright, arching, suckering branches and an especially bushy growth habit. Grow in thickets for erosion control. Leaves are egg-shaped and bluish-green. Bell-shaped pink flowers bloom in spring and summer. Clusters of large pearly white berries form in fall and hang on into winter. Provides food and habitat for birds. Fruit is not palatable for humans. Native to North America, including California.

A dwarf deciduous shrub with an upright, rounded growth habit. Dark green leaves are narrowly heart-shaped. Throughout spring, large conical flower clusters bloom at branch tips in soft pink. Single flowers are cross-shaped with curling petals and a strong fragrance. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Low chill Descanso hybrid. Good for mild winter climates.

A deciduous shrub known for its very early spring blooms before leaf-out. Red, pink, and white flowers bear edible, quince-like fruit that are best tasting when processed in preserves or jellies. Branches are often contorted and spiny. Glossy, finely toothed leaves are characteristic of the rose family.
A deciduous shrub with rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Very large, elongated cone-shaped flower clusters in creamy white aging to blush pink.
A deciduous shrub with rich green leaves that are oval and pointed. Panicle, cone-shaped flower clusters in white maturing to deep strawberry pink.

A deciduous shrub with a dwarf, rounded growth habit. Arching branches light up in spring with prolific, pale to medium pink, funnel-shaped flowers. Egg-shaped leaves are dark green with variegated yellow-cream margins. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage variegated in green and white. Lacecap flower clusters in pale pink to blue, depending on soil conditions.
A rounded deciduous shrub with bare, bright red branches in winter. Leaves are variegated green and white. Fragrant white flower clusters bloom in spring.
A rounded deciduous shrub with bare, bright red branches in winter. Leaves are variegated green and white. Fragrant white flower clusters bloom in spring.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, mounding growth habit. Arching branches light up in spring with prolific, pale to medium pink, funnel-shaped flowers. Egg-shaped leaves are dark green with variegated yellow-cream margins. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.
A deciduous shrub with large and lush, coarsely toothed foliage. Rounded mophead flower clusters in white.

commonName: White Bouquet Butterfly Bush, Summer Lilac
description: A fast-growing deciduous shrub with a fountain-shaped form. Sweetly-fragrant, extravagant flower clusters bloom in crisp white and orange. Leaves are gray-green, felt-textured and lance-shaped. Loved by hummingbirds and butterflies.
Tropical-looking deciduous shrub with showy funnel-shaped single flowers with central tufts of petals.

A deciduous shrub with a compact, vase-shaped growth habit. Aromatic leaves are lobed, fuzzy, deep green, and serrated on the edges. Good fall color. Extra showy, drooping clusters of spring flowers are bright white. Summer Berries are blackish blue with a waxy-powder coating. Attracts birds, especially hummingbirds. Native to California.

A deciduous shrub with a rounded, mounding growth habit. Arching branches light up in spring with prolific, rosy-pink, funnel-shaped flowers. Egg-shaped leaves are dark purple-green and turn blackish burgundy in fall. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

A compact deciduous shrub with bare, bright yellow branches in winter. Green, oval leaves turn bright red in fall. Creamy white flower clusters in spring are followed by small berry-like fruits. Spreads by rhizomes. Can tolerate full shade.

A deciduous tree with a remarkably symmetrical and pyramidal form. Foliage is lanceolate, and glossy green. Fall color is fiery reddish orange. Bark is smooth when the tree is young, and becomes scaly with age.
An ornamental deciduous tree with a graceful, spreading and arching crown. Fragrant, double pale-pink to white flowers. Deep glossy green leaves turn yellow in the fall.

A small deciduous tree with a round crown. Leaves are broad and mid-green. Foliage turns yellow in fall. In late winter and early spring, lightly fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, tulip-shaped, and purple-pink with a white interior. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A high arching canopy develops on this deciduous to semi-evergreen, vase-shaped tree above mottled exfoliating bark. Leaves turn yellow in fall, and the selection shows good resistance to Dutch elm disease and elm leaf beetle. Use it on broad streets and campuses. Sun, deep soil, and structural pruning support a strong frame and clear trunk.

A low-branching, broadly-rounded deciduous tree with palmate leaves that are divided into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Green leaves turn golden yellow in the fall. Bark is rough and fissured. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, crimson-pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage emerges red, matures to green, then turns reddish purple in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Gray bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant hybrid.

Native to South America, this deciduous tree is fast growing with an erect, single trunk and spreading canopy of blue-green foliage. Bipinnate leaves are 4 - 5 inches long and divided into many leaflets. Spikes of yellow flowers appear in summer, followed by seed pods, seeds are edible and sometimes used for livestock fodder.

A deciduous, narrow columnar tree with a tight upright crown, useful where planting space is limited. Medium green leaves turn gold to orange in fall, and spring flowers are followed by winged seeds. It comes from red maple stock native to eastern North America. Best growth comes in moist, acidic, well-drained soil.

A deciduous shade tree selected for reliable red to orange fall color and a clean, upright landscape habit. Green summer foliage casts useful shade, while inconspicuous flowers and winged samaras mark the season. It performs best with regular irrigation, slightly acidic soil, and ample rooting space.

An open and airy deciduous shrub or small tree with shaggy bark and twisted branches. Leaves are narrow, light green, and willow-like. Beautiful pink trumpet-shaped flowers are sterile in this cultivar and do not produce seedpods. Native to the southwestern United States.

A deciduous shade tree selected for reliable red to orange fall color and a clean, upright landscape habit. Green summer foliage casts useful shade, while inconspicuous flowers and winged samaras mark the season. It performs best with regular irrigation, slightly acidic soil, and ample rooting space.

A deciduous shrub or small tree with blue-green foliage that turns orange to red in the fall. Showy white flower clusters become edible, purple-black berries that can be used in pies and preserves. Native to North America.

A deciduous tree with a rounded to oval crown. In spring through summer, red twigs and branchlets are adorned with small, lobed, palmate leaves in glaucous green. Fall foliage is bright scarlet. Showy spring flowers in greenish-yellow. 'Autumn Flame' is a male selection and does not produce fruit. Native to Eastern North America.
A slow-growing deciduous tree with a symmetrical, spreading crown. Fan-shaped leaves emerge bright green and turn brilliant golden-yellow in fall. A fruitless male cultivar.

A small, slow-growing deciduous tree with a bushy, upright form. Circular, multi-lobed leaves emerge a signature burnt orange in spring, and turn pale yellow-green to salmon-pink in summer. Fall foliage turns gold to red. Red-purple spring flowers give way to red samaras. Can tolerate full shade. Needs slightly acidic soil, pH 5.5 - 6.5.

A deciduous tree with a straight trunk and an oval-pyramidal crown. Dark green foliage is divided into many pointed oval leaflets. Long-lasting fall color is wine red to deep purple. Fruitless male selection. Native to eastern U.S.

An upright deciduous tree featuring birch-like, serrated, medium green leaves. Symmetrical, rounded crown transforms to shades of gold and yellow in the fall before dropping. Dark brown, deeply fissured bark gives a characteristic, weathered look and a handsome silhouette when branches are bare. Female flowers are followed by clusters of drooping cream-white, hop-like flowers.

A deciduous tree with a low-branching, compact, upright growth habit. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves are reddish to green with yellow and blue undertones. Stunning clusters of deep purple-pink, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to China.

An evergreen tree with a dwarf, round form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In spring and summer, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are huge, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

A deciduous, broad-canopy tree with large palmate leaves and a strong native woodland character. Spring flower clusters support pollinators, and fall foliage turns yellow to gold. Native to California and the Pacific Coast, it is best in deep soils with room for roots and seasonal moisture.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright to arching branching habit. Frilly, pale pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honey bees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to orange, red, and yellow in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant hybrid.

A semi-evergreen to deciduous tree with an open, spreading crown and fine, fern-like leaves. Large clusters of violet-blue flowers cover the canopy in late spring followed by woody, disk shaped seedpods. Use as a street, lawn, or patio shade tree where fallen flowers are acceptable. It grows best in warm sites with deep, well-drained soil.

commonName: Black Tulip Saucer Magnolia, Tulip Tree
description: A deciduous, upright small tree with a narrow, rounded crown. Large, lightly scented, deep burgundy flowers open on bare branches in late winter and early spring followed by cone-like seed pods that feed birds. Broad green leaves turn yellow in fall. Use as a specimen, patio tree, flowering screen, or bold seasonal accent.

commonName: Black Tupelo Tree, Sour Gum, Pepperidge, Black Gum Tree
description: A deciduous tree with an attractive horizontal branching structure. Glossy, dark green leaves turn stunning shades in fall, from yellow-green to orange-red and reddish-purple. Small, dark blue fruits are produced if a male tree is nearby. Fruit is edible, yet very sour. Flowers and berries are beneficial to pollinators, birds, and other wildlife. Native to the eastern U.S.
An ornamental deciduous tree featuring double, pale pink flowers. Very little to no fruit set. Reddish purple foliage fading to bronzy green.

A large deciduous shade tree with big and maple-like dark green leaves. Attractive shedding bark with patches of brown and cream. Ball-shaped, fuzzy seed clusters persist on the tree in winter. Anthracnose resistant.

A large, slow-growing deciduous tree with a variable form and spreading, contorted, arching branches. Bark becomes checkered and light gray with age. Blue-green to dull green leaves are leathery and oval with shallow, wavy lobes. Fall foliage color is variable and may be yellow-orange or dull brown. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to California. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A dwarf deciduous tree with an oval, spreading crown. Bright green foliage is finely divided and ferny. Showy lavender-blue flower clusters bloom in abundance from spring into summer. Attracts hummingbirds. Spent flowers litter the ground below, followed by woody, ornamental seed pods.
Ornamental deciduous tree with abundant white flowers and broadly oval, glossy green leaves that turn bright red in the fall. Pyramidal form.

A deciduous tree with an oval crown and red branchlets. Palmate leaves with 3 - 5 lobes grow in medium to dark green with dull, blue-gray undersides. Fall foliage enlivens with brilliant reds and purples. Showy spring flowers in greenish-yellow attract birds, butterflies, and squirrels. Male seedless selection; does not produce fruit. Native to Eastern North America. Needs mildly acidic soil, tolerates clay soils.

An open and airy deciduous shrub or small tree with shaggy bark and twisted branches. Leaves are narrow, light green, and willow-like. Beautiful, deep purple-pink, trumpet-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds and produce slender seedpods. Native to the southwestern United States.

A deciduous tree with a low branching growth habit and a rounded, spreading crown. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves grow in bright burgundy to wine red to dull copper green and yellow. Stunning clusters of pink, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.

A deciduous tree with a pyramidal, spreading form. Leaves are broad and mid-green. In spring, fragrant flowers perch upright along the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, cup shaped, and yellow with red stamens. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A large deciduous tree with a broad, rounded form and spreading, twisting, arching branches. Bark becomes furrowed, checked and dark gray-brown with age. Leathery green leaves are large, oval and deeply lobed with sharp, little tips. Foliage emerges reddish in spring and turns gold with red-orange accents in fall. Inconspicuous female flowers and showy male catkins yield acorns. Native from southern Oregon to southern California. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A deciduous tree that gives an incredible show of creamy white flowers in spring. Sour-apple green leaves drop as early as July. Large horsechestnut fruits develop in late summer or early fall. A hallmark California native species.

A deciduous tree with a low branching growth habit and a rounded, spreading crown. Broad, soft, heart-shaped variegated leaves emerge burgundy red, and mature in shades of cream, pink, and light green. Stunning clusters of pink, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright to spreading branching habit. Frilly, dark pinky-purple flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage emerges bronze, matures to green, and turns orange-red in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, dark pinky-red flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from dark green to orange-red in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant.
Ornamental deciduous tree with single white flowers and broadly oval, glossy green leaves that turn purple-red in the fall, columnar form.
A deciduous tree with an attractive branching habit. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by rosy-red and white, petal-like bracts. Bright green foliage turns bright red in the fall.
A deciduous tree with an attractive branching habit. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by rosy-red, petal-like bracts. Bright green foliage turns bright red in the fall.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright to spreading branching habit. Frilly, cherry-pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from dark green to orange-red in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant hybrid.

A deciduous tree with an attractive branching habit. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by white, petal-like bracts. Foliage is variegated bright green with rose-tinged white margins. Leaves turn red in fall.

A deciduous tree with a tall and rounded crown of oblong to lanceolate, moderately serrated, deep green leaves that resemble those of a chestnut. Bark becomes furrowed and grayish-brown with age. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield one inch long acorns.
Semi-evergreen picturesque tree with feathery, deep green leaves. Canopy casts light filtered shade.

commonName: Chinese Evergreen Elm, Weeping Lacebark Elm
description: A semi-evergreen tree with a rounded, weeping crown. The trunk exfoliates its gray and tan bark in mosaic, puzzle-like patterns. Deep green foliage turns golden-yellow, rusty-red and purple in cold weather. Leaves are elliptic, leathery, and sharply toothed on the edges. Disease resistant.

A deciduous tree with an open branching habit and a rounded, flat-topped crown. Leaves are compound, feathery and mid-green. Foliage turns yellow in fall. Long, terminal panicles of golden-yellow flowers bloom in late summer. Rosy-pink, papery seed capsules follow.
A small deciduous tree that is fringed with fragrant, white flowers. Broad green leaves turn yellow in the fall. Bark is golden to gray-brown. Produces small, blackish blue fruits. Attracts birds.
An attractive deciduous tree, especially in the fall when the deep green, divided foliage turns a brilliant orange-red. Clusters of tiny red fruit form if a male variety is nearby.

commonName: Chinquapin Oak, Chinkapin White Oak, Yellow Chestnut Oak
description: A deciduous tree with a broad, open, spreading form. Bark becomes flaky and white-gray with age. Shiny green leaves are lance-shaped and coarsely toothed. Foliage turns yellow-brown in fall. Inconspicuous female and male catkins yield acorns. Native to central and eastern North America. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A deciduous tree with broad, spreading, arching branches. Bark becomes furrowed and dark with age. Glossy, dark green leaves are narrowly oval with rounded, sharp-tipped lobes. Foliage turns ornamental gold and red in fall. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to Texas and Mexico. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.
A deciduous tree with an attractive branching habit. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by white, petal-like bracts. Bright green foliage turns rusty red in the fall. Profuse bloomer.

A deciduous, broadly pyramidal shade tree with a strong trunk and large, deeply lobed leaves. Cream, olive, and brown bark peels in bold patches. Yellow-brown fall color and hanging seed balls add winter interest. This hybrid resists anthracnose and mildew. Use for streets, parks, and large sites. Seed hairs may irritate sensitive people.

A deciduous tree with a tall, upright to arching growth habit and a rounded, shade-giving crown. Leaves are rough, toothed, pointed and medium green. Flowers are small and yellow. Edible fruits mature in fall and resemble small, blackish purple plums. Attracts birds and other wildlife.

A large deciduous tree with a broad, variable canopy and spreading, contorted, arching branches. Bark becomes furrowed and dark gray with age. Leathery, dark green leaves are thick and egg-shaped with sharply toothed, rolled under edges. Inconspicuous female flowers and semi-showy male catkins yield large acorns. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A deciduous tree with a vigorous, upright growth habit. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by narrowly pointed, white petal-like bracts. Flowers are followed by inch-wide, raspberry-like fruits. Pointed, glossy green leaves turn yellow to scarlet in fall. Highly disease resistant. Does not produce fruit. A hybrid of C. florida x C. kousa.

A deciduous, upright small tree with refined foliage and a layered branching habit. Palmate green leaves turn yellow to orange in fall, while young stems display bright coral-red winter color. It is well suited to courtyards and woodland edges with evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil.

commonName: Coral Sun Golden Rain Tree, Coral Sun Pride of India
description: A deciduous tree with an open branching habit and a rounded, shade-giving crown. Twigs and stems are bright red in spring. Leaves are compound, feathery, and yellow-green in youth, maturing to coral pink. Foliage turns handsome yellow in fall. Non-flowering cultivar.

Deciduous tree native to South Africa. Bare branches are angular and attractive, and produce large clusters of deep red-orange tubular flowers. Flowers produce nectar in abundance, attracting birds. After flowering, the tree is adorned with black seed pods that burst open to reveal bright red seeds. In late winter or earlier, flowers give way to new, bright green egg-shaped leaves.

A deciduous tree with a single trunk, a dense pyramidal crown, and upright branches. Smaller leaves are rich green, heart-shaped, and toothed on the margins. Abundant, fragrant, pale yellow flowers bloom in early summer. Attracts bees.
A deciduous shade tree from Europe with a rounded crown. Five-lobed leaves resemble Acer saccarum but are maroon-red in color. Reddish-yellow flowers in the spring are followed by purple samaras.

A deciduous mounding shrub with lacy, deeply-lobed, palmate leaves that divide into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. The foliage is a deep crimson that turns scarlet red in fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil, pH 5.5 - 6.5.

A deciduous shade tree from Europe with a columnar growth habit. Five-lobed leaves resemble Acer saccarum but are deep purple in color. Showy clusters of flowers in the spring are followed by samaras.

A tough, drought-tolerant deciduous tree with an airy, vase-shaped growth habit. Profuse clusters of large, yellow flowers bloom in spring. Leaflets are small, oval, and green to chartreuse. Trunk and branches are bright green. Less seedpod litter than other Cercidium species. Thornless. Prefers well-drained soil.

An open and airy deciduous shrub or small tree with shaggy bark and twisted branches. Leaves are narrow, light green, and willow-like. Beautiful, pink, trumpet-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds and produce slender seedpods. Native to the southwestern United States.

A semi-evergreen tree with a broadly weeping crown. The trunk exfoliates its gray and tan bark in mosaic, puzzle-like patterns. Deep green foliage turns golden-yellow and rusty-red in cold weather. Leaves are elliptic, leathery, and sharply toothed on the edges. Disease resistant.

A deciduous, heat-tolerant shade tree with exfoliating cinnamon, tan, and cream bark. Glossy green leaves show improved resistance to leaf spot and scorch, with yellow fall color. A strong choice for irrigated landscapes, rain gardens, and moist soils in warmer regions.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, scarlet red flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to orange-red in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age.

A deciduous tree with a low-branching growth habit and a rounded, spreading crown. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves are dull to blue-green to chartreuse. Stunning clusters of pink, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.
A deciduous tree with an upright growth habit. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by bright white, petal-like bracts. Light green foliage turns red in fall. A hybrid of C. florida x C. nuttallii.

A deciduous tree with a pyramidal form. Leaves are broad and mid-green. In spring, fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, cup-shaped, creamy yellow, and sterile. Seedy, cone-like fruits are infrequent. Attracts birds.

A vigorous deciduous tree with a dense, shade-giving habit. Trunk is stout, and lined with furrowed gray bark. Leaves are dark green, sharply toothed, and egg-shaped. Fall foliage is yellow to orange.

commonName: Emerald Sunshine Chinese Elm, Lacebark Elm
description: A deciduous, fast-growing shade tree with a sturdy trunk and broad vase-shaped crown. Deep green, ridged leaves open bronze and turn yellow in fall. It resists elm leaf beetle and several elm diseases. Use it for streets, parking areas, or lawns where heat, wind, and dry conditions limit other trees.

A deciduous, graceful small tree with a rounded to layered canopy and finely cut palmate foliage. Spring leaves mature into rich summer color and finish with strong orange-to-red fall tones. It is best used in courtyards, entries, and woodland gardens with evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil.

Fast growing deciduous tree that provides year round interest, with an upright, vase-shaped crown of compound leaves. Foliage emerges in late spring with pinkish tints, and reaches a mature deep blue-green by summer, before dropping in fall. Contorted, arching branches are bare in winter and make a picturesque silhouette. Creamy white to light green flowers are present in spring. Seedless male form.

A deciduous, graceful shade tree with a light canopy, pendulous branch tips, and white bark that develops dark fissures with age. Small green leaves turn yellow in fall. It performs best in cool-summer sites with evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil.

commonName: Evening Light Japanese Snowdrop, Evening Light Japanese Snowbell
description: A charming, ornamental deciduous tree offering a fragrant springtime show of small, white, flowers dangling from deep red stems. New leaves emerge in shades of deep, plum purple and mature to dark green. A slow growth habit leads to an upright, vase-shaped canopy. Attracts local pollinators.

Deciduous tree with an upright and pyramidal form, and medium green palmate leaves. Bark exfoliates to reveal shades of green, brown, and tan. Insignificant blooms lead to sparse ball-like seed heads in spring and summer.

A stately deciduous tree with a rounded crown of compound, medium green leaves. Excellent fall color. Bark is grayish-brown, heavily ridged, and corky in texture. Non-showy yellowish green spring flowers.
A slow-growing deciduous tree with a conical crown. Fan-shaped leaves emerge medium green and turn golden-yellow in fall. A fruitless male cultivar.

A deciduous accent tree with a multi-branching growth habit and a rounded crown. Nearly circular leaves are divided into many lobes. Foliage is an attractive medium green that turns brilliant orange to red in the fall. Needs slightly acidic soil.
A deciduous tree with a narrow, pyramidal growth habit. Green leaves are lobed and maple-like. Foliage turns shades of yellow, orange, pink and red in fall. Seedpods look like spiky spheres.

A low-branching deciduous tree with palmate leaves that divide into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Glowing red foliage does not fade in summer heat. In the fall, leaves become purple-green. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

commonName: Firestarter Black Tupelo Tree, Firestarter Black Gum Tree
description: A deciduous tree with an attractive narrow form and horizontal branching structure. Glossy, dark green leaves turn fiery red in fall. Seedless cultivar.

A small deciduous tree with toothed, lobed, rich green leaves. Takes on a flaming red color in autumn. Fragrant, pendulous, yellow-white flower clusters in spring are followed by showy, red samaras. Known for its vase-like form that becomes more rounded with age.

A deciduous tree with a low-branching growth habit and a spreading, open crown. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves emerge burgundy red, maturing through shades of yellow and gold, to green as they age. Stunning, profuse clusters of purple-pink, double flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.

A suckering, fast-growing, deciduous tree with compound leaves of 3 to 5 toothed leaflets. Variegated foliage emerges pink and ages to green with cream margins. Greenish-yellow flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Separate male and female trees.

commonName: Forest Green Italian Oak, Forest Green Hungarian Oak
description: An upright, vigorous deciduous tree with a strong central trunk. Dark gray furrowed bark contrasts nicely against glossy, dark green leaves. Foliage takes on shades of yellow and bronze with the arrival of fall. Egg-shaped, oblong acorns are present in spring. 'Forest Green' is about half the size of the species.

A deciduous tree with a low branching growth habit and a rounded, spreading crown. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves grow in deep maroon to green to golden orange. Stunning clusters of purple-pink, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.

A deciduous tree with a dense and rounded form. Leaves are deep green, palmate, and are highly disease resistant. Gives an incredible show of pink and yellow flower clusters in spring, flowers are followed by insignificant seed capsules. Well suited for smaller spaces.

commonName: Fragrant Fountain Japanese Snowdrop Tree, Japanese Snowbell
description: A small deciduous tree with a densely branched, weeping crown. Profuse clusters of white, drooping, mildly fragrant flowers bloom in early summer. Dark green foliage turns gold in fall.
A deciduous tree with a columnar growth habit. Bark is gray and furrowed. Leaves are rich green, sharply toothed, and egg-shaped. Fall foliage is gold.

A deciduous tree with an upright, oval crown. Bright yellow-green leaves divide into many oval leaflets. Young shoots carry sharp spines. Fragrant masses of white, sweetpea-like flowers attract bees during the short bloom cycle in late spring.

A semi-evergreen tree with an oval to pyramidal crown. Bark is gray-green and smooth. Deep green foliage turns brilliant purple-red in cold weather. Leaves are smaller, oblong, and toothed on the edges. Disease resistant.

A small deciduous tree with a pyramidal form. Leaves are broad and mid-green. In late spring, flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, cup-shaped, and rosy-purple with a light pink interior. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

commonName: Gambel Oak, Rocky Mountain White Oak
description: Deciduous tree native to the Western US. Bark is rough and light grayish-brown. Leaves are deep green with whitish, hairy undersides. Wonderful fall color palette of golden yellow, orange, and red. One inch, egg shaped acorns appear in late summer to early fall.

A small deciduous tree with a round, upright crown. Leaves are broad and mid-green. In early to late spring, fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, cup-shaped, and deep, rich maroon. Potential to sustain flowers into summer. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A low-branching deciduous tree with a vase-like form that broadens to a rounded canopy. Deeply-lobed, palmate leaves are creamy white with green veins, and purplish leaf tips. Fall foliage turns a classic orange-red palette. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A deciduous tree with a rounded, bushy form. Circular leaves with 9 - 13 lobes emerge bright yellow in spring and become yellow-green in summer. Fall brings an array of gold to orange-red foliage. Reddish-purple spring flowers give way to red samaras, which point upward. Native to Japan. Can tolerate full shade.

A deciduous tree with an open branching habit and a rounded, shade-giving crown. Leaves are compound, feathery and blue-green. Foliage turns handsome yellow in fall. Long, terminal panicles of golden-yellow flowers bloom in late summer. Red-brown, papery seed capsules follow.

Deciduous, cascading dwarf tree with a low mound and finely divided leaves. Spring foliage opens red to purple with pink, cream, and white streaks, then turns bright red in fall. Small flowers give way to winged seeds. Native to East Asian forests. Thrives in sheltered, well-drained, slightly acidic soil. Use as specimen or focal point.

A deciduous tree with a vase-shaped habit that matures to a rounder form. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by narrowly pointed, large, creamy white and rosy pink petal-like bracts. Flowers are followed by inch-wide, raspberry-like fruits. Oval, pointed, lustrous green leaves turn yellow to scarlet in the fall.

A deciduous tree with a low branching growth habit and a rounded, spreading crown. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves grow in pink-red to golden green. Stunning clusters of lavender-pink, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.
One of the showiest of all flowering peaches. Rich pink, double flowers. It blooms late to avoid many frosts, and holds flowers for up to 3 weeks.

A fast-growing deciduous tree with a pyramidal to rounded growth habit. Exfoliating bark is lighter in color than the species. Green leaves are larger, diamond shaped and finely toothed. Fall foliage is deep yellow. Small cone-like fruits in the winter. Resistant to bronze birch borer.

A deciduous, upright shade tree prized for bright white bark and a clean pyramidal to oval canopy. Dark green leaves turn yellow in fall, and pendant catkins add early-season texture. Best suited to cooler sites with acidic, evenly moist soil and root-zone mulch.

A semi-evergreen to evergreen, small flowering tree with a rounded canopy and distinctive twin-lobed leaves. Large orchid-like rose-purple flowers bloom from fall into winter, providing strong seasonal color in mild climates. Useful as a patio or street tree where reflected heat, drainage, and frost protection are favorable.

A rounded, upright deciduous tree with a cascading form. Lacy, deeply-lobed palmate leaves divide into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Red-purple leaves maintain color throughout summer. Foliage becomes a brilliant, crimson red in the fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs mildly acidic soil.
A slow-growing dwarf deciduous tree with a vase-shaped crown. Bi-lobed, fan-shaped leaves emerge bright green and turn golden-yellow in fall. A fruitless male cultivar.

A deciduous tree with a broad, horizontally spreading crown. Leaves are mid-green, roughly oval and pointed with serrated margins. In spring, masses of deep pink buds open to single white flowers. Attracts bees. Clusters of small, yellow to red, apple-like fruits persist throughout fall. Attracts birds and other wildlife. Disease-resistant.

A deciduous, graceful small tree with a rounded to layered canopy and finely cut palmate foliage. Spring leaves mature into rich summer color and finish with strong orange-to-red fall tones. It is best used in courtyards, entries, and woodland gardens with evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil.
A tough and drought-tolerant deciduous tree producing yellow flowers in loose, long clusters. Fine-textured, long and linear foliage. Bright yellow-green trunk and branches, with spiny twigs.

A magnificent deciduous tree cloaked in lustrous, deep green leaves with silvery green undersides. Creamy white flowers emerge with the arrival of spring, and while not spectacular on their own, bloom in such abundance they create a stunning display. Flowers are followed by small, shiny black-blue fruits in late summer. Foliage offers mottled tones of yellows, oranges, and purples during fall season.

A compact deciduous tree with dense foliage. Small, palmate leaves emerge in chartreuse with orange margins, then mature to bright green in summer. Fall foliage turns to yellow and orange. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A deciduous, rounded shade tree with an open, spreading crown. Fine-textured green leaves turn bright orange, red, and crimson in fall. This male selection makes no fruit, reducing litter near paving. Use for streets, parking areas, lawns, and hot inland sites. It grows well in deep, well-drained soil and handles heat once established.

Fast growing deciduous tree that provides year round interest, with an upright and open crown of compound leaves. Foliage emerges in late spring with pinkish tints, and reaches a mature deep blue-green by summer, before dropping in fall. Contorted, arching branches are bare in winter and make a picturesque silhouette. Creamy white to light green flowers are present in spring, followed by reddish-brown seed pods.

Deciduous hybrid of English Oak and Swamp White Oak with a very tight, columnar form. Leaves are dark, glossy green with yellow to yellow-brown fall color, and are highly resistant to powdery mildew. Catkin-flowers yield acorns. Good tolerance of urban soils, drought-tolerance, and tight form make this an excellent street tree.

commonName: Koto No Ito Japanese Maple, Dancing Monkey Tree
description: A medium-sized deciduous tree with a vase-shaped form. Deeply-cut palmate leaves emerge purple-red in spring and turn yellow-orange in fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras.

commonName: Koto No Ito Japanese Maple, Dancing Monkey Tree
description: A medium-sized deciduous tree with a vase-shaped form. Deeply-cut palmate leaves emerge purple-red in spring and turn yellow-orange in fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras.

botanicalName: Cornus kousa, Cornus kousa var. chinensis
description: A deciduous tree with a vase-shaped habit that matures to a rounder form. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by narrowly pointed, white petal-like bracts. Flowers are followed by inch-wide, raspberry-like fruits. Oval, pointed, lustrous green leaves turn yellow to scarlet in the fall.
