An ornamental deciduous tree with an upright, rounded oval form. Features single pink flowers and deep blackish purple foliage. Little to no fruit set.
An ornamental deciduous tree with a broad, vase-shape that becomes more rounded with age. Pendant clusters of double, rosy pink flowers. Foliage emerges bronzy-red.

A medium sized deciduous tree with an upright and spreading crown of leathery, shallow lobed leaves. Bark is light gray and furrowed. New foliage is peach colored, and matures to deep blue-green before dropping in the fall.

A deciduous tree with a low-branching, compact, upright growth habit. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves are reddish to blue green to yellow-red. Stunning clusters of magenta, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to the California foothills at elevations below 4,000 feet. This selection has a bushier habit and darker flowers than the species.

A dwarf deciduous tree with a weeping, umbrella-like growth habit. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves grow in copper-tinted green to deep blue-green to yellow. Stunning clusters of lavender purple, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.

A small deciduous tree with a compact, multi-stemmed, round form. Leaves are broad and mid-green. In early spring, slightly fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are star-shaped with strappy petals, and purple-pink with a white interior. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A deciduous, upright small tree with a dense, rounded to vase-shaped crown. Glossy leaves open deep purple, hold rich burgundy tones, then turn yellow in fall. Pink-purple flowers feed bees and butterflies in early spring, followed by fewer seed pods than many redbuds. A good accent for patios, small gardens, and woodland edges.

A small deciduous tree with a vigorous, round form. Leaves are broad and mid-green. Throughout spring, lightly fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are white and star-shaped with strappy petals. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A deciduous, slow growing tree with glossy dark green summer foliage that shifts to red, orange, and gold during fall. Canopy develops into a dense, upright oval shape. Tolerant of poor soil conditions, and praised for cold hardiness.

A deciduous tree with a low-branching, upright growth habit. Smaller, glossy, wavy-edged, heart-shaped leaves are pale blue-green to gold. Stunning clusters of dark pink, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to Texas and Mexico.

A vigorous deciduous tree with an upright and open habit. Leaves are lance-shaped and glossy green, with silvery undersides. Fragrant, creamy white flowers bloom throughout spring and summer. Good cold hardiness.

A slow-growing deciduous tree with a low-branching growth habit. Circular, multi-lobed leaves emerge bright red in spring and turn yellow-green in summer. Fall foliage is a showy display of orange-yellow-red. Reddish-purple spring flowers give way to red samaras, which point upward. More sun-tolerant than 'Aureum.' Can tolerate full shade. Needs slightly acidic soil, pH 5.5 - 6.5.

A fast-growing deciduous tree that is a hybrid cross of Catalpa bignonioides and Chilopsis linearis. Flowers are frilly and trumpet-shaped with delicate, white petals and purple-striped throats. Leaves are pointed and bright-yellow green. The trunk is slender with chestnut brown bark.

An ornamental deciduous tree with a rounded form and horizontal branching pattern. Pink buds that open to semi-double, white flowers. Foliage emerges bronzy-red, matures to green, then turns brilliant yellow-orange in the fall.
Narrow to vase-shaped deciduous tree with smooth gray bark, and narrowly oval and saw toothed leaves. Yellow to orange fall foliage.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, amethyst-pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to red-orange in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant hybrid.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, white flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from green to red-orange in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant hybrid.
Ornamental deciduous tree with white flowers and broadly oval, glossy green leaves that turn orange-red in the fall. Pyramidal form. More disease resistant than 'Bradford'.
An ornamental deciduous tree with an upright, rounded crown. Features single, pale pink flowers and deep bronzy purple foliage. Bears small fruit crop.

A deciduous shade tree develops a broad, rounded crown with glossy green leaves. Brilliant red fall color arrives late and often lasts for weeks, while red flowers and winged seeds add seasonal detail. The species is native to eastern North American woods and wetlands. Use as a street tree, lawn specimen, or rain-garden anchor.
An ornamental deciduous tree with an oval, upright form. Brilliant display of carmine-pink flowers. Dark green leaves turn shades of yellow, orange, and red in the fall. Heat tolerant.

botanicalName: Cercis canadensis var. texensis 'Oklahoma', Cercis reniformis
description: A deciduous tree with a compact, low-branching, shrubby growth habit. Broad, glossy, heart-shaped, wavy-edged leaves grow in red to dark green to yellow. Stunning clusters of dark red, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern and central North America.

A low-branching deciduous tree with a notably weeping form. Lacy, deeply-lobed, palmate leaves divide into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Leaves emerge orange, mature to green, then turn a fiery reddish-orange color in the fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. 'Orangeola' is more heat tolerant than other maples. Needs mildly acidic soil.

An upright deciduous tree with a rounded crown. Palmate leaves divide into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Foliage of rich olive-orange turns a dramatic crimson in the fall. Tolerates sun and heat well. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

An upright deciduous tree with a spreading crown. Palmate leaves divide into 7 pointed lobes. Bronzy red to green leaves turn scarlet red in the fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A small deciduous tree with exfoliating cinnamon red bark. Coarsely toothed, trifoliate leaves are dark green with silvery-green undersides, turn brilliant orange-red in the fall. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A compact, shrubby deciduous tree known for its year-round delicate, pastel foliage. Palmate leaves divide into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Leaves have ruffled edges and emerge in cream and pink. Summertime foliage matures to cream with green venation and then turns to orange and gold with the fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

An ornamental deciduous tree with an upright and rounded form. Fragrant, double rosy pink flowers begin to bloom in February. Flowers are followed by small and fuzzy, green to yellow apricots which are bitter and inedible. Broadly oval, serrated foliage.

An attractive deciduous tree or shrub with dense, glossy foliage year-round. During autumn, the canopy transforms from shades of emerald green to vibrant hues of yellow, rosy pink, and scarlet red before dropping to the earth. Small, spidery flowers are borne from bare branches during late winter and early spring, and contrast against furrowed, flaky gray bark. 'Vanessa' is a dense and upright form, growing about half as wide as the species.

A deciduous tree with an upright columnar form and shallowly toothed, oval leaves with wavy margins. Foliage emerges pruple, turns deep green with purple margins in the summer, and eventually shades of bright orange-yellow to scarlet in the fall. Exfoliating smooth gray and white bark.

A deciduous tree with an upright columnar form and shallowly toothed, oval leaves with wavy margins. Foliage emerges pruple, turns deep green with purple margins in the summer, and eventually shades of bright orange-yellow to scarlet in the fall. Exfoliating smooth gray and white bark.

A fast-growing deciduous tree that is a hybrid cross of Catalpa bignonioides and Chilopsis linearis. Flowers are frilly and trumpet-shaped with delicate white and pink petals and pink-striped throats. Leaves are pointed and bright-yellow green. The trunk is slender with chestnut brown bark.
A deciduous tree with an attractive branching habit. The true flowers are tiny and surrounded by large, rosy pink, petal-like bracts. Oval, green leaves turn red in the fall.

A small deciduous tree with a low-branching, weeping growth habit. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves grow in red to deep green to yellow. Stunning clusters of lavender pink, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America. More upright than C. canadensis 'Lavender Twist.'

A deciduous, rounded tropical tree for warm courts, streets, and bold spring color. Pink to purple trumpet flowers cover bare branches, then long pods release winged seeds. Native from Mexico through South America, it feeds hummingbirds and bees. Strong wood and a moderate crown make it useful where summer shade is needed.

A deciduous tree with an upright, compact branching habit. Frilly, deep pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage emerges wine red and matures to maroon-green. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant.

A deciduous tree with an upright, rounded crown. Foliage emerges red, matures to dark green, and turns dull orange in fall. Leaves are roughly oval and pointed with serrated margins. In spring, masses of pink-red buds open to single, deep pink flowers. Attracts bees. Clusters of small, purple-red, apple-like fruits persist throughout fall. Attracts birds and other wildlife.

A slow-growing deciduous tree with a symmetrical, dense and upright crown, and strong central leader. Fan-shaped leaves emerge bright green and turn brilliant golden-yellow in fall. A fruitless male cultivar.
A slow-growing deciduous tree with a dense, columnar to conical crown. Fan-shaped leaves emerge medium green and turn golden-yellow in fall. A fruitless male cultivar.

A semi-evergreen to deciduous, small flowering tree with a rounded crown and broad, butterfly-shaped leaves. Showy purple-pink, orchid-like flowers appear in fall and early winter, followed by narrow pods. A useful accent or patio tree for warm sites with good drainage and moderate establishment water.
A semi-dwarf, ornamental deciduous tree with deep purple foliage that holds color well throughout the season. Features single, pale pink flowers. Does not bear fruit.

A deciduous tree with suckering roots and an upright, oval crown, more dense than the species. Blue-green leaves divide into many oval leaflets. Foliage emerges bronze-red. Nonshowy yellow fall color. Fragrant masses of dark violet, sweetpea-like flowers attract bees during the short bloom cycle in late spring. Similar appearance to R. x ambigua idahoensis.
Deciduous tree with triangular leaves that turn bright yellow in the fall and flutter in the breeze, smooth white bark.

A deciduous tree with a straight trunk and a dense, round crown. Mature bark is furrowed and gray-brown. Dark green foliage is divided into many pointed, oval leaflets. Long-lasting fall color is wine red. Seedless selection. Resistant to Ash blight. Native to the Mediterranean.

An upright, weeping deciduous tree with a mounding form. Lacy, deeply-lobed palmate leaves divide into 7 to 11 pointed lobes. Leaves are deep purple and turn bright red in the fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil, pH 5.5 - 6.5.

A deciduous tree with an upright growth habit in youth that ages to a graceful, rounded form. Rounded, heart-shaped foliage emerges deep purple, matures to blue-green, and turns bright yellow-orange in fall. Falling autumn leaves are reported to carry a faint fragrance reminiscent of burnt sugar.

A deciduous, rounded shade tree with large palmate leaves and showy upright spring flower panicles. The canopy provides bold texture, followed by ornamental buckeye-like fruit and fall color. It performs best in deep, well-drained soil with moderate irrigation and room for surface roots.

A deciduous, rounded shade tree with large palmate leaves and showy upright spring flower panicles. The canopy provides bold texture, followed by ornamental buckeye-like fruit and fall color. It performs best in deep, well-drained soil with moderate irrigation and room for surface roots.

A deciduous, graceful small tree with a rounded to layered canopy and finely cut palmate foliage. Spring leaves mature into rich summer color and finish with strong orange-to-red fall tones. It is best used in courtyards, entries, and woodland gardens with evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil.

botanicalName: Quercus rubra, Quercus rubra maxima, Quercus borealis
description: A large deciduous tree with a broadly spreading growth habit. Bark becomes furrowed and dark brown with age. Dark green leaves are thick and roughly oval with sharply toothed lobes. Foliage turns ornamental red-brown in fall. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to eastern North America. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A deciduous, upright, shade-giving tree valued for strong structure and seasonal color. New foliage emerges red to coppery red, matures to green through summer, then shifts to orange-red tones in fall. This non fruiting male variety is a durable choice for streetscapes, parking lots, courtyards, and heat-reflective sites with well-drained soil.

commonName: Red Rage Tupelo, Red Rage Black Gum
description: A deciduous tree featuring glossy, deep emerald green foliage that transforms to lustrous shades of scarlet and orange with the arrival of fall. Small, greenish white flowers may emerge on long stalks during spring, while they are not showy, they provide an important source of nutrition for local pollinators. Flowers are followed by dark blue fruits, attractive to local birds and wildlife. Makes an excellent shade tree, and companion to naturalized landscapes. Native to the Eastern US.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, cherry red flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from dark green to bronze-red in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant.

A deciduous shade tree selected for reliable red to orange fall color and a clean, upright landscape habit. Green summer foliage casts useful shade, while inconspicuous flowers and winged samaras mark the season. It performs best with regular irrigation, slightly acidic soil, and ample rooting space.

A shade-giving deciduous tree with an open branching pattern. Red branchlets compliment the 3 - 5 lobed, vivid green leaves. Fall foliage turns bright scarlet red. Excellent cold hardiness. Needs slightly acidic soil.

commonName: Regal Prince English x Swamp White Hybrid Oak
description: A columnar deciduous tree with a narrow, oval crown. Broad, toothed leaves are glossy, dark green and mildew-resistant. Foliage turns yellow in fall. Catkin-flowers yield acorns. Adapted to a wide range of soil conditions, including moist, well-drained loams and drier established sites.

A deciduous tree with a straight trunk and a round crown. Mature bark is furrowed and gray-brown. Dark green foliage is divided into many large, oval leaflets. Fall color is bright yellow. Inconspicuous flowers appear in spring. One-winged fruit forms on females. Resistant to oak root fungus. Bred in Texas.
A vigorous deciduous tree with a columnar growth habit. Bark is gray and furrowed. Leaves are rich green, sharply toothed, and egg-shaped. Fall foliage is red and gold.

A large California-native, deciduous tree with rough, green, multi-lobed leaves. Foliage is so dense, this makes a good shade tree. Attractive shedding bark with patches of brown, gray, and cream. Ball-shaped, fuzzy seed clusters persist on the tree in winter. Often develops multiple leaning and twisting trunks. Foliage is more deeply cut, and bark is more variegated than the species.

A deciduous, slow growing tree with dark green summer foliage that shifts to red, orange, and gold during fall. Canopy develops into a dense, oval shape. Similar in appearance to Acer saccharum, but smaller in size. Tolerant of poor soil conditions.

A deciduous tree with a rounded, low-branching form. Dense, glossy, dark green foliage turns red in fall. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by pointed, pink, petal-like bracts. A hybrid of C. kousa x C. nuttallii.

A deciduous tree with an upright, spreading crown. Unique cutleaf foliage is dark purple with bronze-orange-purple fall colors. In spring, masses of pink-red buds open to single, bright magenta flowers. Attracts bees. Clusters of small, red, apple-like fruits persist throughout fall. Attracts birds and other wildlife. Disease resistant.

A small deciduous tree with a spreading, round form. Leaves are broad and dark green. In late winter and early spring, lightly fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, double, star-shaped with strappy petals, and white. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A deciduous tree with a compact, low-branching growth habit and a rounded, spreading crown. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves are dull to blue-green to chartreuse. Profuse clusters of larger, white, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Variety endemic to the southwestern United States (West Texas and Northern Mexico) that is more drought and heat tolerant than populations from the Eastern United States.

A dwarf deciduous tree with a weeping, umbrella-like growth habit. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves grow in blackish red to golden rose. Stunning clusters of lavender purple, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.

A small deciduous tree with toothed, lobed, rich green leaves. 'Ruby Slippers' takes on a red color in autumn. Fragrant, pendulous, yellow-white flower clusters in spring are followed by showy, ruby-pink samaras. Grows upright with single, straight trunk and a dense, rounded canopy.

commonName: Ruby Vase Persian Parrotia, Persian Ironwood
description: A deciduous tree with shallowly toothed, oval leaves and wavy margins. New leaves emerge with a red margin and mature to handsome dark green. Excellent fall color. Exfoliating smooth gray and white bark. More upright and narrow than the species.

A deciduous tree with a vase-shaped habit that matures to a rounder form. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by narrowly pointed, rich pink petal-like bracts. Flowers are followed by inch-wide, raspberry-like fruits. Deep green foliage turns red in fall.

A small deciduous tree with a round crown. Leaves are broad and mid-green. Foliage turns yellow in fall. In late winter and early spring, lightly fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, tulip-shaped, and pale-pink with a white interior. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A fast-growing deciduous tree with a vase-shaped crown. Bark is smooth and gray in youth, and reveals a red-brown color with age. Deep green, pointed, oblong, leaves are named for their saw-toothed edges. In fall, foliage turns rusty-red. Good disease resistance.

A large deciduous tree with a broad, spreading form. Bark becomes fissured and gray with age. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with many pointed lobes. Foliage emerges yellow in spring and turns scarlet-red in fall. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to eastern North America. Similar to Q. schumardii. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A suckering, fast-growing deciduous tree with compound leaves of 3 to 5 leaflets. Each leaflet has toothed margins and is green in color, turning yellow in the fall. Greenish-yellow flowers are followed by pairs of samaras in the fall. Seedless male cultivar.

A small, bushy deciduous tree with deeply-lobed palmate leaves that grow in clumped arrangements. Foliage is burgundy-red in summer and bright scarlet in fall. A dwarf version of 'Bloodgood.' Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A deciduous, rounded shade tree with a dense crown and strong heat tolerance. Five-lobed leaves open reddish purple, turn glossy green, then shift to yellow, orange, and red in fall. Small spring flowers lead to winged seeds. Native to northern China and Korea. Use near patios, streets, or smaller lawns with well-drained soil.

A dwarf deciduous tree with tiny palmate leaves. Leaf arrangements are very compact and dense, which gives the tree a very rounded form. Rich green leaves turn orange to scarlet in fall. Small, inconspicuous flowers in spring are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil, pH 5.5 - 6.5.

A rounded, shrubby deciduous tree with a strong branching habit. Deeply-lobed, palmate leaves emerge in sensational cherry red and then turn to light green in summer. Autumn gives way to orange and red foliage. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A deciduous tree with a low-branching, compact, upright growth habit. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves are reddish to green with yellow and blue undertones. Stunning clusters of creamy white, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to China.

commonName: Shishigashira Japanese Maple, Lion's Head Maple
description: A compact and shrubby deciduous tree with crinkled palmate leaves that grow in dense tufts along the stems. Summertime foliage is bright green. Fall foliage emits radiant shades of gold and crimson. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A large deciduous tree with a broad, spreading form. Bark becomes fissured and gray with age. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with many pointed lobes. Foliage emerges yellow in spring and turns yellow-red-brown in fall. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to eastern North America. Similar to Q. coccinea. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A dwarf deciduous tree with a compact, rounded form. Small, multi-lobed leaves emerge light green from spring through summer. Fall foliage is a showy display of yellow and red tones. Red-purple spring flowers give way to red samaras that point upward. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A rapidly growing deciduous tree with a spreading crown and delicate, ferny, rich green leaves. Tufts of fluffy pink, pincushion-like flowers in summer. Attracts pollinators, including birds and butterflies.

A small evergreen tree with a rounded crown of leathery, lance-shaped leaves. Foliage is light green with striking silvery white undersides. Golden-brown acorns are present during spring and provide a food source for local wildlife.

commonName: Single Weeping Flowering Cherry, Weeping Higan Cherry
description: An ornamental deciduous tree with weeping branches that touch the ground. Abundant, single, pale pink flowers. New leaves emerge with a bronzy tint.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, rich pink flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage turns from super dark green to purple-red in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant hybrid.

commonName: Skinny Genes English x White Hybrid Oak
description: A deciduous tree with a very slender, columnar growth habit. Dark green leaves are glossy, lobed and mildew-resistant. Foliage turns yellow in fall. Inconspicuous male and female catkins yield acorns. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.
A deciduous tree with a columnar growth habit. Green leaves are lobed and maple-like. Foliage turns shades of yellow and red in fall. Sparse seedpods look like spiky spheres. Very little fruit drop.
An ornamental deciduous tree with a slightly curving trunk and weeping branches that touch the ground. Semi-double pure white flowers.
Deciduous ornamental tree with single white flowers, broad and upright habit.

commonName: Snowcone Japanese Snowdrop Tree, Japanese Snowbell
description: A small deciduous tree with a dense branching habit and a pyramidal crown. Profuse clusters of white, drooping, mildly fragrant flowers bloom in early summer. Dark green foliage turns yellow-red in fall.

A deciduous tree with a rounded, dense crown. Leaves are dark green, roughly oval and pointed with serrated margins. In spring, abundant red buds open to single, white flowers. Attracts bees. Clusters of small, orange-red, apple-like fruits persist throughout fall. Attracts birds and other wildlife. Cold hardy.
A deciduous tree with smooth gray bark that furrows with age, and oblong, lobular green leaves.

A small deciduous tree with a compact, round form. Leaves are broad and mid-green. In late winter, fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are star-shaped with strappy petals, and white. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A small deciduous tree with a vigorous, round form. Leaves are broad and mid-green. Throughout spring, lightly fragrant flowers open from pink buds, and cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are white and star-shaped with strappy petals. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A deciduous tree with dark green leaves that turn red in fall. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by large, white petal-like bracts. Profuse bloomer. Disease-resistant. A hybrid between C. kousa x C. nuttallii.

A deciduous tree with a vigorous, upright growth habit. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by rosy pink petal-like bracts. Oval, green leaves turn bright orange and red in fall. Does not produce fruit. A hybrid of C. florida x C. kousa.

A deciduous tree noted for its attractive leaves, light green above and silvery underneath, giving the canopy a glimmering glow as wind rustles through them. New foliage emerges silver, and matures through shades of light green and creamy yellow before dropping in the fall. More tolerant to heat than other species.

A hybrid deciduous tree with a uniform columnar growth habit. Bark becomes furrowed and dark brown-gray with age. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with many rounded lobes. Foliage turns rusty-brown in fall. Resistant to mildew. Inconspicuous male and female catkins yield acorns. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A fast-growing deciduous tree with a broad, round crown. Bark is smooth and white-gray. Large, glossy, dark green leaves are irregularly lobed. Foliage turns dull yellow in fall. 'Stribling' is a pollen-producing male form that does not yield fruit.

commonName: Summer Chocolate Silk Tree, Summer Chocolate Mimosa
description: A rapidly growing deciduous tree with a spreading crown and delicate, ferny, rich burgundy-green leaves. Tufts of fluffy pink, pincushion-like flowers in summer. Attracts pollinators, including birds and butterflies.
A graceful deciduous tree with fern-like foliage that emerges gold and ages to golden-green. Thornless and produces few or no seed pods. Tough and hardy tree.

A small deciduous tree with a dwarf, vase-like form. Leaves are broad and mid-green. Foliage turns yellow-bronze in fall. In late spring, lightly fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are huge and cup-shaped with pinkish-white on the inside and fuchsia-purple on the outside. Occasionally reblooms in summer. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A shrub-like deciduous tree with a broad, semi-weeping crown. Very lacy, deeply-lobed, palmate leaves divide into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Leaves are a bugundy-green color that holds well throughout the summer, then becomes bright red in the fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of pink samaras. Needs mildly acidic soil.

A deciduous tree with a low-branching, shrubby growth habit. Broad, roundly heart-shaped, leathery, wavy-edged leaves grow in red to dark green to yellow. Stunning clusters of red, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern and central North America.

A broad, multi-branching deciduous tree with palmate leaves that are smaller than typical. Summertime foliage is bright green, and then turns fiery orange, gold, and red in fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. The only 'dissectum' cultivar with an upright form. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A graceful deciduous tree with a spreading canopy and arching, cascading branches. Leaves are palmately lobed with sharply toothed edges. New growth is rosy pink. Summer foliage matures to whitish green with variegated green veins and edges. Coloration ages to yellow and gold in fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A dwarf deciduous tree with a rounded, slightly weeping crown. Small leaves are mid-green, roughly oval and pointed with serrated margins. In spring, masses of red buds open to single, white flowers. Attracts bees. Clusters of small, red, apple-like fruits ripen throughout fall. Attracts birds and other wildlife.
A deciduous tree with an upright trunk, a shade-giving crown, and smooth, gray bark. Variegated purple-pink, white and green leaves are glossy, oval and have wavy margins.

A deciduous, small to midsize shade tree with a rounded canopy and attractive exfoliating bark with age. Three-lobed green leaves turn orange, red, and gold in fall. It is a durable choice for patios, streetscapes, and courtyards where well-drained soil and moderate irrigation are provided.

commonName: True Green Chinese Elm, Lacebark Elm
description: A semi-evergreen tree with a rounded, weeping habit. More reliably evergreen than other varieties. The trunk exfoliates its gray and tan bark in mosaic, puzzle-like patterns. Deep green foliage turns golden-yellow and rusty-red in cold weather. Leaves are elliptic and sharply toothed on the edges.

A deciduous, tall shade tree with a straight trunk and broad crown for parks and other large sites. Yellow-green, tulip-like flowers have orange bands and feed bees and hummingbirds. Cone-like seed clusters follow, and green leaves turn gold in fall. Native to eastern North America, it grows best in deep, moist, well-drained, slightly acid soil.

A deciduous, upright small tree with a broad crown for streets, patios, and focal plantings. Coral-pink summer flowers rise above green leaves that turn orange-red in fall. Smooth cinnamon bark adds winter interest. This mildew-resistant hybrid handles heat well and grows best in sunny sites with good drainage and open air.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, rich purple flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage emerges bronze, matures to dark green, and turns orange, yellow, or red in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age.

A dwarf deciduous tree with a multi-stemmed habit and contorted branches. Green leaves divide into many oval leaflets. Nonshowy yellow fall color. Infrequent displays of white, sweetpea-like flowers. Blooms attract bees during the short cycle in late spring.

A deciduous tree with a columnar growth habit that broadens with age. Red palmate leaves mature to deep burgundy in summer, and then turn crimson red in fall. Ornamental red branches stand out in the winter landscape. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs sligthly acidic soil.

A deciduous tree with a dense, shade-giving habit. Bark is gray and furrowed. Leaves are dark green, sharply toothed, and egg-shaped. Fall foliage is yellow to orange. 'Fastigiata' has a columnar form in youth and matures to an oval-vase shape.

A deciduous tree with a dense, shade-giving habit. Bark is gray and furrowed. Leaves are dark green, sharply toothed, and egg-shaped. Fall foliage is yellow to orange. 'Fastigiata' has a columnar form in youth and matures to an oval-vase shape.

A deciduous tree with a narrow branching habit and an upright, columnar crown. Leaves are compound, feathery and blue-green. Foliage turns handsome yellow in fall. Long, terminal panicles of golden-yellow flowers bloom in late summer. Red-brown, papery seed capsules follow.

A symmetrical-branching deciduous tree with a pyramidal growth habit. From spring through summer, red twigs and branchlets are adorned with lobed, palmate leaves in medium green. Fall foliage is yellow, orange, and red. Showy spring flowers in greenish-yellow attract birds, butterflies, and squirrels. Native to Eastern North America. Needs mildly acidic soil, tolerates clay soil.
Deciduous tree with a narrow and upright form, glossy dark green leaves, and small acorns. Great mildew and disease resistance. Beneficial to local wildlife.
A compact deciduous tree with an upright and narrow form. Dark green foliage progresses to shades of deep red during fall. Requires low maintenance, and produces few seeds.

A very large deciduous tree with a vase-shaped to rounded form. Branches are arching, spreading, contorted and twisting. Bark becomes checkered, fissured and dark gray with age. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with deep, rounded lobes. Foliage turns yellow in fall. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to valleys of California. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A dwarf deciduous tree with a weeping, umbrella-like growth habit. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves grow in copper-tinted green to deep blue-green to yellow. Stunning clusters of creamy white, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to eastern North America.

A deciduous, rounded flowering tree for courts, woodland edges, and small lawns. Large creamy white bracts surround tiny spring flowers. Sparse red fruit and red-purple fall color follow. This Rutgers hybrid resists anthracnose and powdery mildew. It grows best in rich, well-drained soil with even moisture and cool, shaded roots.

A deciduous, multi-stem small tree or large shrub with a graceful woodland habit. Rounded palmate leaves turn yellow, orange, and red in fall, and winged samaras add seasonal interest. Native to the Pacific Coast region, it appreciates cool root conditions, mulch, and evenly moist, well-drained soil.

A shrub-like deciduous tree with a broad, weeping form. Lacy, deeply-lobed, palmate leaves are divided into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Bright green leaves emerge in spring then change to shades of golden-orange with the arrival of fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A graceful deciduous tree with open, spreading branches. Bark is green. Leaves are three-lobed and bright green. Lengthy, drooping chains of fragrant, golden-yellow flowers bloom from mid-spring to summer. Attracts butterflies and hummingbirds. Similar in appearance to Wisteria.

A small deciduous tree with an oval, round crown. Leaves are broad and mid-green. In late winter and early spring, lightly fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, cup-shaped, and bright ruby-magenta once the tree matures. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A deciduous tree with a rounded crown, spiny branches, and toothed leaves that turn orange and red in fall. Fragrant white flowers are followed by small red fruit. Attracts pollinators. Native to the Southeastern United States.

A deciduous shrub with a broad, weeping form. Lacy, deeply-dissected palmate leaves divide into 5 to 9 pointed lobes. Bright green leaves emerge in spring, then change to gold with red streaks in fall. Inconspicuous spring flowers are followed by pairs of samaras. Needs slightly acidic soil.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, watermelon-red flower clusters develop at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Foliage emerges bronze, matures to dark green, and turns yellow in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age.

A deciduous shade-giving tree that forms a short trunk and a broad, umbrella-like crown. Long, weeping branches are clothed in slender, emerald green leaves. Catkins form in spring. Prefers wetland and riparian habitats.

A deciduous tree with a low-branching, compact, upright growth habit. Broad, soft, heart-shaped leaves are reddish to blue green to yellow-red. Stunning clusters of magenta, sweetpea-like flowers bloom on bare branchlets in early spring. Native to the California foothills at elevations below 4,000 feet.

A large, California-native, deciduous shade tree with rough, green, multi-lobed leaves. Attractive shedding bark with patches of brown, gray, and cream. Ball-shaped, fuzzy seed clusters persist on the tree in winter. Often develops multiple leaning and twisting trunks.

A deciduous, fast-growing riparian tree with an upright oval canopy and clean green foliage. Catkins and small cone-like fruits add seasonal texture, while roots support nitrogen-fixing associations. Native to California, it is well suited to bioswales, creek edges, and landscapes with consistent soil moisture.
A deciduous tree with an attractive branching habit. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by white, petal-like bracts. Oval, green leaves turn red in the fall.

commonName: Wildfire Black Gum Tree, Black Tupelo
description: A deciduous tree with an attractive horizontal branching structure. Glossy leaves emerge bright red in spring, turn green in summer, and mature to reddish-purple in fall. Small, dark blue fruits are produced if a male tree is nearby. Fruit is edible, yet very sour. Flowers and berries are beneficial to pollinators, birds, and other wildlife. Native to the eastern U.S.

A deciduous tree with a rounded, oval crown and spreading, upright to arching branches. Bark becomes furrowed and gray-brown with age. Glossy, dark green leaves are lance-shaped with smooth edges, resembling willow. Foliage turns yellow in fall. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to the southeastern U.S. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A small deciduous tree with a pyramidal, oval crown. Leaves are broad and mid-green. In late spring, flowers cover the branches during leaf-out. Flowers are large, cup-shaped, and bright yellow. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.
An ornamental deciduous tree with a graceful, spreading and arching crown. Fragrant, single pale-pink to white flowers. Deep glossy green leaves turn yellow in the fall.

A deciduous tree with a pyramidal, semi-irregular form. Leaves are broad and dark green. In spring, fragrant flowers cover the branches before leaf-out. Flowers are large, cup shaped, and white, sometimes with purple-tinged bases. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A deciduous tree with a slender trunk and an upright, open branching habit. Frilly, pinky-purple flower clusters bloom at branch tips. Unique flower texture is like ruffled tissue-paper. Blooms last from summer into fall, attracting honeybees and other pollinators. Green color turns red-orange in fall. Alternately arranged leaves are oval, sometimes rounded, and somewhat wavy-edged. Bark exfoliates with age. Mildew resistant hybrid.

Synthetic turf edge that is versatile and easy to install with slip joints. Flexible and durable. For non-structural uses.

commonName: Bonide Captain Jacks Dead Bug Brew
description: For residential use in home gardens, lawns, and ornamentals. For control of foliage feeding worms, thrips, and other pests in fruiting vegetables, cole crops, leafy vegetables, stone fruits, tuberous vegetables, and fruit trees.

Safe for use around children, plants, and pets. Lasts up to 3 months. 1 lb. of clean, dustless and biodegradable granules treats 500 sq. ft. Contains Rucinus communis Oil (castor oil) - 10%.

Monterey Citrus Leafminer Trap & Lure uses pheromones to attract the male leafminer where he is caught in the trap. For monitoring pest populations use one trap and lure per tree. For mass trapping use two per tree.

A gentle organic fertilizer and ideal supplement for all plantings. Provides a natural source of nutrients readily available to garden plants. Helps plants to develop new growth, green foliage, fruit, and beautiful flowers. It makes an ideal supplement to a regular fertilizing program. Also may be added to compost piles to help accelerate decomposition.

E.B. Stone's All Purpose Plant Food is a blend of natural organic ingredients formulated for use throughout the garden. It is suitable for use on vegetables, trees, shrubs, lawns, and flower gardens. E.B. Stone's All Purpose Plant Food is ideal for use when preparing new planting areas and for feeding existing plants. Contains Blood Meal, Feather Meal, Bone Meal, Dried Chicken Manure, Bat Guano, Alfalfa Meal, Kelp Meal, Potassium Sulfate, Humic Acids, and soil microbes including mycorrhizal fungi.

It will encourage growth, green foliage, and beautiful flowers. It is also suited for use on other acid-loving plants including rhododendrons, fuchsias, and evergreen conifers. Contains Blood Meal, Feather Meal, Cottonseed Meal, Bone Meal, Dried Chicken Manure, Bat Guano, Alfalfa Meal, Kelp Meal, Potassium Sulfate, Humic Acids, and soil microbes including mycorrhizal fungi.

E.B. Stone Bone Meal provides a long lasting source of phosphorous and nitrogen for the garden. It is an ideal transplanting fertilizer and an excellent natural source of phosphorous which is essential to plant growth and helps to stimulate root formation, sturdy top growth and flower, fruit and seed development. Bone meal is also suited for use with bulbs and other flowering plants, as well as vegetables like peas and beans. NPK: 1-15-0. Derived from: Bone Meal.
An ideal potting mix for all types of indoor cactus and succulents. Contains Fir Bark, Lava Rock, Canadian Sphagnum Peat Moss, Sand, Redwood Compost and Mushroom Compost.

E.B. Stone Citrus & Fruit Tree Food is a blend of select natural organic ingredients for use with citrus and other home orchard fruit trees and with small fruits like berries and those grown on vines. A natural organic soil conditioner. It helps loosen hard soils, improve soil aeration and conserve water. An excellent addition to native soils.

E.B. Stone's Hibiscus & Palm fertilizer is a blend of select organic ingredients formulated to promote the rich soil conditions required by palms, hibiscus, and other tropical plants. This fertilizer is ideal for use to support vigorous growth and flower production. It is suitable for use on a wide variety of tropical plants. It is blended with humic acid and beneficial soil microbes including mycorrhizae. Contains Blood Meal, Feather Meal, Bone Meal, Dried Chicken manure, Bat Guano, Alfalfa Meal, Kelp Meal, Potassium Sulfate, Humic Acids, and soil microbes including mycorrhizal fungi.

Recipe 420 is a blend of premium Aged Forest Products, Coir, Sphagnum Peat Moss, Pumice, Earthworm Castings, Feather Meal, Seabird Guano, Crab Meal, Fish Bone Meal, Humic Acid from Leonardite, Gypsum, Oystershell Lime (pH adjuster), Dolomite Lime (pH adjuster), Bat Guano, Kelp Meal and Wetting agent (Yucca Schidigera Saponin) enhanced with Mycorrhizal fungi and beneficial soil bacteria.

E.B. Stone Rose and Flower Food is a blend of select natural ingredients designed to encourage sturdy growth and flowering in roses, perennials and other flowering plants. Contains Blood Meal, Feather Meal, Bone Meal, Dried Chicken Manure, Bat Guano, Alfalfa Meal, Kelp Meal, Potassium Sulfate, Humic Acids, and soil microbes including mycorrhizal fungi.

Long lasting stainless steel mesh is soft to the touch, galvanized, and zinc free to ensure maximum protection and to make it suitable for organic gardens. Just set the basket in the plant hole, partially refill the hole within the basket, set the plant in the center, finish filling in, and you're done!

Mix with native soil or use as mulch throughout the garden. Contains natural firbark, composted chicken manure, earthworm castings, bat guano, and kelp meal.

Granular fertilizer formulated with sulfur, iron, manganese, and zinc to help grass lawns maintain a healthy state and a rich green color.
Use to help produce bigger blooms, especially on roses. Helps plants absorb phosphate fertilizer and increases the plants' natural resistance to diseases.

A decorative Fir bark for use as a ground cover and mulch. Ideal for walkways, gardens and play areas. Helps inhibit weed growth and conserves soil moisture. Protects roots from summer heat or winter cold.

An all-purpose ready-to-use potting soil for all indoor and outdoor container plantings. Contains Fir bark, Canadian peat moss, horticultural sand, mushroom compost (wheat straw, cottonseed hulls, peat moss, cottonseed meal, chicken manure and gypsum).
An all-purpose ready-to-use planting mix. Mix with native soil or use it as it comes from the bag. Contains Fir bark, perlite, mushroom compost, earthworm castings and a wetting agent.
A decorative shredded bark used to enhance the appearance of large or small planted areas. Also used as a mulch to conserve soil moisture and reduce weed growth.

Fortified with eleven essential nutrients, this formula can be used to feed virtually all varieties of indoor and outdoor potted plants for up to six months.

Monterey Sluggo Snail & Slug Killer is the only snail and slug control product not based on metaldehyde. It is an organic bait that contains iron phosphate and is safe to use around pets and wildlife. Uneaten pellets break down into soil as fertilizer. Ideal for use in ornamental and vegetable gardens up to the day of harvest. Meets National Organic Program standards for organic gardening.
A thin tape used to seal pipe threads. This tape is durable, flexible, and fills in the small imperfections in threads to help seal and prevent leaks.

Catch-all burlap tarp is 7 feet by 7 feet. Large enough to rake leaves and other lightweight debris onto the tarp for easy carry-off and removal. Once the tarp is full tie the four corners and easily transport the debris to your recycle bin.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces rounded fruit. Skin is yellow. Flesh is crisp and mildly sweet. Self-fruitful or pollenized by Shinseiki, Bartlett, etc. Estimated chilling requirement 300-400 hours.

A deciduous, self-fruitful fruit tree with a compact, productive canopy suited to home orchards and small landscape spaces. Pale pink spring bloom is followed by soft-shelled nuts with a sweet kernel. It benefits from full sun, excellent drainage, and deep, infrequent irrigation during the growing season.

A deciduous fruit shrub or tree with an arching growth habit. Red-orange blossoms attract hummingbirds. Leaves are glossy and narrow. Pomegranates are large to midsize. Skin is pale pink. Arils are purple and sweet-tart. Harvest in early fall. Self-fruitful. 150 chill hours.

A deciduous fruit shrub or tree with an arching growth habit. Red-orange blossoms attract hummingbirds. Leaves are glossy and narrow. Pomegranates are large to midsize. Skin is bright red. Arils are purple, very juicy, and sweet-tart. The seeds are soft enough to eat. Harvest in fall. Self-fruitful. 150 chill hours. An improved variety.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large apples. Skin blushes red over yellow-green. Flesh is crisp, sweet, and slightly tart. Partly self-fruitful; heavier crop when pollenized by Dorsett Golden or Einshemer. 200 - 300 chill hours.
An erect, thornless, heavy producer of large, sweet and juicy blackberries. More hardy and productive than most thornless varieties. Must be pruned.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic, and silvery underneath. Small, spring flowers yield edible olives used for both oil production and fruit. Highest yield in warm summer climates. Self-fruitful.

A slow-growing evergreen tree that keeps a small stature. Single or multiple gray trunks become gnarled with age. Branches form a rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Small, spring flowers yield edible olives used for commercial oil production with a fruity flavor. High yield. Self-fruitful.
A deciduous fruit tree. Large nectarines have red and white skin. White flesh is rich, soft and sweet with low acidity. Harvest in late summer. 700 - 800 chill hours. Self fruitful.
A deciduous fruit tree. Nectarines have smooth, red skin. When ripe, the white flesh is crunchy, super sweet, and freestone. Harvest in mid summer. 600 - 700 chill hours. Self fruitful.
A deciduous fruit tree. Rosy pink, double blossoms show off in spring. Dark red nectarines have sweet, white flesh. Harvest in early to mid summer. 500 chill hours. Self fruitful.
A deciduous fruit tree. Large peaches have lightly fuzzy, red and cream skin. White flesh is freestone, sweet, juicy and aromatic. Harvest in mid summer. 250 - 300 chill hours. Self fruitful.
A deciduous thornless producer of large, super sweet blackberries. This dwarf cultivar has a rounded growth habit.

A deciduous tree producing popular, high quality pears with thin, yellow skin. Sweet and tender flesh. Self fruitful in most climates but may need pollenizer in cooler coastal areas. Estimated chilling requirement is 500-600 hours.

A deciduous tree that consistently produces heavy crops of medium sized fruits. Skin of the fruit is bright red, the flesh is amber to golden yellow with scarlet streaks. Flavor is delicate, and sweet. Low chill requirement.

Evergreen shrub that produces medium sized, powdery blue berries. Fruits have excellent flavor. Medium green, glossy leaves turn red in fall. Small yet showy white flowers are available during spring, and attract pollinators. Low chill requirement.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces the most popular, large, sweet cherries on the market. Skin is deep blackish red. Flesh is purplish, firm, and juicy. Midseason harvest. Pollenized by Black Tartarian, Van, Rainier, and Lapins. 700 chill hours. Heavy producer at maturity.

Native to tropical Americas, this shrub produces peppers that grow straight up from grey-green leaves on stems lined with silvery fuzz. Peppers emerge medium green and age to their characteristic jet-black, and eventually mature to classic red. Flavor is bitter and spicy.

A deciduous tree with a semi-dwarf growth habit. Adaptable to pruning and training. Leaves are large, deeply lobed, and bright green. Trunk is smooth and gray. Harvest fruit mainly from late summer to mid-fall. Fruit is large to very large. Skin is purple-brown. Flesh is red and super sweet. Self-fruitful. 100 chill hours.

A deciduous tree with a large, spreading habit. Leaves are large, deeply lobed and bright green. Bark is smooth and gray. Harvest first breba crop in early summer and main crop from late summer to late fall. Fruit is large. Skin is purple-black. Flesh is red, rich, and delicious. Self-fruitful. Well-adapted to California. Does well on the coast, though heaviest crops occur inland. 100 chill hours.
An erect, thornless, heavy producer of large, oblong, sweet and juicy blackberries.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces midsize, sweet cherries. Skin is blackish purple. Flesh is firm and juicy. Early season harvest. Pollenizer 'Angela,' 'Republican,' 'Sam,' 'Stella,' or 'Van.' 700 chill hours. 'Black Tartarian' is a good pollenizer for other sweet cherry varieties.

A deciduous fruit tree with showy spring bloom, a 400-hour chill requirement, and richly flavored midsummer fruit. Medium orange apricots have firm, aromatic flesh valued for fresh eating, drying, and preserves. This self-fruitful heritage selection performs best with well-drained soil, regular irrigation, and warm ripening weather.

A vigorous deciduous bush that yields midsize blueberries with light blue skin and good flavor. Resists cracking. Northern highbush hybrid. Mid-season harvest. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other northern highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 800+ chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.0, high humus content.

A vigorous semi-deciduous bush that yields midsize blueberries with light blue skin and mildly sweet flesh. Resistant to cracking. Early to mid-season harvest. Northern highbush hybrid native to the United States. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 800+ chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.
A deciduous tree producing long and narrow fruits with pale brown skin. Firm and juicy flesh. Requires pollenizer such as 'Barlett'. Estimated chilling requirement is 500-600 hours.
A thornless fruit shrub that produces large burgundy-red boysenberries. Fruit has a delightful aroma and a sweet-tart taste. Mid-season harvest.
A deciduous fruit tree that produces medium-sized apples. Skin blushes red over yellow-green. Flesh is crisp, sweet, and tangy. Self-fruitful; pollinates well with Fuji. 700 chill hours.

A deciduous tree with a smaller, multi-trunking growth habit. Very adaptable to training and pruning. Leaves are large, deeply lobed and bright green. Trunk is smooth and gray. Harvest first breba crop in early summer and main crop from late summer to fall. Fruit is large. Skin is purple-brown. Flesh is pink, sweet and rich. Self-fruitful. 100 chill hours.
Maroon-purple skin with red flesh, sweet and mild taste, early to midseason harvest, self-fruitful. pruning

A vigorous deciduous bush that yields midsize blueberries with light blue skin and good flavor. Striking, reddish purple foliage ages to deep, reddish green. Early to mid-season harvest. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other northern highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 800+ chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.5 - 5.5, high humus content.

A semi-deciduous shrub that forms a prickly, vining bramble. Green leaves are serrated, compound and divided into three leaflets. On female plants, spring flowers are followed by edible blackberry fruits that ripen from red to purple-black in summer. Fruit is variable, though blackberries are typically small, fragrant, tasty and sweet-tart. Attracts beneficial insects, pollinators and birds. Native to western North America, including California.

A semi-upright tree that produces large, oval walnuts. Shells are thin. Kernel is light colored. Harvest in fall. 700 - 1000 chill hours. High yield. Partly self-fruitful. Pollenize with 'Franquette' or 'Cisco.' Smaller tree than 'Hartley.' Attracts wildlife.

description: A European white wine grape with medium-sized, rounded green fruit. Harvest August to September. Self-fruitfull.

A deciduous tree with a small, shrubby habit. Adaptable to training and pruning. Leaves are large, deeply lobed, and bright green. Bark is smooth and gray. A bit of an early producer, harvest from mid-summer to late fall. Fruit is midsize. Skin is dark purple over light brown. Flesh is pink, sweet and juicy. Self-fruitful. 100 chill hours. Hardy to USDA zone 5 with winter protection. Often dies back in winter, resprouting in spring.
Sometimes red-blushed greenish-yellow skin with white flesh, late season harvest. Generally self fruitful, but does best with a pollenizer present.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Small, spring flowers yield edible olives. Self-fruitful.

A deciduous tree with a vigorous, spreading growth habit. Leaves are large, deeply lobed and bright green. Trunk is smooth and gray. Harvest first breba crop in early summer and main crop from late summer to fall. Fruit is large. Skin is light greenish-yellow. Flesh is amber, sweet and mild. Self-fruitful. 100 chill hours.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces low-acid, sweet cherries similar to Bing. Skin is coral pink, and flesh is glossy dark red. Fruit is firm and large to very large. Early midseason harvest. Pollenized by Bing and Brooks. 400 - 500 chill hours. Heavy, consistent producer.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces medium to large, sweet cherries. Skin is blackish crimson. Flesh is firm with a delicious, complex flavor. Mid-season harvest. Self-fruitful. 500 chill hours. A natural semi-dwarf.

heightText: Can be pruned to any siuze
widthText: Can be pruned to any width
description: Very sweet and excellent quality, deep red and seedless fruit. Late season harvest in early October, self-fruitful.

Self-fruitful tropical tree that produces large, sweet, reddish-orange mangoes. Long clusters of yellow flowers appear at branch tips during spring and summer months. Produces heavier crops in frost-free areas.

A deciduous tree producing large and rounded fruits with yellow to russeted yellow skin. Firm flesh with good flavor. Requires pollenizer such as 'Barlett'. Estimated chilling requirement is 800 hours.
Greenish-yellow skin mottled with red, creamy red and white flesh, taste test winner, harvest in August, requires pollenizer pruning

A hybrid evergreen perennial that freely suckers to form large clumps of tropical foliage. Bright green, paddle-shaped leaves reach up to 8 feet long. Large summer flowers are creamy-yellow. Ornamental bananas are small, seedy, and not edible. Hardiest of bananas.

A semi-evergreen bush that yields large blueberries with light blue skin and firm, mildly sweet flesh. Early season harvest. Northern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 800+ chill hours. Needs acidic soil and high humus content, pH 4.0 - 5.2.

A dwarf deciduous fruit tree that produces a super abundant harvest of midsize mulberries. Fruit resembles elongated blackberries. Flesh is tasty and a bit tart. Skin is blackish-purple. Fruit is good eaten raw or processed. Self-fertile. Harvest throughout summer. Leaves are large, green, and heart-shaped. Attracts birds.

A tropical perennial banana with a tree-like form. Paddle-shaped leaves are long, broad, and green. Pendent flower clusters are followed by large bunches of sweet, small bananas. A tasty fruit harvest requires sufficient heat, water and fertilization, otherwise grow as an ornamental.

A deciduous fruit tree. Abundant pink blossoms in spring. Large peaches have fuzzy, golden, red-blushed skin and a small pit. Yellow flesh is freestone, and all-purpose with a classic peach flavor. Harvest in mid to late summer. 600 chill hours. Self fruitful. Disease resistant.

Large and heart-shaped fruit with dark red mottled skin and red flesh, mid to late season harvest, requires pollenizer like 'Beauty' or 'Santa Rosa'. May be kept any height with pruning. 500 chill hours or less.
Green skin with yellow to amber flesh, exceptionally sweet and mild flavor, mid to late season harvest, requires pollenizer. pruning
A deciduous fruit shrub with a vigorous, bushy growth habit. Fruits are golden-yellow, large to extra large, and very sweet. Everbearing. Self-pollinating. Attracts birds. Cold hardy.

A deciduous fruit tree. Bright pink blossoms show off in spring. Large nectarines have orange-red skin. Yellow, freestone flesh changes from tangy to sweet as the season progresses. Harvest in mid to late summer. 500 or less chill hours. Self fruitful.

widthText: Can be pruned to any width
description: A European table grape with seedless red fruit eaten fresh or used for raisins. Early to midseason harvest. Self-fruitful.
Reddish-purple skin and red flesh, intense spicy and sweet flavor, midseason harvest, requires pollenizer. May be kept any height with pruning. 400 chill hours.
Greenish-yellow skin and yellow-orange flesh, pleasant and sweet flavor, long midseason harvest, requires pollenizer.
Green and maroon mottled skin and red flesh. Taste test winner. Early season harvest. Requires pollenizer. May be kept any height with pruning.

Soft pink berries ripen on this deciduous, rounded fruit shrub after white spring bells. The sweet fruit is unusual among low-chill types, and another rabbiteye cultivar can raise yields. Use it in edible hedges, raised beds, or containers. Acidic soil, steady moisture, and an organic mulch support strong roots and bright fall color.

A deciduous fruit tree with a natural dwarf habit. Double, red blossoms show off in spring. Small to medium peaches have fuzzy, white, red-blushed skin. White flesh is freestone, light and sweet. Harvest in mid summer. 400 chill hours. Self fruitful.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Small, spring flowers yield edible olives. Most common olives used for Tuscan style oil. Self-fertile, but benefits from other pollenizers. Good cross-pollinator for other varieties.

A deciduous fruit tree that tolerates late frost. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Peaches have fuzzy, yellow, red-blushed skin. Yellow flesh is freestone, juicy and delicious. Harvest in mid summer. 700 chill hours. Self fruitful. Resistant to peach leaf curl.

A deciduous fruit tree with spring flowers, a chill requirement under 500 hours, and crisp, very sweet late-season fruit. Medium to large apples have yellow-green skin with a reddish-orange blush and store well after harvest. This low-chill selection is self-fruitful and works as a pollenizer for other apples. Performs best with well-drained soil and regular irrigation.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large to midsize persimmons. Fruit is round and flattened. Skin is rich orange. Flesh is orange, sweet, and never astringent. Can be eaten right off the tree while firm and crunchy, or picked and stored until a softer texture is reached. Self-fruitful. 200 chill hours. Harvest in September to November. Foliage has beautiful fall color.

A deciduous fruit tree with spring flowers, a chill requirement under 500 hours, and crisp, sweet-tart early-season fruit. Medium apples have reddish-orange skin over yellow and rich dessert quality. This low-chill selection is self-fruitful and works as a pollenizer for other apples. Performs best with well-drained soil and regular irrigation.
A dwarf, self-fruitful tree that produces soft-shelled nuts with sweet and flavorful kernels. Hot, dry summers yield the best nuts.

commonName: Golden Delicious Apple, Yellow Delicious Apple
description: A deciduous fruit tree that produces medium to large apples. Skin is yellow with occasional russeting. Flesh is crisp, aromatic, and sweet. Self-fruitful; a great pollenizer for Red Delicious and other varieties. 700 chill hours.

heightText: Can be pruned to any siuze
widthText: Can be pruned to any width
description: Very large and seeded golden-green fruits. Late season harvest, Self-fruitful.

A deciduous fruit tree with spring flowers, a 400-hour chill requirement, and large late-season green apples. Fruit is crisp, tart, versatile for fresh eating and cooking, and stores well after harvest. This self-fruitful selection has a prolonged bloom period and works as a pollenizer for other apples. Performs best with a long summer, well-drained soil, and regular irrigation.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large persimmons. Fruit is acorn-shaped. Skin is red-orange. Flesh is rich orange, sometimes flecked with brown, and astringent until ripe. When ripe, flesh is very sweet. Pick and store until a softer texture is reached. Freeze and thaw fruit to expedite ripening. Self-fruitful. 200 chill hours. Harvest in November to December. Heavy producer. Foliage has beautiful fall color.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces medium to large apricots. Skin is yellow with a red blush. Flesh is juicy and sweet. Self-fruitful. 700 chill hours. Disease resistant to brown rot and perennial canker. Frost hardy.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces medium-sized apricots. Skin is bright orange with a red blush. Flesh is freestone, sweet, firm, and flavorful. 800 chill hours. Disease resistant to perennial canker and brown rot.

A deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in late spring. Nectarines have dark red-yellow skin. Yellow flesh is sweet, firm and freestone. Harvest in mid summer. 800 or less chill hours. Self fruitful. Cold hardy variety.

A vigorous, deciduous vine that produces edible fruit. Emerging leaves are covered in reddish hairs and mature to dark green with white undersides. Fruit is large and egg-shaped with fuzzy, brown skin and tasty, green flesh. Harvest starts in mid fall. Requires a male pollenizer. Tender to frost. Most common market variety. 600 chill hours.
A deciduous fruit shrub with a vigorous, upright growth habit. Fruits are large, red and sweet. Everbearing. Self-pollinating. Attracts birds.

A dwarf deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Peaches have fuzzy, golden, red-blushed skin. Yellow flesh is freestone, sweet, and rich in flavor. Harvest in early to mid summer. 400 chill hours. Partly self fruitful.

A deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Nectarines have red-orange and yellow skin. Yellow flesh is very sweet, subacid and good when picked before peak ripeness. Harvest in early to mid summer. 500 chill hours. Self fruitful.

An ornamental Mediterranean plant that produces large, rounded, edible artichokes. Foliage is broad, arching and silver-green. Purple, thistle-like flowers develop from unharvested fruits and attract bees. This hybrid selection is improved to have a more consistent harvest and less spines.

A vigorous, deciduous fruit vine climbs by tendrils and quickly covers a strong arbor or wire system. Early clusters of small, seedless green grapes have sweet flesh and work fresh or dried. Leaves turn yellow in fall. Full sun, airflow, regular water, and annual pruning support clean fruit; fallen grapes can stain paved areas.
Large prune with purple skin and yellow flesh, freestone and with rich and sweet flavor, late midseason harvest, self-fruitful.

A vigorous semi-evergreen bush that yields large to midsize blueberries with blue skin and very sweet flesh. Early season harvest. Southern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 500 chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.

A deciduous tree with a vigorous, open habit. Adaptable to pruning and training. Leaves are large, deeply lobed and bright green. Trunk is smooth and gray. Harvest breba crop in late spring and the main crop from late summer into fall. Fruit is large. Skin is light greenish-yellow. Flesh is amber, super sweet, and syrupy. Self-fruitful. 100 chill hours. Crops need hot climate to ripen.
A deciduous fruit tree that produces large apricots. Skin is yellow-orange with a red blush. Flesh has a mild, subacid flavor. 400 chill hours.

A twining deciduous vine that produces edible fruit by a combination of a fruiting female vine and male pollinator in one plant. Foliage is smooth and green. White flowers appear in summer before the fruit sets in fall. Fruit is small with smooth green skin and tasty, green flesh.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is large, narrowly elliptic, and silvery underneath. Small, spring flowers yield edible olives. Similar to 'Arbequina' with heavier crops of smaller olives. Self fertile, though best with a pollenizer nearby. Good pollenizer for other varieties.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large, sweet cherries. Skin is bright, rich red. Flesh is purple-red and firm. Early to midseason harvest, a few days after 'Bing.' Self-fruitful. 400 chill hours. 'Lapins' is a good pollenizer for other sweet varieties.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a semi-arching crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Spring flowers yield edible olives that produce oil with distinctive flavor. Requires a pollenizer such as 'Frantoio' or 'Maurino'.

A deciduous tree with spiny, twisting branches. Reddish-brown fruits are rounded, date-like, and contain pits. Self-fruitful, but sets fruit best when J. 'Lang' is nearby as a pollenizer. Harvest in early fall. Leaves are glossy, green, and egg-shaped.

An evergreen shrub or tree with a rounded or vase-shaped crown. Lightly fragrant, white flower clusters are followed by edible fruits with orange skin, orange or white flesh, and large seeds. Fruit flavor varies between sweet, acidic, and subacid. Eat fresh or in preserves. Harvest in spring. Glossy, deep green leaves are toothed, elliptic to lance-shaped and leathery. Some leaves emerge red.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a spreading crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Small, spring flowers yield edible olives shaped like tiny apples. Excellent fruit quality with an easily removed pit. High yield. Good for oil production and pickling.
Deciduous tree that produces large, reddish purple fruits. Flesh is deep crimson red in color, and sweet. Midseason harvest. Good for fresh consumption or used in cooking.

A deciduous fruit shrub with a vigorous, bushy growth habit. Fruits are large, red and very flavorful. Harvest in summer. Self-pollinating. Attracts birds. A popular cultivar for the Pacific Northwest.

heightText: Can be pruned to any siuze
widthText: Can be pruned to any width
description: A European red wine grape with purple-black fruit and thin skins. Harvest September to October. Self-fruitfull.
An evergreen tree producing rounded to pear-shaped, tasty fruit best eaten fresh or used in jellies, purees, or juices. Self-fruitful.
A deciduous fruit tree. Large freestone peaches have lightly fuzzy, red and cream skin. Yellow flesh is sweet and juicy. Harvest in mid summer. 250 chill hours. Self fruitful.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a tall, rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Small, spring flowers yield edible, commercial-grade olives. Good for oil production, and both green and black pickling. Partially self-fertile.

A vigorous semi-evergreen bush that yields large to midsize blueberries with blue skin and delicious, sweet flesh. Early season harvest. Southern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 300 chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.

A deciduous fruit tree with spring flowers, a 600-hour chill requirement, and large late-season fruit. Golden orange apricots have rich, sweet, aromatic flesh suited to fresh use, canning, drying, and preserves. This self-fruitful heirloom selection performs best with well-drained soil, regular irrigation, and warm summer ripening conditions.

A deciduous fruit tree with spring bloom, a productive rounded canopy, and edible fall harvest. Fruit quality and harvest season vary by grafted variety, making it useful for orchard, espalier, and edible landscape designs. It benefits from full sun, fertile well-drained soil, winter chill, and compatible bloom-time pollenizers. Multi-season harvest. Self-fruitful. Please inquire with our sales department about the specific varieties, each tree is different

A vigorous, semi-evergreen vine with showy and intricate, white and purple flowers with wavy filaments. Yellow-green leaves are divided into three lobes. Large and fragrant, purple-skinned rounded fruits ripen in the summer and fall.
A thornless, erect producer of very large, sweet and juicy blackberries.

A dwarf deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Large nectarines have dark red-orange skin. Yellow flesh is sweet, flavorful and freestone. Harvest in early summer. 400 or less chill hours. Self fruitful.

A deciduous fruit tree. Pink, double blossoms show off in spring. Midsize nectarines have smooth, red skin. Yellow flesh is freestone and very rich in flavor. Harvest in mid summer. Typically high yield. 300 chill hours. Self fruitful.

commonName: Northern California Black Walnut, Hinds' Black Walnut
botanicalName: Juglans californica var. hindsii, Juglans hindsii
description: A deciduous tree that produces rounded walnuts. Shells are thick. Meat is rich in flavor. Foliage is divided into long, feather-like leaflets. Native to parts of California, typically found near streams. Drought tolerant. Provides food and habitat for wildlife. Resistant to oak root fungus. Commonly used as rootstock for commercial walnut orchards.

A vigorous, deciduous bush that yields midsize blueberries with blue skin and firm, sweet flesh. Early season harvest. Half-high hybrid. Requires a pollenizer. Interplant with other hybrids. Estimated 800+ chill hours. Cold hardy. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.

A deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Peaches have fuzzy, yellow, red-blushed skin. Yellow flesh is freestone, firm and highly rated flavor. Harvest in late summer. 750 chill hours. Self-fruitful. Vigorous, high-yield tree with resistance to peach leaf curl.

A deciduous bush that yields large blueberries with dark blue skin and sweet, juicy flesh. Early season harvest. Southern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 600 chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large mulberries. Fruit resembles very elongated blackberries. Flesh is succulent, quite firm, sweet-tart, and flavorful. Skin is ruby red to black. Fruit is good eaten raw or processed. Self-fertile. Harvest throughout summer. Leaves are large, green, and heart-shaped. Disease-resistant. Attracts birds.

A deciduous fruit shrub or tree with an arching growth habit. Red-orange blossoms attract hummingbirds. Leaves are glossy and ornamental. Pomegranates are large. Skin is bright red. Arils are pink, very juicy, balanced sweet-tart, and very flavorful. Harvest in fall. Self-fruitful. 100 - 200 chill hours.
A vigorous, semi-evergreen vine with showy and intricate, white and purple flowers. Yellow-green leaves are divided into three lobes. Edible, rounded fruits ripen in the summer and fall.

A small, semi-upright, deciduous tree that produces large, oval walnuts. Kernel is known for having good flavor. Harvest in fall. 400 chill hours. Fair yield. Self-fruitful. Makes a good pollenizer. Attracts wildlife.

Self-fruitful tropical tree that produces large, sweet, reddish-orange mangoes. Long clusters of yellow flowers appear at branch tips during spring and summer months. Produces heavier crops in frost-free areas.

A deciduous tree with a spreading growth habit. Adaptable to training and pruning. Leaves are large, deeply lobed and bright green. Trunk is smooth and gray. Harvest main crop from late summer to mid-fall. Fruit is midsize. Skin is pale golden-green. Flesh is dark amber and honey-sweet. Best in warm climates. Needs good southern exposure in coastal climate for fruit yield. Self-fruitful. 100 - 200 chill hours.

A deciduous fruit tree with spring flowers, a 300 to 400-hour chill requirement, and very crisp late-season fruit. Apples have reddish-pink skin over green, sweet-tart flavor, white flesh that resists browning, and excellent storage quality. This hot-climate selection is self-fruitful in many western climates. Performs best with well-drained soil and regular irrigation.

A deciduous bush that yields midsize blueberries with bright pink skin and super sweet, juicy flesh. Rabbit eye hybrid. Mid to late season harvest. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 300 chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.

Early pink blossoms cover this deciduous, rounded fruit tree before green leaves unfold. Medium apples ripen in late summer with pale skin and vivid pink, tart flesh. A midseason pollenizer improves crops. Use it as an edible accent or small orchard tree. Full sun, winter chill, and deep, regular watering support fruit quality.

A dwarf deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Peaches have fuzzy, golden, reddish-orange blushed skin. Yellow flesh is freestone, sweet, and rich in flavor. Harvest in early to mid summer. 400 chill hours or less. Self fruitful.

A deciduous shrub with a vigorous, bushy habit. Green leaves are rounded and lobed. Nearly thornless variety. Harvest the edible, greenish-pink to purple fruits in mid-summer. Fruit is very flavorful, often used in baking and preserves. Self-pollinating.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large, sweet cherries. Skin is blushing pink over yellow. Flesh is juicy and super sweet. Pollenizer required for fruit harvest. Pollenized by 'Bing,' 'Black Tartarian,' 'Van,' 'Lambert,' and 'Lapins.' Midseason harvest. 700 chill hours. Cold hardy. 'Rainier' has notably gorgeous, long-lasting spring blossoms and colorful fall foliage.
A dwarf deciduous fruiting shrub with a rounded, compact growth habit. Canes are thornless. Fruits are large, dark red and sweet. Harvest in mid-summer. Self-pollinating. Attracts birds.

A deciduous fruit tree. Pink, double blossoms show off in spring. Peaches have fuzzy, yellow, red-blushed skin. Yellow flesh is freestone, juicy and rich. Harvest in mid summer. 250 chill hours. Self-fruitful. Popular in Southern California and Texas.
