A deciduous fruit tree that produces large apples. Skin is classic red, sometimes striped. Flesh is crisp and sweet. Self-fruitful; good pollenizer for other varieties. Cross-pollinates well with Granny Smith, Golden Delicious, Fuji, or Gala. 700 chill hours.

A deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Peaches have slightly fuzzy, yellow, red-blushed skin. Yellow flesh is freestone, firm and sweet. High yield harvest in mid summer. 800 chill hours. Self-fruitful. Resistant to leaf spot.

A deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Large peaches have fuzzy, yellow, red-blushed skin. Yellow flesh is freestone, rich and sweet. Harvest in late summer. 800 chill hours. Self-fruitful.
Firm fruit with excellent, sweet flavor. Early season harvest, requires pollenizer.

A deciduous, upright fruit tree with a rounded to spreading canopy and productive garden-scale habit. White spring flowers are followed by red-purple plums with amber flesh that ripen midseason. Self-fruitful, with heavier crops when planted near another Japanese plum; best fruit quality develops with good drainage and adequate winter chill.
A deciduous tree with a weeping habit, that produces dark purple fruits with mottled skin, and amber flesh. Early season harvest, self-fruitful.
Mottled dull red skin and dark red flesh, mild and sweet flavor with a small pit, midseason harvest, requires pollenizer. pruning

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large mulberries. Fruit resembles plump, elongated blackberries. Flesh is sweet-tart and flavorful. Skin is black. Fruit is good eaten raw or processed. Self-fertile. Early harvest from late spring throughout summer. Leaves are extra large, green, and heart-shaped. Pest and disease-resistant. Attracts birds.

A vigorous semi-evergreen bush that yields midsize blueberries with dark blue skin and tasty flesh. Early season harvest. Southern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 200 chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.
A deciduous fruit tree that produces medium to large sized, round fruit. Skin is bright yellow. Flesh is crisp, sweet, and juicy. Self-fruitful. Estimated chilling requirement 250 - 300 hours.
A deciduous fruit tree. Pink blossoms show off in spring. Nectarines have red-blushed skin. White flesh is sweet, juicy and freestone. Harvest in mid summer. 250 - 300 chill hours. Self-fruitful.

A vigorous deciduous bush that yields large blueberries with bright blue skin and delicious flesh. Mid season harvest. Southern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 400 chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content, likes sandy soils.

An herbaceous perennial with a mounding habit. Hairy, dark gray-green leaves have a strong aroma and a spicy flavor. Clustered pinkish blossoms bloom in summer. Attracts pollinators. Edible, used as a culinary herb.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large, sweet cherries. Skin is blackish red. Flesh is firm and juicy. Self-fruitful. A good pollenizer for other sweet varieties. Late season harvest. 400 chill hours. Crack resistant.

A semi-dwarf semi-evergreen bush that yields midsize blueberries with light blue skin and tangy-sweet flesh. Mid season harvest. Southern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 150 chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.

A deciduous fruit shrub or tree with an arching growth habit. Red-orange blossoms attract hummingbirds. Leaves are glossy and narrow. Pomegranates are large. Skin is light pinkish red. Arils are pink, very juicy, and very sweet. Harvest in fall. Self-fruitful. 100 chill hours. Good variety for coastal climates.

A deciduous tree with an ornamental quality. Adaptable to pruning and training. Leaves are large, deeply lobed, and bright green. Bark is smooth and gray. Harvest breba crop in early summer and main crop from late summer into fall. Fruit is small to midsize. Skin is striped pale yellow-green and dark green. Flesh is deep red and flavorful. Self-fruitful. 100 chill hours. Fruit needs warm, long summers to ripen.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces large apricots. Skin is golden orange with a red blush. Flesh is firm and pleasantly sweet-tart. Partly self-fruitful; heavier crop when pollenized by other varieties. 500 chill hours.

A dwarf deciduous bush that yields small blueberries with bright blue skin and sweet, firm flesh. Mid season harvest. Northern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 1000 chill hours. Needs acidic soil and high humus content, pH 4.0 - 5.2.

A deciduous bush that yields large blueberries with dark blue skin and sweet, firm flesh. Mid season harvest. Northern highbush hybrid. Self-pollinating. Interplant with other highbush hybrids to encourage a heavier crop. Estimated 800+ chill hours. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 5.2, high humus content.
A semierect, thornless, heavy producer of large, tasty, and sweet-tart blackberries. Ripens earlier than 'Chester'. Does well with trellising in the second year.

Red berries ripen on this deciduous, suckering fruit shrub, with much of the crop carried on first-year canes in late summer and fall. White spring flowers feed bees before the sweet fruit forms. Use it in edible rows or trained screens. Full sun, rich soil, and regular water support yield; thorny canes spread by suckers.
A thornless, trailing producer of large, firm, sweet blackberries. Fruits are prized for small seed size. Mid to late season harvest. Must be pruned.

A deciduous tree producing long-necked fruit with pale green, red-blushed skin. Smooth (not gritty) flesh with superb, sweet buttery flavor. Self fruitful. Estimated chilling requirement is 600 hours. Resistant to fireblight.

A deciduous tree with an open habit. Adaptable to training and pruning. Leaves are large, deeply lobed and bright green. Bark is smooth and gray. Harvest the main crop from late summer through late fall. Fruit is large. Skin is pale green. Flesh is pink, flavorful and delicious. Self-fruitful. 100 chill hours. Does well on the coast, as well as inland.

A deciduous fruit tree that produces medium to large apples. Skin is pale yellow, blushing red. Flesh is crisp and juicy with a subacid flavor. Self-fruitful; great pollenizer for other varieties. 400 chill hours. Adapted to mild coastal climates.

A deciduous fruit shrub or tree with an arching growth habit. Red-orange blossoms attract hummingbirds. Leaves are glossy and narrow. Pomegranates are large. Skin is deep red and shiny. Arils are dark red, juicy, tangy, and flavorful. Seeds are soft enough to eat. Harvest in fall. Self-fruitful. 150 chill hours. Most popular commercial variety.

Glossy leaves cover this evergreen, rounded fruit shrub or small tree. White flowers feed bees, then small yellow fruit ripens with scented, tangy flesh that can be eaten fresh or cooked. Use it in edible hedges, containers, or warm courtyards. Sun, drainage, and steady moisture support crops; dropped fruit and seedlings need routine cleanup.

heightText: Can be pruned to any siuze
widthText: Can be pruned to any width
description: A European red wine grape with juicy and round, purple-black fruit. Used for making fruity red wines. Early to mid-season harvest. Self-fruitfull.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, upright form. Leaves are glossy, small and rounded with finely toothed edges. Foliage emerges reddish-green and matures to dark green. Red stems age to gray-brown.

An evergreen shrub that forms an upright, rounded mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and silver-green. Small, deep violet, star-shaped flowers bloom year round. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

commonName: Anchor Bay California Lilac, Point Reyes Ceanothus
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of deep blue in spring. Foliage is holly-like and dark green. Natural growth habit is low and spreading. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

commonName: Apple Blossom New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, irregular branching habit and dense foliage. Dark green, needle-like leaves sometimes tint pink in cold weather. Dainty, fall-spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and light pink fading to white. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.
An evergreen shrub or small tree with upright branches and leaves. Willow-like foliage is bright green. Small flowers are followed by papery, tan, ribcage-shaped seed capsules.

Native to coasts and mountains of Northern California. Forms a low mat of soft, grey-green leaves that are pointed like arrowheads. Yellow to creamy flowers held in umbels above foliage. Attracts pollinators.

A perennial shrub with a mounding habit. Leaves are wavy-edged, egg-shaped, fuzzy, and gray-green. Globe-shaped clusters of tiny flowers bloom in pale-pink. Beneficial for wildlife, birds, and pollinators, especially butterflies. Native to Southern California.

commonName: Asian Star Jasmine, Yellow Star Jasmine
description: An evergreen groundcover with twining stems. If trained as a vine, it can grow 20 - 30 feet high. Distinctively fragrant flowers are small, white, and pinwheel-shaped. Flowers have yellow centers. Leaves are elliptic, dark green, and are smaller than T. jasminoides.
An evergreen shrub prized for intensely fragrant, loosely double, velvety white flowers. Glossy, bright green, lance-shaped leaves. Hardy to 20 degrees.

A large, evergreen woody shrub with an upright, sculptural habit and smooth red-brown bark. Gray-green leaves frame clusters of pale pink winter flowers that support pollinators, followed by berry-like fruit. Useful as a specimen, screen, or large dry-slope planting. Performs best with excellent drainage and little summer irrigation once established.

A low-growing and spreading evergreen shrub with long leaves cut in a saw-tooth pattern. Flat and broad, unlike the typical needle-like foliage of most Grevilleas. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, deep red flowers.

A large evergreen shrub or tree that forms a dense, rounded screen. Takes well to shearing. Good for hedges or topiaries. Deep green leaves are glossy, oblong, and emerge reddish. Creamy white flowers are followed by red, edible fruit that tastes best when processed, rather than raw.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub or small tree with a twisted trunk and a sprawling crown. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown. Branches sometimes droop to the ground. Gray-green foliage is oval and smooth. In spring, small, single, rose-like flowers bloom in white.
An evergeen shrub with dark green leaves edged in red, arranged in neat, opposing pairs. Spike-like flower clusters in deep lavender-blue. Best grown in cool summer - mild winter climates.

A semi-woody perennial shrub with a bushy growth habit. More compact than the species. Silvery-gray-green foliage is aromatic, egg-shaped, and toothed on the edges. Whorls of small, azure blue flowers bloom in summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
This evergreen shrub is slow growing with an extremely compact form. The glossy green foliage retains its color year round. Used for clipped hedges and topiaries.

A semi-woody evergreen shrub with a vigorous, dense growth habit. Small leaves are oval, dark green, and semi-rough. Chatreuse, bell-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.

An evergreen shrub with a fine, dense texture. Branches are thin and arching. Golden-green leaves are tiny, glossy and egg-shaped. Foliage tints bronze in winter. Creamy white flowers are small, bell-shaped and fragrant. Blooms in summer, followed by purple fruits.

A woody evergreen shrub with a sprawling, rounded growth habit. Leaves are deep green and pinnately divided. Flowers resemble fluffy, red feather dusters with long, silky stamens. Attracts hummingbirds. Native to Baja, California.

An evergreen shrub with a tidy, compact, round form. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with serrated edges. Foliage tints bronze-red in winter. Slightly fragrant masses of deep rose-pink flowers bloom in clusters at branch tips. Blooms in winter, spring and sometimes fall are followed by dark blue fruits. Wind resistant.

A large evergreen shrub with a round, compact form. Broad leaves are dark green. In spring, fragrant, banana-scented flowers bloom from fuzzy buds. Cup-shaped flowers are light yellow and outlined in purple. Non-edible Fruits follow. Attracts birds.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorous mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Bandana series stays compact and has larger flower clusters than the species. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters in a range of colors. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

An evergreen shrub with sturdy, upright stems that can be turned in skewers. Light green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, lilac-blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators. 'Barbeque' is a favored selection for use as a culinary herb.

A dense, fast-growing evergreen shrub with a naturally dense and compact growth habit. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and light green. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

A bold woodland perennial with a clumping, bushy form. Lobed, glossy, deep green leaves can grow up to 2 feet long. Tall flowering spikes carry hooded flowers in white and purple. The most commonly grown Acanthus. Can tolerate full shade.

A low, mounding evergreen shrub with trailing stems that root as they touch the ground. Small, oval, dark green leaves densely cloak the branches. Tiny white flowers are followed by abundant, salmon red cranberry-like fruits. Attracts birds and bees.

A low-maintenance evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display crepe paper petals of bright white with golden stamens. Leaves are narrow, resinous, and bright green. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.

A woody evergreen shrub with a dense, mounding habit. Densely leafed branches form a nearly flat ground cover. Small green leaves are rounded to egg-shaped. Clusters of white and pale pink, drooping, urn-shaped flowers are beneficial to many bird species. The berries are edible. Native to California.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub with an open, multi-branching growth habit. Leaves are gray-green, multi-lobed and maple-like. Large, saucer-shaped, hollyhock-like flowers are pale lavender-pink with dark purple veins and centers. Blooms from midspring to fall. Attracts butterflies.

Smooth red bark and twisting limbs shape this evergreen, upright California native shrub or small tree. Blue-gray leaves frame white to pale pink winter flowers, followed by large red berries that feed wildlife and are edible. It anchors dry screens and habitat slopes. Open soil and summer-dry conditions support long life; berries can drop below.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a dwarf, tidy mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters in a variety of colors. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.
An evergreen shrub with purple stems clothed in blue-green, lustrous and spiny foliage. Pollinator for 'Blue Princess' and other female varieties.
An evergreen shrub that forms a spreading mound of small, narrow, bright silvery-green leaves. Violet-blue, funnel-shaped flowers bloom from spring to winter. Attracts birds and butterflies.

An evergreen shrub that forms an upright, rounded mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and silver-green. Small, violet-blue, star-shaped flowers bloom year round. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.
An evergreen shrub with rough, deeply lobed, gray-green foliage. Large, glossy, light purple flowers resemble hibiscus. Beneficial for pollinators.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of powder blue in spring. Foliage is small, leathery, and dark green. Natural growth habit is upright and adaptable with pruning. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

commonName: Blue Moon Princess Flower, Glory Bush
description: An evergreen shrub with an open-branching, upright growth habit. Light purple flowers are silky, saucer-shaped and display interesting, curved stamens. Blooms from summer into fall. Foliage is lush green, oval and covered in velvet. Leaves have unique venation.

An evergreen shrub with an adaptable, upright growth habit. Light gray-green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, lavender-blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators. 'Blue Spires' is a favored selection for use as a culinary herb. Cold hardy.

An evergreen shrub with a bushy, climbing growth habit. Leaves are narrowly oval, rich green, and glossy. Summer flowers are nodding, bell-shaped, and lavender-blue. Cylindrical, dark blue fruits ripen in fall. With support, it can climb up to 8 feet high. Drought tolerant once established. Native to Australia. Attracts birds and bees.

An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge bronzy red and age to olive green. Bright pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

An evergreen shrub with upright stems and a compact, bushy form. Slender, oval leaves are green with burgundy new growth. Foliage tints purple in winter. Female flowers are made up of burgundy-red bracts that surround light green cones. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

commonName: Blush Pink Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Copper-pink new growth matures to light green, turning vivid pink-red in winter. Non-flowering, compact form of 'Firepower.'
An upright evergreen shrub with dark green, finely divided, needle-like foliage. Brush or spider-like clusters of long and curved, coral red flowers.

commonName: Bonfire Heavenly Bamboo, Bonfire Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Swirling, red-orange new growth matures to deep green, turning vivid purple-red in fall and winter. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, mounding habit. Gray green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
An evergreen shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Deep green leaves are small, oval, and have scalloped edges.

An evergreen shrub with leathery, lustrous, deep green leaves that are similar to Buxus. Fragrant white blooms are followed by fleshy, red, edible fruits that are similar to large cranberries. Compact and thornless.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Leathery, gray-green leaves are spiraled along stems. Flowers are golden orange. Modified styles form a broad, waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub with an upright, multi-branching growth habit. Leaves are gray-green, three-lobed and maple-like. Saucer-shaped, hollyhock-like flowers are rich pink with dark pink veins. Blooms from mid-spring to fall. Attracts butterflies.
A dense, upright evergreen shrub with pointed oval, glossy deep green foliage. Spikes of fragrant white flowers followed by small black fruits. Best used as a clipped hedge or screen.
A low-maintenance, groundcover evergreen shrub with small and narrow, gray-green foliage. Small, vibrant orange, papery blooms similar in appearance to Cistus.

An evergreen shrub with an upright form. Leathery, light green leaves are spiraled along very long stems. Abundant, large flowers are rich red. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers.

commonName: Burgundy Peppermint Tree, Australian Willow Myrtle
description: An evergreen, graceful Australian tree with weeping branchlets and narrow aromatic foliage. Small white spring-to-summer flowers dot the canopy, followed by fine seed capsules. It is useful as a light screen, specimen, or patio tree and thrives in well-drained soil with moderate to low irrigation after establishment.

commonName: Burgundy Queen New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, irregular branching habit and dense foliage. Dark green, needle-like leaves flush burgundy in cold weather. Dainty, fall-spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and deep red. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.
An evergreen shrub with an upright form. Dark green leaves are leathery, oval and serrated on the edges. Fragrant, tiny, white flowers bloom heaviest in spring.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded, multi-branching, upright form. Leaves are leathery, lance-shaped, and dark green. Large, showy flowers are fragrant and white with yellow centers. Attracts pollinators. Blooms in late spring and summer. Native to California. Does well with some shade inland.

commonName: Bush Flame Heart Leaf Flame Pea
description: An Australian evergreen shrub with super vibrant, sweet pea-like flowers in orange and pink from late winter to spring.

A semi-woody perennial shrub with a bushy growth habit. Takes well to shearing. Stems are white. Silvery-gray-green foliage is aromatic, egg-shaped, and toothed on the edges. Whorls of small, blue flowers bloom in summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
A Mediterranean evergreen shrub with silvery green, lance-shaped foliage. Funnel-shaped flowers display fused white petals and yellow centers.
A California native perennial shrub with finely textured, woolly gray-green leaves. Ball-shaped flower clusters in white to pale pink.

commonName: California Glory Hybrid Flannel Bush, Fremontia
description: A fast-growing evergreen shrub or small tree with an upright, spreading habit and bold architectural structure. Velvety, lobed gray-green foliage provides year-round texture, while large cup-shaped yellow flowers with orange-red backs bloom heavily in spring to early summer. Useful as a specimen, informal screen, espalier, or dry slope shrub where full sun, good drainage, and low summer irrigation support best performance. Best sited with room to mature and away from high-contact areas, as the leaf hairs can irritate skin and eyes.

A semi-evergreen tree with a fast growing habit, useful as a screen or hedge. Glossy, dark green leaves are leathery, pointed and oval. Showy clusters of frothy, creamy white flowers are followed by profuse black berries. Flower fragrance is often considered unpleasant. Evergreen in warm winter climates. Native to Japan.
A dense and upright evergreen shrub with dark green, finely textured, needle-like foliage. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, rose red flowers.

commonName: Candy Cane New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, irregular branching habit. Dark green, needle-like leaves are densely set. Dainty, fall-spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and two-toned light and dark pink. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.
An evergreen shrub with arching branches and flat, linear, gray-green leaves. Bristlelike flowers are known for their long, soft pink stamens. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

An evergreen vining shrub with a sprawling growth habit that can climb with provided support. Leaflets are feather-shaped and glossy dark green. Showy trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in clusters of bright orange-red. Blooms from fall through spring. Attracts hummingbirds.

A California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of light blue in spring. Foliage is glossy, oval, 2 inches, and bright green. Natural growth habit is low and creeping. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A very low, evergreen groundcover with dense trailing stems and small glossy green leaves. White to pale pink winter flowers support early pollinators, followed by small red fruit. Excellent for coastal banks, slopes, and weed-suppressing masses. Performs best with good drainage and little summer irrigation once established.

An evergreen, dense shrub or small tree with glossy green leaves and fragrant white spring flowers. Small black fruit feeds birds, while leaves and seeds are poisonous if eaten. Use it for tall screens, clipped hedges, or wind protection. It grows best in well-drained soil and handles heat, salt, and pruning.

commonName: Cavatine Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A dwarf, shade-loving evergreen shrub with a compact, upright habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of white, urn-shaped flowers bloom in early spring. Leaves are dark green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of dark blue in spring. Foliage is small, leathery, and dark green. Natural growth habit is low and spreading. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorously trailing mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are bright yellow. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested. Cold hardy to 0 degrees F.

An evergreen shrub with an upright growth habit and whorled, horizontal foliage. Long, compound leaves are holly-like with spiny edges. Foliage is glossy green. Large spikes of yellow flowers in early winter are followed by blue berries in summer. Attracts birds and bees.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, upright to arching growth habit. Grayish-green, finely textured, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, violet-blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators. 'Chef's Choice' is a favored selection for use as a culinary herb.

A rounded, fast-growing evergreen shrub. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Bright cherry red blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a tall, bushy form. Slender, oval leaves are green with bright red new growth. Flowers are made up of pale pink and light yellow bracts that surround large, yellow cones. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

A large evergreen shrub or small tree with a multi-trunking growth habit. Cinnamon-brown bark exfoliates to reveal white underneath. Aromatic, dark green leaves are rounded with acutely pointed tips. Small, white flowers are saucer-shaped with showy brush-like stamens. Blooms in summer. Blue-black fruits follow.

A compact evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves are olive green. White flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

An evergreen shrub with a tidy, round form. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with serrated edges. New foliage emerges copper-red. Lightly fragrant masses of white flowers bloom from pink buds in clusters at branch tips. Blooms in spring are followed by dark blue fruits.

commonName: Cliff Schmidt California Tree Lilac, Feltleaf Ceanothus
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of powder blue in spring. Foliage is glossy and dark green with white undersides on sturdy, thick stems. Natural growth habit is upright and adaptable with pruning. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

An evergreen shrub that forms an upright, rounded, mound. Leaves are linear, gray-green, and similar in appearance to rosemary. Small, white, star-shaped flowers bloom all year in mild climates. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.
A low and spreading evergreen shrub with woolly and narrow, gray-green leaves densely set along the branches. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, pink and cream flowers. Frost tolerant.

An evergreen, upright Australian shrub with exceptionally fine, silky silver-green foliage and a soft, cloud-like texture. Small red tubular flowers provide understated pollinator interest. It is valuable for coastal and Mediterranean plantings and thrives in sharply drained, low-phosphorus soil with light shearing.

An evergreen, upright Australian shrub with exceptionally fine, silky silver-green foliage and a soft, cloud-like texture. Small red tubular flowers provide understated pollinator interest. It is valuable for coastal and Mediterranean plantings and thrives in sharply drained, low-phosphorus soil with light shearing.
An evergeen shrub with red stems clothed in dark green leaves arranged in neat, opposing pairs. Spike-like flower clusters in purple-pink. Best grown in cool summer - mild winter climates.

A semi-woody evergreen shrub with a dense, upright growth habit. Rich green leaves are leathery, more narrow than the genus, and point upward. Yellowish, bell-shaped flowers bloom attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.

Collingwood Ingram Rosemary An evergreen shrub with a semi-upright, semi-trailing habit. Grayish dark green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible, though the flavor is reported to be unpleasant. Tiny, dark blue flowers dot the foliage in winter and spring. Attracts bees and other pollinators. Not the best selection for use as a culinary herb.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

A slow-growing evergreen shrub with a round form. Green, oval to lance-shaped leaves are aromatic when crushed. Flowers are fragrant, white and saucer-shaped with many fluffy, spiky stamens. Summer blooms are followed by small, blue-black berries. Leaves, flowers, and berries are edible.

A semi-woody perennial shrub with a dense, rounded growth habit. More compact than the species. Silvery-gray-green foliage is aromatic, egg-shaped, and toothed on the edges. Whorls of small, deep blue flowers bloom in summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
A dense and upright evergreen shrub with pointed oval, glossy deep green foliage. Spikes of fragrant white flowers followed by small black fruits. Best used as a clipped hedge or screen.

A semi-woody perennial shrub with a dense, upright growth habit that slowly spreads. Dark green foliage is aromatic, egg-shaped, and toothed on the edges. Whorls of small, mauve and pink flowers bloom in summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

A dwarf evergreen shrub that forms a rounded, uniform hedge. Takes well to shearing. Leaves are linear to oval, leathery, and bright green. Clusters of small, reddish-pink flowers bloom in spring and fall. Attracts pollinators.

A Mediterranean native perennial shrub with upright stems clothed in woolly and wrinkled, lance-shaped, gray-green foliage. The upper half of stems carry whorls of deep yellow, two-lipped, hooded flowers.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Compound leaves are glossy and holly-like with spiny edges. Foliage emerges bronze-red, matures to dark green and turns purple-red in winter. Clusters of yellow flowers in spring are followed by edible, blue-black berries in fall. Berries are tasty in jams. Plant parts have medicinal uses. Attracts birds and bees. Native to the Pacific Northwest, including northern California.
An evergreen shrub with a versatile branching habit. Foliage emerges bronze and matures to bright green. Leaves are pointed, oval and glossy. Does well as a hedge.

Compact and evergreen, this dense shrub or small tree carries glossy green leaves and peeling cinnamon-brown bark. White, urn-shaped flowers open from fall into winter, followed by round red fruit that is edible and feeds birds. The species is native to Mediterranean woodlands and southwestern Ireland. Use for hedges, screens, containers, or small-space specimens.

commonName: Compact Texas Ranger, Texas Sage, Ceniuzo, Barometer Bush
description: A semi-evergreen shrub with a rounded form, smaller than the species. Foliage is small and silver-gray. Rosy-pink flowers cover the branches in abundance. From summer into fall, flowers bloom in cycles after a spike in humidity, such as a rain. Thrives in heat. Tolerates drought, as well as regular water. Attracts pollinators and birds. Native to Texas and Mexico.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters, which form a sea of dark blue in spring. Foliage is leathery, 1-inch long, and dark green. Natural growth habit is upright and adaptable with pruning. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorously spreading mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are multicolored yellow, pink and purple. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

An evergreen shrub with small and glossy oval leaves in deep green edged in creamy white variegation. Leaves are tinged with bronze to maroon in cooler weather. Flared, bell-shaped flowers in pale pink. Semi-evergreen in colder climates.

From the Sunset Western Garden Collection, this California native evergreen shrub exhibits an upright, compact growth habit and variegated green and white foliage. Light blue blossoms attract pollinators in spring. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes.

A low evergreen shrub with trailing stems that root as they touch the ground. Bright glossy green leaves densely cloak the branches. Tiny white flowers are followed by abundant coral-red berries. Attracts birds and bees.

A spreading, evergreen shrub that is native to coastal Australia. Commonly called 'Flamebush' for its scallop-edged, wedge-shaped leaves that emerge in blazing bright pink. Foliage grows out to a cool silver-green. Insignificant flowers are dull red and jug-shaped. Do not fertilize with phosphorus.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a low, compact mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Variegated light yellow and green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are multicolored red, orange and yellow. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.
An evergreen shrub with an upright growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, obovate leaves are multi-colored lime green, dull burgundy, and bright copper red.
A prostrate evergreen shrub with dense, cascading foliage. Leaves are feathery, needle-like and likened to pine needles. Functions as a weed-suppressing groundcover. Native to Australia.

commonName: Cousin Itt Bower Wattle, River Wattle
description: An evergreen, cascading shrub with dense, fine-textured foliage that forms a soft mound. The narrow green leaves create a flowing effect for banks, retaining walls, and large containers, with small pale yellow spring flowers. It thrives in well-drained soil and is effective as a low-water groundcover.

An evergreen, upright California native shrub selected for a denser, more garden-ready habit than the straight species. Glossy green foliage and small cream flowers support habitat plantings, coastal sites, and informal screening. It is well suited to slopes and restoration work where drainage is good and summer water is limited.

An evergreen, upright California native shrub selected for a denser, more garden-ready habit than the straight species. Glossy green foliage and small cream flowers support habitat plantings, coastal sites, and informal screening. It is well suited to slopes and restoration work where drainage is good and summer water is limited.

An evergreen, upright California native shrub selected for a denser, more garden-ready habit than the straight species. Glossy green foliage and small cream flowers support habitat plantings, coastal sites, and informal screening. It is well suited to slopes and restoration work where drainage is good and summer water is limited.

commonName: Cream de Mint Japanese Mock Orange
description: A dense evergreen shrub. Leaves are narrow, rounded, leathery, and green with creamy white margins. Fragrant clusters of small white flowers smell of orange blossoms.

commonName: Creeping Mountain Lilac, Joyce Coulter California Lilac
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of lavender blue in spring. Foliage is leathery, 1 inch, and medium green. Natural growth habit is fast, low, and arching. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

An evergreen shrub with a low, spreading growth habit. Compound leaves are glossy and holly-like with spiny edges. Dark blue-green foliage tints bronze-purple in winter. Spikes of yellow flowers in spring are followed by edible, blue-black berries in late summer. Berries are tasty in jams. Plant parts have medicinal uses. Attracts birds and bees. Native to the Pacific Northwest, including California.

An evergreen shrub with a bushy, rounded growth habit. Leaflets are feather-shaped and dark green. Showy trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in clusters of red. In summer, flowers may turn pink. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts hummingbirds.

commonName: Crimson Glory New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, irregular branching habit. Bronzy green, needle-like leaves are densely set. Dainty, fall-spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and crimson-red. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.

A low-maintenance evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display bright white, burgundy-spotted, crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are narrow, resinous, and dark green. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.

An evergreen shrub with upright stems and a rounded, bushy form. Finely textured leaves are light gray green and slightly hairy. This is a female selection with flowers composed of ruby-pink cones and pink-tinged bracts. Flowers bloom at branch tips in spring. Best color in full sun. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorously spreading mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are bicolored golden-orange and red. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.
A fast-growing evergreen shrub or small tree with spreading branches. Linear, olive-green foliage flushes dark burgundy, especially in full sun. Small, white, single flowers bloom in summer.

commonName: Dark Star California Lilac, Small Leaf California Lilac
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of cobalt-blue in spring. Foliage is rough-textured, tiny, and dark green. Natural growth habit is compact and vase-shaped. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.
A spiny evergreen shrub with small, leathery, holly-like leaves. Abundant orange-yellow flowers are followed by dark blue berry-like fruits that attract birds.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, mounding growth habit. Dark green foliage tinges burgundy in fall. Leaves are glossy, elliptical in shape, and have distinctively deep veins. Red twigs are ornamental. Showy berries ripen to metallic-blue in fall and attract birds. In spring, pink buds bloom into rounded clusters of small, white flowers.

commonName: Davis Gold Toyon, Christmas Berry, California Holly
description: A California native evergreen shrub or small tree with dark green and leathery toothed leaves. Clusters of white flowers followed by small golden-yellow berries in the fall and winter.
An dense and rounded evergreen shrub with soft and lance-shaped, olive green foliage. Clusters of long and tubular, bright red flowers.

commonName: Dorothy Wycoff Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with a compact, upright habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of pale pink, urn-shaped flowers bloom from dark red buds in early spring. New foliage emerges bronze-red at branch tips, maturing to dark green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.

A large, evergreen shrub or small tree with an upright branching habit and smooth dark red bark. Glossy green leaves and white winter flowers create strong specimen value, followed by red fruit for wildlife. Useful as a native focal point or informal screen. Performs best with good drainage and deep, infrequent irrigation.
An evergreen shrub with finely divided, thread-like foliage. In the late winter and spring, spiky and rounded flower heads appear in purple-pink.

A semi-woody evergreen shrub with a dense, low growth habit. Small, oval leaves are slightly downy and gray-green. Drooping, tubular, carmine pink flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.
An evergreen shrub with deep green, lustrous and nearly spineless new foliage. Produces abundant bright red berries without male pollenizer.

An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Copper-pink new growth matures to green, turning vivid purple-red in fall and winter. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries.

commonName: Dwarf Indian Hawthorn, Dwarf Yedda Hawthorn
description: An evergreen shrub with a compact, round form. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with wavy edges. New foliage emerges copper-red. Lightly fragrant masses of white flowers bloom in clusters at branch tips. Blooms in spring are followed by dark blue fruits.
An evergreen shrub. Leaves are rounded, hairy, and gray-green. New growth emerges in a brighter yellow-green. Fragrant maroon flowers bloom in the spring.
Compact evergreen shrub with interesting flowerheads made up of colorful pink to red bracts, reaching up to 1 foot across. Leathery dark green leaves.
An evergreen shrub with a low, spreading growth habit. Leaves are small, oval, and medium green. Foliage is less glossy than the genus. Branches are beige-brown.

A slow-growing evergreen shrub with a dwarf, round form. Green, oval to lance-shaped leaves are aromatic when crushed. Flowers are fragrant, white and saucer-shaped with many fluffy, spiky stamens. Summer blooms are followed by small, blue-black berries. Leaves, flowers, and berries are edible.

botanicalName: Coleonema pulchrum 'Compact Form', C. pulchellum, Diosma pulchra
description: An airy, pleasantly fragrant evergreen shrub. Branches are flimsy and clothed in fine, needle-like leaves. Dainty pinkish flowers dot the bright green foliage. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
A short and spreading evergreen shrub with bright green, lance-shaped foliage. Brush-like clusters of unusual light pink flowers.
A mounding and compact evergreen shrub with soft, needle-like foliage resembling rosemary. Brush-like clusters of long and curved flowers in pink and cream. Hardy to 18-20 degrees.

commonName: Dwarf Purple Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Purple-green leaves turn vivid purple-red in fall and winter. Rarely flowers. Dwarf, upright form.

A slow-growing evergreen shrub with a dwarf, round form. Oval to lance-shaped leaves are green with variegated white margins. Foliage is aromatic when crushed. Flowers are fragrant, white and saucer-shaped with many fluffy, spiky stamens. Summer blooms are followed by small, blue-black berries. Leaves, flowers, and berries are edible.

A compact evergreen shrub or small tree with a multi-branching growth habit and a bushy crown of foliage. Green and cream variegated, long-stemmed leaves are divided into long, feathery, wavy-edged leaflets. Flowers bloom in late summer.
An evergreen shrub with dark green, small and narrow, shallowly toothed foliage. Red berries are often hidden among the leaves.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Leathery, gray-green leaves are spiraled along stems. Flowers are rich coral-orange. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Early blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers.

An upright, evergreen shrub grown for its bold, long-lasting cones and colorful bracts. It brings strong structural interest to Mediterranean and low-water landscapes. Narrow deep burgundy to near-black foliage is tipped with showy bracts that deepen to rich red tones in the cooler months, creating high seasonal contrast. Excellent for cut flower production and mass planting, this cultivar performs best in full sun with sharply drained, low-nutrient soils and benefits from infrequent, deep irrigation once established. Well-suited to coastal conditions and mild frost areas, it offers reliable color with minimal maintenance. Sensitive to phosphorus in soil and fertilizer.

A Mediterranean native perennial shrub with upright stems clothed in soft and woolly, broadly lance-shaped, gray-green foliage. The upper half of stems carry whorls of large and bright yellow, two-lipped, hooded flowers.

A semi-evergreen, arching shrub with a rounded, informal habit for borders, low screens, and foundation plantings. Glossy green foliage backs clusters of pink to lilac-pink, lightly fragrant summer-to-fall flowers. It performs well in heat and benefits from well-drained soil and periodic renewal pruning.
A fast-growing, bushy evergreen shrub with widely lobed, bright green leaves. Small, funnel-shaped, 1" wide flowers bloom in magenta pink with darker pink venation and dark eyes.
A compact evergreen shrub with a mounded form. Silvery-green leaves are small, glossy, oval, and pointed. Stems are dark brown. Dense, dwarf form reaches only 2 feet high and wide.

An evergreen shrub with leathery, lance-shaped, dark green leaves and fragrant, white flowers with yellow centers. Native to California. Flowers of 'Elizabeth' are smaller than the species. Attracts pollinators.

An evergreen shrub with a sprawling, mounding growth habit. Variegated leaves are small, oval, and have scalloped edges. Coloration is dark green with thick golden-yellow margins. In cooler weather, leaves blush rosy-pink. Spreads by runners.

A low, evergreen groundcover with dense, spreading stems and small glossy green leaves. Pale pink to white winter flowers support early pollinators, followed by red berry-like fruit. Useful for slopes, parkways, and mass plantings under open canopies. Performs best with good drainage and little summer irrigation once established.

An evergreen shrub with a sprawling, mounding growth habit. Variegated leaves are small, oval, and have scalloped edges. Coloration is dark green with cream margins. In cool weather, some leaves blush rosy-pink.

commonName: Emerald Snow Dwarf Chinese Fringe Flower
description: A compact evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge bright green and age to olive green. Abundant masses of white flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in summer and fall with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

commonName: Emerald Wave Sweet Bay, Grecian Laurel
description: An upright, compact evergreen shrub or small tree with bright green, elliptical, aromatic foliage used as a flavorful seasoning. Small greenish yellow flowers in spring are followed by black berries. Does well in a container.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of dark violet blue in spring. Foliage is holly-like and dark green. Natural growth habit is small, low, and spreading. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.
An evergreen shrub with broad and leathery, rich green leaves. Small spikes of fragrant, creamy-white flower followed by small black fruits. Popular choice for hedges or screens.

A semi-evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Leaves are small, oblong, and dark gray-green. Tight clusters of blushing, highly fragrant flowers bloom heaviest in early spring. Does best in fast draining soils. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can tolerate full shade.

A versatile evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded growth habit. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with rolled under margins. Small flowers are followed by large berries that ripen to red-black by autumn. Attracts pollinators, birds and other wildlife. California native.
An evergreen shrub with an upright, rounded growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Leaves are small, oval, and variegated green and gold with rusty red fall color.

A compact evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves are dark burgundy year round. Deep red flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.
An evergreen shrub prized for intensely fragrant, rose-like, velvety white flowers. Glossy, bright green, lance-shaped leaves. Hardy to 20 degrees. Reliable bloomer valued for long flowering season.

An evergreen shrub that forms a dense thicket. Foliage emerges reddish-bronze and matures to lustrous dark green. Leaves are simple, oval, and toothed on the edges. Spring flowers are pinkish white, urn-shaped, and pendent. Edible fruits are dark purple, tasty, and can be eaten raw, dried, or in place of blueberries in a recipe. Fruit ripens in early fall. Attracts pollinators, birds, and other wildlife. Native to the foggy Pacific Coast, including California. Needs acidic soil, pH 4.0 - 6.0.
A California native evergreen shrub grown for pendulous greenish-white catkins up to 10 inches long. Dense foliage made up of gray-green, wavy-edged leaves.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, mounding form. Oval leaves are glossy and rich green. Fragrant, creamy white flowers bloom in dome-shaped clusters throughout spring. Bright red berries form on female plants when a male pollenizer is nearby.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in bright red fading to reddish-brown. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in creamy white.
An evergreen shrub with a rounded growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, obovate leaves are variegated green, pink, and cream with fiery red fall and winter color.

A compact evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge ruby-red to purple and age to red-tinged green. Deep pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

commonName: Fire Power Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Light green new growth matures to reddish-green, turning vivid scarlet in fall and winter. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries. Low, compact form.
An evergreen shrub with small and narrow leaves. Red, snapdragon-like, tubular flowers with flared lips. More compact version than species.
An evergreen shrub prized for intensely fragrant, large and double, rose-like and spiraled, velvety white flowers. Glossy, bright green, lance-shaped leaves. Hardy to 20 degrees.

commonName: Flaming Silver Lily of the Valley
description: An elegant evergreen shrub with narrowly oval, glossy green foliage edged with white. New foliage emerges brilliant red with pink margins. Abundant clusters of pendulous, urn-shaped flowers in white.

An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Burgundy-red new growth matures to blue-green, turning red in fall and winter. Maintains red color for most of the year. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries. Dwarf, mounding form.

commonName: Forest Flame Lily of the Valley
description: A handsome evergreen shrub with narrowly oval leaves that emerge red, fade to creamy pink, and then mature to dark green. String-like clusters of large and pendulous, urn-shaped flowers in white.

An evergreen shrub that forms a ground cover. Spreads by rhizomes. Glossy green leaves are slender, pointed and alternating. In mid-winter and early spring, abundant white flowers are intensely fragrant. Glossy dark blue fruit develops in early summer. Tolerates deep, dry shade.

An evergreen shrub that forms a rounded mound. Glossy dark green leaves are oval, pointed and alternating. In mid-winter and early spring, small white flowers are intensely fragrant. Glossy dark red fruit develops in early summer. Tolerates deep, dry shade.

An evergreen shrub that forms a ground cover. Spreads by rhizomes. Glossy green leaves are slender, pointed and alternating. In mid-winter and early spring, abundant white flowers are intensely fragrant. Glossy dark blue fruit develops in early summer. Tolerates deep, dry shade.
An evergreen shrub prized for intensely fragrant, velvety white flowers. Glossy, bright green, lance-shaped leaves. Flower buds are undamaged by late spring frosts.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of deep blue and shimmering white in spring. Foliage is leathery, half inch, and dark green. Natural growth habit is dense, upright, and adaptable to pruning. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A thorny evergreen shrub that is well-suited for a low-maintenance screen or hedge. Leaves are oval, wavy-edged, and olive-green with rusty dots. New growth is silvery. Tiny, fragrant winter flowers are followed by silvery red fruit. Attracts birds.

A semi-woody perennial shrub that forms low, slowly spreading patches. Silvery-gray-green foliage is strongly aromatic and narrow. Whorls of small, lavender-purple flowers bloom in summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

commonName: Gaiety Girl New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: A slow-growing evergreen shrub with a compact, oval form. Reddish green, needle-like leaves are densely set. Dainty, fall-spring flowers are saucer-shaped, semi-double, and deep pink Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a dense, bushy form. Fine, linear leaves are gray-green. Male plants produce bright yellow pom-pom flowerheads. Female plants produce cones in soft gray-pink. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen shrub with an upright growth habit. Leaves are dark bronze-red with purple veins. Pendent, tubular flowers are coral red. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Long bloom cycle followed by fruits.

An evergreen shrub with a dwarf, round form. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with serrated edges. Slightly fragrant masses of white flowers bloom from pink buds in clusters at branch tips. Blooms in spring are followed by dark blue fruits. Disease resistant.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, upright form. Foliage is needle-like and medium green with cream-tipped new growth. Rosy-pink, urn-shaped flowers bloom from fall to spring. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Best in acidic soils, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

Ghostly silver leaves brighten this evergreen, upright California native shrub, set against smooth mahogany bark. White winter flowers feed bees, then small fruits serve birds and other wildlife. Its narrow frame fits dry screens, coastal slopes, and moon gardens. Full sun, sharp drainage, and summer-dry soil preserve the pale color and compact growth.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded, spreading form. Leathery, dark green leaves are spiraled along stems. Larger flowers are fiery orange. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers.

A thornless evergreen shrub that is well-suited for a low-maintenance screen or hedge. Leaves are oval, pointed, and variegated dark green with yellow margins. Tiny fragrant flowers are followed by red fruit. Attracts birds.

A semi-evergreen shrub with an upright growth habit. Small leaves are glossy green and tinted bronze. Stems are red. Pendent, tubular flowers are bicolored magenta and purple. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Long bloom cycle followed by fruits. Mite resistant.
An evergreen shrub with gracefully arching branches, small and glossy oval leaves in deep green. Flared, bell-shaped flowers in pale pink to white. Semi-evergreen in colder climates.

commonName: Glossy Leaved Manuzanita, Fort Bragg Manuzanita
description: A woody evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded growth habit. Branchlets are thin, red, and hairy. Small, glossy, green leaves are rounded to egg-shaped. Clusters of white, drooping, urn-shaped flowers are beneficial to many bird species. The berries are edible. Native to the coastal forests of Northern California.

An evergreen tree with a dense, rounded crown and a prolific self-sowing habit. Glossy, dark green leaves are leathery, pointed and oval. Large, showy clusters of frothy, yellow-white flowers are followed by profuse black berries. Dropped fruit is messy and staining, along with fallen seeds that sprout all over the garden.

An evergreen shrub with a sprawling habit. Variegated leaves are glossy green with bright yellow margins. Tubular, purple-blue flowers are followed by clusters of yellow fruits. Attracts birds and butterflies.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub with leathery, chartreuse yellow, compound leaflets of three. Clusters of fragrant white flowers look like small orange blossoms. Please note that all Choisya sales are final and deliveries may be restricted based on quarantine zones. Please ask your salesperson for more information.
A dense, fast-growing evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval and variegated in gold and green. Stems are dark brown. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

commonName: Gold Star Esperanuza, Gold Star Trumpet Flower
description: A semi- evergreen shrub with a bushy, rounded growth habit. Leaflets are feather-shaped and dark green. Showy trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in large clusters of bright gold. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts hummingbirds.

A dense, fast-growing evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and green, splashed with creamy-white and chartreuse. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

A semi-tropical, broadleaf evergreen shrub with thin stems and fuzzy, maple-like leaves. Drooping, cup-like flowers in bright golden yellow up to 3 inches across. Spring through fall blooms attract hummingbirds and butterflies.

botanicalName: Coleonema pulchrum 'Sunset Gold', C. pulchellum, Diosma pulchra
description: An airy, pleasantly fragrant evergreen shrub. Branches are flimsy and clothed in fine, needle-like leaves. Dainty pinkish flowers dot the bright golden green foliage. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, upright growth habit. Variegated leaves are large, oval to rounded, and have scalloped edges. Coloration is glossy green with thick, golden-yellow margins.

An evergreen shrub with mat-forming foliage and upright flowers. Leaves are oval, green, and turn burgundy in cold weather. Globe-shaped clusters of tiny flowers emerge bright-yellow, and mature to rusty-orange. Beneficial for wildlife, birds, and pollinators, especially butterflies. Native to western Colorado.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a dense, bushy form. Slender leaves are bright green. Flowers are made up of bright yellow bracts that surround cones. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Leathery, gray-green leaves are spiraled along stems. Large flowers are golden yellow. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub with leathery, chartreuse yellow, compound leaflets of three. Clusters of fragrant white flowers look like small orange blossoms. Hybrid cultivar of 'Sundance' and 'Arizonica'. Please note that all Choisya sales are final and deliveries may be restricted based on quarantine zones. Please ask your salesperson for more information.
An evergreen shrub with a with a dense and remarkably rounded form. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and bright green. Stems are dark brownish black.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, upright form. Variegated foliage emerges red, then turns dark green with irregular spots of pink, orange, yellow and white. Leaves are leathery and toothed like holly. Sweetly fragrant, tiny white flowers bloom in fall.

An evergreen shrub with a vigorous, upright growth habit. Spreading branches are armed with sharp thorns. Leaves are dark green, small and oblong. White flowers bloom in spring and summer. Abundant clusters of dark red, pea-sized berries retain color from early fall into winter. Attracts birds.

commonName: Graham Blandy Common Boxwood, English Boxwood
description: An evergreen shrub commonly used for clipped hedges or topiaries. Densely arranged leaves are small, glossy, elliptic to oval, and dark green with yellow-green undersides. Growth habit is upright and columnar.
Evergreen shrub with slender branches densely covered with myrtle-like, large green leaves. Bright purplish-pink sweet pea like flowers.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense pom-pom trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.
A low, mat-forming evergreen shrub with leaves that are similar to Buxus. Fragrant white blooms are followed by fleshy, red, edible fruits that are similar to large cranberries.

An evergreen, dense globe-shaped shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded form. Foliage is dark green, deeply divided, and leathery. Bright yellow, daisy-like flowers bloom from spring through summer.

An evergreen, dense spiral-trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense spiral-trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense spiral-trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen, dense spiral-trained shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen shrub with a narrow, upright growth habit. Tightly stacked leaves are small to midsize, oval, and have scalloped edges. Coloration is glossy dark green on top with light green undersides.

commonName: Green Supreme Bearberry, Green Supreme Kinnickinnick
description: A low, evergreen groundcover with dense spreading stems and small glossy dark green leaves. Pale pink spring flowers support pollinators, followed by red berry-like fruit. Useful as a durable native mat for slopes, edges, and open woodland plantings. Performs best with good drainage and low summer water once established.

commonName: Green Tower Common Boxwood, English Boxwood
description: An evergreen shrub commonly used for clipped hedges or topiaries. Densely arranged leaves are small, glossy, elliptic to oval, and dark green with yellow-green undersides. Growth habit is upright and columnar.
A compact evergreen shrub commonly used for clipped hedges or topiaries. Leaves are glossy, elliptic to oval, and deep green year round.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact, rounded mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and powdery gray-green. Stems are grayish white. Small, white, star-shaped flowers bloom mostly in spring. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

commonName: Gulf Stream Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Red new growth matures to blue-green, turning vivid red in fall and winter. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries. Dense, rounded form with uniquely upright branches.

An evergreen shrub with cane-like stems and compound foliage that resembles bamboo. New leaf growth is tinted with pink and matures to light green, turning brilliant burgundy in the fall and winter. Loose terminal clusters of tiny white flowers followed by sprays of shiny red berries. Dwarf habit.

commonName: Harbour Dwarf Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Copper-pink new growth matures to green, turning purple-red in fall and winter. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries. Dense, spreading form works as a groundcover or border.
A dense, fast-growing evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and variegated in green and yellow. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

A low-maintenance, groundcover evergreen shrub with small and narrow, silvery-green foliage. Small, velvety red, papery blooms similar in appearance to Cistus. Has a longer blooming period than similar cultivar 'Dazzler.'

An evergreen, compact shrub with a dense, rounded habit and colorful Protea-family foliage. Olive green leaves on red stems flush with red, plum, and orange tones from winter into spring, accented by yellow cone-like flower structures at the branch tips. Well suited to containers, coastal plantings, and low-water Mediterranean-style landscapes; thrives in well-drained, acidic, low-phosphorus soil.

An evergreen shrub with multiple, unbranched, upright stems and a rounded, bushy form. Lance-shaped leaves are light gray green with red edges and tips. Foliage turns ornamental red in fall. Bright yellow spring flowers bloom abundantly at branch tips. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

commonName: Hearst Ranch Buckbrush, San Simeon Ceanothus
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of medium blue in spring. Foliage is puckered and medium green. Natural growth habit is prostrate and very low. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of lavender blue in spring. Foliage is holly-like and bronze-green. Natural growth habit is low and spreading. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Copper-pink new growth matures to deep green, turning vivid purple-red in fall and winter. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries.

commonName: Heavenly Cloud Texas Ranger, Texas Sage, Ceniuzo, Barometer Bush
description: A mostly evergreen, rounded shrub with green leaves for screens, foundations, and hot walls. Masses of lavender flowers appear in summer and fall as humidity rises. Blooms feed bees and other pollinators. This nursery hybrid grows well in lean, well-drained soil. Its dense form works well in loose, low-care designs.

commonName: Helene Strybing New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, irregular branching habit and dense foliage. Green, needle-like leaves sometimes tinge pink in cool weather. Larger, fall-spring flowers are saucer-shaped, single, and light pink with a dark pink center. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.
A low-maintenance, groundcover evergreen shrub with small and narrow, gray-green foliage. Small, deep orange-red, papery blooms similar in appearance to Cistus.

An evergreen shrub with an upright form. Leathery, gray-green leaves are spiraled along stems. Flowers are bright golden yellow. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers. Disease resistant. Improved L. 'Yellow Bird'.

An evergreen shrub with a bushy, sprawling, suckering habit. Large, gray-blue-green leaves have saw-tooth margins. Foliage emits a salty, nutty scent. Tall reddish-brown flower spikes bloom from late winter to early spring.

A durable, evergreen woody shrub with a rounded habit, smooth red-brown bark, and glossy green leaves. Pale pink winter flowers attract pollinators, followed by small red fruit. This adaptable selection is useful in native gardens, slopes, and informal screens. Performs best with good drainage and occasional deep summer irrigation in hotter sites.

An evergreen shrub that forms a dense, cascading ground cover. Dark green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, light blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators. Does not become woody like R. 'Prostratus'.
Semi-evergreen shrub with medium green foliage and clusters of light blue flowers at branch ends.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a bushy form. Narrowly oval leaves are gray green. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by bright yellow bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen, rounded desert shrub with velvety gray-green foliage and a soft, architectural presence. Golden yellow, cup-shaped flowers appear over a long warm-season bloom, drawing bees and hummingbirds. It is native to the Sonoran Desert region and thrives with excellent drainage and lean, mineral soils.

A heat-loving perennial with a vigorous, mounding habit. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are multicolored bright yellow, pink and magenta. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.
A dense, compact evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and green marbled with white. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

An evergreen shrub with a mounding, vigorously trailing growth habit. Rich green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, bright violet flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
An evergreen shrub with small and narrow leaves. Red, snapdragon-like, tubular flowers with flared lips.

A California native evergreen shrub that forms a dense mound with arching, climbing stems. Elliptical leaves are small, and yellow-green to medium green. Scarlet red, tubular to trumpet shaped flowers are available during summer and fall months, and attract hummingbirds.
An evergreen shrub with an adaptable growth habit, often placed as a hedge or screen. Rich green leaves are oval and glossy. Pea-sized berries ripen from green to dark red by fall.
An evergreen shrub or small tree. Leaves are small, oval, and variegated in green and ivory. Stems are dark brownish black.
A California native evergreen shrub grown for pendulous greenish-white catkins up to 12 inches long. Dense foliage made up of gray-green, wavy-edged leaves.
An evergreen shrub with dense, tropical-looking foliage. Large, deeply lobed leaves are glossy green. Rounded clusters of creamy white flowers are followed by small black fruit.

An evergreen, dense rounded shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.
A dense evergreen shrub. Leaves are narrow, rounded, leathery, and dark green. Fragrant clusters of small white flowers smell of orange blossoms. Makes an excellent screen.

commonName: Jauzuz Hands Bold Chinese Fringe Flower
description: An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Jazz Hands series has excellent form, larger leaves and larger flowers than other Loropetalums. Oval leaves emerge ruby-red and age to purple-green. Deep pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

commonName: Jauzuz Hands Dwarf Pink Chinese Fringe Flower
description: A compact evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Jazz Hands series has excellent form, larger leaves and larger flowers than other Loropetalums. Oval leaves are cranberry-purple. Bright pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

commonName: Jauzuz Hands Mini Chinese Fringe Flower
description: Purple leaves spread in a low, evergreen mound on this compact woody shrub. Bright pink fringe flowers appear in spring and may repeat, giving pollinators an early food source. Use it as a colorful groundcover, low edging, or container accent. Sun or light shade, drained soil, and occasional pruning maintain the dense, trailing form.

A Mediterranean native perennial shrub with upright stems clothed in soft and woolly, lance-shaped, gray-green foliage. The upper half of stems carry whorls of bright lemon yellow, two-lipped, hooded flowers.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a tall, compact form. Narrowly oval, variegated leaves are green, pink and cream. Flowers are made up of yellow cones surrounded by bright pink-red bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

A low, spreading evergreen shrub with coppery new growth that matures to gray-green foliage. Pink winter flowers and red berry-like fruit add seasonal interest and support wildlife. Useful as a bank cover, large-scale groundcover, or foreground shrub. Performs best with good drainage and limited summer irrigation once established.
