An evergreen shrub with an adaptable growth habit, often placed as a hedge or screen. Bright green leaves are oval and glossy. Pea-sized berries ripen from green to dark red by fall. A fast growing, long lived variety.

An evergreen to semi-evergreen, compact mounding shrub valued for bright variegated foliage. New growth opens gold and green, matures with warm orange tones, and is paired with small white summer flowers. Useful for low borders, accents, and containers; color is strongest with good drainage and regular establishment care.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, dense growth habit. Leaves are small, glossy, and olive green. Drooping, tubular, bright red to yellow-tipped flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.
An evergreen shrub or small tree. Leaves are rounded, hairy, and gray-green. Fragrant maroon flowers bloom in the spring. Perfect for use as an upright hedge.
An evergreen shrub with a compact growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, egg-shaped leaves are green and edged with a deep burgundy tinge.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form and showy foliage. Leaves are glossy, small and oval. Color is bugundy, turning bronze in summer. White myrtle-like flowers bloom in summer. Small reddish black berries follow.

commonName: Katsura Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with a robust, upright habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of rosy pink, urn-shaped flowers bloom in early spring. New foliage emerges stunning wine red at branch tips, maturing to dark green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. A fast-growing variety. Attracts bees.

commonName: Ken Taylor Hybrid Flannel Bush, Fremontia
description: A compact evergreen shrub with a lower, spreading habit and dense, irregular branching. Lobed dark green to gray-green foliage has a soft, felty texture, and pendant cup-shaped yellow flowers with orange backs appear from spring into early summer. A useful selection for dry slopes, native gardens, habitat plantings, and smaller low-water landscapes where a bold flowering shrub is needed at a more manageable scale. Thrives in full sun with excellent drainage and low summer irrigation once established. Leaf hairs can irritate skin and eyes.

An evergreen shrub with a sprawling growth habit. Gray-green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, dark blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
An evergreen shrub prized for intensely fragrant, single and star-shaped, velvety white flowers. Glossy, bright green, lance-shaped leaves. Reported to survive temperatures of 0 degrees.
A dense, fast-growing evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, pointed, and medium green. Stems are dark brown. Small, fragrant flowers in spring are followed by small orange fruits.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a dense, uniform mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are bi-colored rosy pink and creamy yellow. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.
A low-growing evergreen shrub with pungent and finely textured, needle-like foliage. Brush or spider-like clusters of long and curved, orange and red flowers.
An evergreen shrub with star-shaped, inch-wide lavender flowers with yellow centers. Dark green, oval, and finely toothed leaves.

A versatile evergreen shrub with a mounding growth habit. Foliage is very dark green. Leathery, oval leaves have rolled under margins. New stems are reddish. Small white flowers are followed by red-black berries in fall. Attracts pollinators, birds and other wildlife. California native.

An evergreen shrub with upright, suckering branches and horizontal foliage. Long, compound leaves are glossy green and holly-like with spiny edges. Clusters of yellow flowers in early spring are followed by blue-black berries in early summer. Attracts birds and bees. Native to Asia.

An evergreen shrub with a fine, dense texture. Branches are thin and arching. Variegated leaves are tiny, glossy and egg-shaped. Foliage is dark green with yellow edges. Creamy white flowers are small, bell-shaped and fragrant. Blooms in summer, followed by purple fruits.
An evergreen shrub with flat, elliptic leaves, which smell of lemon when bruised. Bristlelike flowers are known for their long, showy stamens. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

commonName: Lemon Lime Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Lemon-lime green new growth matures to bright green, staying green through the cold season. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries. Rounded, compact form. Disease resistant.

An evergreen shrub with an upright, spreading habit. Adaptable to training and pruning. Foliage resembles Coast Live Oak. Leathery, green leaves are oval with toothed, rolled under edges. Winter-spring, white-pink flower clusters are followed by edible fruits that are tasty in lemonade-type drinks. Skin is reddish and pulp is tart. Fruits are larger than those of R. ovata. Attracts birds. Good for erosion control. Southern California native. Likes coastal conditions.

A large, evergreen shrub with an open, sculptural framework and smooth mahogany bark. Gray-green leaves and pale pink winter flowers create refined texture for native and Mediterranean-style plantings. Berry-like fruit supports birds and wildlife. Performs best with excellent drainage and deep, infrequent irrigation during establishment.

A semi-evergreen shrub with an upright, tree-like growth habit. Leaves are lush and glossy green. Large clusters of light pink flowers bloom from dark pink buds. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Long bloom cycle followed by edible, sweet, dark purple fruits. Flowers are also edible. Mite resistant.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a short, bushy form. Slender leaves are gray-green. Flowers are made up of showy red and green cones surrounded by creamy yellow, red-edged bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.
A low and spreading evergreen shrub with woolly and narrow, gray-green leaves densely set along the branches. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, pink and cream flowers. Frost tolerant.

commonName: Little Heath Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with a compact, upright habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of white, urn-shaped flowers bloom in early spring. New foliage emerges pink at branch tips, maturing to variegated gray-green with yellow-green edges. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.
A dwarf evergreen shrub with flat, elliptic, blue-green leaves. Bristlelike flowers are known for their long, bright red stamens. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

A low-maintenance, dwarf evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display bright white, crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are variegated medium green and yellow. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.
A dwarf evergreen shrub that forms a multi-branching hedge. Dark green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Rarely ever produces pollen or fruit.

commonName: Little Ragu Sweet Bay, Grecian Laurel
description: A compact, pyramidal evergreen shrub or small tree with dark green, elliptical, aromatic foliage used as a flavorful seasoning. Small greenish yellow flowers in spring are followed by black berries. New stems are reddish. Does well in a container.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a short, bushy form. Slender leaves are bronzy-green. Flowers are made up of showy yellow and green cones surrounded by vibrant red bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

A robust, dwarf evergreen shrub. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Deep red blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

A compact evergreen shrub with pointed, oval leaves. Glossy, deep green foliage takes on a bronze tint in the fall. Citrus-scented, trumpet-shaped, white and pink flowers last from spring to winter. Semi-evergreen in colder climates.
A rounded and upright evergreen shrub with long and thin and needle-like foliage. Large, brush-like clusters of long and curved, dark pink and orange flowers.

A large, evergreen shrub with an upright, open habit and smooth burgundy-red bark. Gray-green leaves and pink winter flowers provide strong native garden character, followed by berry-like fruit for wildlife. Useful as a specimen or informal screen. Performs best with good drainage and little summer irrigation once established.
A low-growing evergreen shrub with small and narrow blue-green leaves densely set along the branches. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, dark pink flowers.

An evergreen shrub that forms a low, spreading mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear, whorled, and light gray-green. Small, white, star-shaped flowers bloom mostly in spring. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

An evergreen shrub with a vigorous, low growth habit. Spreading branches are armed with sharp thorns. Leaves are dark green, small and oval. White flowers bloom in spring and summer. Abundant clusters of bright orange, pea-sized berries retain color from early fall into winter. Attracts birds.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a compact, upright mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters in a range of colors. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

A compact semi-evergreen shrub with a rounded, bushy habit and thin, branching stems. Soft, maple-like green leaves set off large, pendant, bell-shaped red flowers that bloom over a long season from spring to fall, and nearly year-round in mild coastal and frost-free climates. Well suited to containers, hanging baskets, small borders, patios, and protected entries where its compact scale and hummingbird-attracting flowers can be used up close.

An evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded form. Foliage is small and gray green. Lavender-purple flowers cover the branches in abundance. From summer into fall, flowers bloom in cycles after a spike in humidity, such as a rain. Thrives in heat. Tolerates drought. Attracts pollinators and birds. Native to Texas and Mexico.

A low-maintenance evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display bright magenta, crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are narrow, woolly, and gray-green. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.

An evergreen shrub or small tree with a round form. Bark is gray-brown and fissured. Dark green leaves are oval and leathery. Foliage emerges bronze. Light fragrant masses of pink flowers bloom in clusters at branch tips. Blooms in fall, winter, or spring are followed by dark blue fruits.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, mounding form. Oval leaves are glossy and rich green. Fragrant, pink-tinged, creamy white flowers bloom in dome-shaped clusters throughout spring. Males have more showy flowers, but no berries.
A tropical evergreen tree with an upright and rounded form. Large, drooping ovate leaves are glossy emerald green. Inconspicuous spring flowers lead to small mallet-shaped pods in winter.
An evergreen shrub with a spreading, upright growth habit. Glossy dark green leaves are large to midsize, oval, and have scalloped edges.
An evergreen shrub with an upright, rounded growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Larger, obovate leaves are variegated rich green with speckled white margins.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Lance-shaped leaves are variegated dark green with yellow margins. Tight clusters of pale pink, highly fragrant flowers bloom heaviest from late winter to early spring. Does best in fast draining soils. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can tolerate full shade.
Evergreen shrub with rounded bright green leaves, and bright purplish-pink sweet pea like flowers.

A dense, fast-growing evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and light green with creamy white margins. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

An evergreen shrub with a vining, sprawling, semi-upright growth habit. Adaptable to pruning and training. Densely arranged leaves are bright green and ribbed. Flared trumpet-shaped flowers emit appetizing hues of yellow, orange and red from spring to fall. Heavy blooms from spring to fall. Attracts butterflies and hummingbirds.
A rounded and upright evergreen shrub with bright green, deeply divided foliage. Large, 6" brush-like clusters of long and curved, apricot-orange flowers.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a tall, bushy form. Slender leaves are gray-green. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by creamy yellow, red-tinged bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen shrub with a dense, mounding form. Foliage is needle-like and medium green with yellow-tipped new growth. Ivory white, urn-shaped flowers bloom from winter to spring. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Best in acidic soils, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

A semi-dwarf evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Wavy-edged, lance-shaped leaves are variegated dark green with thick yellow margins. Tight clusters of pink, highly fragrant flowers bloom heaviest from late winter to early spring. Does best in fast draining soils. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can tolerate full shade.
A heat tolerant evergreen shrub with furry gray-green leaves and profuse white flowers with deep red central blotches. Hybrid between Halimium and Cistus salviifolius.

An evergreen shrub or tree with a rounded crown and a multi-stemmed form. Glossy dark green leaves divide into many oval-oblong leaflets. Fragrant, wisteria-like clusters of dark violet flowers are followed by long seedpods. Blooms in spring.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub with leathery, dark green, compound leaflets of three. Clusters of fragrant white flowers look like small orange blossoms. Please note that all Choisya sales are final and deliveries may be restricted based on quarantine zones. Please ask your salesperson for more information.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact, upright, rounded mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and gray-green. Small, pale violet, star-shaped flowers bloom year round. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

A low-maintenance evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display bright white, crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are variegated green and gold. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded, compact growth habit. Flowers and leaves are sweetly fragrant. Narrow foliage is dark green with woolly white undersides. Velvety purple flowers are arranged in upright stalks. Flowers display long, curling stamens. Blooms in spring, summer, and fall. Attracts hummingbirds and bees. Only plant in soil with good drainage.
An evergreen shrub prized for intensely fragrant, small and double, velvety white flowers. Glossy, bright green, lance-shaped leaves. Hardy to 20 degrees.
An evergreen shrub with small and glossy oval leaves variegated in green and yellow. Flared, bell-shaped flowers in lavender to light pink. Semi-evergreen in colder climates.

An evergreen, upright Australian shrub with an open, lightly branching habit and finely cut green foliage. Large hibiscus-like violet-purple flowers appear over a long warm season and attract pollinators. It is effective as a dry garden accent or informal screen in well-drained soil.

A compact evergreen shrub that forms a dense, rounded screen. Takes well to shearing. Good for hedges or topiaries. Deep green leaves are glossy, oblong, and emerge reddish. Creamy white flowers are followed by burgundy, edible fruit that tastes best when processed, rather than raw.

commonName: Moon Bay Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Lime green leaves turn vivid red in fall and winter. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries. Dwarf, rounded form.

A bushy, semi-tropical evergreen shrub with thin stems and maple-like leaves. Drooping, cup-shaped flowers in pale yellow. Spring through fall blooms attract hummingbirds and butterflies. A compact cultivar.
A fast-growing, upright evergreen shrub with deeply divided, fern-like foliage. Large, brush-like clusters of long and curved, creamy white flowers.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Lance-shaped leaves are variegated dark green with yellow margins. Tight clusters of pink, highly fragrant flowers bloom heaviest from late winter to early spring. Does best in fast draining soils. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can tolerate full shade.

An evergreen shrub with a sprawling, mounding growth habit. Variegated leaves are large to midsize, oval to rounded, and have scalloped edges. Coloration is yellowish-cream with irregular, dark green margins. In cooler weather, some leaves tinge rosy-pink.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and gray-green with variegated white edges. Small, white, star-shaped flowers bloom mostly in spring. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

botanicalName: Rhamnus californica 'Mound San Bruno', Frangula californica
description: A versatile evergreen shrub with a compact, mounding growth habit. Light green foliage is leathery and oval. Small white flowers are followed by red-black berries in fall. Attracts pollinators, birds and other wildlife. California native.

commonName: Mountain Fire Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with a round, upright habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of pinkish-white, urn-shaped flowers bloom in early spring. New foliage emerges flaming red, maturing to forest green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-shaped with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.
A rounded evergreen shrub with outstanding red stems. Leaves are leathery, aromatic, oval to lance-shaped, and rich green. Milky chartreuse flowers are followed by black fruits in fall.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a low mound. Small leaves are fuzzy, egg-shaped and gray-green. Most of the year and heaviest in spring, saucer-shaped flowers bloom in violet with yellow centers. Attracts butterflies and bees. In fall, little tomato-like fruits attract birds. Native to California. All parts toxic.

A rounded, fast-growing evergreen shrub. Dark green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Salmon pink, double-form blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.
A low and spreading evergreen shrub with woolly and narrow, gray-green leaves densely set along the branches. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, pink and cream flowers. Frost tolerant.
An evergreen shrub that forms a low, spreading mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and dark gray-green. Small, white, star-shaped flowers bloom mostly in spring. Native to Australia.
An evergreen shrub prized for intensely fragrant, formal double, velvety white flowers. Glossy, bright green, lance-shaped leaves. Hardy to 20 degrees.

Tall bare stems float above the low leaves of this herbaceous California native perennial. Flower heads open white, cream, or pale pink and feed native bees and butterflies; dry seeds later serve birds. Use it in meadow drifts and habitat slopes. Sun, lean soil, and good drainage maintain the airy form and low water use.
An upright evergreen shrub with flat, elliptic, gray-green leaves. Bristlelike flowers are known for their long, neon pink stamens. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorous, trailing mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are deep golden yellow. Blooms from late spring to fall. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

An arching, perennial, evergreen shrub with velvety, gray green leaves. Ornamental berries follow the blossoms that bloom from spring through fall. Flowers are crimson red, long, tubular, and tightly clustered. Beneficial for butterflies and hummingbirds.

An arching, perennial, evergreen shrub with velvety, gray green leaves. Ornamental white berries follow the blossoms that bloom from spring through fall. Flowers are white, long, tubular, tightly clustered, and fragrant at night. Beneficial for night pollinators.
An open and rounded evergreen shrub with dark green, needle-like foliage. Brush-like clusters of long and curved flowers in rosy red.
A dense evergreen shrub. Leaves are dark green in color, and elliptical in shape, with wavy margins and pointed tips. Small and tubular, fragrant creamy white flowers bloom in the spring.

An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Fiery red new growth matures to bronze-green, turning red in winter. Loose clusters of tiny white flowers are followed by sprays of shiny red berries. Dense, slow-growing, upright form. Improved 'Gulf Stream'.

An evergreen tree with ornamental reddish bark that becomes furrowed and gray with age. Leaves are oblong, dark green, and leathery. Deep pink, bell-shaped flowers are followed by bright orange-red fruit with a strawberry-like texture.
A semi-tropical, broadleaf evergreen shrub with fuzzy, arrow-like leaves. Pendulous, cup-like flowers in orange with red venation. Flowers are held in prominent deep burgundy calyxes.

commonName: Orange Jubilee Esperanuza, Orange Jubilee Trumpet Flower
description: A semi-evergreen shrub with a bushy, rounded growth habit. Leaflets are feather-shaped and dark green. Showy trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in large clusters of golden-orange. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts hummingbirds.

An evergreen shrub with a suckering, rounded growth habit. Compound leaves are glossy and holly-like with spiny edges. Foliage emerges bronze-red, matures to dark green and turns purple-red in winter. Clusters of yellow flowers in spring are followed by edible, blue-black berries in fall. Berries are tasty in jams. Plant parts have medicinal uses. Attracts birds and bees. Native to the Pacific Northwest, including northern California.
An evergreen shrub with lustrous and oblong, dark green leaves. Showy spikes of fragrant, creamy-white flower followed by small black fruits.

A low, spreading evergreen shrub with fine-textured gray-green foliage and a broad, ground-hugging habit. Pale pink winter flowers are followed by small red fruit, supporting pollinators and wildlife. Useful on slopes, parkways, and large banks. Performs best with excellent drainage and little summer irrigation once established.
An evergreen shrub with an upright growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, egg-shaped leaves are variegated chocolate-maroon with cherry pink margins.

commonName: Pacific Sunset Hybrid Flannel Bush, Fremontia
description: A fast-growing evergreen shrub or small tree with an upright, vase-shaped habit and broad, arching branches. Coarse, lobed gray-green foliage creates a rugged native texture, while large yellow flowers with strong orange-red coloring bloom profusely in spring. Effective as a specimen, screen, or dry garden focal point where it has full sun, well-drained soil, and space to develop. Once established, it is highly drought tolerant and performs best with low summer irrigation. Leaf hairs can irritate skin and eyes.
An evergreen shrub with an upright growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, egg-shaped leaves are variegated cherry red with chocolate-maroon margins.

An evergreen shrub that forms a vigorous, upright, multi-trunking hedge. Adaptable to pruning and training. Bright to dark green leaves are glossy, narrow, serrated and aromatic when crushed. Yellow flowers in spring are followed by waxy purple berries. Attracts birds and butterflies. Coastal California native.

A rounded, evergreen shrub with distinctive coppery new growth, gray-green mature leaves, and smooth reddish bark. Pink winter flowers attract pollinators, followed by small red fruit. Useful in native screens, slopes, and mixed dry borders. Performs best with excellent drainage and limited summer irrigation once established.

An evergreen shrub with arching branches and a sprawling habit. Can be trained as a vine or tree. Slender leaves are mid-green. From spring to fall, salver-shaped flowers bloom in violet with yellow centers. Fruits ripen in fall. All parts are toxic.

A large, mounding evergreen shrub with fountain-like branches. Dark green leaves reveal woolly gray undersides. White flowers are followed by clusters of bright red cranberry-like fruits. Attracts birds and bees.

A heat-loving perennial, evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are multicolored in vibrant shades of pink, orange and gold. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

An evergeen shrub with red stems clothed in dark green leaves arranged in neat, opposing pairs. Spike-like flower clusters in bright purple and white. Best grown in cool summer - mild winter climates.

A dense and rounded evergreen shrub with deeply divided bright green foliage that develops bronze highlights in the winter months. Brush-like clusters of long and curved flowers that begin greenish-yellow and age to shades of yellow, pink, and orange.
A low-growing and rounded evergreen shrub with finely textured and needle-like, gray-green foliage. Brush or spider-like clusters of long and curved, red flowers.

An evergreen, graceful Australian tree with weeping branchlets and narrow aromatic foliage. Small white spring-to-summer flowers dot the canopy, followed by fine seed capsules. It is useful as a light screen, specimen, or patio tree and thrives in well-drained soil with moderate to low irrigation after establishment.

An evergreen shrub with a larger, upright, open-branching form. Leaves are lance-shaped and dark green with lime green new growth. Extra large, extra showy clusters of pink, highly fragrant flowers bloom heaviest from late winter to early spring. Does best in fast draining soils. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can tolerate full shade.

commonName: Petite Butterflies Dwarf Sweet Pea Shrub
description: Compact evergreen shrub with rounded gray-green leaves, bright purple-pink sweet pea-like flowers.

A dwarf evergreen shrub. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Creamy white blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with small leaves and flowers. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Soft pink blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and very floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with small leaves and flowers. Gray-green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Creamy peach blooms open from salmon pink buds from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and very floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with smaller leaves and flowers. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. White blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and very floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

An evergreen, prostrate California native shrub forming a dense, durable groundcover. Small, glossy green leaves create a clean texture, with inconspicuous cream flowers that benefit native insects. A practical choice for large-scale slope coverage, coastal exposure, and erosion control where drainage is good and irrigation is reduced after establishment.

A fruiting evergreen shrub that can be trained as a patio tree, or a hedge when planted in a group. Oval leaves are dark green above and felty white below. Early summer brings forth edible flowers with showy red stamens and sweet, purple-white petals. Fruit is ripe when it begins to drop, sometime during fall. Fruit resembles a large, rounded, matte blue-green egg. The flesh has been described to taste like a blend of pineapple and strawberry. Fruit production is most favorable in areas with mild summers and frost-free winters. Self-fertile, but better fruit set with a pollenizer nearby. Attracts birds and bees.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, gradually upright growth habit. Leaves are leathery, rich green, and oval. Light pink, bell-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, gradually upright growth habit. Leaves are leathery, rich green, and oval. Light pink, bell-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.

A tall, vigorous evergreen shrub. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Large pink blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

botanicalName: Coleonema pulchrum, C. pulchellum, Diosma pulchra
description: An airy, pleasantly fragrant evergreen shrub. Branches are flimsy and clothed in fine, needle-like leaves. Dainty magenta pink flowers dot the bright green foliage. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

botanicalName: Coleonema pulchrum 'Magenta', C. pulchellum, Diosma pulchra
description: An airy, pleasantly fragrant evergreen shrub. Branches are flimsy and clothed in fine, needle-like leaves. Dainty magenta pink flowers dot the bright green foliage. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorous, trailing mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are soft pink and yellow. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

commonName: Pink Cascade New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with a low, sprawling habit. Dark green, needle-like leaves are densely set. Larger, spring flowers are saucer-shaped, single, and dark to light pink. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.
An evergreen shrub with flat, elliptic leaves that smell of lemon when bruised. Bristlelike flowers are known for their long, bright pinky-purple stamens. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, dense growth habit. Leaves are small, oval, and dark green. Bell-shaped, salmon-pink flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.
A semi-tropical broadleaf evergreen shrub with large, soft maple-like leaves. Pendulous, cup-shaped flowers in soft pink.

An upright evergreen shrub with interesting flowerheads, made up of stiff pink and white bracts. Flowers are available throughout winter months, and are choice for flower arrangements. Leathery, dark green leaves.

An evergreen shrub with a round, mounding form. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval with serrated edges. New foliage emerges burgundy-bronze. Lightly fragrant masses of rich pink flowers bloom in clusters at branch tips. Blooms in spring are followed by dark blue fruits.
A semi-tropical, broadleaf evergreen shrub with maple-like leaves. Pendulous, cup-shaped flowers in mauve pink. Spring through fall blooms attract hummingbirds and butterflies.
A dense and upright evergreen shrub with dark green, finely textured, needle-like foliage. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, showy rose-red flowers. Frost hardy to the low 20's.

commonName: Pink Pearl New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, irregular branching habit. Dark green, needle-like leaves are densely set. Dainty, fall-spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and white from pink buds. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.

commonName: Pink Powder Puff, Red Powder Puff
description: Evergreen shrub or small tree native to South America. Foliage is divided into leaflets of dark green leaves. New growth emerges glossy copper-yellow. Raspberry-like buds explode open to form large pink to red puff flower heads. Blooms primarily in winter and fall, rarely in spring and summer months.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub that forms a screen or hedge. Takes well to shearing. Fragrant leaves are linear to rounded, leathery, and dark green. Clusters of small, pink flowers bloom in spring and fall. Attracts pollinators.

A low-maintenance evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display pale pink, crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are narrow, woolly, and gray-green. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.
An evergreen shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, egg-shaped leaves are variegated green with yellow margins that age to hot pink.

An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge purple and age to green. Rosy pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.
An upright evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and green with yellow edges. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a vigorous, bushy form. Narrowly oval leaves are silvery-green. Flowers are made up of large, silver cones surrounded by yellow-green bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge rosy-purple and age to bronze-purple-green. Deep pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.
An evergreen shrub with a compact, spreading growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, egg-shaped leaves are variegated bright green, rosy pink, and chocolate-plum-purple.

commonName: Plum Passion Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with cane-like stems and compound foliage that resembles bamboo. New growth is flushed with deep purple and matures to dark green, turning purple-red in the fall and winter. Loose terminal clusters of tiny white flowers followed by sprays of shiny red berries.

commonName: Point Reyes Bearberry, Point Reyes Kinnickinnick
description: A low, evergreen groundcover with trailing stems and small glossy green leaves. Pale pink winter to spring flowers attract pollinators, followed by red berry-like fruit. Useful on slopes, parkways, and coastal or inland native plantings. Performs best with good drainage and little summer irrigation once established.

commonName: Point Reyes California Lilac, Glory Mat
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of blue in spring. Foliage is holly-like and bronze-green. Natural growth habit is low and spreading. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of frosted white-blue in spring. Foliage is leathery, small, and gray-green. Natural growth habit is slow, low, and mounding. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.
A perennial sometimes treated as a houseplant, with large and single pale purple flowers. Woody stems clothed in whorls of 8" long, glossy rich green leaves.
An upright evergreen shrub with flattened and deeply cut, sawtooth-like foliage. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, golden yellow flowers. Takes well to shearing, excellent for screening.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of white in spring. Foliage is leathery, larger, and gray-green. Natural growth habit is low and mounding. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A large evergreen shrub with a round, compact form. Broad leaves are dark green. In spring, fragrant, banana-scented flowers blooms from fuzzy buds. Burgundy-outlined, cream flowers are cup-shaped and magnolia-like. Fruits follow. Attracts birds.
An evergreen shrub with lustrous and narrow, dark green leaves. Long and showy spikes of creamy-white flower followed by small red to purple fruits. Dark red stems.

commonName: Prelude Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A dwarf, shade-loving evergreen shrub with a compact, mounding habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of white, urn-shaped flowers bloom in early spring. New foliage emerges pink at branch tips, maturing to dark green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.

An evergreen shrub with an open-branching, upright growth habit. Silky, saucer-shaped, royal purple flowers display interesting, curved stamens. Blooms from summer into fall. Foliage is lush green, oval and covered in bronze-toned velvet. Leaves have unique venation.

An evergreen, spreading shrub used as a durable groundcover for large slopes and parkway plantings. Narrow green phyllodes create a clean texture, and small yellow spring flowers add seasonal interest. It is well adapted to heat, reflected light, and lean, well-drained soils once established.

An evergreen, spreading shrub used as a durable groundcover for large slopes and parkway plantings. Narrow green phyllodes create a clean texture, and small yellow spring flowers add seasonal interest. It is well adapted to heat, reflected light, and lean, well-drained soils once established.

An evergreen shrub that forms a mounding, spreading ground cover. Rich green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, light blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

commonName: Purity Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with a compact, round habit. Showy red buds persist from late summer to spring, blooming into abundant, chain-like clusters of white, urn-shaped flowers in spring. Large-flowered, late-blooming variety. New leaves emerge bronze-chartreuse, maturing to rich green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.
Evergreen shrub with rounded bright green leaves, vivid purple-pink sweet pea-like flowers.

commonName: Purple Diamond Semi-Dwarf Chinese Fringe Flower
description: A compact evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves are rich burgundy, holding color well all year round. Bright pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

A Mediterranean native perennial shrub with upright stems clothed in soft and woolly, lance-shaped, gray-green foliage. The upper half of stems carry whorls of purplish pink, two-lipped, hooded flowers.

An evergreen shrub or small tree with upright branches and leaves. Willow-like foliage is bronze-green and flushes burgundy-red in cooler weather. Small flowers are followed by papery, tan, ribcage-shaped seed capsules.

An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge dark burgundy and age to rich purple. Bright pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

A low-maintenance evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display deep pink, burgundy-spotted, crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are narrow, resinous, and gray-green. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded to sprawling growth habit. Leaves are glossy green, pointed and oval. Tubular, five-petaled, purple and white flowers are followed by clusters of orange fruits. Spring to fall blooms attract birds and butterflies.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a trailing, mounding ground cover. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are lavender-purple with white eyes. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

A low, vigorous evergreen shrub with trailing stems that root as they touch the ground. Small, oval, rich green leaves densely cloak the branches. Tiny white flowers are followed by abundant, bright red cranberry-like fruits. Attracts birds and bees.

A rounded evergreen shrub with small, glossy, and oval leaves. Foliage is variegated silvery-green with white margins. Flared, bell-shaped flowers bloom in pinkish white. Semi-evergreen in colder climates.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorous, spreading mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are bicolored bright orange-red. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

An evergreen shrub with an upright, rounded growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, obovate leaves are variegated green, creamy yellow, gold, and pink. Fall color is infused with rich scarlet red.

A California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of lilac-blue in spring. Foliage is leathery, 2 - 3 inches, and dark green. Natural growth habit is upright and adaptable with pruning. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, compact growth habit. Leaves are small, glossy, and bright green. Orange, bell-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.

An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge burgundy and age to olive green. Raspberry-pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Lance-shaped leaves are variegated gray-green with yellow margins. Tight clusters of pale pink, highly fragrant flowers bloom heaviest from late winter to early spring. Does best in fast draining soils. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can tolerate full shade.

commonName: Red Bird of Paradise, Dwarf Poinciana
description: A tender, upright shrub with airy leaves and a tropical look for hot courts, screens, and desert accents. Orange-red flower clusters with long red stamens bloom through summer and feed hummingbirds and butterflies. Native to tropical America, it grows back fast after frost. Thorny stems and toxic seeds need careful placement.

commonName: Red Buckwheat, San Miguel Island Buckwheat
description: A perennial shrub with prostrate foliage and upright flowers. Leaves are spoon-shaped, woolly and gray-green. Globe-shaped clusters of tiny flowers emerge in ruby-pink and mature to rusty pale pink. Beneficial for wildlife, birds, and pollinators, especially butterflies. Native to the Channel Islands.

An evergreen, rambling shrub with arching stems and glossy green leaflets. Red-orange trumpet flowers open from fall into winter and feed hummingbirds and butterflies. Train it on a support, clip it as a hedge, or let it cover a bank. It grows well in warm sites with good soil drainage.

An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves are dark burgundy year round. Bright red flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form and showy foliage. Leaves are glossy, small and oval. Color is pink-red to burgundy, turning vibrant dark red in fall and winter. White myrtle-like flowers bloom in summer. Small reddish black berries follow.
A semi-tropical broadleaf evergreen shrub with large, soft, maple-like leaves. Pendulous, cup-shaped flowers in dark maroon.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a compact, bushy form. Slender leaves are mid-green, tinted red on the edges and tips. Foliage tints red in fall. Flowers are made up of red bracts that surround cones. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.
An upright evergreen shrub with flattened and deeply cut, sawtooth-like foliage. Showy brush-like clusters of long and curved, bright red flowers. Takes well to shearing, excellent for screening.
A semi-tropical broadleaf evergreen shrub with maple-like leaves. Pendulous, cup to bell-shaped flowers appear in red.

An evergreen shrub with a large, rounded form. Leathery, light gray leaves are spiraled along stems. Flowers are bright orange-red. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub with a compact, multi-branching growth habit. Leaves are gray-green, three-lobed and maple-like. Saucer-shaped, hollyhock-like flowers are red-magenta on burgundy stems. Blooms from midspring to fall. Attracts butterflies.
A large evergreen shrub with glossy, oval leaves that emerge bronzy-red and mature to deep green. Clusters of small white flowers in spring. Dense growth makes this an ideal screen or hedge.

An evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded form that stays symmetrical with very little pruning. Foliage is small and grayish green. Lavender-blue flowers cover the branches in abundance. From summer into fall, flowers bloom in cycles after a spike in humidity, such as a rain. Thrives in heat. Tolerates drought. Attracts pollinators and birds. Native to Texas and Mexico.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a tall, bushy form. Narrowly oval leaves are green. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by cream and bright red bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

commonName: River Nymph Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with a round, upright habit. Prolific, heavy, chain-like clusters of white, urn-shaped flowers bloom from pearly buds in late winter and early spring. New leaves emerge red, maturing to rich green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.
A dense and rounded evergreen shrub with fern-like, deeply divided foliage. Brush-like clusters of long and curved, dark salmon pink flowers. Long blooming period.

An evergreen shrub with a sprawling, dwarf growth habit. Grayish green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, lilac blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

An evergreen shrub with a narrow, upright growth habit. In spring, buds bloom into flat-topped clusters of small, pinkish white flowers. Attracts pollinators. Showy blue fruits attract birds. Foliage is dark green. Leaves are more rounded than the species. Less prone to mildew than the species.

commonName: Royal Robe Paraguay Nightshade, Blue Potato Bush
description: An evergreen shrub with arching branches and a sprawling habit. Can be trained as a vine or tree. More compact than the species. Slender leaves are mid-green. From spring to fall, salver-shaped flowers bloom in violet with yellow centers. Fruits ripen in fall. All parts are toxic.

commonName: Ruby Glow New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, irregular branching habit and dense foliage. Dark green, needle-like leaves take on a bronzy-purple tint. Dainty, spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and ruby red. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a compact, tall form. Narrowly oval leaves are pale green. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by bright yellow bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a tall, compact form. Narrowly oval leaves are green. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by bright red bracts that fade to cream. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

A low-maintenance, dwarf evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display white, crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are wrinkled and gray-green. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.
An evergreen shrub with small and pink, urn-shaped, drooping flowers. Edible black berries. Large and glossy, bright green leaves.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorous, trailing mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Variegated foliage is coarsely textured and dark green with irregular cream edges. Rounded flower clusters are vibrant yellow. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

commonName: San Gabriel Hybrid Flannel Bush, Fremontia
description: A fast-growing evergreen shrub with an upright to arching habit and a broad, open framework. Felty, lobed gray-green leaves contrast with large golden yellow flowers that open from orange-tinted buds in spring. Well suited to native plantings, dry banks, large borders, and informal screening where it receives full sun and well-drained soil. Once established, it performs well with low supplemental irrigation and warm, sunny exposure. Leaf hairs can irritate skin and eyes.
An evergreen shrub with an upright form. Dark green leaves are leathery and toothed like holly. Sweetly fragrant, cream to orange flowers bloom heaviest in fall.

An evergreen shrub with an upright, rounded growth habit. In spring, buds bloom into loose clusters of pinkish white flowers. Fragrance is disliked by some. Sparse, showy red to black fruits attract birds. Foliage is dark green. Leaves are glossy, elliptical, and deeply veined.
An evergreen shrub with rough, deeply lobed, gray-green foliage. Large, glossy, violet blue flowers resemble hibiscus. Beneficial for pollinators.

An evergreen shrub with a vigorous, unruly growth habit. Spreading branches are armed with sharp thorns. Leaves are dark green, small and oblong. White flowers bloom in spring and summer. Abundant clusters of bright red, pea-sized berries retain color from early fall into winter. Attracts birds.

A perennial shrub with a mounding habit. Leaves are long, narrow, fuzzy, and gray-green. Umbel-like clusters of tiny flowers emerge in off-white to pale-pink and mature to chocolate-red. Beneficial for wildlife, birds, and pollinators, especially butterflies. Native to the Channel Islands.

commonName: Saratoga Sweet Bay, Saratoga Grecian Laurel
description: A large evergreen shrub or small tree with dark green, elliptical, aromatic foliage used as a flavorful seasoning. Small greenish yellow flowers in spring. Male cultivar does not produce fruit. More tree-like habit than the species. Resistant to laurel psyllid and soft scale.

commonName: Scarlet O'Hara Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with an upright, layered habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of white, urn-shaped flowers bloom from pink buds in early spring. New leaves emerge scarlet-bronze red, maturing to rich green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.

An evergreen shrub with a large, rounded form. Leathery, green leaves are spiraled along stems. Large flowers are salmon pink and bright purple-red. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers. More tolerant of varied soils. Hardy to 25 deg F.
A mounding and compact evergreen shrub with soft, needle-like foliage resembling rosemary. Brush-like clusters of long and curved flowers in deep pink and cream. Hardy to the low 20's.

A dense, multi-stemmed evergreen shrub often used as a low-maintenance hedge. Leaves are glossy, dark green and narrow. Fragrant white flower clusters bloom in spring. A hardy selection down to USDA zone 5b.

An evergreen shrub with an upright, bushy habit. Foliage is needle-like and dark green. Light pink, urn-shaped flowers bloom from winter to spring. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Best in acidic soils, pH 5.1 - 6.0.
An upright evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and silvery green. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

An upright, evergreen shrub with a narrow, vase-shaped habit and attractive red-brown bark. Glossy green leaves and pale pink winter flowers provide structure and seasonal pollinator value. Its vertical form fits tighter native plantings, entries, and background screens. Performs best with good drainage and occasional deep irrigation in warm sites.
An upright evergreen shrub that is prized for its fragrant, pink, star-shaped flowers. Leaves are licorice-scented, oval and glossy green. Native to Australia.

A compact and rouded evergreen shrub with small and glossy oval leaves in deep green, flushed with purple in the fall. Flared, bell-shaped flowers in pale lavender-pink. Semi-evergreen in colder climates.
An evergreen shrub with a versatile branching habit. Foliage emerges bronze and matures to bright green. Leaves are pointed, oval and glossy. Does well as a hedge.
An evergreen shrub with a dense and stout form. Glossy, dark green leaves and long reddish purple flower spikes. Attracts butterflies.

A tropical evergreen shrub that forms a sprawling bush. Leaves are glossy, bright green and oval. Terminal clusters of white flowers with overlapping coppery-red bracts resemble shrimp. Native to Mexico.

commonName: Sienna Sunrise Heavenly Bamboo, Sacred Bamboo
description: An evergreen shrub with compound, bamboo-like foliage and cane-like stems. Fiery red new growth matures to green, flushing red in fall and winter. Sparse flowers, followed by shiny red berries. Compact, rounded form.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Leaflets are feather-shaped and dark green. Showy trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in clusters of coral-apricot. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts hummingbirds.

A woody semi-evergreen shrub with a densely-branched, rounded growth habit. Leaves are deep green and pinnately divided. Flowers resemble fluffy, pinky-red feather dusters with long, silky stamens. Attracts hummingbirds. Hybrid cross between C. californica and C. eriophylla. California native.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a tall, compact form. Narrow leaves are dark green, tinged red. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by burgundy bright red bracts that fade to yellow. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen shrub with silver stems and foliage. Leaves are palmate and pinwheel-shaped. Upright spikes of fragrant, pea-like flowers bloom in spring and summer. Flowers are violet-blue. Attracts many pollinators. Thrives in poor, fast-draining soils. California native.
An evergreen shrub with an upright growth habit. Variegated leaves are midsize, oval, and have scalloped edges. Coloration is gray-green with thick silvery-cream margins.

An evergreen shrub with an open-branching, upright growth habit. Silky, saucer-shaped, royal purple flowers display interesting, curved stamens. Blooms from summer into fall. Foliage is lush green, oval and covered in silver-toned velvet. Leaves have unique venation.
An upright, airy evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and gray with creamy pink edges. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.
A compact evergreen shrub. Leaves are small, glossy, oval, and super silvery-green. Stems are dark reddish brown. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.
An evergreen shrub with a bushy, upright growth habit. Variegated leaves are midsize, oval, and have scalloped edges. Coloration is silvery gray-green with thick, yellowish-cream margins.
A large evergreen shrub with with airy, fine-textured foliage. Very small, oval, and glossy silvery-green leaves. Dark brownish black stems. Takes well to shearing as a formal hedge.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. pink blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Red blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

A rounded, vigorous evergreen shrub. Green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Bright white blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge bronzy red and age to purple green. Foliage turns bright red in fall. Bright pink flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.
A columnar evergreen shrub with small, leathery, finely toothed foliage. Black berries. Foliage often looks more like Buxus than Holly.

commonName: Skylark California Lilac, Blue Mountain Lilac
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of dark blue in spring. Foliage is glossy, oval, 2 inches, and medium green. Natural growth habit is compact. Tolerates summer irrigation. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.
A narrow, upright evergreen shrub with flat, elliptic, silvery-blue-green leaves. Bristlelike flowers are known for their long, bright red stamens. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact, rounded mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and gray-green. Small, pale violet, star-shaped flowers bloom year round. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

commonName: Small Leaf Mountain Lilac, Julia Phelps California Lilac
description: A California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of vivid indigo blue in spring. Foliage is small, crinkled, leathery, and dark green. Natural growth habit is upright and adaptable with pruning. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact, upright mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and gray-green with variegated white edges. Small, white to pale purple, star-shaped flowers bloom mostly in spring. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

An evergreen shrub with spreading, arching branches. Oval leaves emerge red and age to light olive-green. Masses of white flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

commonName: Snow Flake New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, irregular branching habit. Dark green, needle-like leaves are densely set. Dainty, spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and white with maroon centers. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of snow white in spring. Foliage is glossy, 2 inches, and medium green. Natural growth habit is upright and adaptable to pruning. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

An evergreen shrub with an upright, vase-like form. Oval leaves are gray green. Abundant masses of white flowers are fringe-like and spidery. Main bloom in late winter and spring with sporadic flowering throughout the year. Semi-deciduous in cold winters.

commonName: Snow White New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with a compact, bushy branching habit and dense foliage. Gray-green, needle-like leaves tint pink in cool weather. Dainty, fall-spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and white with green centers. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.

commonName: Snowball California Lilac, White Monterey Lilac
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of snow white in spring. Foliage is holly-like and medium green. Natural growth habit is low and mounding. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A large evergreen shrub with reddish brown stems and soft, needle-like leaves that come in matte gray-green with reddish tips. New growth is yellow-green. Fragrant, bright yellow, puffy flower clusters bloom in winter. Shrub matures to take on a sprawling, bushy form.

This evergreen shrub is a spineless selection with a dwarf, mounding habit. Finely textured compound leaves are divided into narrow, green leaflets. Showy spikes of yellow flowers in fall are followed by dark blue fruits. Attracts birds and bees. Native to Asia.

A semi- evergreen shrub with a bushy, rounded growth habit. Leaflets are feather-shaped and bright green. Showy trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in large clusters of orange and gold. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts hummingbirds.

An evergreen vining shrub that climbs with support. Compound leaves are glossy and deep green. White, star-shaped flowers appear in clusters at branch tips. Little to no fragrance. Blooms from summer into fall. Attracts pollinators.

An evergreen shrub with dense, tropical-looking foliage. Large, deeply lobed, variegated leaves are glossy green, heavily speckled in white. Rounded clusters of creamy white flowers are followed by small black fruit.
A graceful and upright evergreen shrub with soft and finely textured, gray-green foliage. Brush or spider-like clusters of long and curved, rosy red flowers.

A multi-stemmed evergreen shrub that grows well in dry shade. Variegated leaves are large, glossy, and dark green with bold yellow centers. This is a female selection that produces bright red berries when pollenized by a male variety.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorously spreading mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters change from golden-orange to peachy-pink. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a vigorously spreading mound. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters change from golden-orange to pink-red. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

An evergreen shrub with a dense, compact growth habit. From late winter to early spring, buds bloom into fragrant, rounded clusters of small, white flowers. Attracts pollinators. Showy purple fruits attract birds. Foliage is dark green. Leaves are oval and smaller than the species.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with a prostrate habit. Foliage is needle-like and medium-green. Pink, urn-shaped flowers bloom from winter to spring. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Best in acidic soils, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

A dwarf evergreen shrub with a prostrate habit. Foliage is needle-like and medium-green. White, urn-shaped flowers bloom from winter to spring. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Best in acidic soils, pH 5.1 - 6.0.

A perennial shrub with a mounding habit. Leaves are oval, woolly and gray-green. Flat-topped clusters of tiny, lacy flowers emerge in off-white to light pink, and mature to rusty-red. Beneficial for wildlife, birds, and pollinators, especially butterflies. Native to the Channel Islands.

A tall, evergreen woody shrub with upright branching, smooth red bark, and gray-green foliage. Pale pink winter flowers and red berry-like fruit support native pollinators and birds. Useful as a specimen, dry screen, or structural native planting. Performs best with excellent drainage and little summer irrigation once established.
An evergreen shrub with dark green, small and narrow, shallowly toothed foliage. Male variety.

Cream-edged leaves make this evergreen, compact shrub bright even when it is not in bloom. White buds open to pink flower spikes from summer into fall and feed bees. Its neat round habit suits low hedges, path edges, and containers. Sun or light shade, open soil, and modest water keep the foliage dense and colorful.
A nearly prostrate evergreen shrub with rounded glossy green leaves that turn red and purple in fall. Small pink flowers are followed by red cranberry-like fruits. Attracts birds and bees.

An evergreen shrub with a neat, upright, round growth habit. Dark green foliage is egg-shaped, pointed, and leathery. Spring, white-pink flower clusters are followed by fuzzy red fruits that are tasty in lemonade-type drinks. Fruits are smaller than those of R. integrifolia. Attracts birds. Good for erosion control. Southern California native. Likes hot, dry climates.

An evergreen, compact shrub with upright red stems and narrow, willow-like foliage. New growth colors red through spring and summer, aging to pale green, while red and cream bracts surround cone-like structures at the branch tips. Performs best with excellent drainage, acidic soil, and low-phosphorus fertility, especially in coastal and mild-winter Mediterranean climates.
An evergreen shrub prized for its rose-like double flowers. Each bloom is pure white, and intensely fragrant. Glossy, bright green, lance-shaped leaves. Hardy to 20 degrees.

commonName: Summer Sunset Asian Star Jasmine, Yellow Star Jasmine
description: An evergreen groundcover with twining stems. If trained as a vine, it can grow 20 - 30 feet high. Distinctively fragrant flowers are small, white, and pinwheel-shaped. Flowers have yellow centers. Glossy, variegated leaves emerge apricot-red and mature to mottled pale yellow and gray-green. Foliage is smaller than T. jasminoides.

botanicalName: Teucrium chamaedrys 'Summer Sunshine', T. x lucidrys
description: A semi-woody perennial shrub with a dense, upright growth habit that stays low and tidy. Golden-green foliage is aromatic, egg-shaped, and toothed on the edges. Whorls of small, pale pink flowers bloom in summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub with leathery, golden-chartreuse to green, compound leaflets of three. Clusters of fragrant white flowers look like small orange blossoms. Please note that all Choisya sales are final and deliveries may be restricted based on quarantine zones. Please ask your salesperson for more information.

An evergreen shrub with pointed, oval leaves. Glossy, deep green leaves are edged in yellow, and take on a red-orange tint in the fall. Citrus-scented, trumpet-shaped, white flowers last from spring to winter. Semi-evergreen in colder climates.

A dense, evergreen shrub with rounded form, bronze new growth, and glossy green mature leaves. Pinkish white winter flowers support pollinators, followed by red berry-like fruit. Useful for screens, slopes, and native garden structure. Performs best with good drainage and occasional deep irrigation in warm inland sites.
An evergreen shrub with a dense form that works well as a hedge or topiary. Golden-chartreuse leaves are small, wavy-edged and egg-shaped. This flowerless sterile variety does not self-sow.
A rounded evergreen shrub with fern-like, deeply divided foliage. Large brush-like clusters of long and curved, fiery orange-red flowers.
A fast growing evergreen tree with long, feathery, needle-like leaves. Bark is grayish-brown and scaly. Leaves cascade from drooping branches. Native to Australia.
An evergreen shrub with rough, deeply lobed, gray-green foliage. Large, glossy, purple flowers resemble hibiscus. Beneficial for pollinators.
A large evergreen shrub or small tree with dark green, elliptical, aromatic foliage used as a flavorful seasoning. Small greenish yellow flowers in spring are followed by black berries.

An evergreen shrub that forms a ground cover. Spreads by rhizomes. Glossy green leaves are pointed, alternating, and more slender than the species. In spring, small white flowers are intensely fragrant. Glossy dark blue fruit develops in early summer. Tolerates deep, dry shade.
An evergreen shrub with an upright form. Dark green leaves are leathery and oval. Super fragrant, tiny, white flowers bloom heaviest in late summer-fall.
Evergreen shrub with pointed oval gray-green leaves, bright purplish-pink sweet pea like flowers.
An evergreen shrub or tree with glossy and narrow, dark green leaves. Golden yellow flowers with a strong orange fragrance, followed by seedpods.

An evergreen tree with a rounded, billowy, shrub-like form and bright green, lance-shaped leaves. In late winter or early spring, golden-yellow flower spikes appear along branches. Fast growing with a 20 - 30 year life span. Good for erosion control on hillsides.

A bushy, semi-tropical evergreen shrub with thin stems and maple-like leaves. Drooping, bowl-shaped flowers in salmon to orange with yellow-green sepals. Spring through fall blooms attract hummingbirds and butterflies.

An evergreen shrub with an upright, compact form. Long, leathery, green leaves are spiraled along stems. Flowers are rich orange-red. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Later blooms at branch tips in spring and summer. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers.
A fast-growing, bushy evergreen shrub with widely lobed, bright green leaves. Small, funnel-shaped, 1" wide flowers bloom in light pink with darker pink venation and dark eyes.
A large evergreen shrub or tree. Leaves are lance-shaped, wavy-edged, and light green. Honey-scented yellow flowers bloom in spring.

commonName: Temple Bells Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with a compact, mounding habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of white, urn-shaped flowers bloom in early spring. Large-flowered variety. New leaves emerge red, maturing to bronze then rich green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Small, obovate leaves are variegated rich green with golden margins that become marbled orange and gold.
An evergreen shrub or small tree with rough, narrow, gray-green leaves. Showy white flowers with yellow throats appear and reappear from spring to fall.

commonName: Texas Ranger, Texas Sage, Ceniuzo, Barometer Bush
description: A semi-evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Foliage is small and silvery-gray. Rosy-pink flowers cover the branches in abundance. From summer into fall, flowers bloom in cycles after a spike in humidity, such as a rain. Thrives in heat. Tolerates drought. Attracts pollinators and birds. Native to Texas and Mexico.
A low-maintenance, groundcover evergreen shrub with small and narrow, deep gray-green foliage. Small and white, papery blooms similar in appearance to Cistus.
A semi-tropical, broadleaf evergreen shrub with maple-like leaves are heavily speckled in yellow. Pendulous, cup-shaped flowers in salmon-orange.

A thorny evergreen shrub that is well-suited for a low-maintenance screen or hedge. Leaves are oval, wavy-edged, and gray-green with rusty dots. Tiny, fragrant winter flowers are followed by silvery red fruit. Attracts birds.

A semi-evergreen shrub with an upright, arching growth habit. Leaves are small and glossy green. Tiny, pendent flowers age from light pink to dark magenta pink. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Long bloom cycle followed by fruits. Resistant to fuchsia gall mite.

An evergreen, upright shrub with maple-like leaves and pendent, lantern-shaped flowers. Red-orange veined blooms with warm golden tones provide a long season of color and hummingbird interest. Best used in protected courtyards, espaliered against walls, or in mild-climate borders with fertile, well-drained soil.

An evergreen shrub to small tree with glossy, toothed green leaves and an upright, arching habit. Fragrant yellow spring flowers are held in small clusters along the stems and attract pollinators. Useful as a screen, espalier, or woodland-edge specimen. Performs best with well-drained soil and moderate to regular irrigation.

A self-sowing evergreen shrub with towering spike-like stalks of deep rosy pink flowers. Whorled leaves are hairy, lance-shaped and silver-green. Does well in coastal gardens. Attracts pollinators. Typically biennial.
A California native evergreen shrub or small tree with dark green and leathery toothed leaves. Clusters of white flowers followed by small red berries in the fall and winter.

commonName: Tricolor St. John's Wort, Tricolor Gold Flower
description: A semi-evergreen shrub with reddish stems and neatly arranged, green foliage with white margins tinged in pink. Golden cup-shaped flowers with prominent, showy stamen. Small reddish berries.

commonName: True Dwarf Common Boxwood, English Boxwood
description: An evergreen, dense dwarf edging shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

A perennial shrub with large, textured, olive-green leaves reminiscent of sage. The upper halves of the stems exhibit whorls of light yellow, hooded, two-lipped flowers in summer. Evergreen and drought-tolerant with an upright, mounding form.

An evergreen shrub with an upright, semi-columnar growth habit. Green, needle-like leaves are aromatic and edible. Tiny, lavender-blue flowers dot the foliage in spring and summer. Flowers are slightly larger than the species. Attracts bees and other pollinators. 'Tuscan Blue' is a favored selection for use as a culinary herb.

An evergreen shrub with leathery, lustrous, deep green leaves that are similar to Buxus. Fragrant white blooms are followed by fleshy, red, edible fruits that are similar to large cranberries. Compact and dense growth.

An evergreen, low-growing California native shrub with a broader, mounding groundcover habit. Dense green foliage covers slopes, parkways, and large open areas, with small cream flowers that support pollinators. It is valued for durability in coastal and inland landscapes and benefits from well-drained soil.

A fast-growing evergreen shrub. Variegated foliage is irregularly edged in light yellow. Leaves are leathery and lance-shaped. Rich pink blooms from late spring to fall. Flowers are funnel-shaped, five-petaled, and set in loose terminal clusters. Fragrant and floriferous. All plant parts are highly toxic.

commonName: Valley Valentine Japanese Andromeda, Lily of the Valley
description: A shade-loving evergreen shrub with an upright, layered habit. Abundant, chain-like clusters of pink-red, urn-shaped flowers bloom in late winter. New leaves emerge bronze-red, maturing to rich green. Leaf shape is oblong to lance-like with finely serrated edges. Attracts bees.

commonName: Valley Violet California Lilac, Violet Maritime Ceanothus
description: A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of lavender purple in spring. Foliage is leathery, small, and gray-green. Natural growth habit is small, mounding, and rounded. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

A woody evergreen shrub with a low, mounding form. Branches are crooked and sculptural with smooth red bark. Small, bright green leaves are rounded to egg-shaped. Clusters of pale pink, drooping, urn-shaped flowers are beneficial to many bird species. The berries are edible. Native to California. Tolerates serpentine and clay soils.

An evergreen shrub to small tree with fine-textured green leaves edged in cream and graceful, arching branches. Tiny fragrant yellow flowers bloom in late winter to spring, adding scent near paths and entries. Useful as a bright screen, espalier, or small patio tree. Performs best with well-drained soil and regular moisture.
An evergreen shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Variegated leaves are small, oval, and have scalloped margins. Coloration is dark green and edged in a thin line of cream.

A low, spreading, evergreen California native shrub grown as a colorful groundcover. Glossy oval leaves are variegated lime green, deep green, and golden yellow, with the brightest yellow tones in warm, sunny conditions. Pale blue flower clusters appear in spring and provide seasonal value for bees and butterflies. Best with fast-draining soil, light shade in warmer inland sites, and occasional summer water once established.

A compact evergreen shrub commonly used for clipped hedges or topiaries. Densely arranged leaves are small, glossy, and elliptic to oval. Coloration is dark green with variegated white-yellow margins and yellow-green undersides.
An evergreen shrub with a low, spreading growth habit. Small, oval leaves are variegated green with cream-white margins. Foliage is less glossy than the genus. Branches are beige-brown.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, slow-growing habit. Variegated foliage is dark green with white margins. Leaves are leathery and toothed like holly. Sweetly fragrant, tiny, white flowers bloom in fall.

A broadleaf evergreen shrub with dense branching and large glossy leaves heavily speckled with gold. Inconspicuous spring flowers may be followed by red berries on female plants when a male pollenizer is nearby. Useful for deep shade, containers, and foundation plantings. Performs best with rich, well-drained soil and regular irrigation.
An evergeen shrub with green and cream variegated leaves arranged in neat, opposing pairs. Spike-like flower clusters in purple. Best grown in cool summer - mild winter climates.
