An evergreen shrub with an adaptable growth habit, often placed as a hedge or screen. More compact than the species. Variegated foliage is dark green with white margins. Leaves are oval and glossy. Pea-sized berries ripen from green to dark red by fall.
A dense evergreen shrub. Leaves are narrow, rounded, leathery, and gray-green with cream margins. Fragrant clusters of small white flowers smell of orange blossoms. Makes an excellent screen.
An evergreen shrub or small tree. Leaves are rounded, hairy, and gray-green with cream margins. Fragrant maroon flowers bloom in the spring. Perfect for use as an upright hedge.
An evergreen shrub prized for intensely fragrant, small and double, velvety white flowers. Glossy, bright green leaves irregularly edged in yellow to cream. Hardy to 20 degrees.
Evergreen shrub with medium green leaves edged in white, abundant small purplish-pink flowers, minty fragrant foliage.

A slow-growing evergreen shrub with a round form. Oval to lance-shaped leaves are green with variegated white margins. Foliage is aromatic when crushed. Flowers are fragrant, white and saucer-shaped with many fluffy, spiky stamens. Summer blooms are followed by small, blue-black berries. Leaves, flowers, and berries are edible.

commonName: Variegated Sky Flower, Dewdrop, Pigeon Berry
description: An evergreen shrub with a sprawling growth habit. Variegated leaves are glossy green and edged in creamy white. Fragrant, pale blue, tubular flowers are followed by clusters of orange fruits. Attracts birds and butterflies.

botanicalName: Echium fastuosum 'Star of Madeira', E. candicans 'Star of Madeira'
description: A self-sowing evergreen shrub with large spike-like stalks of small lavender-blue flowers. Whorled leaves are hairy, lance-shaped and variegated gray-green with cream-white margins. Does well in coastal gardens. Attracts pollinators. Typically biennial.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form. Wavy-edged, lance-shaped leaves are variegated dark green with thin yellow margins. Tight clusters of pink, highly fragrant flowers bloom heaviest from late winter to early spring. Does best in fast draining soils. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can tolerate full shade.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded, spreading form. Leathery, dark green leaves are spiraled along stems. Flowers are yellow and red. Modified styles form a waxy, pincushion-like inflorescence. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Prefers acidic soils. Do not use phosphorus fertilizers.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, prostrate growth habit and distinctively glossy foliage. Leaves are small, obovate, and green. Considered an improved C. x kirkii.
A semi-tropical broadleaf evergreen shrub with deep green, maple-like leaves. Large, pendulous, cup-shaped flowers in salmon-orange. Spring through fall blooms attract hummingbirds and butterflies.

A low-maintenance evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display rosy pink to white, crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are narrow, woolly, and gray-green. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.

A large evergreen shrub or tree. Leaves are wavy-edged, glossy, lance-shaped and bright green. Fragrant clusters of creamy white flowers are followed by small orange berries. Makes an excellent hedge or screen.

A low growing evergreen shrub with excellent disease and pest resistance. New leaves emerge lime green, and turn glaucous blue-green as they mature. Petite, bright red flowers appear on the ends of stems during winter.

A semi-woody perennial shrub with a dense, upright growth habit that stays low and tidy. Dark green foliage is aromatic, egg-shaped, and toothed on the edges. Whorls of small, purple-pink flowers bloom in summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

This evergreen California native shrub grows upright with a dense green crown. Smooth copper-red bark adds color all year. Pink urn-shaped flowers feed early bees, and later fruit feeds birds. Use it for a dry screen, slope cover, or bold accent. Sun, open soil, and little summer water keep the form firm and clean.

A perennial shrub that forms an adaptable groundcover. Leaves are finely textured, woolly and gray-green. Globe-shaped clusters of tiny flowers emerge in off-white to pale-pink and mature to russet-brown. Beneficial for wildlife, birds, and pollinators, especially butterflies. Native to Southern California.

Dense and evergreen, this upright shrub has thick, glossy green leaves and responds well to shearing. Clusters of white flowers appear in spring and summer, attracting pollinators, followed by dark fruit that feeds birds. The species is native to East Asia. Use for formal hedges, privacy screens, clipped shapes, or a neat evergreen foundation planting.

botanicalName: Correa alba var. pannosa 'Western Pink Star'
description: A semi-woody evergreen shrub with a dense, low growth habit. Small leaves are oval, gray-green and slightly rough. Drooping, star-shaped flowers of pink attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.
A dense, dwarf evergreen shrub. Leaves are narrow, rounded, leathery, and dark green. Fragrant clusters of small white flowers smell of orange blossoms.

A semi-woody evergreen shrub with a dense growth habit. Oval leaves point upward to reveal gray-green undersides, which gives the plant a white-gray appearance. White, bell-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring.

An airy, pleasantly fragrant evergreen shrub. Branches are flimsy, grow mostly upright, and are clothed in fine, needle-like leaves. Dainty white flowers dot the bright green foliage. Attracts bees and other pollinators.
Semi-evergreen shrub with medium green foliage and clusters of white flowers at branch ends.

commonName: White Cloud Manuzanita, White Hair Manuzanita
description: A woody evergreen shrub with an upright, treelike form. Branches are furry and stems are covered in white hairs. Broad, gray-green leaves are rounded to egg-shaped. Clusters of white, drooping, urn-shaped flowers are beneficial to many bird species. The berries are edible. Native to California. Tolerates serpentine and clay soils.
A bushy, semi-tropical evergreen shrub with thin stems and maple-like leaves. Drooping, bowl-shaped flowers in white. Spring through fall blooms attract hummingbirds and butterflies.

commonName: White New uzealand Tea Tree, Manuka
description: An evergreen shrub with an upright, bushy branching habit. Green needle-like leaves are densely set. Dainty, spring flowers are saucer-shaped, double, and white. Bark is shaggy and gray-brown.

An evergreen shrub with a larger, upright, open-branching form. Leaves are lance-shaped and dark green with lime green new growth. Extra large, extra showy clusters of white, highly fragrant flowers bloom heaviest from late winter to early spring. Does best in fast draining soils. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can tolerate full shade.

A low-maintenance evergreen shrub with profuse blooms that open and drop daily. Single flowers display bright white crepe-paper petals and golden stamens. Leaves are rough, wrinkled, and gray-green. Tolerates heat, poor soil, and seaside conditions. Attracts butterflies.
An evergreen shrub with rough, deeply lobed, gray-green foliage. Large, glossy, white flowers resemble hibiscus. Beneficial for pollinators.

A self-sowing evergreen shrub with large spike-like stalks of small white flowers. Whorled leaves are hairy, lance-shaped and silver-green. Does well in coastal gardens. Attracts pollinators. Typically biennial.

A heat-loving perennial that forms a trailing, mounding ground cover. Evergreen in frost-free zones. Dark green foliage is coarsely textured. Rounded flower clusters are white with yellow eyes. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies. Foliage and ripe berries are toxic to animals when ingested.

A semi-woody perennial shrub with a dense, upright growth habit that stays low and tidy. Dark green foliage is aromatic, egg-shaped, and toothed on the edges. Whorls of small, white flowers bloom in summer. Attracts bees and other pollinators.

An evergreen shrub with a sprawling, mounding growth habit. Variegated leaves are midsize, oval, and have scalloped edges. Coloration is dark green, patch-worked in yellow-green, and heavily mottled in white. New growth is mostly white. In cool weather, some leaves blush rosy-pink.
A bold woodland perennial. Large, lobed leaves are variegated deep green, splashed in white. Tall, striking flowering spikes carry hooded white and pink flowers. Can tolerate full shade.
An evergreen shrub or tree with lustrous, deep green leaves with nearly spineless edges. Produces red berries when male plant is present for pollenization.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a tall, compact form. Narrowly oval, stiff leaves are green. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by bright red bracts that fade to yellow. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen, dense rounded shrub with small glossy green leaves and a formal, fine-textured presence. Slow to moderate growth responds well to shearing, making it useful for clipped hedges, borders, containers, and architectural accents. It performs best in well-drained soil with even moisture during establishment.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a compact, bushy form. Slender, pale green leaves tint purple-red in fall and winter. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by red and cream bracts. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

An evergreen shrub with an upright growth habit and whorled, horizontal foliage. Long, compound leaves are holly-like with spiny edges. Foliage is glossy, dark green. Large spikes of yellow flowers throughout winter are followed by blue berries in late summer. Attracts birds and bees.
A low-maintenance, groundcover evergreen shrub with small and narrow, gray-green foliage. Small and yellow, papery blooms similar in appearance to Cistus.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded, upright growth habit. Flowers and leaves are sweetly fragrant. Narrow foliage is bright green with woolly white undersides. Velvety violet-blue flowers are arranged in upright stalks. Flowers display long, curling stamens. Blooms in spring, summer, and fall. Attracts hummingbirds and bees. Native to California. Only plant in soil with good drainage.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, upright form. Leaves are small, glossy, wavy-edged, and silvery blue. Stems are dark brownish black. Small, fragrant, deep purple flower clusters bloom in spring.

An evergreen shrub with a dense growth habit. Bell-shaped, apple-red flowers attract hummingbirds. Blooms are most abundant from late fall to spring. Oval, variegated leaves are gray-green with creamy yellow margins.

An evergreen shrub that forms an upright, rounded mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and silver-green. Small, violet, star-shaped flowers bloom year round. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact, tidy, rounded mound. Rosemary-like leaves are linear and gray-green with variegated yellow edges. Small, mauve-pink, star-shaped flowers bloom year round. Adaptable to pruning. Native to Australia.

An evergreen shrub with red, upright stems and a tall, compact form. Narrow leaves are green, tinged reddish. Flowers are made up of cones surrounded by burgundy red bracts that fade to creamy yellow. Blooms at branch tips in winter and spring. Long-lasting cut flower. Likes acidic soils. Does not tolerate phosphorous fertilizers.

A coastal California evergreen shrub with fragrant flower clusters that form a sea of rich blue in spring. Foliage is glossy, oval, 2 inches, and deep green. Natural growth habit is fast, low, and spreading. Do not overwater. Does well on slopes. Beneficial to pollinators and wildlife.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, rounded growth habit. Leaflets are feather-shaped and dark green. Showy trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in clusters of bright lemon yellow. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts hummingbirds.

A semi-evergreen shrub with an open and airy structure. Foliage is medium green and fernlike. Flowers grow in showy clusters of bright yellow with long red stamens. Most cold hardy Caesalpinia species. Native to South America.
An evergreen shrub with a dense, rounded form. Foliage is gray-green, deeply divided, and leathery. Bright yellow, daisy-like flowers bloom from spring through summer.
An evergreen shrub from tropical America. Pansy-like flowers change color from violet to lavender to white in three days time. Leaves are rich green. Attracts birds and butterflies.
An evergreen shrub with lustrous and narrow, dark green leaves. Showy spikes of fragrant, creamy-white flower followed by small black fruits. Branches grow upright and outwards from the base.
A shrubby evergreen tree with a compact, upright form. Gray-green foliage is oval and leathery. From mid-spring to mid-summer, bright orange-red, bottlebrush flowers attract pollinators of all sorts.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a rounded crown. Blue-gray foliage is long, narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Rarely ever produces pollen or fruit.

A medium to large deciduous tree with an open branching habit, adaptable to training. Trunk becomes gnarled with age. Abundant, arching spikes of bright scarlet red candle-like flowers bloom from spring to summer. Attracts hummingbirds. Lush leaves are leathery, bright green, and decorated with sharp thorns.

An evergreen tree with a low canopy and an oval crown. Branches take on a slightly weeping habit over time. Leaves are silvery green, drooping, and willow-like with a fine texture. Dark gray bark is rough. Tiny flower clusters in spring.
A heat and drought-tolerant evergreen tree. Finely-divided, blue-gray leaves are feathery with a tender, fern-like quality. Fragrant, yellow, pom-pom flower clusters cover the branches in winter.

A fast-growing, evergreen tree develops a rounded crown of fine, dark green leaves. Pale yellow flower balls feed bees before dark seed pods form. Use it for quick screens, wind protection, or slope cover where roots can spread. Sun and well-drained soil support strong growth; fallen seed may sprout freely.
A fast-growing evergreen tree with fissured, dark gray bark and lance-shaped, dark green foliage. Creamy white, ball-like flower clusters bloom in winter to early spring.
A small evergreen tree with chocolate brown branches and narrow, silvery blue leaves. Bright yellow, ball-like flower clusters bloom in the winter. Fast-growing and drought-tolerant.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Nearly fruitless, though rarely bears a small immature crop.

An evergreen to semi-evergreen, upright tree with a dense canopy of glossy green, variable leaves and a stout trunk. Bell-shaped cream flowers with reddish markings may appear in warm weather, followed by woody pods. A durable street, screen, or shade tree for heat, drought, and well-drained soils.
An evergreen tree with a graceful, weeping habit. Lush-looking, narrow, bright green leaves cover the branches. Bright yellow, ball-like flower clusters bloom in winter.

An evergreen tree with a compact, oval-pyramidal form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, brown undersides. In late spring, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds. More cold hardy than the species.

An evergreen, upright shade tree with a dense canopy and durable urban landscape character. Leathery deep green leaves create strong screening and shade, while reddish-brown bark peels to reveal smooth pale bark beneath. Fragrant, creamy white flowers bloom in spring and summer, and fruit is woody, green, and capsule-like. This Australian species is useful for streets, screens, and large landscapes, with good tolerance of heat and urban conditions.

An ornamental evergreen shrub or small tree with toothed, elliptic leaves that emerge bronze-red and mature to glossy, deep green. Lightly fragrant, white flower clusters appear in spring. Does not produce edible fruit.

An evergreen tree with an oval, rounded crown. White bark is spongy and exfoliating. Bright green leaves are elliptic. Poofy, white, brush-like flower clusters bloom in summer or fall. Attracts bees. Native to Australia.

commonName: California Laurel, California Bay, Oregon Myrtle, Pepperwood
description: An evergreen tree with a multi-trunking habit and a rounded crown. Densely arranged foliage is dark green above and pale green below. Aromatic leaves are lance-shaped with netted veins and smooth margins. Bay leaves can be used as a seasoning in foods, though the flavor is much stronger and may not come across as favorably as the European Sweet Bay, Laurus nobilis. Use just a pinch in recipes to avoid an overpowering flavor. On female trees, small yellow flowers in spring are followed by green-purple fruits that resemble gumball-sized avocados. Native to California and Oregon.

An evergreen, broad weeping tree with feathery green leaves, rough bark, and light shade. Small yellow-white flowers feed bees, and female trees carry red berry-like fruit into winter. Native to the southern Andes, it suits large dry landscapes and informal groves.

A large, architectural, evergreen tree that forms a broad, dense canopy. Leaves are glossy, green, and smell strongly of camphor when crushed. New growth is reddish. Inconspicuous greenish flowers bare small black fruits. Leaf litter in spring.

A semi-evergreen tree with a broad, spreading, arching habit. Bark becomes furrowed and gray-brown with age. Dark green leaves are leathery and lance-shaped with shallow, pointed lobes. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to Texas and Mexico. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.
A tough evergreen tree with glossy dark green leaves that divide into many leaflets. Small flowers produce yellow-orange fruit that contains black, marble-sized seeds.

An evergreen to semi-evergreen tree with a uniform, upright pyramidal crown. Glossy dark green leaves have pale undersides, and fall acorns feed birds and other wildlife. This selection of a southeastern U.S. native makes a strong street, avenue, or large shade tree. Allow space for its broad mature crown and seasonal acorn drop.

A midsize evergreen tree with a broad, variable canopy, a single or multi-trunk form, and spreading, contorted, arching branches. Bark becomes furrowed and dark gray with age. Leathery, dark green leaves are thick and egg-shaped with sharply toothed, rolled under edges. Inconspicuous female flowers and semi-showy male catkins yield acorns. Native to coastal ranges of California. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A midsized and fast growing evergreen tree, with a dense and rounded form. Lance shaped leaves are dark green and glossy. Creamy white flowers available from spring into midsummer. Attracts birds and pollinators.
A small evergreen tree with a narrow columnar habit. Foliage is light green to yellowish-green, and reddish flower buds burst open to reveal coral red & yellow blooms throughout the year.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with a broad, rounded growth habit and twisted, spreading branches. Bark becomes corky, furrowed, and dark gray-brown with age. Leathery green leaves are egg-shaped with spiny, rolled under edges. Inconspicuous female flowers and male catkins yield acorns. Native to northern Africa and southern Europe. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

An evergreen, pyramidal tree with a straight trunk and broad shade canopy. Large glossy leaves show rich rusty-brown undersides. Fragrant white flowers open in late spring and summer, followed by cone-like seed pods with red seeds. Native species from the southeastern United States. Use as a specimen, screen, or formal avenue tree in well-drained soil.

An evergreen tree with a dense, pyramidal form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In summer, strongly fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds. More cold hardy than the species.

An evergreen tree with a narrow trunk and a spreading to rounded crown. Reddish-gray bark peels off to reveal smooth, white bark underneath. Deep green leaves are leathery, lance-shaped, and aromatic. Foliage emerges reddish. Abundant, fragrant, yellow flowers bloom in spring and summer. Attracts bees.

A moderately fast growing evergreen tree with a rounded, spreading form. Light grayish-brown bark is furrowed and scaly, the trunk becomes more gnarled and twisted with age. Leaves are oblong to ovate, bluish-green, and leathery to the touch. Insignificant spring flowers are followed by mid-sized acorns that provide an important source of food to local wildlife in winter. Native to Southern California.

A broad, evergreen to semi-evergreen crown forms on this long-lived shade tree, with thick dark leaves and rough gray bark. Acorns feed birds and mammals, while deep roots handle heat, wind, and drought. Native to Texas, Oklahoma, and northeastern Mexico, it suits large streets and parks. Sun and well-drained soil support a strong framework.

An evergreen to semi-evergreen, slow-growing tree with a dense, compact canopy and broad shade-tree character. New growth can emerge pink-tinged before maturing to glossy green leaves with gray-green undersides; small greenish spring flowers are followed by red winged samaras. A rare maple for mild-climate landscapes, performing well with well-drained soil and regular irrigation during establishment, with increased drought tolerance as it matures.
Ornamental evergreen tree with white flowers and broadly oval, glossy green foliage. May be partially deciduous in cooler winters.

An evergreen tree with a round, pyramidal form. Leaves are long, broad, and rich green. In spring and summer, fragrant flowers cover the branches. Flowers are white and magnolia-like, yet smaller. Fruits follow. Attracts birds.

commonName: Fernleaf Catalina Ironwood, Santa Cruuz Island Ironwood
description: An evergreen tree with a narrow, conical crown. Deep green leaves palmately divide into scallop-edged leaflets. Clusters of white flowers form in summer. Bark is fibrous, reddish-brown, and shedding. Attracts birds. Native to the Channel Islands of California.

An evergreen shrub with a rounded form that can be trained into a tree shape. Young leaves are small, silvery-blue, spade-shaped, and are used in floral arrangement. Mature leaves are green and scythe-shaped. Reddish seed pods bloom into abundant white flowers in summer. Native to Australia.
An evergreen tree with a strong and smooth trunk that is green in color. Leaves are medium green and maple-like. Abundant fiery red blooms create a dramatic display in late spring and early summer.

Pale papery bark and narrow leaves give this evergreen, rounded tree a light look. White flowers cover the crown in summer and feed bees. Woody seed cups stay on the twigs. It comes from wet parts of Australia and works as a screen or tree. Sun and deep water while young build a steady crown.

commonName: Fragrant Himalayan Champaca, Joy Perfume Flower
description: An evergreen tree with a round, pyramidal form. Leaves are long, broad, and rich green. From mid-winter through spring, highly fragrant flowers cover the branches. Yellow flowers are magnolia-like with strappy petals. Dry, nut-like fruits follow, containing essential oil used in perfumes. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.

An evergreen shrub with a prostrate, weeping form. Broad, oval leaves are dark green. From early spring to summer, fragrant flowers bloom from fuzzy buds. Cup-shaped flowers are creamy white with yellow centers. Fruits follow. Attracts birds. Susceptible to winter burn and leaf drop in cold winters.
A semi-evergreen, multi-branched shrub or small tree with a spreading to weeping habit. Bright green, compound leaves split into many leaflets. Showy, deep yellow flowers grow in terminal clusters.

An evergreen shrub with semi-weeping branches. Needlelike foliage is soft, furry, and light smoky-gray. Poofy, light yellow, brush-like flower clusters bloom in spring. Attracts bees. Native to Australia.

A tropical evergreen tree with upright branches and dense foliage. Adaptable to pruning as a hedge, screen, or standard. Leaves are large, dark green, glossy and leathery. Popular as an indoor tree. Produces multiple aerial roots in wet areas. Best in containers due to aggressively spreading root systems. Considered the premier variety within the species.

An evergreen tree with a broad, round crown and weeping branches. Foliage is more dense and uniform than the species. Bright green leaves are small, oval and fan out at right angles to the stems. Bark is fissured and dark gray-brown. Inconspicuous flowers in spring. Native to Chile.

An evergreen tree with a dense, rounded crown and a variable habit. Takes on a shrubby form in coastal climates. Bark becomes dark gray and smooth or cracked with age. Dark green leaves are oval with spiny, holly-like or smooth margins. Inconspicuous female and male catkins yield acorns. Native to the Mediterranean. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

A tropical evergreen tree with upright branches and dense foliage. Adaptable to pruning as a hedge, screen, or standard. Leaves are large, dark green, glossy and leathery. Popular as an indoor tree. Produces multiple aerial roots in wet areas. Best in containers due to aggressively spreading root systems.

Strips of bark peel from this evergreen, upright tropical tree and reveal green, blue, orange, and maroon. The tall canopy carries glossy leaves and white flowers. Native to wet forests from the Philippines to New Guinea, it needs space. Use only on large frost-free sites with deep soil, steady water, and room for falling limbs.

An evergreen shrub with a dense, vertical form. Broad leaves are dark green. From early spring to summer, highly fragrant flowers bloom from fuzzy buds. Creamy white, yellow-centered flowers are cup-shaped and magnolia-like. Fruits follow. Attracts birds.

An evergreen tree with a variable, shrubby form and a dense canopy. Bark becomes fissured and reddish brown to dark gray with age. Leathery green leaves vary from lance-shaped to egg-shaped, sometimes with spiny, rolled under edges. Inconspicuous female flowers and semi-showy male catkins yield acorns. Native from southern Oregon to southern California. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

An evergreen tree with a single or multi-trunking habit and a variable form, depending on location. Bark becomes scaly and gray-brown with age. Shiny, dark green leaves are oval with prominent venation and toothed, rolled-under edges. Inconspicuous female and male catkins yield acorns. Native to the Channel Islands of California. Thrives in moist conditions. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

Glossy dark green leaves form a dense, rounded crown on this evergreen tree, while fresh growth opens red for added seasonal color. Small white flowers are followed by blue-black, olive-like fruit that feeds birds. Native to forests of East Asia, it makes a useful screen, shade tree, clipped specimen, or formal evergreen backdrop.

An evergreen tree with a compact, oval form. Broad leaves are dark green and super glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In summer, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

A small evergreen tree with triangular to wedge-shaped leaves in gray-green. Bright yellow, ball-like flower clusters bloom in winter to early spring. A multi-trunked, bushy form serves well as a screen or barrier plant.

An evergreen tree with a tall, narrow trunk that graduates to an open-branching crown. Bark is smooth and whitish in color. Leaves are lemon-scented, lance-shaped, and yellowish-green. Inconspicuous white flowers. Native to Australia.

An evergreen, compact tree with a narrow, dense crown for screens, patios, and small sites. Glossy dark green leaves have rusty brown undersides. Large, scented white flowers open from late spring into summer. Cone-like fruit later shows red seeds that feed birds. The parent species is native to the southeastern United States.

An evergreen, slow-growing tree with an open crown, gray bark, and narrow gray-green leaves. This nearly fruitless selection gives classic olive form without heavy fruit drop. Use it as a patio, street, or specimen tree in hot, dry sites. It grows best with full sun, good drainage, and room for its broad crown.

An evergreen tree with an oval-pyramidal form. Broad, extra long leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, brown undersides. In early summer, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are huge, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

A broadleaf evergreen tree with a rounded canopy, smooth cinnamon-red peeling bark, and glossy green leaves. Clusters of pink urn-shaped flowers appear from fall into winter, followed by rounded red to orange fruit. Useful as a specimen or patio tree. Performs best with good drainage and deep, infrequent irrigation once established.

Evergreen oak common in open woodlands, foothills, and canyons of the Southwest United States. Deep grayish blue leaves are leathery, and populate a broad and open canopy. Bark is deeply fissured and grayish brown. Inconspicuous flowers bloom in May, followed by acorns.

A fast growing hybrid evergreen shrub or tree with large, white camellia-like flowers. Elongated semi-evergreen leaves are deep green, and some adopt shades of orange and red in fall, while the others remain green.

An evergreen to semi-evergreen tree with lush green leaves that are leathery and rough to the touch. True flowers are tiny and surrounded by greenish-white petal-like bracts. Flowers are followed by fleshy, strawberry-like fruits.

Evergreen and broadly rounded, this small tree has a light canopy of narrow silver-gray leaves. Golden flower clusters in spring feed bees, then flat seed pods follow. Its deep roots and open shade suit windbreaks, dry screens, and habitat plantings. It grows best in heat, lean soil, and fast drainage.

Deciduous tree native to Eastern Mexico, from Tamaulipas to Oaxaca. Bizzare branching form makes this a handsome specimen, with or without foliage and flowers. Fiery red candlestick-like flowers bloom at the tips of twisting, thorny branches from February to June.

commonName: Narrow-Leaf Bottle Tree, Queensland Bottle Tree
description: A swollen bottle-shaped trunk gives this semi-deciduous, upright tree a striking sculptural form. Narrow green leaves cast light shade, and small cream flowers carry red markings before woody pods form. Native to dry eastern Australia, it suits hot streetscapes and courtyards. Sun and deep, well-drained soil support the trunk; pod hairs can irritate skin.

Evergreen tree, semi-deciduous in colder climates, with a broad, columnar form. Obovate leaves emerge brilliant scarlet then age to a leathery, lustrous dark green. Leaf undersides are heavily tomentose and feature prominent veining, which gives the tree its common name. Scaly acorns emerge in fall. Bark is silvery brown and exfoliates with age. Extremely cold hardy. Native to Mexico. Excellent choice for screens where tomentose leaves trap large amounts of particulate pollution.

A shrubby evergreen tree with an upright, rounded form. Dark green foliage is oval and leathery with woolly, white undersides. From winter to early summer, bright orange-red, bottlebrush flowers attract pollinators of all sorts.

commonName: Norfolk Island Hibiscus, Queensland White Oak
description: A narrow oval crown and gray-green leaves shape this evergreen, upright tree. Pink, hibiscus-like flowers dot the canopy, followed by woody capsules filled with silky fibers. Native to islands off Australia, it suits coastal streets, tall screens, and windbreaks. Sun and room for roots support growth; capsule hairs can cause strong skin and eye irritation.

A fast growing evergreen tree. Juvenile leaves are broad, rounded, and deep bluish green. Mature, elongated leaves emerge after ten to fifteen years of growth. New growth is tinged pink. Cut foliage is used in floral design. Makes an excellent screening tree. Cold hardy to 0 degrees F.

Native to Australia, this evergreen tree has an upright and spreading habit. Old gray-brown bark sheds to feature new orange and red-brown bark in spring. Rich green leaves are oval and lance-shaped. Small white flowers in summer.

An evergreen, fast-growing Australian shrub or small tree with fine-textured foliage and showy yellow winter-to-spring bloom. The open canopy and bright flowers bring seasonal structure to low-water landscapes. It performs best in well-drained soil, with light pruning used to develop a durable framework.

Semi-deciduous tree with a stout trunk and conical habit. Leaves are palmately lobed and deep bluish-green, with pale green felty undersides. Showy, deep pink or red bell-shaped flowers are followed by fruits.

An evergreen tree with an upright, open form. Bark is smooth and white or light gray. Leaves are bluish green or gray-green to dark green, sickle-shaped, and tinge bronze in winter. Fluffy pink flowers bloom in winter or spring. Native to Australia.

An evergreen tree with gnarled, ascending branches. Beige-gray-brown bark is spongy and exfoliating. Gray-green leaves are narrow and rounded. Poofy, pink, brush-like flower clusters bloom throughout the year. Attracts bees. Native to Australia.

Evergreen tree with a dense and spreading form. Bluish-green leaves are oval in shape, bark is smooth and light brown in color and later matures to gray. Abundant, creamy white flowers are available in spring and summer. Attracts birds and pollinators.

A crown of dark pointed leaves tops this evergreen, rounded tree. White bottlebrush flowers line the branches and feed bees, while pale papery bark adds winter texture. Native to Australian forests and streams, it works as a tall screen or street tree. Sun, drainage, and establishment water support growth; leaf tips can scratch skin.

An evergreen, fast-growing Australian shrub or small tree with fine-textured foliage and showy yellow winter-to-spring bloom. The open canopy and bright flowers bring seasonal structure to low-water landscapes. It performs best in well-drained soil, with light pruning used to develop a durable framework.

commonName: Purple Peppermint Tree, Australian Willow Myrtle
description: An evergreen, graceful Australian tree with weeping branchlets and narrow aromatic foliage. Small white spring-to-summer flowers dot the canopy, followed by fine seed capsules. It is useful as a light screen, specimen, or patio tree and thrives in well-drained soil with moderate to low irrigation after establishment.

An evergreen tree that is rounded or vase shaped. Bark is blackish-brown, furrowed, and non-shedding. Lance-shaped leaves are gray-blue to gray-green and tinge bronze in winter. Fluffy, pink or red flowers bloom in fall through spring. Tolerant of drought and various soil types. Native to Australia.

A fast growing small tree with a broad, low branching canopy. Leaves are long and sickle-shaped, and a smooth white trunk is spotted with patches of rough brown bark. Showy yellow flowers pop out of red-capped buds in fall and spring.

An evergreen tree with a narrow trunk and an open-branching crown. Bark is gray-brown and furrowed. Leaves are dark green, leathery, and are usually egg-shaped or lance-shaped with frequent variations. Showy, red flowers are arranged in long clusters. Native to Australia.

A fast growing evergreen tree with exfoliating brownish grey bark. Leaves are gray-green, sickle-shaped and tinge bronze in winter. Fluffy, white flowers bloom in summer, followed by goblet-shaped capsules. Native to Australia.
Evergreen tree with an upright and spreading habit. Narrow, gray-green foliage. Produces little, if any, mature fruits.

An evergreen tree with a round, oval form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, russet-brown undersides. In summer, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

A large, semi-evergreen tree with smooth dark brown bark and light green, simple, ovate leaves. Historically recognized as a sacred tree and often found in religious sites, as hinted to by the species name.

An evergreen tree with a round, oval form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In summer, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

An evergreen, narrow-canopy tree with graceful, willow-like foliage and a light-filtering shade effect. Creamy yellow flower clusters appear seasonally, followed by narrow seed pods. It suits streetscapes, open landscapes, and dry-climate sites where deep, infrequent irrigation and well-drained soil support strong rooting.

commonName: Shrub Coral Tree, Bidwell's Coral Bean
description: A deciduous shrub or small tree with an open branching habit, adaptable to training. Abundant, arching spikes of crimson red, beak-like flowers bloom from spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds. Lush leaves are leathery, bright green, and decorated with sharp thorns. Native to South America.
A large and upright evergreen tree with fine-textured ferny foliage. Brush-like clusters of long curved flowers in golden orange.

An evergreen tree with an oval, pyramidal crown. Broad leaves are dark green with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In late winter and spring, highly fragrant flowers profusely cover the branches. Abundant, white flowers are cup-shaped and magnolia-like. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds.

An evergreen tree with a rounded crown and smooth, peeling bark in cream and gray tones. Young stems carry round, blue-gray leaves often used for cutting, while mature leaves become longer and green. Small white flowers followed by woody seed capsules feed bees. Use as a drought-tough shade, screen, or specimen tree where falling bark and capsules can be managed.

An evergreen tree with an open-branching crown. Bark is brown and exfoliating. Young leaves are silvery green, coin shaped, and are often used in floral arrangements. Mature leaves are medium green and lance shaped. Inconspicuous white flowers. Native to Australia. Tolerates coastal exposure.

An evergreen tree with an upright, conical form and an irregular spreading habit at maturity. Bark is gray. Lance-shaped, light green leaves are densely coated in silky hairs than shine silver in sunlight. Male and female flowers are cone-like and appear on separate plants at branch tips. Male flowers emit a vanilla-scent and are composed of pinkish-yellow florets, tightly packed in the shape of a golfball. Female flowers resemble a small artichoke-like globe and produce a nut after fertilization.

An evergreen tree with a dense pyramidal crown of glossy, dark green leaves with yellowish undersides. Inconspicuous blooms are followed by medium-sized acorns in fall. Consistent upright growth makes this tree ideal for use as a street tree planting, or it can be planted en masse. Attracts birds and wildlife.

A dwarf, slow-growing evergreen shrub or tree with a rounded growth habit. Gray-green foliage is small, narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Rarely sets fruit unless another fruiting olive is nearby to pollenize.

An upright evergreen tree with spreading, pendulous branches. Vivid green, oval leaves are leathery in texture, and slightly toothed at the margins. Intricate, star-shaped greenish white flowers are available in abundance at branch tips, from late spring into mid-summer. Flowers are folowed by pinwheel shaped fruits. Attracts beneficial insects.

Tropical evergreen tree with an upright, rounded form and rough gray bark. Emerald green, sickle-shaped leaves crowd branch tips. Small creamy white flowers are available in summer, followed by edible plum-like fruits. Fruits are often used in jams or jellies.

commonName: Southern Live Oak, Virginia Live Oak
description: A semi-evergreen tree with a stout trunk and massive, spreading, contorted branches that sometimes touch the ground. Bark becomes dark and checkered with age. Shiny, dark green leaves are oval, unlobed and thick. Inconspicuous female and male catkins yield acorns. Native to the southeastern U.S. and Mexico. Provides habitat and food for numerous animal species.

An evergreen tree with a round, pyramidal form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In late spring, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

An evergreen tree with a compact, pyramidal form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In summer, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

A small evergreen tree with broad, dark green leaves. In late spring and early fall, wine red to pink colored, banana scented flowers emerge. Seedy, cone-like fruits follow. Attracts birds. Can be sheared to form hedges.

An evergreen Australian-native tree with a gracefully arching, multi-trunk form. Smooth red bark peels to reveal white layers beneath. Shiny, gray-green leaves are linear, and held at branch tips. Creamy golden yellow flowers bloom in small clusters in summer, followed by ornamental fruit capsules.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple trunks that are light gray and become gnarled with age. Branches form a rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is long, narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. Certified fruitless variety is grafted onto disease-resistant rootstock. Rarely produces pollen or fruit. For complete information on planting and caring for Swan Hill Olives® trees, please visit https://swanhillolives.com/ .

commonName: Sydney Red Gum, Smooth Barked Apple
description: Native to Australia, this evergreen tree has an upright and spreading habit. Grey bark exfoliates to reveal rusty-red layers underneath. Leaves are lanceolate, and lustrous dark green. Small white flowers in summer.

An evergreen tree with a dwarf, pyramidal form. Broad, rounded leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In summer and fall, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

A deciduous to evergreen, columnar oak tree with dark green, deeply veined leaves and pale, felted undersides. It stays evergreen in warm climates but may shed leaves where winters are colder. Young bark has a bold, ridged texture. Small acorns feed wildlife. Use as a shade tree, vertical accent, or climate-ready specimen in large landscapes.

An evergreen tree with a round, vase-shaped form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. From spring to fall, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

A semi-deciduous flowering tree with a stout, shade-giving, umbrella crown and a single trunk. Lengthy compound leaves are divided into many oblong, light green leaflets. Flowers are frilly, lipped, and peachy yellow. Blooms from late spring through summer. Papery wing-shaped fruit swirls like helicopter blades when tossed in the air.

A small evergreen tree with a rounded, shrubby form. Oval, leathery foliage is dark green with variegated gold-splashed centers. From winter to early summer, bright orange-red, bottlebrush flowers attract pollinators of all sorts.

An evergreen tree with a round, pyramidal form. Broad leaves are dark green and glossy with fuzzy, rusty-brown undersides. In late spring, fragrant flowers emerge from velvety buds. Flowers are large, white, and cup-shaped. Seedy, cone-like fruits mature in fall. Attracts birds.

An evergreen tree with a narrow trunk and a spreading to rounded crown. Reddish-gray bark peels off to reveal smooth, white bark underneath. Deep green leaves are leathery, lance-shaped, and aromatic. Foliage tinges red in cool weather. Fragrant, yellow flowers bloom in spring and summer. Attracts bees. Native to Australia.
An evergreen shrub with weeping branches and flat, elliptic, silvery-blue-green leaves. Bristlelike flowers are known for their long, red stamens. Attracts bees and hummingbirds.

An evergreen shrub with a dense, vertical form. Broad leaves are dark green. From early spring to summer, highly fragrant flowers bloom from fuzzy buds. Creamy white, yellow-centered flowers are cup-shaped and magnolia-like. Fruits follow. Attracts birds.

commonName: White Fragrant Himalayan Champaca, Joy Perfume Flower
description: An evergreen tree with a round, pyramidal form. Leaves are long, broad, and rich green. From mid-winter through spring, highly fragrant flowers cover the branches. White flowers are magnolia-like with strappy petals. Dry, nut-like fruits follow, containing essential oil used in perfumes. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.

An evergreen, fast-growing Australian shrub or small tree with fine-textured foliage and showy yellow winter-to-spring bloom. The open canopy and bright flowers bring seasonal structure to low-water landscapes. It performs best in well-drained soil, with light pruning used to develop a durable framework.

A slow-growing evergreen tree with single or multiple gray trunks that become gnarled with age. Branches form a dense, rounded crown. Gray-green foliage is narrowly elliptic and silvery underneath. This variety is semi-fruitless- not reliably fruitless. It may go years with no fruit, but some years it may bear a large crop.
A vigorous, fast-growing tree fern with a tall trunk and bright green fronds. Can tolerate full shade.
A vigorous, fast-growing tree fern with a tall trunk and bright green fronds. Can tolerate full shade.

A semi-evergreen fern with triangular, arching, cool green fronds. Coppery pink new growth unfurls from the center of each clump. Fall color changes to rust-red. Red sori develop on the undersides of fronds in winter. Forms offsets via rhizomes.
A tropical evergreen fern with a dense, clump-forming habit. Lush green fronds are mostly upright and divide into narrow teeth. Spreads by rhizomes.

commonName: Brilliance Autumn Fern, Japanese Shield Fern
description: A semi-evergreen fern with triangular, arching, cool green fronds. Brilliant coppery pink new growth unfurls from the center of each clump. Fall color changes to rust-red. Red sori develop on the undersides of fronds in winter. Forms offsets via rhizomes.

commonName: Button Fern, New uzealand Cliff Brake
description: An evergreen fern that forms a compact, spreading clump. Arching, lush green fronds are divided into small, rounded teeth. Leaf stalks age to dark red. Spreads by rhizomes.
A tropical semi-evergreen fern with a compact, clump-forming habit. Fronds are yellow-green, mostly upright, and divide into small, rounded teeth.

An evergreen fern with a clumping habit. Flattened, fingerlike foliage resembles arching, variegated ribbons with slightly wavy edges. Grayish-green in color, each blade has a white stripe down its center.
An evergreen fern with attractive dark-green fronds. On the same plant, sterile fronds are low and spreading while fertile fronds are stiff and upright.
A graceful deciduous woodland fern that tends to be a slow spreader. Lacy, upright fronds are silvery-gray. Stems are dark purple.

A large evergreen fern with a clumping habit. Fronds are deep green, leathery, and arching. Pinnae are divided into a fishbone pattern. Sori develop in a chain-like pattern on the undersides of pinnae. Native to western North America, including California.
An evergreen fern that spreads to form a bushy, understory groundcover. Fronds are leathery, stiff, triangular, and deep green with a frilly, finely cut look. Popularly used in floral arrangements.
A spreading evergreen fern with stiff fronds that are clad in glossy, dark green, holly-like leaflets.
A graceful deciduous woodland fern that tends to be a prolific spreader. Lacy, silver-green fronds are arching, slightly twisted, and contrast beautifully with dark purple midribs and stems.
An evergreen fern with a bushy, clumping growth habit. Fronds are triangular, glossy, dark green, and lacy. Unfurling fiddleheads resemble drooping tassels.
An evergreen fern that forms a dense clump of lush green foliage. Fronds are lacy, triangular and upright to arching. Fiddleheads in winter are very fuzzy. Spreads by rhizomes.
An evergreen fern that spreads to form a bushy, understory groundcover. Fronds are leathery, stiff, triangular, and deep green with a frilly, finely cut look. Popularly used in floral arrangements.

An evergreen perennial that forms upright canes, which are clothed in fluffy, thread-like, bright green foliage. Small white flowers bloom in spring and give way to orange fruits. Can tolerate full shade.
A graceful fern with outwardly arching, very finely-cut, light green fronds that emerge from a single crown.

A clumping, evergreen perennial with upright foxtail-like stems densely clothed in fine bright green foliage. Small white flowers may be followed by red berries on mature plants. Useful in containers, shaded borders, and protected courtyards. Performs best with well-drained soil and regular to moderate irrigation.
A hardy deciduous fern that forms a vase-shaped clump of arching, feathery fronds in rich green. Spreads by rhizomes.

commonName: Red Dwarf Tree Fern, Red Brauzilian Tree Fern
description: An evergreen fern with a crown of spreading, dark green fronds that emerge pinkish-bronze. Develops a short trunk with maturity.
A spreading evergreen fern with stiff fronds that are clad in glossy, deep green, holly-like leaflets.

A hairy-stemmed fern with a clumping, slowly-spreading growth habit. Deep-green, leathery, diamond to fan-shaped pinnules are held together by dark, wiry stems. New growth is rosy-pink. Place in a shady, moist, and well-drained site. Thrives best in humusy soil. Appreciates humidity. Deciduous in the temperate climates of USDA zones 8 - 10; evergreen in semi-tropical to tropical climates.

commonName: Silver Lady Fern, Dwarf Tree Fern
description: An evergreen fern with attractive bright green fronds that grow atop a short, slender trunk. Noted for fast growth and a symmetrical crown.
An evergreen fern with a clumping, fountain-like growth habit. Fronds are triangular, glossy, medium green, and lacy.

A soft, delicate fern with fan-shaped, cool-green leaflets held together by dark, wiry stems. Place in a shady, moist, and well-drained site. Thrives best in humusy soil. Appreciates humidity. 'Mairisii' is a cold-hardy variety; evergreen in mild winter climates.

An evergreen perennial with arching, trailing stems that are covered in soft, needle-like leaves. Inconspicuous flowers give way to bright red berries. Often used in hanging baskets and containers. Can tolerate full shade.

An evergreen tree fern forms a fibrous trunk topped by a broad crown of soft, arching green fronds. Spores develop beneath mature fronds instead of flowers or fruit. It is native to cool, moist forests of southeastern Australia and Tasmania. Use it for shaded courtyards, entries, and woodland beds with rich soil and steady moisture.

A tropical semi-evergreen fern with a dense, clump-forming habit. Fronds are bright green, mostly upright, and divide into narrow teeth. Spores develop on undersides of fronds. Spreads by fuzzy rhizomes.

An evergreen fern with a robust, clumping growth habit. Fronds are upright to arching, leathery, dark green, and lance-shaped. Pinnae are single-divided in a fishbone pattern. Native to North America, including California. Provide regular water during growth, occasional watering after establishment.

commonName: Adagio Japanese Silver Grass, Eulalia, Dwarf Maidenhair Grass
description: An ornamental perennial grass that forms a dwarf, fountain-like clump. Fine, arching leaves are silvery gray-green. Fall foliage turns orange-purple in cool climates. From late summer to frost, tall stalks are topped with pinkish, tassel-like flowerheads that mature to large, fluffy, tan-white plumes. Flower stalks extend 1 - 2 feet above the foliage.
An elegant, shade-loving perennial grass for woodland gardens. Gracefully arching blades in bright golden-green.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Leaves are variegated light green with white edges. Fine, upright-arching foliage forms a compact, fountain-like clump. Small, yellow flower spikes emit a sweet fragrance in summer. Tolerates seaside, inland, and drought conditions.

A semi-evergreen perennial grass that forms a large, fountain-like clump. Fine-textured leaf blades are yellowish-gray-green. Tall flower heads age from gray-green to amber-tan. Blooms in spring and summer. Native to Morocco.
An elegant, shade-loving perennial grass for woodland gardens. Gracefully arching blades in rich green with yellow striping.
A perennial grass that forms a tussock of narrow leaf blades in lime green. Tan to silver-white flowerheads bloom from late summer to fall.

A perennial grass that forms airy, fountain-like clumps with woody stems. Leaf blades are bright green and resemble bamboo. In late summer through fall, lacy flower stalks emerge light lavender and turn creamy tan.
An evergreen perennial grass that forms a dense, fountain-like clump. Fine-textured leaf blades are vibrant blue-gray. Flower heads age to amber-tan. Blooms in summer. Native to Europe.

A shade-tolerant grass-like perennial that forms a slowly spreading tuft of evergreen foliage. Black-purple leaves are fine and arching. White-pink, bell-shaped summer flowers are followed by small glossy fruits.

A warm-season, deciduous ornamental grass with upright blue-green foliage and chartreuse seedheads that mature to long-lasting blonde. The distinctive horizontal inflorescences provide strong texture in meadows, mass plantings, and dry borders. It thrives in lean, well-drained soil and is native to western North America.

An evergreen perennial that forms a robust, grass-like, fountain-shaped clump. Blue-green stems are stiffly upright, cylindrical and leafless. Small yellow-brown flower clusters are present in spring and summer.

commonName: Blue Dune Blue Lyme Grass, Blue Rye
description: A semi-evergreen, rhizomatous perennial grass with an upright, spreading habit. Broad, metallic blue-gray blades form bold clumps that provide strong color contrast in mass plantings, coastal landscapes, dry slopes, and large containers. Wheat-colored flower spikes rise above the foliage in summer. Best placed where its vigorous spread is useful for fast coverage, erosion control, or contained in planters. Thrives in sandy, well-drained soils and performs well with coastal exposure, wind, salt, and heat.

A semi-evergreen perennial grass that forms a compact, fountain-like clump. Fine-textured leaf blades age from blue-green to dark green to buff. Flower heads age to amber-tan. Blooms in summer. Native to Europe.

A warm-season, deciduous to semi-evergreen grass with fine blue-green blades and distinctive eyelash-like seedheads held horizontally above the foliage. This western North American native is useful in meadow plantings, low-water lawns, and dry borders. It thrives in lean, well-drained soils and high heat.
A perennial grass forming graceful, fountain-like clumps of narrow blue-gray leaves. Tall beige flower heads appear in spring.
An evergreen perennial with silvery blue, grass-like foliage. Roots typically form wide, arching tufts. Native to New Zealand.

commonName: Blue uzinger Blue Sedge, Glaucous Sedge
description: An evergreen perennial that forms wide, arching tufts. Grasslike foliage is glaucous gray-blue-green. Native to New Zealand.
An evergreen grass-like perennial. Fine, green, arching foliage forms a rounded clump. Small, yellow flower spikes emit a sweet fragrance in spring. Tolerates seaside, inland, and drought conditions.

A warm-season ornamental grass with a compact, vase-like form. Showy flower plumes in creamy-buff are fuzzy, fluffy and bottlebrush-like. From early summer into fall, feathery blooms top the slender leaf blades. Green foliage flushes red in spring and summer, turning fully bright burgundy in fall. Fine in containers. Tolerates drought and poor soils.

A semi-evergreen perennial grass that forms a fountain-like clump. Coarse-textured leaf blades are powdery-blue-green. Nodding, feathery flower heads age to amber-tan. Blooms in spring and summer. Native to California.

An herbaceous perennial with deep green, upright, grass-like foliage. Clumping roots spread to form a sturdy carpet that can tolerate moderate foot traffic. Native to coastal California. Goes dormant in peak summer heat.

An evergreen perennial that forms a grass-like clump. Gray-green stems are stiff, cylindrical and leafless. Nonshowy yellow-brown flower clusters are present from spring to fall. Tolerates more heat, dry shade, and drought than J. effusus. Native to California and beyond.

An herbaceous evergreen perennial with medium green, long, grassy foliage. Sturdy roots spread to form a finely textured carpet that can tolerate moderate foot traffic. Native to sandy California dunes.

A cool-season bunchgrass that forms a clump of bright green leaf blades. Without irrigation in hot summers, foliage turns gold and regenerates green in winter. Spikes of silvery, papery flowerheads rise up in summer. Does well under oaks and in dry shade. California native.
A perennial grass that forms a tussock of narrow leaf blades in blue-green. Tan to silver-white flowerheads bloom from late summer to fall.
A perennial grass that forms a tussock of narrow leaf blades in vibrant emerald green. Tan to silver-white flowerheads bloom from late summer to fall.

commonName: Canyon Prince Lyme Grass, Giant Wild Rye
description: A perennial grass that forms open, mounding clumps of coarse, icy silver-blue leaf blades. Tan flower spikes arise 1 - 2 feet above the foliage in summer. Spreads vigorously by rhizomes to form colonies. Continues to spread if not contained. Good for erosion control. Drought tolerant but looks better with occasional spring/summer water, especially inland. Native to the Channel Islands and Southern California.

A compact South African marsh plant with upright, jointed, matte blue-green stems that grow as wide as the diameter of a pencil. Each joint is enveloped by an ornamental papery bracht that blends hues of cream, rust, scarlet, and brown. Dark brown flower heads grow at the tips of the foliage.

commonName: Carman's Gray Spreading Rush, Wire Grass
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a grass-like clump. Bluish-gray stems are stiff, cylindrical and leafless. Nonshowy yellow-brown flower clusters are present from spring to fall. Tolerates more heat, dry shade, and drought than J. effusus. Native to California and beyond.

An evergreen perennial that forms a grass-like, fountain-shaped clump. Glossy, bright green stems are stiff, cylindrical and leafless. Small yellow-brown flower clusters are present in spring and summer.

A warm-season ornamental grass with a compact, densely clumped form. Fuzzy, pink flower plumes are long, feathery and bottlebrush-like. Blooms start in early summer, slowly maturing to a tan color well into fall. Fine-textured foliage is light grayish-green, turning a dormant straw-brown in winter. Tolerates summer-dry conditions as well as coastal climates. Spreads slowly via rhizomes. Drought tolerant once established.

An evergreen perennial that forms a grass-like, fountain-shaped clump of unusual, spiral-type foliage. Glossy, dark green stems are corkscrewed, cylindrical and leafless. Small yellow-brown flower clusters are present in spring and summer.

A clumping evergreen grass that forms a dense, upright to arching fountain. Leaf blades are lengthy, finely-textured, and gray-green. From late summer through fall, slender flower stalks emerge light purple and age to honey-tan. Native to California and beyond.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Fine, light green foliage forms a mounding clump. Small, inconspicuous yellow flower spikes in summer. Tolerates seaside, inland, shade and drought conditions. Resistant to root rot.

A warm-season ornamental grass with a dwarf, vase-like form. Pinkish buff-white flower panicles are fuzzy, fluffy and bottlebrush-like. From mid-summer into fall, the feathery plumes top slender, green leaf blades. Foliage turns bronze-orange in fall. Fine in containers. Tolerates poor soils and drought once established.
A rush-like perennial with hollow, upright stems. Stems are bright green with dark brown rings at the nodes. Spreads to develop a fine-textured, dense mat.

A shade-tolerant evergreen perennial that forms a slowly spreading tuft of grass-like foliage. Dark green leaf blades are fine and arching. Nonshowy summer flowers are followed by small glossy fruits. Tolerates light foot traffic.

A hybrid, warm-season ornamental grass with a dwarf, fountain-like form. Feathery, pinkish flower panicles are long, fluffy and foxtail-like. Plumes age to a creamy buff from late summer through fall. Burgundy-bronze-infused foliage is finely textured and upright to arching. Semi-evergreen. May self-sow aggressively, depending on the location. Sometimes sold as 'Red Riding Hood' or 'Rubrum Dwarf.'

A compact South African marsh plant with upright, jointed, matte blue-green stems that grow as wide as the diameter of a pencil. Each joint is enveloped by an ornamental papery bract that blends hues of cream, gold, rust, and brown. Dark brown flower heads grow at the tips of the foliage.
An evergreen perennial grass that forms a durable, fountain-like clump. Fine-textured leaf blades are silver-blue. Flower heads age to amber-tan. Blooms in summer. Native to Europe.

commonName: Elk Blue California Gray Rush, Wiregrass
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a grass-like clump. Blue-gray stems are stiff, cylindrical and leafless. Nonshowy yellow-brown flower clusters are present from spring to fall. Tolerates more heat, dry shade, and drought than J. effusus. Native to California.

commonName: European Grey Sedge, Eurasian Grey Sedge, "Berkeley Sedge"
description: An evergreen perennial with dark green, grass-like foliage. Roots form dense, broad, arching clumps. Spikes of small flower heads emerge green and turn brown. Native to central Europe and northern Africa.
An herbaceous evergreen perennial with golden-green, grass-like foliage. Roots form arching tufts. Native to Japan. Can tolerate full shade.
An herbaceous evergreen perennial that forms an arching, mounding tuft. Grass-like foliage is rich green with variegated lime-green edges. Native to Japan. Can tolerate full shade.

A warm-season ornamental grass with an upright form. Vertical foliage is finely textured and bluish-green. Airy, pinkish flower panicles are long and foxtail-like. Flowers age to a dark wheat-gold from late summer through fall. Evergreen in mild climates. Drought tolerant once established, but more robust with regular water. Sparsely spreads, if it all.

commonName: Fiber Optic Grass, Low Bulrush, Bullrush
description: An evergreen sedge that forms a dense bunch. Slender leaf blades are bright green. In spring, wiry stems topped with small flowerheads resemble a mound of fiber optics. Native to California and beyond.
An evergreen grass-like perennial. Fine, blue-green foliage forms a compact, mounding clump. Small, brownish flower spikes appear in summer. Tolerates seaside, inland, shade and drought conditions.

An evergreen perennial with dark green, grass-like foliage. Roots slowly spread to form wide, arching, mop-like clumps. Spikes of small flower heads emerge pearly-green and turn brown. Native to California.

botanicalName: Pennisetum massaicum, P. messiacum, Cenchrus massiacus
description: A deciduous, warm-season ornamental grass with a neat, fountain-like form. Feathery, red flower panicles are fuzzy and foxtail-like. Blooms start in summer, aging to a creamy-tan in fall. Medium green foliage is finely textured and arching. Heat and drought tolerant once established. Aggresively self-sows, depending on the location. Invasive in some areas.

botanicalName: Pennisetum setaceum, Pennisetum rupellii, Cenchrus setaceus
description: A deciduous, warm-season ornamental grass with a neat, fountain-like form. Feathery, red flower panicles are fuzzy and foxtail-like. Blooms start in summer, aging to a creamy-tan in fall. Medium green foliage is finely textured and arching. Heat and drought tolerant once established. Aggresively self-sows, depending on the location. Invasive in some areas.
A large, clumping, rush-like perennial with tall, arching reed-like stems. Fluffy, feathery whorls grow along evenly spaced nodes. Lush and rich green. Good in marshy, wet soils.

An evergreen perennial used as an ornamental grass. Foliage is a frosty silver-blue-green. Fine textured leaves form relaxed, mop-like clumps. May spread vigorously in moist areas. Great in containers and in borders. Native to New Zealand.

A perennial grass that forms a low clump of finely textured, gray-green leaf blades. Shimmering buff-gold flowerheads appear on tall, sturdy stalks in summer. The feathery flowerheads audibly rustle in the breeze.

A semi-evergreen perennial grass that forms a large clump of long, arching leaf blades. Grayish green foliage fades to yellow-beige by winter. Wispy summer flowers bloom in hazy plumes of tan-gold. Birds and some mammals enjoy the seeds. Deep root systems aid in erosion control. Native to the Southwestern U.S., including California.

commonName: Gold Bar Japanese Silver Grass, Eulalia
description: An ornamental perennial grass that form an upright clump. Linear, slightly arching leaves are dark green with boldly variegated horizontal yellow bands. From late summer to frost, tall stalks are topped with burgundy, tassel-like flowerheads that mature to large, fluffy, tan-white plumes. Flower stalks extend 1 - 2 feet above foliage.
An herbaceous evergreen perennial with variegated creamy yellow and deep green, grass-like foliage. Roots form arching, mounding tufts. Native to Japan. Can tolerate full shade.

An evergreen, clumping grass-like perennial with narrow gold-and-green variegated blades. The low, tidy texture works along water features, shaded paths, and container edges. It thrives in consistently moist to wet soil and can tolerate shallow standing water, making it useful where irrigation is regular.
A rush-like perennial with hollow, upright stems. Stems are bright green with dark brown rings at the nodes.
Clump forming ornamental grass with medium green blades and red tips that intensify in summer and fall

commonName: Japanese Silver Grass, Eulalia, Maiden Grass
description: An ornamental perennial grass that forms an upright, fountain-like clump. Linear, arching leaves are green. Many cultivars have bold variegation. From late summer to frost, tall stalks are topped with tassel-like flowerheads that mature to large, fluffy, silvery-white plumes. Flower stalks extend 1 - 2 feet above the foliage.
A perennial grass that forms a tussock of narrow dark green leaf blades. Mauve-tan flowerheads bloom from spring to summer.
A sturdy perennial grass that forms fountains of bright green foliage. Feathery flower heads grow 6 feet high in plumes of purple to beige.

botanicalName: Pennisetum orientale 'Karley Rose' PP 12,909, Cenchrus orientalis
description: A warm-season ornamental grass with an upright, clumping form. Feathery, smoky-pink flower panicles are long, fuzzy and bottlebrush-like. Flower persist from mid-summer into fall. Fine-textured, fountain-like foliage is darker green and more cold hardy than the species. Drought tolerant once established.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Strappy, rich green foliage forms an arching, fountain-like clump. Very large, yellow flower clusters emit a sweet fragrance in late spring. Tolerates seaside, inland, shade and drought conditions. Tolerates more water than other Lomandras. Slow to reach full size. Evergreen to zone 9.

A South African marsh plant with upright, jointed, matte blue-green stems that grow as wide as the diameter of a pencil. Each joint is enveloped by an ornamental papery bracht that blends hues of cream, gold, rust, and brown. Dark brown flower heads grow at the tips of the foliage.

commonName: Leafy Reed Grass, Mendocino Reed Grass
description: A California native bunchgrass that forms a fountain of blue-green foliage. Arching, silvery-purple seedheads age to golden-brown. Blooms in mid-spring and early summer. Low maintenance and hardy.

Lime and cream stripes run through the narrow leaves of this evergreen, clumping strappy-leaf perennial. The arching mound adds year-round motion without blocking views, and small yellow flower spikes sit near the base. Use it on slopes, medians, or dry shade edges. Sun or shade, drained soil, and occasional deep water keep the foliage fresh.

commonName: Lime Tough / Lime Tuff Dwarf Mat Rush
description: An evergreen grass-like perennial. Fine, bright green, upright foliage forms a compact clump. Small, yellow flower spikes emerge in summer. Adaptable to many soils.
A perennial grass that forms dense clumps. Leaf blades are finely-textured, arching, and light blue-gray. In late summer through fall, plume-like flower stalks emerge purple and age to silvery-gray.

A deciduous prairie grass that forms an upright clump. Finely textured leaf blades turn from blue-green to showy bronze-red in fall and winter. Non-showy late summer flowerheads age to fluffy silvery seedpods.

A warm-season, vase-like ornamental grass, one of the the smallest dwarfs available. Showy, buff-white flower panicles are fuzzy, fluffy and bottlebrush-like. From late summer into fall, the feathery plumes top slender, green leaf blades. Foliage turns golden-brown in fall. Fine in containers. Tolerates poor soils and drought once established.

A dwarf, African sedge with smooth, triangular stalks that splay out into whorls of finely textured, grassy green foliage. Thrives in wetlands and with its roots submerged in water. Spreads quickly by rhizomes to form colonies. May spread aggressively. Dies back in frost. Fine in containers.

commonName: Mexican Feather Grass, Silky Thread Grass
description: A perennial grass with a billowing, undulating form. Bright green foliage is very fine and airy. Feathery, green awns age to golden-tan in summer-fall. Generously self-sows. Known to spread invasively in California.

A semi-evergreen perennial grass that forms spreading, rolling clumps. Can be mowed to 1 - 2 inches. Sweeping, fine-textured leaf blades are silvery-blue. New growth starts in late winter, early for the species. Tall flower heads age to amber-tan. Blooms in summer. Native to North America and Eurasia, including California. Tolerates more shade than other fescues.
A shade-tolerant grass-like perennial that forms a slowly spreading tuft of evergreen foliage. Dark green leaves are fine and arching. Nonshowy summer flowers are followed by small glossy fruits.

commonName: Morning Light Japanese Silver Grass, Eulalia
description: An ornamental perennial grass that forms an upright, fountain-like clump. Fine, arching leaves are silvery-green with variegated white margins. From late summer to frost, tall stalks are topped with copper-red, tassel-like flowerheads that mature to large, fluffy, silvery-white plumes. Flower stalks extend 1 - 2 feet above the foliage.
An ornamental grass with a fountain-like habit. Leaf blades are spiky and gray-green. Foliage turns red in fall. Feathery, ruby-pink flowerheads rise up in summer.
A bunchgrass with gracefully arching, variegated dark green and white leaf blades. Foliage blushes pink in cool weather. Tan, airy flowers arise on tall stalks in spring and summer.

A perennial ornamental grass with a clumping growth habit. Drooping seed heads resemble flattened oats that emerge green and mature to bronzy-mauve. Leaves are broad, arching and bright green. The leaf structure resembles bamboo. Native to North America.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Fine, blue-green foliage forms a fountain-like clump. Small yellow flower spikes emit a sweet fragrance in spring. Tolerates seaside, inland and drought conditions. Slightly larger than L. 'Breeze' with more broad, upright leaf blades.

An ornamental perennial grass that forms a stiff, upright clump. Rush-like foliage is gray-green and slightly hairy. Tall flower stalks carry fluffy, tassel-like inflorescences in cream to brown. Flower stalks extend 1 - 2 feet above the foliage.

A perennial that forms stiff, upright clumps of spiky, strap-like leaves. Foliage is striped in glowing orange and olive green. Branching clusters of pure white flowers bloom from spring into summer. Flower are iris-like, though less frilly. Spreads by rhizomes.
An herbaceous evergreen perennial with orange and olive green, finely textured, grass-like foliage. Roots form dense, weeping tufts. Native to New Zealand.

A sturdy perennial grass that forms clumps of variegated green and white foliage. Feathery flower plumes are toned pinkish-golden-green. Blooms in summer are followed by sterile seedheads. A compact variety.
A California native bunchgrass that forms fountains of deep green to tan foliage. Arching, silvery-purple seedheads age to golden-brown.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Fine, weeping, blue-gray to gray-green foliage forms a compact, mounding clump. Small, yellow-orange flower spikes emit a sweet fragrance in summer. Tolerates seaside, inland, shade and drought conditions. Resistant to root rot.

An African sedge with smooth, triangular stalks that splay out into whorls of finely textured, grassy green foliage. Thrives in wetlands and with its roots submerged in water. Spreads quickly by rhizomes to form colonies. May spread aggressively. Dies back in frost.

A coastal semi-evergreen grass that forms spreading, rolling clumps. Can be mowed to 1 - 2 inches. Sweeping, fine-textured leaf blades are vibrant silvery-blue. Tall flower heads age to amber-tan. Blooms in summer. Native to North America and Eurasia, including California. Tolerates more shade than other fescues.

A perennial grass that forms upright clumps of finely textured, windswept leaf blades. Foliage turns from medium green to golden-brown. Shimmering silver-white flowerheads appear like feathers above the foliage in summer. Flowerheads audibly rustle in the breeze.

commonName: Pheasant's Tail Grass, New uzealand Wind Grass
description: A semi-evergreen ornamental grass with arching, medium green foliage that turns copper in fall. Feathery green-purple flower heads emerge in summer.
A perennial grass that forms tidy, fountain-shaped clumps. Leaf blades are stiff, finely textured, and green. From late summer through fall, very thin flower stalks emerge mauve and turn creamy tan.

Shimmering pink flower heads float above this clumping, warm-season perennial grass and fade to cream as seeds form. Blue-green leaves may turn red or purple in cool weather. Use it in dry drifts, containers, or meadow edges. Full sun, lean soil, and limited water keep stems upright; seedlings may appear where ripe seed drops.

commonName: Pink Muhly Grass, Pink Hair Grass
description: An evergreen grass that forms fountain-shaped clumps. Leaf blades are slender, cylindrical, and dark green. In late summer through fall, finely-textured flowerheads form a ruby-pink cloud that rests just above the foliage. When planted in mass, flowerheads shroud the foliage in a magnificent, gauzy haze.
A perennial grass that forms dense, tufted clumps. Leaf blades are grayish green. Tall flowerheads top the plant throughout summer. Native to California and beyond.

A warm-season ornamental grass with an upright, fountain-like form. Feathery, purple-pink flower panicles are long, fluffy and foxtail-like. Blooms age to a creamy copper from late summer through fall. Burgundy foliage is finely textured and upright to arching. Semi-evergreen.

A summer-deciduous bunchgrass with fine, grayish green foliage. Nodding, purplish awns age to glimmering gold in spring-summer. Generous self-sowing and deep roots make it good for erosion control and suppressing invasive weeds. The state grass of California.

A warm-season perennial bunchgrass with fine green to blue-green blades and airy purple-tinged seed heads. The open inflorescences catch light and movement in meadow, restoration, and dry border plantings. Native to California and much of the West. Performs best with lean, well-drained soil and minimal irrigation once established.

commonName: Regal Mist Pink Muhly, Pink Hair Grass
description: An evergreen grass that forms fountain-shaped clumps. Leaf blades are slender, cylindrical, and dark green. In late summer through fall, finely-textured flowerheads form a rosy-pink cloud that rests just above the foliage. When planted in mass, flowerheads shroud the foliage in a magnificent, gauzy haze.
A rush-like perennial with hollow, upright stems. Stems are bright green with dark brown rings at the nodes.

A spreading, grass-like perennial with bright, evergreen foliage. Small reddish flower spikes appear in spring. Strong root system and tough leaves. Tends to spread aggressively in its ideal conditions. Good in containers and bioswales. Native to California and Oregon.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Fine, weeping, gray-blue foliage forms a compact, mounding clump. Small, yellow flower spikes emit a sweet fragrance in summer. Tolerates seaside, inland, shade and drought conditions. Resistant to root rot.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Fine, gray-green foliage forms an upright-arching, compact clump. Profuse, yellow flower spikes emit a sweet fragrance in summer. More flowers than other Lomandras. Tolerates seaside, inland, drought and humid conditions.
An ornamental grass forming cascading clumps of narrow blue-green leaves with red tips. Foliage turns red in early fall. Loose and airy flowers clusters in red.

commonName: Shorty Mat Rush, Pom Pom Mat Rush
botanicalName: Lomandra confertifolia ssp. pallida 'Pom Pom' PP 32,554
description: A compact, grass-like plant that forms mounds of semi-erect, bright lime green foliage. Small cream colored flowers are inconspicuous, nearly concealed by leaves. Useful as groundcover, accent, or container plant. Similar to 'Lime Tuff,' but 2/3 the size.
