A shade-tolerant evergreen perennial that forms a slowly spreading tuft of grass-like foliage. Arching, variegated leaves are dark green with silvery-white stripes. Nonshowy summer flowers are followed by small glossy fruits.

A grass-like perennial that forms gracefully arching, dense clumps of lustrous, very narrow, pale green leaves that age to greenish-brown. Inconspicuous brown flower heads emerge in summer. Tolerant of coastal exposure.

An evergreen perennial grass that forms an upright, fountain-like clump. Extra long, fine-textured leaf blades are chalky silver-blue. Tall flower heads age to amber-tan. Blooms in spring and summer. Cold hardy.

A warm-season ornamental grass with a fountain-like form. From summer into fall, wiry stems rise 3 - 4 feet high, topped by tawny-brown, foxtail-like flower panicles. Finely textured foliage is medium to dark green. Semi-evergreen. Tolerates heat and coastal climates.

An evergreen perennial that forms a grass-like, fountain-shaped clump. Glossy, bright green stems are stiff, cylindrical and leafless. Small yellow-brown flower clusters are present in spring and summer. Native to California and beyond.

An evergreen perennial grass that forms a fountain-like clump. Foliage is extra fine-textured. Leaf blades are thread-like and silvery-blue-green. Nodding, feathery flower heads age from purple to amber-tan. Native to Europe.

A deciduous prairie grass that forms mop-like clumps. Finely textured leaf blades turn from blue-green to showy bronze-red in fall and winter. Non-showy late summer flowerheads age to fluffy silvery seedpods.

commonName: Tomales Bay Idaho Fescue, Blue Bunchgrass
description: A semi-evergreen perennial grass that forms a dense, fountain-like clump. Fine-textured leaf blades age from deep blue-green to buff. Tall flower heads age to amber-tan. Flower stalks sometimes tinge silver or pink. Blooms in spring and summer. Native to a wide range of North America, including California. Tolerates some foot traffic.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Strappy, yellowish green foliage forms an upright, fountain-like clump. Large, yellow flower clusters emit a sweet fragrance in late spring. Tolerates seaside, inland, shade and drought conditions. Tolerates more water than other Lomandras. Slow to reach full size. Evergreen to zone 9.

A cool-season bunchgrass that forms rounded clumps of finely textured, rich green leaf blades. Glistening, airy flower stalks rise above the foliage in spring and summer. Summer-deciduous. Native to many landscapes across the globe, including California.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Leaves are variegated light green with white stripes. Fine, upright-arching foliage forms a compact, fountain-like clump. Small, yellow flower spikes emit a sweet fragrance in summer. Tolerates seaside, inland, and drought conditions.

A wetland perennial evergreen that thrives in boggy or moist areas. Tufts of sweetly-scented, grass-like leaf blades slowly spread to form a dense groundcover via rhizomatous roots. Foliage is variegated, striped in white and green.

An ornamental perennial grass that forms a very tall, upright clump. Fine, arching leaves are dark green with boldly variegated horizontal yellow bands. Foliage turns yellowish in winter. From late summer to frost, tall stalks are topped with copper-red, tassel-like flowerheads that mature to large, fluffy, silver-white plumes. Flower stalks extend 1 - 2 feet above the foliage.

An evergreen grass-like perennial. Leaves are variegated light green with white stripes. Fine, upright-arching foliage forms a compact, fountain-like clump. Small, yellow flower spikes emit a sweet fragrance in summer.

A warm-season ornamental grass with a fountain-like form. Purple to buff flower panicles are fuzzy, long and tassle-like. Throughout summer, feathery plumes top the slender leaf blades. Variegated foliage is striped in white, green, burgundy and pink. Fine in containers. Tolerates poor soils and drought once established. Does not self-sow.

An evergreen, grass-like marginal perennial with upright, narrow leaves striped green and cream. The clean vertical texture is useful around ponds, bioswales, wet edges, and contemporary containers. Best color and density develop in consistently moist to wet soil, including shallow water at the root zone.

Fine green leaves arch from this evergreen, clumping grass-like perennial and form a soft, weed-blocking mass. It grows from sun into shade and handles dry soil after establishment. Use it beneath trees, along paths, or across low-maintenance slopes. Good drainage and occasional grooming keep the mound fresh; seedlings may appear where seed heads remain.

commonName: White Awn Muhly, White Cloud Muhly
description: An evergreen grass that forms fountain-shaped clumps. Leaf blades are slender, cylindrical, and dark green. In late summer through fall, finely-textured flowerheads form a milky-white cloud that rests just above the foliage. When planted in mass, flowerheads shroud the foliage in a magnificent, gauzy haze.

commonName: Yaku Jima Japanese Silver Grass, Eulalia
description: An ornamental perennial grass that forms a compact, fountain-like clump. Fine, arching leaves are green. Foliage turns reddish-brown in fall. From mid-summer to frost, tall stalks are topped with copper-red, tassel-like flowerheads that mature to large, fluffy, silvery-white plumes. Like a dwarf version of M. s. 'Gracillimus'.

botanicalName: Chamaerops humilis var. cerifera, C. h. argentea
description: A slow-growing palm with a clumping, multi-trunking form. Crowns of frosty silver-blue, fan-like fronds have spines along their petioles. Native to Northwest Africa. Tolerates humidity. Cold hardy down to 15 degrees F or less.

One massive silver-blue fan crowns this evergreen, single-trunk palm and creates a strong focal point. Native to open habitats in western Madagascar, it handles heat once established. Use it in large civic, resort, or estate landscapes with open overhead space. Full sun and deep drainage build color; heavy fronds and fruit may fall below.
A palm with a heavy patterned trunk and gracefully arching, feathery fronds. Female trees produce dates.
An evergreen fan palm with a narrow, fibrous, dark brown trunk. Dark green fronds have silvery undersides. Smaller fronds and overall size than T. fortunei.

A graceful, evergreen palm with a smooth green crownshaft and a clean, upright trunk. Arching feather fronds form a full canopy, followed by clusters of small lavender flowers and bright red fruit on mature plants. Useful for patios, entries, and sheltered groves. Performs best with rich soil, regular irrigation, and wind protection.

An evergreen fan palm with thin, upright trunks that grow in bamboo-like clumps. Canes are sheathed in dark brown fiber. Fronds are large, deep green and fan-like. Yellow flowers in spring. Does well indoors.

A slow-growing palm with a clumping, multi-trunking form. Crowns of green, fan-like fronds have spines along their petioles. Native to Europe. Tolerates humidity. Cold hardy down to 15 degrees F or less.

commonName: Mexican Blue Palm, Blue Hesper Palm
description: A fan palm with silvery blue, 4 - 6 foot long fronds that grow atop a stout, solitary trunk. In summer, 15 foot long flower clusters emerge in creamy-white.

An evergreen palm with a tall, slender trunk and large, fan-shaped, sunny green fronds. Spent leaves shed slowly, and leave a cross-hatched pattern of fibrous, cinnamon-colored leaf stubs. Native to Mexico.
A palm tree that forms a crown of arching, gray-green leaves. The thick trunk is notched with stubs of old leaves. Showy flower clusters are followed by edible red fruit.
A small palm with slender, patterned trunks. Forms a dense crown of finely textured and feathery, gracefully arching fronds in bright green. Can be grown indoors with bright indirect light.

An evergreen, single-trunk palm with a tall, graceful crown of arching green fronds. Cream flowers are followed by heavy clusters of orange fruit that feed birds but can create litter below. Native to subtropical South America, it brings quick height to streets, pools, and large courtyards. Balanced palm fertilizer supports strong green growth.

A palm-like Japanese cycad that slowly grows tall and broad. Dark green fronds are stiff, spiky, and pinnately divided. All foliage branches out from a central, woody, pineapple-like trunk. Offsets form with maturity.
An evergreen fan palm with a narrow trunk that is covered in thick fibrous hairs on the upper half. Dark green fronds have silvery undersides.

A tender perennial that forms a compact, uniform mound. Extra showy daisy-like flowers are white with a violet, double center. Abundant blooms in spring and summer stay open all day and night. Foliage is bright green, narrowly oval and slightly toothed.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a patch of coarse, green leaves. Large, single flowers are white with yellow centers. Abundant summer blooms rise above the foliage on rigid stalks. Good cut flower. Attracts butterflies.
A woodland perennial groundcover with white and light green leaves that are large and heart-shaped. Sky blue springtime flowers look similar to forget-me-nots. Can tolerate full shade.
An evergreen perennial forming a carpet of dense and rounded flower clusters in pure white. Narrow and shiny, finely textured dark green leaves. May be semi-evergreen in colder winter climates.

A spreading perennial groundcover from woodlands of the southeastern United States, semi-evergreen in mild climates. Blue-green leaves develop silver mottling and may turn red in fall. Fragrant white and pink flower spikes open in spring; small dry capsules may follow. It forms slow, noninvasive colonies. Use beneath trees, on shaded slopes, or along woodland paths.

commonName: Allen Chickering Cleveland Sage, California Blue Sage
description: An evergreen shrub that forms a billowy mound. Gray-green leaves are quilted, toothed, and very fragrant. Tall stalks carry elaborate whorls of two-lipped flowers in lavender-purple. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts all sorts of pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to California.

A perennial that forms a trailing, cascading ground cover. Silvery-green foliage is soft, fine and needle-like. Vibrant scarlet red flowers are shaped like birds' beaks. Blooms in spring and summer. Good in hanging pots.

A perennial that forms a trailing, cascading ground cover. Silvery-gray foliage is soft, fine and needle-like. Vibrant red-orange flowers are shaped like birds' beaks. Blooms in spring and summer. Good in hanging pots.

A moisture-loving woodland perennial with a clump-forming growth habit. Erect, plume-like flowers bloom into light, airy clusters of amethyst-pink. Fern-like foliage is divided into deep green leaflets with finely serrated edges. Attracts butterflies.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact mound. Bright green leaves are oval and fragrant like blackcurrants. Upright stalks carry two-lipped, bi-colored flowers in amethyst purple and white. Flower color changes slightly with the seasons. Blooms from spring to frost. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects and wildlife.
A perennial forming compact mounds of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in deep silvery-purple. Wiry stems carry small and nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink.
A compact perennial that forms mounds of finely divided, gray-green foliage, decorated with a profusion of inch-wide, amethyst-blue flowers. Native to Australia.

An evergreen perennial prized for its foliage, that forms rosettes of broad, bright white, heart shaped and velvety leaves. Non-showy yellow flowers emerge from the center of each rosette during summer months.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers in dark reddish-pink. Handsome and leathery, marbled palmate foliage.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Flowers and linear, silvery-green foliage are aromatic. Plump, dark violet flower heads are topped by light mauve, flag-like bracts. Blooms in spring and reblooms in favorable conditions. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. Selected for disease resistance and cold hardiness.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Plump, dark blue-violet flower heads are topped by large, white, flag-like bracts. Blooms in spring, and reblooms in favorable conditions. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. Good resistance to foliar disease.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, gray to green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in a palette of soft pinks on 2 - 3 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.

An evergreen subshrub with an upright, multi-branching growth habit that come become a bit rangy. Leaves are downy, crinkled and gray-green. Tall, wand-like stalks carry outstanding cup-shaped flowers in pink-orange-red blends. Blooms from summer into fall. Attracts bees and other pollinators. Native to the Southwest, including California.
A colorful perennial with daisy-like flowers in golden yellow with a darker pinkish-orange ring around the center. Valued for very long blooming period.
A colorful perennial with daisy-like flowers in coppery-red. Valued for very long blooming period.
A colorful perennial with daisy-like flowers in coppery-red surrounded by a ring of yellow petal tips. Valued for very long blooming period.

commonName: Aromas Cleveland Sage, California Blue Sage
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a compact mound. Gray-green leaves are quilted, toothed, and very fragrant. Tall stalks carry elaborate whorls of two-lipped flowers in lavender-purple. Heaviest blooms in spring and summer. Attracts all sorts of pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to California. Similar to S. 'Allen Chickering'.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender gray-green leaves have variegated bright yellow edges. New growth emerges pink-red. Foliage turns pink-red-orange in fall. Bright yellow, lime-green, red-eyed inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A woody evergreen perennial that forms a shrubby mound. Green leaves are slender and rough-textured. Daisy-like flowers are deep blue with yellow centers. Long bloom season from spring to fall. Attracts butterflies. Native to South Africa.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a trailing carpet via rhizomes. Flowers are silky, fragrant, and pansy-like. Petals are lavender, blue, or white. Eyes are usually purple. Blooms in spring and summer. Beneficial for butterflies. Leaves are kidney-shaped and bright green. Likes more heat than other violas.

commonName: Autumn Colors Gloriosa Daisy, Black Eyed Susan
description: An herbaceous perennial that forms a compact self-sowing patch of profuse summer-fall blooms. Oversized daisy-like flowers display a dark brown center disk and multi-color rays in yellow, orange, red and brown. Green leaves are lance-shaped and hairy. Good cut flower atop a long, sturdy stem. Often grown as an annual. Attracts butterflies and birds.

A semi-evergreen, compact shrub with bright green, scented leaves. Soft lavender-purple flowers rise above the foliage from spring through fall and feed hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies. Use as a low border, groundcover, container plant, or dry garden accent. It thrives in lean, rocky, well-drained soil and stays dense with light seasonal trimming.
A perennial groundcover that forms mats of tiny green foliage. Spreads indefinitely by creeping stems. Useful between flagstones or as a groundcover in damp and shady spots.

A perennial tuber that blooms all summer and dies back in winter. Showy double flowerheads come in vivid purple and are 6" to 8" across. Green leaflets are toothed and bushy. Needs slightly acidic soil, pH 6.5. - 7.0.
A perennial selected for hanging baskets or as a small-scale groundcover. Leaves are small, toothed, and cool blue-green. Purple-blue flowers are dainty, five-petaled and cupped.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a low, dense mound. Dainty, saucer-shaped flowers are light pink with purple veins and maroon eyes. Blooms throughout summer. Grayish green leaves are fancifully lobed.
A well-branched evergreen shrub. Tubular, red flowers flare into frilly, purple, bat-faced tips. Leaves are medium green and have a sand-paper texture. Attracts pollinators.

A perennial ground cover that spreads vigorously from a central crown via above-ground runners. Glossy, dark green leaves are three-lobed, rounded and toothed. White, five-petaled flowers bloom in spring. Blossoms are occasionally followed by small, seedy strawberry-fruits. Native to North and South America, including the California Pacific coast.

commonName: Beacon Silver Dead Nettle, Yellow Archangel
description: A perennial mat-forming groundcover that likes shade. Variegated foliage is silver-white with fine, dark green edges. Scalloped, quilted, heart-shaped leaves are arranged in opposite pairs on square stems. Short upright stalks carry hooded pink flowers throughout summer.
A winter-blooming, evergreen perennial with deeply divided and narrow foliage. Clusters of nodding, bell-shaped flowers in pale greenish-yellow. Bruised flowers and foliage emit an unpleasant aroma.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a dense, mounding ground cover. Silvery-gray-green leaves are velvety, slender, crinkled, and fragrant. Upright stems carry dense whorls of profuse lavender-blue flowers. Blooms in spring and early summer. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators and beneficial insects. Hybrid of two California native sages.

A mat-forming perennial with finely dissected, bright green foliage. Lightly fragrant flowers with bright yellow, scarlet-tipped petals bloom continually in mild weather. Attracts bees and butterflies.

An evergreen shrub prized for large and fragrant, white flower heads held in terminal, spike-like clusters. Finely divided, narrow gray-green foliage. This 'Beezee' series is grown for profuse flowering that will keep all pollinators busy. Excellent uniformity, earliness, and spike quality. Winter hardy and cold-tolerant, with good tolerance to foliar diseases compared to other lavenders.

commonName: Belle of Dawn Border Penstemon, Beardtongue
description: A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers are rosy purple with white throats. Abundant waves of blooms from spring to fall. Very attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators.
Heat and drought tolerant perennial with tall and airy flower clusters in white to deep pink.
Heat and drought tolerant perennial with tall and airy flower clusters in white.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact, shrubby clump. Edible, gray-green leaves are aromatic, soft-textured and oval. Short stalks carry spikes of two-lipped flowers in lavender-blue. Blooms in summer. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. S. officinalis is known for its culinary and medicinal uses.

An evergreen shrub that forms a tight, dense mound. Bluish-green foliage is small, egg-shaped, slightly glossy, and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped, bright pink flowers held in dark pink calyxes. Blooms from spring to frost. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators, and beneficial insects.

An evergreen shrub that forms a dense, upright to spreading mound. Bluish-green foliage is egg-shaped, texured, slightly glossy, and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in bright rosy pink. Blooms from spring to frost. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators, and beneficial insects.

An evergreen perennial that forms an aggresively spreading mound. Flowers are 5-petaled pinwheels of periwinkle-purple. Springtime blooms are tucked into the deep green foliage. Leaves are thick, heart-shaped, and larger than V. minor. Difficult to contain.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a self-sowing mound. Purple-blue flowers are dainty and saucer-shaped with heart-shaped petals. Long bloom cycle lasts from spring through fall. Soft green leaves are deeply lobed.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a spreading, mounding ground cover. White-pink flowers are dainty, saucer-shaped and clustered above the foliage on forked stems. Blooms from early spring into summer. Mid-green leaves are fancifully lobed.

commonName: Black & Bloom Salvia, Brauzilian Blue Sage
botanicalName: Salvia guaranitica 'Black and Bloom' PP 27,183, S. ambigens
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a multi-branching mound. Medium green leaves are triangular, textured and fragrant. Tall black stalks carry dark violet-blue, two-lipped flowers held in dark calyxes. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Likes heat and humidity.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, gray to green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in white on 1 - 2 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, dark purple-black leaves. Wiry stems carry small but showy cherry-red flowers atop the foliage. Blooms in late spring to early summer.

botanicalName: Delphinium Pacific Giant Round Table 'Black Knight'
description: A classic cottage perennial with upright stalks of semi-double flowers in dark violet with black centers. Blooms finish in peak summer heat. Foliage is coarsely lobed and bushy. Short-lived with a 3 year life span. Attracts hummingbirds, butterflies, and other pollinators. Requires staking.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a billowy mound. Dark green leaves are linear, textured and aromatic. Long stems carry tiered whorls of two-lipped flowers in white or light lavender. Blooms from early spring into summer. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects, birds and wildlife. Native to California.

A semi-evergreen, spreading groundcover with low rosettes and short spikes of blue spring flowers. Textured foliage knits quickly between stepping stones, under shrubs, and along shaded borders. It performs best with regular moisture and organic soil, especially where a dense, low mat is desired.

commonName: Black and Blue Anise Scented Sage, Brauzilian Sage
botanicalName: Salvia guaranitica 'Black and Blue', S. ambigens
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a multi-branching mound. Medium green leaves are triangular, glossy, textured and fragrant. Tall stalks carry violet-blue, two-lipped flowers held in dark calyxes. Blooms in summer and fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A perennial with upright stems, multibranching from the base. A tall, bushy variety. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of tubular, trumpet-shaped flowers are deep bluish burgundy. Long bloom cycle from summer to frost. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, velvety leaves are tinted dark purple over gray-green. Best color in full sun. Chartreuse-green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop red stems in spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.
Compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed evergreen leaves in purple-black. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in creamy white.

Flame-colored daisies cover this mounding, tender perennial, blending orange-red petals with bright yellow tips. Fine green leaves trail gently over bed edges and pots. Bees and butterflies visit through a long warm-season bloom. Use it as fast color in borders or containers. Sun, drained soil, and even moisture keep flowers coming.
A perennial with wiry stems carrying ruffled and rose-like flowers in bright red. Attractive foliage forms lush green mounds.

An evergreen perennial shrub, often grown as an annual. Rich green leaves are long, elliptical, and arranged in opposite pairs. Tiny star-shaped flowers grow in clusters of rich, warm colors. Attracts many beneficial insects, especially the Monarch butterfly.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a mounding ground cover. Spreads by runners. Purple-pink, dark-veined flowers are dainty and saucer-shaped. Long bloom cycle lasts from spring through fall. Dark green leaves are fragrant and deeply lobed. Foliage turns deep red in fall.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with oval to heart-shaped, blue-green foliage that radiates outwards from the center. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.

A summer-blooming perennial with aromatic, gray-green foliage and whorled, showy dark blue to royal purple flowers that grow on vertical spikes. Anise-scented leaves make a delicious herbal tea. Great selection for pollinator gardens; attracts hummingbirds, butterflies, bees.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Spring-summer flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Flower spikes bloom in deep purple and fade to gray-blue. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.

A tender perennial that forms a compact mound. Daisy-like flowers are light yellow with violet-ringed, dark blue eyes. Abundant blooms spring thru fall. Flowers close at night. Foliage is bright green, narrowly oval and slightly toothed.

An evergreen perennial that forms a mounding groundcover. Medium green leaves are semi-fleshy and toothed. Abundant fan-shaped flowers bloom in violet-blue with yellow eyes. Long bloom period from late spring to frost. Attracts butterflies, bees and other pollinators. Heat tolerant. Does well in a hanging basket. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A summer-blooming perennial with aromatic, gray-green foliage and whorled, powder-blue flowers that grow on vertical spikes. Anise-scented leaves make a delicious herbal tea. Great selection for pollinator gardens; attracts hummingbirds, butterflies, bees.
A clump-forming perennial with slender, gray-green leaves. Upright stalks carry whorls of two-lipped flowers in deep blue. Blooms in summer and fall. Attracts pollinators.

botanicalName: Perovskia atriplicifolia 'Blue Jean Baby' PP 29,281, Salvia yangii
description: This compact, deciduous woody perennial sends up lavender-blue flower spikes. Scented silver leaves form a neat base. Bees crowd the summer bloom, while deer tend to pass it by. Use it in dry beds, street strips, or drifts. Full sun, lean soil, and fast drainage keep the stems firm and the mound from falling open.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers in deep purple-blue. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated margins.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a very compact clump. Gray-green leaves are slender, textured and fragrant. Tall, upright stalks carry plump spikes of fuzzy, two-lipped flowers in bright violet-blue. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with rounded and curved, blue to gray-green foliage that radiates outwards from the center. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.

commonName: Blue My Mind Brauzilian Dwarf Morning Glory
description: An herbaceous perennial with a mounding form and trailing stems. Silver-green leaves are oval and downy. White-eyed, deep blue flowers are funnel-shaped with flat, open faces. Resembles a non-climbing morning glory. Blooms from spring through summer. Flowers close at night.

A low-water perennial with a low, mounded form. Foliage is more green than gray. Leaves are aromatic, soft and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of bright blue flowers bloom from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators.

Violet-blue flower spikes rise from this evergreen, mounding woody perennial above narrow silver leaves. The scented foliage and summer bloom feed bees while resisting deer. Use it in low hedges, gravel gardens, or repeated border groups. Full sun, lean soil, and sharp drainage keep the mound firm; shear lightly after bloom without cutting old wood.

A shrubby perennial with fine, feathery, aromatic, gray-green foliage. Lavender-blue flowers appear in tall, airy, branched stalks. Blooms in summer. Attracts bees and butterflies. A vigorous, upright variety.

A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Blue-green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers are bright blue with violet and pink undertones. Blooms from late spring into summer. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. California native.
A creeping ground-cover perennial with tiny, lush green foliage similar in appearance to Baby Tears. Profuse star-shaped flowers in lavender-blue. Ideal between stepping stones or under shrubs.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, wide bush. Dark green leaves are egg-shaped and fragrant. Dark, upright stalks carry spikes of large, two-lipped flowers in blue. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects, and wildlife. Very shade tolerant.

commonName: Blue Violet Tapien Verbena, Carpet of Blossoms
description: A tender, spreading perennial groundcover with fine green leaves and a dense, low mat. Blue-violet flower clusters bloom from late spring to frost and feed butterflies. This mildew-resistant hybrid works along paths, over walls, in pots, or as a weed-blocking carpet. It grows best in well-drained soil and responds well to light trimming.

An herbaceous perennial with a cascading, trailing growth habit. Flowers are star-shaped, and light violet-blue with white throats. Blooms from late spring through summer. Foliage is medium green. Forms a small, showy groundcover. Attracts hummingbirds.

A low-water perennial with a low, mounded form. Foliage is more green than gray. Leaves are aromatic, soft and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of periwinkle-blue flowers bloom from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators. Flowers and foliage are larger than typical.

An evergreen perennial that forms a trailing, mounding ground cover. Bright green leaves are semi-fleshy and toothed. Abundant fan-shaped flowers bloom in violet-blue with yellow eyes. Long bloom period from late spring to frost. Attracts butterflies, bees and other pollinators. Heat tolerant. Does well in a hanging basket.

An evergreen perennial with a compact, mounding habit. Aster-like flowers bloom from spring to summer, opening up to 2 inches across. Threadlike petals appear in lavender. Yellow button-centers attract all sorts of pollinators. More abundant blooms than the species. Medium to dark gray-green leaves are spoon to lance-shaped. Native to coastal California and Oregon.
A perennial with an upright growth habit. Spike-like clusters of fragrant, four-petaled flowers bloom in lavender-mauve in winter and spring. Gray-green leaves are long and narrow.

An evergreen shrub that forms a slowly creeping, prostrate ground cover. Foliage is glossy and deep green, partially turning rusty-maroon in cool weather. Small leaves are rounded, lobed, and crinkled. Small, white, spring-summer flowers are followed by edible orange berries that ripen in fall. Native to Taiwan.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in deep green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in bright colors.
Perennial with basal clump of wavy-edged foliage and tall spike-like flower clusters.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a compact clump with flowers borne on upright stalks. Dark green leaves are rounded and lobed. Delicate cup-shaped flowers are rosy-red. Blooms in summer and fall. Attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Native to the Pacific Coast, including California.
A semi-evergreen groundcover with crinkled leaves of bronze-green. Lavender-blue flower spikes bloom in spring and early summer. Spreads by runners. Can tolerate full shade.
A semi-evergreen groundcover with crinkled, round leaves of bronze-green. Blue flower spikes bloom in spring and early summer. Spreads by runners. Can tolerate full shade.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a bushy mound. Lavender-blue, white-eyed flowers are dainty, saucer-shaped and set above the foliage. Blooms from spring to fall. Bright green leaves are fancifully lobed. Foliage tints red in fall.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, dense bush. Slender leaves are gray-green. Chartreuse-green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms in club-shaped clusters atop stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.
A tree peony prized for single white flowers with slightly ruffled petals. Sweetly fragrant. Lush and dark green, attractively divided foliage.

A semi-evergreen, spreading groundcover with low rosettes and short spikes of blue spring flowers. Textured foliage knits quickly between stepping stones, under shrubs, and along shaded borders. It performs best with regular moisture and organic soil, especially where a dense, low mat is desired.

A tender perennial or annual with a compact, upright, clumping growth habit. Gray-green foliage is finely lobed and ferny. Wiry stems carry frilly, pincushion-like flowerheads in lavender-blue. Blooms from midsummer through fall. Attracts butterflies. A good cut flower.

An evergreen perennial shrub. Rich green leaves are long, narrow, and arranged in opposite pairs. Tiny star-shaped flowers grow in clusters of tangerine orange. Attracts many pollinators and beneficial insects, especially caterpillars of the Monarch butterfly.
An herbaceous perennial with a compact form, featuring tall and airy, wand-like flower clusters in white. Narrow and lance-shaped foliage.

A spreading, herbaceous perennial with leafy green stems and late-season daisy-like lavender flowers with yellow centers. This California native provides nectar for butterflies and beneficial insects when many summer flowers are fading. Useful in meadows, borders, and habitat plantings. Performs best with good drainage and occasional summer irrigation.

A spreading, herbaceous perennial with leafy green stems and late-season daisy-like lavender flowers with yellow centers. This California native provides nectar for butterflies and beneficial insects when many summer flowers are fading. Useful in meadows, borders, and habitat plantings. Performs best with good drainage and occasional summer irrigation.

An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a mounding habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Bright red, trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in summer and fall. Leaves are felt-textured, linear to oval, and gray-green. Native to western United States, and northern Mexico.

A semi-evergreen perennial with a clump-forming growth habit. Leaves are lance-shaped and green. Horizontal plumes of tiny golden yellow flowers bloom from late summer to early fall. Attracts birds and pollinators. Native to California.

A rhizomatous, herbaceous California native perennial with upright stems and aromatic gray-green leaves with silvery undersides. Small summer flower heads support habitat plantings while the foliage provides soft texture in meadows, bioswales, and naturalized edges. Performs best with seasonal moisture, well-drained to heavier soils, and occasional summer irrigation.

A winter-dormant, upright perennial with narrow green leaves and a soft, open form. Pale pink to lavender flower clusters bloom from summer into fall, feeding native bees and monarchs. Smooth pods release silky seeds. Native across California and the western United States. Use in habitat gardens and meadows. Milky sap is toxic if eaten.

A drought-deciduous to evergreen California native shrub with finely divided, aromatic silver-gray foliage and a loose, rounded habit. Inconspicuous summer flower heads provide habitat value while the foliage brings soft texture to coastal sage scrub and restoration plantings. Performs best with good drainage and very little summer irrigation once established.

A deciduous herbaceous perennial with broad gray-green leaves and upright stems. Rounded clusters of fragrant pink flowers bloom in summer and provide nectar for pollinators while supporting monarch larvae. Useful in meadows, restoration sites, and habitat gardens. Performs best with well-drained soil and occasional irrigation during establishment.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a multi-branching bush. Slender, silvery white, velvet-coated leaves are very aromatic with the signature scent of sage considered sacred by some. In summer, very tall stalks carry pale, two-lipped flowers. Attracts native bees, hummingbirds, other pollinators, and beneficial insects. Use on slopes for erosion control. Native to California.

An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a mounding habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers appear in rich red-orange. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, oval to linear, and gray-green. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a mounding ground cover. Blue-tinted pink flowers are dainty, saucer-shaped and clustered above the foliage on forked stems. Blooms from early spring into summer. Mid-green leaves are fancifully lobed.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, outward facing flowers cream and pale pink. Handsome and leathery, dark green palmate foliage. Burgundy stems.

An evergreen biennial that forms spikes of flared, bell-shaped flowers which emerge from stalks of whorled, gray-green leaves. Flowers appear in a bright throughout their bloom season from spring through summer.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in glossy dark green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in dark pink and white.

A low, spreading evergreen to drought-deciduous shrub with aromatic silver-gray foliage and a broad cascading habit. Fine texture and pale color make it effective on slopes, walls, and dry native garden edges. Inconspicuous flowers are secondary to foliage effect. Performs best with good drainage and minimal summer irrigation once established.

An evergreen, spreading groundcover perennial with low gray-green leaves and many lavender daisies with yellow centers. Flowers appear from spring through summer and feed bees and butterflies. Native to California's coast, it works well on banks, along paths, and near the ocean. It grows best with drainage and light shade inland.

A perennial tuber that forms a dramatic clump. Deep green leaves are spotted white, are broad, arrow-shaped, and glossy with prominent veins. Spring and summer-blooming flowers are elegant, cone-shaped, and fragrant. Lemon-yellow, petal-like spathes surround a yellow spadix of tiny true flowers.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact clump. Gray-green leaves are slender, soft and fragrant. Dark purple, upright stalks carry spikes of fuzzy, two-lipped flowers in purple. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Cold hardy.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in golden apricot. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in light pink.

Bright and mounded, this evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial has lime-green leaves with soft silver marks. Thin stems carry small white flowers that feed hummingbirds and insects. Use it along shaded paths, in pots, or under open trees. Filtered sun, rich open soil, and even water keep leaves full and reduce dry brown edges.

An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in bronzy-green with pink and peach. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white. Exceptional heat and humidity tolerance.

A perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is a gradient of crisp white, soft pink, and pastel yellow. Maroon markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower.

An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a dense, mounding habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in red-orange. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, oval to linear, and gray-green. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

Perennial with an upright form and narrow, pointed foliage. Tall clusters of flared, bell-shaped flowers are bright pink, and attract butterflies and hummingbirds. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

commonName: Catherine De La Mare Foothill Penstemon
description: A perennial with a low, open habit, multi-branching from the base. Blue-green leaves are larger than the species. Spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers fade from glistening blue to pinkish-purple. Long bloom cycle from late spring into fall. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators.

A semi-evergreen, spreading groundcover with low rosettes and short spikes of blue spring flowers. Textured foliage knits quickly between stepping stones, under shrubs, and along shaded borders. It performs best with regular moisture and organic soil, especially where a dense, low mat is desired.

A low-water perennial with a rounded, mounding form. Gray-green foliage is soft and aromatic. Leaves are small, ovate and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of bright lavender-blue flowers bloom spring to fall. Attracts pollinators. Sterile hybrid.
A shrubby perennial featuring lacy green foliage with scalloped margins. Leaves smell of celery. Clusters of airy magenta flowers. Can be grown as annuals or houseplants outside of hardiness zones.

An evergreen perennial that forms a rounded mound. Edible, gray leaves are small, oval and aromatic. Tall stalks carry elaborate whorls of fragrant, two-lipped, glowing blue-violet flowers held in pink bracts. Blooms from spring to summer. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to California.

An evergreen shrub that forms an upright mound. Mid-green leaves are oval and fragrant like blackcurrants. Tall stalks carry two-lipped flowers in bright magenta. Flower color changes slightly with the seasons. Blooms from summer to frost. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects and wildlife.

A perennial with a compact, upright form. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of large, tubular flowers in a variety of colors. Long bloom cycle from summer to fall. Very attractive to bees and other pollinators. Heat tolerant and cold hardy.
A low-growing, groundcover perennial with multi-colored foliage in green with yellow, pink, and red.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a sub-shrub of upright, unbranched stems. Summer dormant in hot, dry climates. Leaves are slender, dark green, and sticky. Lobed, funnel-shaped flowers are mottled orange, red, and creamy white. Spring to fall blooms attract butterflies and other pollinators. California native.

A perennial ground cover that spreads vigorously from a central crown via above-ground runners. Super glossy, rich green leaves are three-lobed, rounded and toothed. Foliage is dense. White, five-petaled flowers bloom in spring. Blossoms are occasionally followed by small, seedy strawberry-fruits. Native to North and South America, including the California Pacific coast.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in reddish-brown. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in cherry red.

A self-sowing perennial flower. Leaves are gray, lobed, rough, and woolly. Long-stemmed daisy-like flowers typically display black composite centers surrounded by a ring of contrasting yellow. Petals are deep cherry red. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A North American perennial that forms mounds of tall, upright blooms throughout summer. A multicolored mix of flowers appear with brownish seed cones and drooping petals in white, purple, and all the warm colors in between. Low-growing leaves are lance-shaped, green, and slightly hairy. A popular herbal remedy today, all plant parts have been used in Native American medicine for hundreds of years. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

An evergreen perennial that forms a dense mound. Rich green leaves are large and oval with deep venation. Sweeping stalks carry whorls of two-lipped flowers in bright magenta pink. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Does fine in dry shade.
A bold and tropical perennial with giant furry leaves 4 - 8 feet across. Corncob-like flower clusters that form near the base.

A perennial tuber that carries elegant blooms atop naked stems, which rise above low patches of green leaves. Deep, dark red flowers are chocolate-scented, saucer-shaped flowers, and deep, attractive to butterflies. 'Chocamocha' is said to be shorter, more strongly fragrant, and more red than the species.
A dwarf semi-evergreen groundcover with narrow, chocolate-brown leaves. Blue flower spikes appear in spring and early summer. Spreads by runners. Can tolerate full shade.
Shrubby perennial with pale green and maroon variegated foliage and clusters of pale lavender colored flowers. Can be grown indoors or as an annual in all zones.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed, ruffled leaves in chocolate-purple. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in creamy white.

A North American perennial that forms compact mounds of tall, upright blooms throughout summer. Large, fragrant flowers appear with drooping bright-light-yellow petals and yellow-orange seed cones. Low-growing leaves are lance-shaped, green, and slightly hairy. A popular herbal remedy today, all plant parts have been used in Native American medicine for hundreds of years. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

An evergreen shrub that forms a dense, upright mound. Gray-green leaves are soft, quilted, and uniquely fragrant. Upright stalks carry tiered whorls of two-lipped flowers in violet-blue. Heaviest blooms in spring and fall. Attracts all sorts of pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to California.

A semi-evergreen perennial with a sprawling habit. Glossy, dark green leaves are heart-shaped. Red-orange, tubular flowers bloom from spring to early summer. Attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators. Native to California.

An herbaceous semi-evergReen shrub with a low, mounding habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in rich orange. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, oval to linear, and gray-green. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

A bushy perennial shrub that does well on the coast, on slopes, and in poor soils. Leaves are gray-green, textured, and roughly diamond-shaped. Daisy-like flowers show off bright yellow petals and dark brown centers. Blooms are prolific in spring and fall, though less vigorous in the heat of summer. Very attractive to pollinators. Native to Southern California.

An annual or perennial with a self-sowing, clump-forming growth habit. Flowers are silky, four-petaled, and cup or saucer shaped. Petals radiate from golden orange at the base to bright yellow at the tips. Blooms from spring through summer. Foliage is delicate, finely divided, and blue-green. California native.

A clump-forming woodland perennial with dangling, pink and white, heart-shaped flowers. Pale green foliage is larger than other varieties and is similar in appearance to carrot tops. Blooms in cool weather. Attracts hummingbirds.

A perennial tuber that forms a dramatic clump. Deep green leaves are broad, arrow-shaped, and glossy with prominent veins. Spring and summer-blooming flowers are elegant, cone-shaped, and fragrant. Creamy-white, petal-like spathes surround a yellow spadix of tiny true flowers.

A low, spreading, semi-evergreen perennial groundcover that forms a dense, walkable mat. Small green leaves spread by rooting stems, with rounded clusters of white to lavender-pink flowers appearing from spring into fall and supporting bees and butterflies. Useful as a low-water lawn alternative, between stepping stones, on banks, and in meadow-style plantings. California native status makes it especially valuable for habitat-focused landscapes. Performs best with occasional deep irrigation for a greener, fuller appearance and adapts to a wide range of soils.

A perennial, clumping herbaceous plant with ferny aromatic foliage and flat-topped flower clusters held above the leaves. Long-season bloom supports bees, butterflies, and beneficial insects, and the stems are useful fresh or dried. It is a dependable low-water perennial for sunny borders with well-drained soil.
Heat and drought tolerant compact perennial with tall and airy flower clusters in blush to deep pink.

A shrubby perennial native to the Western US and Northern Mexico. Forms an upright and arching mound of gray-green foliage and striking, soft coral to salmon pink tubular flowers. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.

Stiff stems rise from this clumping, herbaceous perennial and hold broad plates of mustard-yellow flowers. Silver-gray, fern-like leaves stay neat below the blooms. Bees and butterflies visit through summer. It works well in dry borders, meadow bands, and cut-flower beds. Lean, well-drained soil keeps the growth sturdy and compact overall.
A winter-blooming, clumping evergreen perennial with bold and serrated, large and leathery leaves. Clusters of cup-shaped, nodding flowers in lime-green.

An evergreen perennial with a robust, mounding form. Leaves are furry, gray-green and strongly fragrant of mint. Light purple, two-lipped flowers are arranged in large, showy globes. Blooms from spring into early summer. Attracts butterflies, bees and hummingbirds. California native. Requires soil with good drainage. Does well on slopes.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a vigorously self-sowing, spreading mound. Light purple-pink, pale-centered flowers are dainty and saucer-shaped. Long bloom cycle from spring through fall. Bright green leaves are finely lobed with a wiry, grassy texture.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a compact clump with flowers borne on upright stalks. Dark green leaves are rounded and lobed. Delicate cup-shaped flowers are bright pink with white centers and veins. Blooms in summer and fall. Attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Native to the Pacific Coast, including California.

A perennial ground cover that forms a mat of rounded, bright green leaves. Branches root as they spread. Small yellow flowers bloom in early summer. Evergreen in mild winters. Tolerates light foot traffic.
A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a creeping, mounding mat. Thin, wiry stems carry tiny, round, dark green leaves. Tiny, translucent, white fruits follow inconspicuous flowers in late summer.

A self-sowing, ornamental perennial known for its large, nodding flowers that come in crimson and white. Flowers display sweet, nectar-filled spurs and yellow stamens. Leaves are lacy, green, and mounding. Beneficial to many birds, butterflies, and other pollinators.

An herbaceous perennial with a trailing, mat-forming growth habit. Flowers are less than 1 inch wide, star-shaped, and bright violet-blue. Blooms from late spring through summer. Cool green foliage forms a showy groundcover. Attracts hummingbirds.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers in dusty purple-pink. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated leaf margins.

commonName: Dancing Can Can Cabbage Palm, Ti Kouka
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a fountain of arching, swordlike leaves. Coloration is variegated gray-green with cream and hot pink stripes. At maturity, it forms a multi-trunked palm-like shrub or tree. Fragrant flower clusters bloom in late spring.

commonName: Dara's Choice Hybrid Sage, Creeping Sage
description: An evergreen shrub that forms a spreading mound. Edible gray green leaves are quilted, slender and fragrant. Upright stems carry tiered whorls of two-lipped flowers in light lavender-blue. Blooms in late spring. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact, upright clump. Dark green leaves are oval, toothed and fragrant. Tall stalks carry large, two-lipped flowers in raspberry-red. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in purple-black. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in hot pink.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a compact patch of coarse, green leaves. Single flowers are white with big, yellow centers. Abundant summer blooms rise above the foliage on rigid stalks. Good cut flower. Attracts butterflies.

commonName: David Verity Cigar Plant, Large Firecracker Plant
description: A bushy, compact evergreen shrub. Long, tubular flowers come in fiery red-orange with purple embellishments at the tips. Leaves are dark green and roughly oval. Attracts pollinators.

commonName: David's Choice Sandhill Sage, Coastal Sagewort
description: A compact, evergreen California native perennial with finely cut, aromatic silver foliage and a low mounding habit. Soft texture and light color are useful in coastal gardens, rock gardens, and dry borders. Small yellow flower heads are secondary to the foliage display. Performs best with good drainage and limited summer irrigation.

A low and spreading perennial with colorful daisy-like flowers in a mix of cheery colors. Narrow, gray green foliage. Tough and low-maintenance. 'Bronze' has bright, bronze-red petals. 'Orange' has yellow-orange petals. 'Pink' has rosy pink petals with slight orange striping. 'Redstripe' has golden yellow petals with a dark red stripe down the middle. 'White' has white petals with a slight yellow tint radiating from the center. 'Yellow' has bright lemon yellow petals.

commonName: De La Mina Cedros Island Verbena
description: A tender perennial that forms a bushy, rounded mound. From spring into fall, tall, forked stems carry rounded clusters of fragrant, lilac-purple flowers. Attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Leaves are dark green, narrow, and have serrated edges. Native to southwest California.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Spring-summer flowers and linear, silver-green foliage are aromatic. Violet flower spikes are topped by long, purple, flag-like bracts. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

commonName: Denver Daisy Gloriosa Daisy, Black Eyed Susan
description: An herbaceous perennial that forms a self-sowing patch of profuse summer-fall blooms. Large, daisy-like flowers display high-contrast, bi-color rays that turn from bright yellow to brown at the bases and a dark brown center disk. Green leaves are lance-shaped and hairy. Good cut flower atop a long, sturdy stem. Often grown as an annual. Attracts butterflies and birds.

commonName: Desert Eve Terracotta Common Yarros, Milfoil
description: A compact, upright perennial with ferny, scented green foliage and flat flower clusters from spring into summer. The series offers deep rose, red, terracotta, light yellow, and yellow forms. Flowers feed bees and butterflies, and dry seed heads feed birds. Good for sunny borders and containers.

A moisture-loving woodland perennial with a clump-forming growth habit. Erect, plume-like flowers bloom into light, airy clusters of white. Fern-like foliage is divided into bright green leaflets with finely serrated edges. Attracts butterflies.
A woodland perennial groundcover with large, heart-shaped leaves in shades of chartreuse and lime green. Blue springtime flowers look similar to forget-me-nots. Can tolerate full shade.

A shrubby evergreen perennial that forms an upright, mounding ground cover. Tiny leaves are oval, lemon-scented and dark green. Foliage tips turn yellow in cool weather. Dainty lilac-pink flowers bloom in summer. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.

This evergreen, clumping perennial bears white, double to semi-double flowers in winter. The blooms face out above thick green leaves and brighten dark beds. Deer tend to leave the foliage alone. Use it in entry pots, woodland beds, or shaded borders. Rich, well-drained soil helps roots grow. Every part is toxic if eaten.

Layered white petals edged in rose open on this evergreen, clumping perennial during winter and early spring. Leathery green leaves give shade beds year-round structure, and deer usually pass them by. Use it beneath deciduous trees or beside shaded paths. Rich, well-drained soil and mulch support deep roots; all parts are toxic if eaten.
An evergreen perennial flower that forms compact cushions of green, grass-like leaf blades. Stiff, upright stems bear bright rosy-pink poofy flower heads throughout summer. Tolerant of heat and salt.

botanicalName: Silene uniflora 'Druett's Variegated', S. vulgaris maritima
description: An herbaceous perennial that forms a low cushion. Small leaves are variegated gray-green with irregular light yellow margins. White, unusual flowers form a deep cup that flares with rounded petals at the mouth. Buds are blush pink. Long bloom season in mild climates. Attracts butterflies and hummingbirds.
An herbaceous perennial prized for large and fragrant, double white flowers with light yellow centers. Lush and dark green, attractively divided foliage.

A dwarf semi-evergreen shrub that forms a multi-branching bush. Slender, silvery white, velvet-coated leaves are very aromatic with the signature scent of sage considered sacred by some. In summer, very tall stalks carry pale, two-lipped flowers. Attracts native bees, hummingbirds and other pollinators, and beneficial insects. Use on slopes for erosion control. Native to California. More compact than the species.

commonName: Dwarf Heronsbill, Bishop's Form Alpine Geranium
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a low, mounding groundcover. Dark green leaves are small, oval, and scalloped on the edges. Large, saucer-shaped flowers are light pink with dark pink veins. Attracts pollinators. Blooms from late spring through late summer. Can tolerate light foot traffic.

An evergreen shrub that forms a dwarf rounded mound. Silvery foliage is finely divided, conifer-like and pungently fragrant when touched. Button-like flowerheads bloom in bright mustard-yellow throughout summer.

An herbaceous perennial with a more compact growth habit than the species. From spring through fall, tall forked stems carry rounded clusters of vivid pinkish-purple flowers. Attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Leaves are dark green, lance-shaped, and have serrated edges. Self-sows.

commonName: Dwarf Mouse Eared Tickseed, Lobed Tickseed
description: An easy-to-grow perennial with golden yellow flowers that rise above a mound of simple green leaves. Dead-head regularly to extend a long blooming season. Attracts pollinators. Prefers more moisture than others in the genus.

An evergreen perennial that forms a trailing carpet. Flowers are 5-petaled pinwheels of periwinkle blue. Springtime blooms are tucked into the dark green foliage. Leaves are thick, elliptic, and smaller than V. major.

A deciduous shrub with a wiry-stemmed, mat-forming growth habit. Late summer flowers are five-petalled and bright blue. Foliage is fresh green, oval to egg-shaped, and turns bronze-red in fall. Spreads by rhizomes.

A self-sowing, ornamental perennial known for its captivating flowers that nod and sway in the wind. Flowers are bright red and yellow with sweet, nectar-filled spurs and yellow stamens. Leaves are lacy and fresh green. Beneficial to many birds, butterflies, and other pollinators. Native to woodland areas of the Pacific Coast.

An evergreen perennial that forms a trailing carpet. Flowers are 5-petaled pinwheels of white. Springtime blooms are tucked into the dark green foliage. Leaves are thick, elliptic, and smaller than V. major.

An annual bulb that forms a compact, trailing tuft of grassy foliage. Disk-shaped, double flowers feature pale pink petals with fringed edges and maroon centers. Long bloom cycle from spring into fall. Attracts bees and butterflies. Makes a good cut flower. Flowers are fragrant and edible.

An annual bulb that forms a compact, trailing tuft of grassy foliage. Disk-shaped, double flowers feature bright white petals with fringed edges. Long bloom cycle from spring into fall. Attracts bees and butterflies. Makes a good cut flower. Flowers are fragrant and edible.

An easy-to-grow perennial with double to semi-double, golden daisy-like flowers that rise above compact mounds of narrow, hairy leaves. Attracts pollinators. Dead head regularly get the most out of the blooming period.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact clump. Mid-green leaves are crinkled, slender, and fragrant. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in bright violet-blue. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A sterile-hybrid perennial shrub that forms a compact bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Pale pink to bright white flowers and linear, bright green foliage are aromatic. Thin flower spikes bloom on very long stems in summer, good for drying. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

An evergreen, mounding California native shrub-like perennial with a dense, rounded habit. Slightly sticky green foliage is covered from spring into summer with soft yellow flowers edged in white, each marked with orange in the throat. A strong choice for native, habitat, and pollinator-focused plantings, where it attracts hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies. Best performance comes with good drainage, light shade in hot inland sites, and occasional deep watering once established.

A shrubby perennial that forms a slowly creeping ground cover. Tiny leaves are oval, aromatic and deep green. Dainty lilac-pink flowers bloom in early summer. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, uniform, well-branched bush. Evergreen in mild winters. Bright purple-blue flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Throughout summer, large, dense flower spikes bloom on sturdy stems. Flowers in the first year. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. Good tolerance to foliar diseases. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact clump. Dark green leaves are egg-shapeed and fragrant. Upright stalks carry tubular, two-lipped flowers in bright coral pink and red. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

commonName: Emerald Blue Moss Pink, Moss Phlox
description: Low-growing perennial with narrow needle-like foliage, and abundant and showy spring and summer flowers.

commonName: Emerald Falls Ponysfoot, Silver Nickel Vine
description: A creeping, cascading perennial that does well in a hanging basket. Leaves are emerald-green and kidney-shaped. More compact than 'Silver Falls'.

A short-lived perennial that forms a bushy, spreading carpet. From late spring into fall, constant blooms attract butterflies. Midsize flowers in a variety of colors open in rounded clusters, nestled among the well-branched foliage. Opposite leaves are green, egg-shaped, and coarsely toothed. Resistant to powdery mildew. Cold and heat tolerant. 'Endurascape Blue' has bright, violet-blue flowers. 'Endurascape Hot Pink' has hot pink flowers. 'Endurascape Purple' has deep royal purple flowers. 'Endurascape Red' has fiery red flowers. 'Endurascape White Blush' has white flowers with a pink blush. 'Endurascape White' has white flowers.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Purple-blue flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Flower spikes bloom from late spring into summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.
A perennial selected for hanging baskets or as a small-scale groundcover. Leaves are small, toothed, and medium to light green. Flowers are dainty, five-petaled and white with yellow centers.

An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a low, trailing habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers appear in scarlet-red. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, oval to linear, and silver-green. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Flowers and green linear foliage are aromatic. Plump, dark blue-violet flower heads are topped by extravagant, large, flag-like bracts. Blooms in spring, and re-blooms in favorable conditions. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. Good resistance to foliar disease.
An evergreen perennial forming a carpet of dense and rounded flower clusters in pure white. Narrow and shiny, dark green leaves. May be semi-evergreen in colder winter climates.

commonName: False Heather, Mexican Heather, Hawaiian Heather
description: An upright to trailing evergreen shrub. Profusely re-blooming flowers are small, star-shaped and lavender-purple. Leaves are small, glossy and lance-shaped. Stems are reddish-brown. Attracts pollinators.

commonName: False Heather, Mexican Heather, Hawaiian Heather
description: An upright to trailing evergreen shrub. Profusely re-blooming flowers are small, star-shaped and lavender-purple. Leaves are small, glossy and lance-shaped. Stems are reddish-brown. Attracts pollinators.
A colorful perennial with pinwheel-like flowers in burnt orange. Valued for very long blooming period.

A hybrid perennial shrub that forms an airy bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Dark violet-blue flowers and silver-green foliage are pungently aromatic. Ferny leaves are finely divided. Unique flower spikes, forked into three parts, bloom throughout summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.
An herbaceous perennial prized for large, double white flowers with red flecks near the centers. Lush and dark green, attractively divided foliage.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in bright wine red. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink and white.

White double flowers carry bold magenta edges on this evergreen, clumping perennial, creating strong winter contrast. Dark leaves hold the mound together after bloom and resist most deer browsing. Use it along shaded walks, beneath open trees, or in seasonal containers. Rich, drained soil and mulch keep roots cool; all parts are toxic when eaten.

A compact, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with upright, branching stems and a tidy border habit. Glossy, lance-shaped green leaves line reddish-brown stems, with bright crimson, tubular bell-shaped flowers produced from late spring into fall. A strong choice for perennial borders, pollinator gardens, coastal plantings, and cut flower use, with nectar-rich blooms that attract hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies. Benefits from well-drained soil and deadheading to support repeat bloom.
A subshrub with a finely textured, multi-branching form. Bright green, nearly leafless stems carry masses of coral-red, tubular flowers. Blooms in spring and summer. Attracts hummingbirds.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in bright green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in vibrant red.
An annual that forms a trailing mound. Rosy pink blooms from late spring into fall attract butterflies and other pollinators. Excellent powdery mildew resistance.
An annual that forms a trailing mound. Medium purple blooms from late spring into fall attract butterflies and other pollinators. Excellent powdery mildew resistance.
An annual that forms a trailing mound. Bright red blooms from late spring into fall attract butterflies and other pollinators. Excellent powdery mildew resistance.
An annual that forms a trailing mound. Bright white blooms from late spring into fall attract butterflies and other pollinators. Excellent powdery

Blood-red flowers open above this spreading, herbaceous perennial, then soften to orange and gold. Aromatic, fern-like leaves form a green mat below. Long summer bloom supports bees and butterflies. Use it to knit together sunny borders or stabilize slopes. Lean soil, good drainage, and light shearing help stems stay firm.

A perennial that forms showy flowers amongst tufts of grassy blue-gray foliage. Single flowers feature fringed, magenta-pink petals with white centers. Blooms emit a spicy fragrance. Attracts butterflies and bees. Makes a good cut flower. Flowers are edible.
An evergreen perennial forming a carpet of dense and rounded flower clusters in pale lavender. Narrow and shiny, dark green leaves. May be semi-evergreen in colder winter climates.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a multi-branching mound. Tiny leaves are dark green and elliptic. Dark, upright stalks carry intense red, two-lipped flowers held in maroon calyxes. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators and beneficial insects.

A perennial that forms a trailing, cascading ground cover. Silvery-green foliage is soft, fine and needle-like. Fiery golden-orange flowers are shaped like birds' beaks. Blooms in spring and summer. Works well in hanging pots.
A bushy, compact evergreen shrub. Long, tubular flowers come in fiery purplish lavender. Leaves are dark green and roughly oval. Attracts pollinators.

A perennial with a mounding or trailing habit. Purple or white daisy-like flowers with highly unique, spoon-like petals bloom from spring through fall. Flowers close at night. Foliage is bright green and narrowly oval. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A tender perennial that forms a compact, upright mound. Abundant, bright white blooms spring thru fall. Flowers close at night. Foliage is bright green, narrowly oval and slightly toothed. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A tender perennial that forms a compact, upright mound. Abundant, deep reddish-purple blooms spring through fall. Flowers close at night. Foliage is bright green, narrowly oval and slightly toothed. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Blue-green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers are bright blue, touched with purple. Blooms from late spring into summer. Attractive to bees and other pollinators. California native.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in rich purples. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in magenta.
An evergreen perennial that forms a compact mound of vibrant red foliage and stems. Leaves are ruffled and multi-lobed. Wiry stems carry small, white, bell-shaped flowers in summer.

commonName: Fragrant Pitcher Sage, Island Pitcher Sage
description: A semi-evergreen perennial subshrub. Strongly fragrant leaves are fuzzy, green and semi-triangular. Scented blooms in spring and summer attract many pollinators. Like strands of lavender lanterns, foxglove-like flowers are held in calyces along lax stems. California native.
Woodland perennial with lovely arching stems, broad oval leaves with white margins, and small clusters of fragrant bell-shaped greenish white flowers.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with oval to heart-shaped, corrugated, deep green leaves with white margins. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with broadly heart-shaped, corrugated, blue-green leaves with yellow margins. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.

A sterile-hybrid perennial shrub that forms a mounding bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Purple flowers and linear, silver-green foliage are aromatic. Thin flower spikes bloom on very long stems in summer, good for drying. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A perennial shrub that forms a mounding bush or hedge. In mild winter climates, foliage is evergreen and light purple-blue flower spikes bloom nearly year round. Flowers and foliage are aromatic. Ferny, gray-green leaves are linear with square-toothed margins. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A semi-evergreen herbaceous perennial that forms an upright clump. Tall stalks bear large, two-lipped, vibrant purple flowers held in dark plum calyxes. Blooms from spring to frost. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators, and beneficial insects. Green leaves are triangular, textured, and aromatic when touched.

A semi-deciduous perennial that spreads by rhizomes. Bright green leaves are large, rounded, hairy and arranged in low-growing rosettes. White, rose, or purple flower clusters bloom on thick stems in spring.
A low and spreading perennial with colorful daisy-like flowers in a mix of cheery colors. Narrow, silvery green foliage. Tough and low-maintenance.

A tender perennial with a shrublike form. Stems are slender and red. Leaves are oblong to ovate, shiny, and green. Pendent, fuchsia-like flower clusters in pink or red bloom from fall through spring. Can tolerate full shade. Does not survive frost. Treat as an annual in colder climates, or move indoors throughout winter.

commonName: Furman's Red Autumn Sage, Cherry Sage
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a robust mound. Green leaves are crinkled and slender. Dark stalks carry two-lipped, bright magenta-red flowers held in blackish calyxes. Blooms from summer through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, velvety glaucous leaves are blue-green, flushed with pink. Chartreuse-green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a shrubby, compact clump. Edible, gray-green leaves are aromatic, soft-textured, and oval. Short stalks carry spikes of two-lipped flowers in lavender-blue. Blooms in summer. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. S. officinalis is known for its culinary and medicinal uses.

A perennial with upright-sprawling stems, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are more slender than the species. Spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers are garnet red. Super abundant blooms from late spring to fall. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. Longer lived than most other penstemons.
An herbaceous perennial featuring tall and airy, wand-like flower clusters in white to pink. Narrow and lance-shaped foliage. Valued for long blooming season, especially if occasionally sheared.

botanicalName: Veronica peduncularis 'Georgia Blue', V. umbrosa 'Georgia Blue'
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a low, spreading mound. In spring, prolific blooms attract hummingbirds and other pollinators. Tiny, saucer-shaped flowers are blue with white centers. Foliage emerges reddish, matures to deep green and turns burgundy-bronze in cool weather. Leaves are lance-shaped and have toothed edges.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in silvery peachy pink. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in creamy white.

A perennial with a compact, mounding growth habit that spreads slowly by underground runners. Gray-green leaves are small, textured and fragrant. Upward reaching stems carry two-lipped flowers in bright blue. Blooms from spring to fall with heaviest blooms in warm weather. Attracts pollinators. Native to Mexico.

botanicalName: Lavandula steochas ssp. pedunculata 'Ghostly Princess' PP 29,697
description: A perennial shrub that forms a compact, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Flowers and linear, silvery-green foliage are aromatic. Plump, violet flower heads are topped by pale pink, flag-like bracts. Blooms in spring and reblooms in favorable conditions. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. Selected for disease resistance and cold hardiness.

A water-loving, woodland perennial that forms slowly spreading clumps of broad, lush foliage. Gigantic, kidney-shaped leaves are glossy green. In fall, tall flower stalks carry yellow, daisy-like blooms.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in ginger yellow to copper. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in yellow and light pink.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, gray-blue-green leaves have variegated white margins. Creamy yellow inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Abundant blooms cluster atop stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.
A perennial with a compact, mounding growth habit. Masses of fragrant, four-petaled flowers bloom in yellows and oranges from spring to summer. Medium green leaves are long and narrow.

commonName: Gold Coin, Sea Aster, Sea Daisy
description: A perennial groundcover with a low, spreading growth habit that forms mounds of silvery-green foliage. Abundant, daisy-like flowers bloom in bright golden-yellow.

A perennial that forms a trailing, cascading ground cover. Silvery-green foliage is soft, fine and needle-like. Golden-orange, red-tipped flowers are shaped like birds' beaks. Blooms in spring and summer. Does well in hanging pots.

A clump-forming woodland perennial with dangling, rosy pink, heart-shaped flowers. Chartreuse foliage is larger than other varieties and is similar in appearance to carrot tops. Blooms in cool weather. Attracts hummingbirds.

A perennial forming compact mounds of maple-like, wine-red leaves with chartreuse green margins. Thin upright stalks carry wands of airy flower clusters in white. Hybrid between Huechera and Tiarella.

A perennial with a low, mounding growth habit. Foliage is lacy, aromatic, and golden-green. White, daisy-like flowers rise in clusters on bare stalks. Attracts pollinators. Edible flowers are used in herbal teas and medicine.

A shrubby perennial that forms a spreading, mounding ground cover. Tiny leaves are narrow, aromatic, and bright green with variegated golden edges. Leaves are edible. Dainty light pink flowers bloom in early summer. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.

An herbaceous perennial with a compact, clumping growth habit. Flowers are upturned, less than 1 inch wide, star-shaped, and light lavender-blue with white throats. Blooms from late spring to fall. Bright golden-green foliage forms showy cushions. Attracts hummingbirds.

A vigorous mat-forming perennial with finely dissected, bright green foliage. Lightly fragrant, bright yellow flowers bloom continually in mild weather. Attracts bees and butterflies. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a self-sowing patch of summer-fall blooms. Large daisy-like flowers have golden rays and a conical, dark brown center disk. Green leaves are lance-shaped and hairy. Good cut flower. Often grown as an annual. Attracts butterflies.

A perennial shrub that forms a dense bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Deep purple flowers and silvery-white-green foliage are aromatic. Linear leaves are toothed like L. dentata, though are more broad. Long, dense flower spikes bloom in summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.
