An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Fleshy, triangular, blue-green leaves are arranged in spirals. Chartreuse-green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A semi-woody perennial that forms a spreading, mounded ground cover. Linear foliage is dark green and hairy. In late spring, deep violet-blue flowers dot the foliage. Flowers are small and star shaped.

A perennial shrub that forms a mounding bush or hedge. In mild winter climates, foliage is evergreen and light purple-blue flower spikes bloom nearly year round. Flowers and foliage are aromatic. Ferny, gray leaves are linear with square-toothed margins. New leaves are downy. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.
Perennial with colorful daisy-like flowers with brown and yellow centers. Evergreen dark green foliage with woolly undersides. USDA zones: 8 - 11
An herbaceous woodland perennial with oval to heart-shaped, blue-green leaves with bold chartreuse centers. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.
Perennial with tiny deep green leaves. Can be used as groundcover or between stepping stones.
A perennial groundcover with tiny, deep green leaves forming a dense, evergreen carpet. Perfect between stepping stones, in rock gardens, or as a lawn substitute.
An evergreen shrub that forms a compact rounded mound. Deep green foliage is finely divided, rosemary-like and fragrant when touched. Button-like flowerheads bloom in butter-yellow throughout spring.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in silvery green with burgundy veining. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink.

A sterile-hybrid perennial shrub that forms a mounding bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Dark purple-blue flowers and linear foliage are intensely aromatic. Green leaves age to gray-green. Plump flower spikes bloom on very long stems in summer, good for drying. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A Mediterranean evergreen perennial with fuzzy gray-green, lance-shaped foliage. Funnel-shaped flowers display fused, lavender blue petals and white centers. Blooms in summer. Makes a good groundcover.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with oval to heart-shaped, gold and lime-green leaves. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped, fragrant flowers.
A perennial selected for hanging baskets or as a small-scale groundcover. Leaves are small, toothed, and medium to light green. Flowers are dainty, five-petaled and medium blue.
A perennial selected for hanging baskets or as a small-scale groundcover. Leaves are small, toothed, and medium to light green. Flowers are dainty, five-petaled and pure white.

A tropical perennial with 3 to 6 foot long, arrow-shaped, prominently veined, ruffled leaves of bright green. Flowers are greenish-white and not too showy. Can tolerate full shade. Can be grown indoors.

A showy, well-branched perennial. Star-shaped flowers are lightly fragrant and dramatically colorful. 'Hawaiian Flare' is known for its spectacular orange hues. Blooms in summer, as well as continually in mild weather. Foliage is lacy and green. Attracts bees and butterflies. 'Orange Drop' has bi-colored scarlet and gold petals around a gold center. 'Red Drop' has apricot-red-orange petals around a gold center. 'Yellow Drop' has bi-colored yellow and orange-red petals around a gold center.

A semi-deciduous perennial that spreads by rhizomes. Dark green leaves are large, toothed and arranged in low-growing clumps. White, rose, or purple flower clusters bloom on thick stems in spring. Foliage turns red in fall. Used as a groundcover.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a compact, rounded mound. Green leaves are fragrant and egg-shaped. Upright stems carry large, two-lipped flowers in a variety of colors. Blooms from summer through fall. Attracts pollinators. 'Heatwave' series thrives in hot, dry conditions. 'Blast' has salmon pink flowers. 'Blaze' has crimson red flowers with dark calyxes. 'Breeze' has bluish-purple flowers with dark calyxes. 'Brilliance' has hot magenta pink flowers with dark calyxes. 'Sparkle' has pink flowers with white centers and dark calyxes. 'Glow' has soft peachy pink flowers. 'Glitter' has light pinkish-purple flowers. 'Glimmer' has crisp cream-white flowers with dark calyxes. 'Glare' has bright white flowers.

commonName: Helene von Stein Lamb's Ear, Big Ears
botanicalName: Stachys byuzantina 'Helene von Stein', Helen von Stein
description: A perennial that forms a dense mat of mounding rosettes. Velvet-soft leaves are extra large, silvery-green and narrowly oval with serrated edges. Rarely flowers.
Perennial with rough, dark green leaves with prominent veins and rounded clusters of tiny, sweetly fragrant flowers. Can be grown as a summer annual.

A perennial tuber that forms a dramatic clump. Leaves are broad, arrow-shaped, and glossy with prominent veins. Coloration is deep green with variegated white spots. Spring and summer-blooming flowers are elegant, cone-shaped, and fragrant. White spathes surround a yellow spadix of tiny true flowers.

A perennial shrub that forms a mound compact enough to be considered dwarf. Evergreen in mild winters. Super dark violet-blue flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Flower spikes bloom throughout summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.

A perennial shrub that forms a mounding bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild climates. Deep violet flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Large, plump flower spikes bloom on long stems throughout summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.

A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are larger than the species. Spikes of nodding, bell-shaped flowers are white, accented with pink. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators.

A tender perennial that forms a bushy, trailing mound. From late spring into fall, blooms attract butterflies and other pollinators. Bright purple flowers open in large, rounded clusters, nestled among the foliage. Densely arranged leaves are green and nettle-shaped. Resistant to powdery mildew.
A vigorous hybrid annual that forms a trailing mound. Bright red blooms from late spring into fall attract butterflies and other pollinators. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

botanicalName: Anemone x hybrida 'Honorine Jobert', A. x hybrida 'Alba'
description: A semi-deciduous, clumping herbaceous perennial with dark green, grape-like basal foliage and tall, branching flower stems. White semi-double flowers with yellow stamens bloom from late summer into fall, adding late-season brightness to borders and woodland edges. Performs best with rich, well-drained soil and consistent moisture.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact mound. Bright green leaves are oval and fragrant like blackcurrants. Upright stalks carry two-lipped, bi-colored flowers in bright cherry red and white. Flower color changes slightly with the seasons. Blooms from spring to frost. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects and wildlife.
A low bushy perennial with fuzzy gray leaves and orange tubular flowers. Attracts hummingbirds in summer.

An herbaceous perennial that forms an upright, slowly spreading ground cover. Large, light green leaves are aromatic, crinkled, toothed and triangular. Upright stalks carry large whorls of fragrant, two-lipped flowers in rosy pink. Blooms in spring and summer. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to California. Tolerates dry shade.

botanicalName: Epilobium canum ssp. canum, uzauschneria californica
description: An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a mounding habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers appear in red-orange. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, linear to oval, and gray-green. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

An upright evergreen shrub with hairy, tubular flowers that are red at the base and creamy golden yellow to orange at the tips. Leaves are lance-shaped, dark green and flushed with bronze-maroon. Attracts pollinators.

A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Maroon-green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers are pinkish-white. Blooms from mid spring to early summer. Very attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. Well-suited for hot, humid summers.

A vigorous winter-blooming, clumping evergreen perennial with bold and serrated, large and leathery leaves. Clusters of cup-shaped, nodding flowers in a variety of colors. More robust than other Helleborus cultivars. 'Red' has deep purplish red flowers. 'Rose' has light, rosy pink flowers. 'White' has pure white flowers.

An evergreen perennial that forms magnificent flower spikes, which emerge from a central stalk of whorled, dark green leaves. Flared, bell-shaped flowers are apricot-orange with freckled, creamy orange throats and edged in dark pink. Attracts pollinators throughout their long bloom season from summer through fall. An award-winning sterile hybrid of Digitalis and Isoplexis.

A trailing evergreen groundcover that resembles strawberry, but with smaller, nearly tasteless fruit. Glossy green leaflets stay low to the ground. Tiny yellow flowers appear from late spring to early fall. Leaves, flowers, and fruits are said to be medicinal and edible. Attracts birds. Native to East Asia.

commonName: Indian Summer Gloriosa Daisy, Black Eyed Susan
description: An herbaceous perennial that forms a self-sowing patch of upright, long-stemmed, summer-fall blooms. Oversized, daisy-like flowers have yellow petals and conical, brown centers. Green leaves are lance-shaped and hairy. Good cut flower. Often grown as an annual.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a round, upright mound. Purple-tinged, gray-green leaves are egg-shaped and fragrant. Tall stalks carry spikes of fuzzy, two-lipped flowers in violet-blue. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects, and wildlife.

A moss-like perennial that forms a carpet of tiny, deep green leaves. Small white flowers dot the foliage in spring. Good for use along pathways or between stepping stones. Can tolerate light foot traffic. Tolerates more sun than Scotch Moss.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in marbled dark green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in pale pink.

botanicalName: Achillea millefolium rosea 'Island Pink', 'Pink Island Form'
description: A perennial, clumping herbaceous plant with ferny aromatic foliage and flat-topped flower clusters held above the leaves. Long-season bloom supports bees, butterflies, and beneficial insects, and the stems are useful fresh or dried. It is a dependable low-water perennial for sunny borders with well-drained soil.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped flowers in white opening from pink buds. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated leaf margins.

commonName: Ivory White Sticky Monkey Flower, Shrubby Monkey Flower
botanicalName: Mimulus aurantiacus x 'Ivory White', Diplacus 'Ivory White'
description: A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a sub-shrub of upright, unbranched stems. Summer dormant in hot, dry climates. Leaves are slender, dark green, and sticky. Lobed, funnel-shaped flowers are creamy ivory white. Spring to fall blooms attract butterflies and other pollinators. California native.

A shrubby perennial featuring glossy, bright green foliage with pointed lobes like Hedera (ivy). Rounded clusters of bright and showy flowers. Can be grown as annuals or houseplants outside of hardiness zones.
A woodland perennial groundcover with green-veined, silvery-white leaves that are large and heart-shaped. Blue springtime flowers look similar to forget-me-nots. Can tolerate full shade.

A shade-loving, evergreen perennial that forms a shrubby groundcover. Spreads by rhizomes. Dark green leaves are glossy and egg-shaped with toothed margins. Foliage is dense and whorled and branch tips. Small white flower spikes bloom in spring.
An evergreen shrub prized for fattened flower heads containing tiny dark purple flowers, topped with royal purple bracts resembling rabbit ears. Linear, gray-green foliage.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Spring-summer flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Plump flower heads are green with tiny violet flowers and are topped by white, flag-like bracts. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a rounded, upright subshrub. Leaves are slender, dark green, and sticky. Frilly, lobed, funnel-shaped flowers in a range of colors. Spring to fall blooms attract butterflies and other pollinators. California native. Color choices include: ‘Betabel’ - deep rosy-magenta Close ×

An easy-to-grow perennial. Daisy-like flowers display golden, fluted petals. Dark green foliage forms bushy mounds below the blooms. Attracts pollinators. Dead-head regularly to get the most out of the blooming period.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a dense, spreading mound. Blue-violet flowers are saucer-shaped and larger than the species. Long bloom cycle lasts from spring through fall. Dark green leaves are deeply lobed.
Perennial with oval to heart-shaped green foliage that radiates outwards from the center, with thin spikes that carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.

A low-water perennial with a mounding, trailing form. Gray-green foliage is soft and aromatic. Leaves are small, ovate and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of lavender-blue flowers bloom spring to fall. Attracts pollinators. Sterile selection of N. 'Walker's Low.'

A perennial that forms showy flowers amongst clumps of grassy gray-green foliage. Single flowers feature notched, purple-pink petals with white anthers. Blooms emit a spicy fragrance. Attracts butterflies and bees. Makes a good cut flower. Flowers are edible.

A semi-evergreen, mat-forming perennial groundcover. Scented, rounded green leaves turn red in cool weather. Lilac-pink flowers open from dark red buds from late spring into summer and feed butterflies. Sterile blooms make no seed. It spreads into a neat carpet for edging, slopes, rock gardens, and spaces beneath shrubs in well-drained soil.

A perennial, clumping herbaceous plant with ferny aromatic foliage and flat-topped flower clusters held above the leaves. Long-season bloom supports bees, butterflies, and beneficial insects, and the stems are useful fresh or dried. It is a dependable low-water perennial for sunny borders with well-drained soil.

An herbaceous perennial with a mounding, trailing habit. Lightly aromatic, heart-shaped leaves are silvery blue-green. Cascading, hop-like flower clusters are made of tiny purple blossoms tucked into pale green bracts that blush rosy pink. Blooms in summer and fall. Attracts pollinators.

A deciduous herbaceous perennial with a mounding growth habit. Cheerful late summer flowers bloom into multitudes of carmine, lavender, or purple petals that surround yellow centers. Beneficial to butterflies, moths, bees, and other pollinators.

An evergreen shrub with a compact, upright growth habit. Dark gray-green leaves are glossy, egg-shaped and aromatic. Dark, upright stems carry whorls of two-lipped flowers in intense cranberry red. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, dark gray-green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in creamy yellow on 6 - 8 inch tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.
A low and spreading perennial with colorful daisy-like flowers in a mix of cheery colors. Narrow, deep green foliage. Tough and low-maintenance.

A low-water perennial that forms a compact mound. Gray-green foliage is soft and aromatic. Leaves are very small, ovate and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of lavender-blue flowers bloom spring to fall. Attracts pollinators.

A low-water perennial with a rounded, mounding form. Gray-green foliage is soft and aromatic. Leaves are small, ovate and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of bright lavender-blue flowers bloom profusely and continuously. Attracts pollinators.
Low-growing perennial with rounded bronzy green leaves and small pink rounded flower heads.
A perennial that forms a basal clump of grassy leaves, more compact than the species. Purple, feathery, foxtail-like flowerheads top rigid, upright stalks in summer. Attracts pollinators.

A warm-season, slow-spreading perennial sod and groundcover grass with a low, mounding habit. Fine, deep green blades form dense, soft, undulating mats suited to no-mow lawn areas, paving joints, gentle slopes, and modern or Asian-inspired plantings. Best performance comes with warm conditions, good drainage, and consistent moisture during establishment.

A tender perennial or annual with a compact, upright growth habit. Deep green foliage is finely lobed. Wiry stems carry pincushion-like flowerheads in pure white. Blooms from spring through summer or fall. Attracts butterflies. A good cut flower.

A summer-blooming perennial with a compact growth habit. Foliage is aromatic and gray-green. Whorled flowers grow on vertical spikes. Anise-scented leaves make a delicious herbal tea. Great selection for pollinator gardens. Attracts hummingbirds, butterflies and bees. ‘Ambrosia’ has flowers in shades of pale rose and orange. ‘Coral’ has flowers in shades of coral-pink. ‘Gold’ has flowers in shades of golden-orange. ‘Silver Blue’ has flowers in shades of light lilac-blue. ‘Yellow’ has flowers in shades of bright yellow.

A low-growing perennial with a clumping growth habit and a soft texture. Bright green leaves are nearly circular with scalloped edges. Yellow-green flowers form frothy clusters in summer. Historically used as a medicinal herb. Can tolerate full shade.

From a low mat of gray-green leaves, this herbaceous perennial sends tall stems topped with flat white flower clusters. It comes from inland California populations and feeds many native insects. Use it in meadow plantings, oak-edge gardens, and dry slopes. Sun, open soil, and sharp drainage encourage a sturdy, natural form.

botanicalName: Stachys byuzantina, S. lanata, S. olympica
description: A perennial that forms a dense mat of mounding rosettes. Velvet-soft leaves are silver-green and tongue-shaped with serrated edges. Purple-pink two-lipped flowers arise in spike-like clusters in late spring or summer.

A tender perennial that forms a trailing, vigorous mound. From late spring into fall, blooms attract butterflies and other pollinators. Large flowers in bright colors open in rounded clusters, nestled among the well-branched foliage. Leaves are green and multi-lobed. Resistant to powdery mildew.

An upright, mounding evergreen shrub with pointed, dark green leaves. Tubular, red-orange flowers resemble sticks of dynamite. Blooms in abundance throughout summer. Attracts pollinators including butterflies, bees, and hummingbirds.

A hybrid perennial tuber that forms a dramatic clump. Deep green leaves are broad, arrow-shaped, glossy, and speckled with white. Burgundy red, petal-like spathes surround a golden spadix of tiny true flowers. Cone shaped flowers bloom in spring and summer.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, gray to green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in lavender pink on 1 - 2 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.

An evergreen shrub that forms a compact rounded mound. Silvery-gray-geen foliage is finely divided, conifer-like and fragrant when touched. Button-like flowerheads bloom in bright yellow throughout summer.
An upright evergreen shrub with spreading branches. Profusely re-blooming flowers are small, star-shaped and lavender-purple. Leaves are small, bright green and lance-shaped. Attracts pollinators.

A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of large, bell-shaped flowers are pastel purple with white throats. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a shrubby mound. Medium green leaves are slender and fragrant. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in light yellow. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A shrubby evergreen perennial that forms a creeping ground cover. Tiny leaves are oval, aromatic and deep green. Edible leaves are lemon-flavored. Dainty lilac-pink flowers bloom in early summer. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers in a variety of colors. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated margins.

An herbaceous perennial that forms upright, bushy mounds of soft, edible, gray-green leaves with a minty scent and flavor. Flowers are summer-blooming, two lipped, and colored white with a purple hue. Native to Europe.
A low growing perennial grown mainly for small and woolly, pale green leaves. Leaves emit a pleasant licorice fragrance in hot weather.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in deep green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in pale pink.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed, ruffled leaves in lime green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in lime green with ruffled edges. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white.

A shrubby evergreen perennial that forms a mounding, creeping ground cover. Tiny leaves are oval, aromatic and lime green. Dainty lilac-pink flowers bloom in summer. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.
A low growing perennial grown mainly for small and woolly, chartreuse green leaves. Leaves emit a pleasant licorice fragrance in hot weather.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a tall, bushy mound. Rich green leaves are large, heart-shaped, textured, and fragrant like pine. Upright stalks carry two-lipped, vibrant violet-blue flowers held in chartreuse-lime bracts. Blooms from summer through fall. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects and wildlife.

An evergreen shrub with an upright, clumping growth habit. Orange, woolly, tubular flowers are arranged in whorls up and down the stems. Blooms from late spring to fall. Leaves are dark green and narrow with slightly serrated margins. Often treated as a perennial because it dies back from frost, but will resprout from older woody stems. Attracts pollinators.

A resilient semi-evergreen shrub that forms a rounded mound. Green leaves are small and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in rosy red. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A showy perennial ground cover that creeps from a central crown via above-ground runners. Glossy, dark green leaves are three-lobed, rounded and toothed. Flowers are bright rosy-red, five-petaled and bloom from spring through fall. Blossoms are occasionally followed by small, seedy strawberry-fruits. A hybrid between Fragaria and Potentilla.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in marbled dark blue-green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in coral pink.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a neat, compact mound. Bright green leaves are oval and fragrant like blackcurrants. Upright stalks carry two-lipped, bi-colored flowers in bright red and white. Flower color changes slightly with the seasons. Blooms year round in frost-free zones. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects and wildlife. Disease resisitant.

commonName: Little Miss Gina Peruvian Lily, Lily of the Incas
description: A dwarf hybrid perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is bright pink with a yellow blotch. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower.

commonName: Little Miss Tara Peruvian Lily, Lily Of The Incas
description: A dwarf hybrid perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower color is red-pink with a yellow blotch and black markings. A superb cut flower.

A dwarf self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, gray to green, and aromatic. Cheery yellow flat-topped flower umbels grow in on 1 - 2 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.

botanicalName: Perovskia atriplicifolia 'Little Spire' PP 11,643, Salvia yangii
description: A shrubby perennial with fine, feathery, aromatic, gray-green foliage. Lavender-blue flowers appear in tall, airy, branched stalks. Blooms from summer to early fall. Attracts bees and butterflies. A compact variety.

A low-water perennial with a short, spreading form. Gray-green leaves are soft and aromatic. Leaves are small, ovate and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of lavender-purple flowers bloom spring to fall. Attracts pollinators.
A small, bushy perennial with rich green foliage and an abundance of small, daisy-like, light to blush pink flowers. Flower centers are yellow. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.
A woodland perennial groundcover with silvery-white, green-veined leaves that are large and heart-shaped. Blue springtime flowers look similar to forget-me-nots. Can tolerate full shade.

An evergreen subshrub with an upright, multi-branching growth habit that come become a bit rangy. Leaves are downy, crinkled and gray-green. Tall, wand-like stalks carry outstanding cup-shaped flowers in deep red. Blooms from summer into fall. Attracts bees and other pollinators. Native to the Southwest, including California.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a fountain-shaped clump. Dark green leaves are aromatic, toothed and oval. Upright stalks carry spikes of tubular, two-lipped flowers in bright and dark purple. Blooms from early spring through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Related to S. 'Wendy's Wish'.

An evergreen biennial that forms spikes of flared, bell-shaped flowers which emerge from stalks of whorled, gray-green leaves. Flowers appear in rich purple-pink with maroon-freckled white throats. Attracts pollinators throughout their bloom season from spring through summer.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed, frilly leaves. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white. 'Vivid' has bright, lime green foliage.

A semi-evergreen perennial with clumping, fibrous roots and lobed, glossy green foliage. Upright, wiry stems carry single, saucer-shaped flowers. Petal-like sepals are fuchsia-pink and stamens are golden-yellow. Blooms from late summer through fall. Flowers provide nutrient-rich pollen for butterflies and bees. Spent flowers form white, cottony seedheads. Creeping underground roots will naturalize plantings over time.
A clump-forming woodland perennial with dangling, pinkish red, heart-shaped flowers. Rich green foliage is similar in appearance to carrot tops. Blooms in cool weather. Attracts hummingbirds.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a sturdy, well-branched clump. Gray-green leaves are slender, crinkled, soft and fragrant. Tall stalks carry large spikes of two-lipped flowers in white. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Cold hardy.

A perennial shrub that forms a dense, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Summer flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Plump, dark purple flower heads are topped with bright purple, flag-like bracts. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A perennial shrub that forms a dense, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Summer flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Plump, rosy-purple flower heads are topped with light pink, flag-like bracts. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A North American perennial that forms mounds of tall, upright blooms throughout summer. Large, fragrant flowers appear with drooping soft-pink petals and brownish-orange seed cones. Low-growing leaves are lance-shaped, green, and slightly hairy. A popular herbal remedy today, all plant parts have been used in Native American medicine for hundreds of years. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.
A semi-evergreen perennial groundcover with crinkled leaves of green and dark burgundy-brown. Blue flower spikes appear in spring and early summer. spreads by runners. Can tolerate full shade.

A dwarf semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact clump. Mid-green leaves are slender and fragrant. Upright stalks carry chunky spikes of two-lipped flowers in dark violet. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

An herbaceous perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Blue-green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers fade from sky blue to purple. Blooms from late spring into summer. Attractive to bees and other pollinators. California native.
Fast growing perennial vine with heart-shaped or three-lobed leaves in golden-green.

commonName: Marin Pink California Fuchsia, Hummingbird Trumpet
description: An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a mounding habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers appear in pink. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, linear, and gray-green. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

A perennial with a rounded, mounding growth habit that spreads slowly by underground runners. Silvery-gray leaves are small, textured, and fragrant. Upright stems carry small two-lipped flowers in dark violet-blue. Blooms in summer. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Cold hardy.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in peachy-gold. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in reddish pink.
Shrubby perennial with heart to kidney-shaped foliage with crinkled margins. Loose and rounded clusters of showy and colorful flowers.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, deep green leaves often emerge burgundy. Lime-green, red-eyed inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop red stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A deciduous perennial shrub with an upright form that spreads wider by rhizomes. Large flowers display white crepe-papery petals and poofy yellow stamens. Blooms in spring and summer. Attracts pollinators. Leaves are gray-green, narrowly lobed, and rough to the touch. Native to Southern California.

An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a tidy, clumping habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers appear in vibrant scarlet red. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Silver leaves are felty, pointed, oval, and larger than those of E. canum. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

An evergreen perennial that forms a dense, mounding ground cover. Bright green leaves are toothed on the edges. Abundant fan-shaped flowers bloom in two-toned lilac-mauve. Long bloom period from late spring to frost. Attracts butterflies, bees and other pollinators. Heat tolerant. Does well in a hanging basket.

commonName: Mauve Creeping Thyme, Mother Of Thyme
description: A shrubby perennial that forms a creeping ground cover. Tiny leaves are oval, aromatic, fuzzy and green. Dainty mauve colored flowers bloom in spring or summer. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a trailing, mounding ground cover. Dainty, saucer-shaped flowers are pink with dark veins and pale centers. Long bloom cycle lasts from spring through fall. Soft grayish green leaves are deeply lobed. Sterile hybrid.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a multi-branching clump. Mid-green leaves are aromatic, scallop-edged, and slender. Tall, upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in violet-indigo. Blooms in summer. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A perennial shrub with a compact, mounding form. Evergreen in mild winters. Purple-blue flowers and linear, variegated foliage are aromatic. Leaves are gray green with light yellow margins. Flower spikes bloom in late spring and summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. High tolerance to heat, drought and humidity.

A perennial selected for hanging baskets or as a small-scale groundcover. Leaves are small, toothed, and medium to light green. Flowers are dainty, five-petaled and either blue, pink, or pure white. Megacopa series is noted for larger flowers, heat tolerance, and uniform branching habit.

A perennial tuber that forms a dramatic clump. Deep green leaves are broad, arrow-shaped, glossy, and speckled with white. Spring and summer-blooming flowers are elegant, cone-shaped, and fragrant. Petal-like spathes are apricot orange with a pink blush, and surround a creamy white spadix of tiny true flowers.
Perennial with rough gray-green foliage and colorful single to double daisy-like flowers that appear over a long blooming period.

A perennial shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit. Daisy-like flowers are fragrant, bright yellow, and have golden centers. Blooms in fall, winter, and spring. Attracts pollinators. Deep green leaves are intensely fragrant, narrow, and finely divided.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a robust, spreading mound. Dark gray-green leaves are lance-shaped, white and hairy below, and aromatic. Long, sweeping stalks carry white, two-lipped flowers held in fuzzy, bright purple calyxes. Blooms from fall through spring in mild climates. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators, and beneficial insects. Native to Mexico.

An evergreen shrub that forms a rounded bush. Leaves are glossy, mid-green and oval. Showy terminal clusters of tubular, bright orange flowers attract hummingbirds and butterflies. Blooms nearly year round.

A perennial that spreads quickly by rhizomes. Stems are tinted red. Green leaves are finely textured. From spring through fall, stalks bloom with red and yellow flowers. Flowers are tubular with flared, trumpet-like tips. Attracts butterflies and hummingbirds.

A perennial shrub with an upright, spreading growth habit. Daisy-like flowers are fragrant, bright yellow, and have golden centers. Blooms in fall, winter, and spring. Attracts pollinators. Deep green leaves are intensely fragrant, narrow, and finely divided.

A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Blue-green, purple-tinged leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of nodding, bell-shaped flowers are dark bluish purple. Blooms from late spring to fall. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. Longer lived than most other penstemons.

commonName: Midnight Mexican Bush Sage, Velvet Sage
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a robust, rounded clump. Dark gray-green leaves are lance-shaped, white and hairy below, and fragrant. Long, sweeping stalks carry two-lipped, bright purple flowers held in fuzzy, deep purple calyxes. Blooms from fall through spring in mild climates. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in burgundy spotted with hot pink. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, dull green leaves turn dark ruby-purple in fall. New growth comes in dark burgundy. Chartreuse-green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop red stems in spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.
Perennial with oval to heart-shaped green and white foliage that radiates outwards from the center, with thin spikes that carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.

A compact semi-evergreen shrub that forms a rounded mound. Green leaves are small and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in bright red. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A compact semi-evergreen shrub that forms a rounded mound. Green leaves are small and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in bright purple held in dark purple calyxes. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A compact semi-evergreen shrub that forms a rounded mound. Green leaves are small and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in bright pink held in burgundy to green calyxes. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A compact semi-evergreen shrub that forms a rounded mound. Green leaves are small and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in salmon-pink. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A compact semi-evergreen shrub that forms a rounded mound. Green leaves are small and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in soft pink. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A compact semi-evergreen shrub that forms a rounded mound. Green leaves are small and aromatic. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in pure white held in medium green calyxes. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

An evergreen biennial that forms spikes of flared, bell-shaped flowers which emerge from stalks of whorled, gray-green leaves. Flowers appear in a mixed variety of colors. Attracts pollinators throughout their bloom season from spring through summer.

A clumping herbaceous perennial with green foliage and long-blooming lavender-blue daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. Flowers appear from summer into fall, supporting pollinators and extending border color. Useful in mixed perennial plantings and cut-flower programs. Performs best with well-drained soil and moderate, consistent irrigation.

Silver, scented leaves cover this evergreen, rounded California native shrub. Violet-blue flowers sit among large rose-purple bracts and feed bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. It grows wild on dry mountain slopes. Use it in habitat beds and on dry banks. Full sun, lean soil, and fast drainage keep the mound dense with little summer water.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers in creamy white with a light green flush. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated leaf margins.

botanicalName: Fragaria vesca ssp. californica 'Montana de Oro'
description: A perennial ground cover that spreads from a central crown via above-ground runners. Glossy, mid-green leaves are three-lobed, rounded and toothed. Flowers are white, five-petaled, and bloom in spring. Blossoms are followed by small, flavorful strawberry-fruits. Native to regions with a Mediterranean-like climate near the California coast. Does well in understory and dry shade.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, gray-green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in soft yellow on 1 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.

An easy-to-grow perennial. Daisy-like flowers display creamy yellow petals above bushy mounds of finely textured, threadlike foliage. Attracts pollinators. Dead head regularly to get the most out of the blooming period. Ideal for cut flower arragements.

An evergreen perennial that forms a shrubby mound. Bright green leaves are slender and fragrant when touched. Upright stalks carry two-lipped flowers in pale creamy yellow. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A clumping, evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial with soft gray-green leaves and flat yellow flower heads. Blooms rise above the foliage from spring into fall and feed butterflies. Use it in borders, dry gardens, or cut-flower plantings. It grows best in sunny sites with well-drained soil and occasional summer water during bloom.
A dense, mounding perennial subshrub. Foliage is silvery-green and fine. Long bloom cycle with peak in winter. Large, daisy-like flowers have white rays and broad, yellow centers.
A perennial with wiry stems carrying ruffled and rose-like flowers in scarlet orange. Attractive foliage forms lush green mounds.

commonName: Mrs. Robb's Bonnet, Robb's Wood Spurge
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, deep green leaves tint red in fall. Bright green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop stems in spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, mounding bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Cool purple-blue flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Profuse flower spikes bloom from late spring into summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.
Tuberous perennial with black foliage and bright, fiery red, star-shaped flowers.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact mound. Purple-tinged, gray-green leaves are egg-shaped and fragrant. Tall stalks carry spikes of fuzzy, two-lipped flowers in violet-blue. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects, and wildlife. Known as a dwarf S. 'Indigo Spires'.
An evergeen vine with sharply pointed and deeply lobed dark green leaves. Rounded greenish-white flower clusters followed by small black berries. Most often used as a groundcover.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, gray to green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in clean 1 foot tall stems in a range of colors. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat. 'New Vintage Red' has ruby red flowers. 'New Vintage Rose' has rose-pink flowers. 'New Vintage Violet' has cool magenta-pink flowers. 'New Vintage White' has bright white flowers.

A perennial ground cover that forms a dense, creeping carpet. Fills in cracks between stepping stones. Gray-green leaves are feathery and finely cut like miniature fern fronds. Foliage turns bronze in fall. Yellow button-like flowers. Tolerates regular foot traffic.

An herbaceous perennial with a short, mounding growth habit and abundant, petunia-like flowers in various shades. Exceptionally heat tolerant, works well in hanging baskets. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in bright silver, with wine-red undersides. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink. More cold hardy than other Heucheras.

A semi-evergreen perennial with a low, sprawling growth habit. Green leaves are narrow and fragrant. Upright stems carry two-lipped flowers in bright violet. Blooms from summer through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Very similar to S. greggii 'Purple'.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in rich green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in soft pink.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, flowers in dark purples, grays, and near-black. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated margins.

A hybrid perennial that forms rosettes of woolly, silvery-gray leaves. Long-stemmed daisy-like flowers have dark-brown composite centers. Flower colors vary by cultivar. Blooms in spring. 'Rose' aka 'KLEAT12610' displays petals in light rosy pink. 'Orange' aka 'KLEAT12609' displays petals in goldfish-orange. 'Fire' aka 'KLEAT12611' displays petals striped in rich orange and red.

An annual or perennial with a self-sowing, clump-forming growth habit. Yellow-orange flowers are silky, four-petaled, and cup or saucer shaped. Blooms from spring through summer. Foliage is delicate, finely divided, and blue-green. California native.

commonName: Orchid Frost Dead Nettle, Yellow Archangel
description: A perennial mat-forming groundcover that likes shade. Variegated foliage is frosty-white with dark green edges. Scalloped, quilted, heart-shaped leaves are arranged in opposite pairs on square stems. Short upright stalks carry hooded orchid-pink flowers throughout summer.

A deep blue-purple center gives each pale daisy on this mounding, tender perennial a clear eye. Flowers sit just above compact green leaves and draw bees during the cooler months. Use it in mass bedding, mixed pots, or low borders. Bright sun, drained soil, and regular light feeding keep the plant full and flowering.

A vigorous perennial with a mounding or trailing habit. Large purple daisy-like flowers bloom from spring through fall. Flowers close at night. Foliage is bright green and narrowly oval. Trailing habit, works well in hanging baskets. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A perennial shrub that forms a dense, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Summer flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Plump, dark purple flower heads are topped with large, light purple, flag-like bracts. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.
A winter-blooming, clumping evergreen perennial with bold and serrated, large and leathery variegated leaves. Clusters of cup-shaped, nodding flowers in lime-green.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in purple-red. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in pink.

A fast growing bushy perennial shrub that does well on the coast, on slopes, and in poor soils. Leaves are gray-green, textured, and roughly diamond-shaped. Daisy-like flowers show off bright yellow petals and dark brown centers. Blooms are prolific in spring and fall, though less vigorous in the heat of summer. Very attractive to pollinators.

A semi-evergreen perennial with clumping, fibrous roots and lobed, glossy green foliage. Upright, wiry stems carry double, saucer-shaped flowers. Petal-like sepals are rose-pink and stamens are golden-yellow. Blooms from late summer through fall. Flowers provide nutrient-rich pollen for butterflies and bees. Spent flowers form white, cottony seedheads. Creeping underground roots will naturalize plantings over time.

Dark purple leaves form a compact, deciduous mound on this clumping perennial, then golden daisy-like flowers rise above it in summer. The bold foliage gives wet shade a clear focal point. Use it beside ponds, shaded entries, or woodland paths. Cool soil, rich compost, and regular moisture keep leaves broad; slugs may need routine control.

A perennial, clumping herbaceous plant with ferny aromatic foliage and flat-topped flower clusters held above the leaves. Long-season bloom supports bees, butterflies, and beneficial insects, and the stems are useful fresh or dried. It is a dependable low-water perennial for sunny borders with well-drained soil.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in coral-orange. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in creamy white.
Woody evergreen perennial forming loose mounds of rounded gray-green foliage with dainty upright flower clusters.

An annual that forms a tidy mound of blush pink blooms and medium green, finely dissected foliage. Flowers bloom in abundance during spring and summer months. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with oval to heart-shaped, deep green leaves with wide, irregular white margins. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with oval to heart-shaped, greenish-gold foliage with blue-green margins. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in peachy-red. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in creamy white.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in peachy pink with dark orange veining. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, flowers in pink and chartreuse. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated margins and hot pink veins.

A shrubby perennial featuring soft and rounded bright green leaves that smell of peppermint. Airy flower clusters of white flowers with purple markings. Can be grown as annuals or houseplants outside of hardiness zones.
A tropical perennial with gigantic, ribbed, arrow-shaped leaves in bright green. Flowers are greenish-white and not too showy. Can tolerate full shade.

A sterile-hybrid perennial shrub that forms a vigorous bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Bright violet-blue flowers and linear, silver-green foliage are aromatic. Thin flower spikes bloom on very long stems in summer and re-bloom in fall. Good for drying. High oil content. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. Resistant to winter die-back, rot and foliar diseases. Tolerates extreme heat and humidity.
Perennial with narrow, pointed foliage and loose terminal clusters of flared, bell-shaped flowers in lavender.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a shrubby, multi-branching bush. Light green leaves are deeply veined, heart-shaped, and smell sweet like pineapple. Upright stems carry tubular flowers in bright red. Blooms in late summer and fall. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to Mexico. The edible flowers and leaves of Salvia elegans are known for their culinary and medicinal uses.

A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of tubular, trumpet-shaped flowers are bright pink with pinkish-white throats. Blooms in summer. Very attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators.

A shrubby evergreen perennial that forms a creeping ground cover. Tiny leaves are oval, aromatic, fuzzy and gray-green. Dainty salmon-pink flowers bloom in early spring. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.

An evergreen perennial that forms compact cushions of green, grass-like leaf blades. From spring to early summer, upright stems bear poofy flower heads in pink. Tolerates alkaline and limestone soils.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, mounding groundcover. Dark green leaves are small, oval, and scalloped on the edges. Large, saucer-shaped flowers are pink with dark pink veins. Attracts pollinators. Blooms from late spring through late summer. Can tolerate light foot traffic.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers pale to deep pink. Handsome and leathery, dark green palmate foliage. Burgundy stems.

commonName: Pink Mexican Bush Sage, Velvet Sage
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a robust mound. Dark gray-green leaves are lance-shaped, white and hairy below, and aromatic. Long, sweeping stalks carry two-lipped, pink flowers held in fuzzy, white calyxes. Blooms nearly year round. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to Mexico.

A tender perennial or annual with a compact, upright, clumping growth habit. Gray-green foliage is finely lobed and ferny. Wiry stems carry frilly, pincushion-like flowerheads in lavender-pink. Blooms from midsummer through fall. Attracts butterflies. A good cut flower.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in metallic pink to dark berry pink. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in soft pink.

A perennial mat-forming groundcover that likes shade. Variegated foliage is silver-white with gray-green edges. Scalloped, quilted, heart-shaped leaves are arranged in opposite pairs on square stems. Short upright stalks carry hooded pink flowers throughout summer.

An evergreen shrub that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Old stems become woody while new stems root as they touch the ground. Leaves are small, fleshy, and bright green. Tiny, pink, star-shaped flowers bloom in summer. Suitable for erosion control.

commonName: Pink Santa Barbara Daisy, Mexican Daisy, Fleabane
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a compact groundcover. Aster-like flowers bloom nearly year-round, opening up to 1 inch across. Threadlike petals appear in light pink. Yellow button-centers attract all sorts of pollinators. Medium to dark green leaves are spoon to lance-shaped.

A self-sowing perennial flower. Leaves are gray, lobed, rough, and woolly. Long-stemmed daisy-like flowers typically display dark composite centers surrounded by a ring of contrasting yellow. Petals radiate golden yellow to vibrant pink.

commonName: Pink Tapien Verbena, Carpet of Blossoms
description: A tender perennial that forms a bushy, spreading carpet. From late spring into fall, profuse blooms attract butterflies. Dainty, true-pink, white-eyed flowers open in rounded clusters, nestled among the well-branched foliage. Opposite leaves are green, narrowly dissected, and finely textured. Resistant to powdery mildew.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers in smokey pink and purple shades. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated leaf margins.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Purple-blue flowers and linear, variegated foliage are aromatic. Leaves are gray green with highlighted cream-yellow edges. Flower spikes bloom in summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.

Plum, silver, and dark green leaves build a dense mound on this evergreen to semi-evergreen perennial. Thin white flower stems feed hummingbirds in spring and summer. Use it in pots, along paths, or in woodland borders. Filtered light, rich open soil, and even water keep the leaf pattern clear and the crown compact.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in silvery plum-purple with dark veining. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in creamy white.

A perennial with upright stems, multi-branching from the base. Burgundy-tinged leaves are oppositely arranged on dark red stems. Spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers are lavender-pink. Blooms throughout summer. Very attractive to butterflies and other pollinators.

botanicalName: Aster chilensis, Symphyotrichum chilense 'Point Saint George'
description: An herbaceous perennial with a low, vigorously spreading growth habit. Cheerful summer flowers bloom into a multitude of slender, pale lavender petals that surround yellow centers. Native to California. Beneficial to butterflies, moths, bees, and other pollinators.

commonName: Point Sal Purple Sage, Low Purple Sage
description: An evergreen shrub that forms a mounding, spreading ground cover. White-silver leaves are velvety, quilted and aromatic. Long stems carry tiered whorls of two-lipped, light purple flowers. Blooms in spring. Attracts all sorts of pollinators, beneficial insects and wildlife. Native to California.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, dark gray-green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in bright magenta on 1 - 2 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, velvety leaves are gray-blue-green. Bronze-gold inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms in large clusters atop stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A North American perennial that forms compact mounds of tall, upright blooms throughout summer. Large, fragrant flowers appear with drooping, overlapping white petals and golden-brown seed cones. Low-growing leaves are lance-shaped, green, and slightly hairy. A popular herbal remedy today, all plant parts have been used in Native American medicine for hundreds of years. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A North American perennial that forms compact mounds of tall, upright blooms throughout summer. Large, fragrant flowers appear with drooping, overlapping bright-berry-pink petals and golden-brown seed cones. Low-growing leaves are lance-shaped, green, and slightly hairy. A popular herbal remedy today, all plant parts have been used in Native American medicine for hundreds of years. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A mounding, evergreen to semi-evergreen woody perennial with finely divided silver-gray aromatic foliage. The soft texture and pale color provide durable contrast in dry borders, Mediterranean plantings, and containers. Small yellow flowers are secondary to the foliage. Performs best with full sun, good drainage, and lean to average soil.

commonName: Pouzo Blue Hybrid Grey Musk Sage
description: An evergreen shrub that forms a compact mound. Gray-green leaves are quilted, toothed, and very fragrant. Tall stalks carry elaborate whorls of two-lipped flowers in lavender-purple. Heaviest blooms in spring and fall. Attracts all sorts of pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to California.

commonName: Prairie Sun Gloriosa Daisy, Black Eyed Susan
description: An herbaceous perennial that forms a self-sowing patch of upright, long-stemmed, summer-fall blooms. Oversized, daisy-like flowers have yellow petals that warm up to an orange ring which surrounds the conical, milky green center. Green leaves are lance-shaped and hairy. Good cut flower. Often grown as an annual.

An evergreen perennial bulb that forms clumps of grassy, bright green leaves. Apricot-pink, lily-like flowers peak out from the tops of the foliage. Blooms from mid summer into fall. Abundant blooms after rain showers.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Summer flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Plump, purple-blue flower heads are topped with greenish-white, flag-like bracts. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A perennial that forms a dense mat of mounding rosettes. Foliage emerges golden-green, matures to silver-green in summer, and back to gold in fall. Velvet-soft leaves are tongue-shaped with serrated edges. Purple-pink two-lipped flowers arise in spike-like clusters through summer.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is true orange with a yellow splotch. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is yellow and orange. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is white with a yellow splotch. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is white with a faint yellow splotch. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-shaped flowers. Flower colorations is striped yellow and pink with maroon markings, which channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with variegated white and green foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is white and pale pink. Maroon markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is dark red with a pastel yellow splotch. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is pinky-red with a bright yellow splotch. Maroon markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is pinky-red with a yellow splotch. Maroon markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is golden, yellow, and rouge. Maroon markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is purple with a creamy yellow to white splotch. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

A dwarf perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is bright pink with a yellow splotch. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower. Princess series is bred to be compact in the garden with abundant, long-lasting blooms.

An evergreen shrub that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Old stems become woody while new stems root as they touch the ground. Leaves are small, fleshy, and bright green. Tiny, white, star-shaped flowers bloom in summer. Suitable for erosion control.

A sterile-hybrid perennial shrub that forms an upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Light violet-blue flowers and linear, silver-green foliage are aromatic. Thin flower spikes bloom on very long stems in summer, good for drying. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

A self-sowing perennial flower. Leaves are gray, lobed, rough, and woolly. Long-stemmed daisy-like flowers typically display dark composite centers surrounded by a ring of contrasting yellow. Petals radiate burnt orange to golden yellow.

A self-sowing perennial flower. Leaves are gray, lobed, rough, and woolly. Long-stemmed daisy-like flowers typically display black composite centers surrounded by a ring of contrasting colors. Petals are bright magenta-purple. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

commonName: Purple Dragon Dead Nettle, Yellow Archangel
description: A perennial mat-forming groundcover that likes shade. Variegated foliage is silver-white with gray-green edges. Scalloped, quilted, heart-shaped leaves are arranged in opposite pairs on square stems. Short upright stalks carry hooded bright purple flowers throughout summer.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact clump. Edible, gray-green leaves are aromatic, soft-textured, and oval. New growth emerges purple. Short stalks carry spikes of two-lipped flowers in lavender-purple. Blooms in summer. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. S. officinalis is known for its culinary and medicinal uses.

A spreading, herbaceous perennial with green foliage and a dense, late-season display of purple daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. This California native selection supports butterflies and beneficial insects in borders, meadows, and habitat plantings. Performs best with good drainage and occasional summer irrigation.

Long violet flower spikes trail across this spreading, herbaceous perennial above silver-gray scented leaves. Bees visit for weeks, while deer usually leave the foliage alone. Its low habit softens walls, paths, and sunny slopes. Full sun, lean soil, and sharp drainage keep the mat compact; trimming after bloom can bring a fresh flush.
A perennial ground cover that forms a dense, creeping mat. Bright green leaves are small, narrow, and toothed. Purple, tubular, two-lipped flowers bloom in late spring. Evergreen in mild climates.

An evergreen shrub that forms a bushy mound. White-gray leaves are velvety, quilted and aromatic. Long stems carry tiered whorls of light purple flowers. Blooms in spring. Attracts all sorts of pollinators, beneficial insects and wildlife. Native to California.

A tender evergreen perennial with a low-growing, trailing groundcover habit. Deep purple stems and lance-shaped purple leaves provide strong foliage color, especially in brighter exposure. Small pink to pale purple flowers with yellow stamens appear during warm months. Fast growth makes it useful for seasonal color, containers, edging, frost-protected massing, and interiorscapes.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, dull green leaves turn dark ruby-purple in fall. New growth comes in red. Chartreuse-green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop red stems in spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, gray to green, and aromatic. Purple flat-topped flower umbels grow in on 1 - 2 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.

An evergreen shrub that forms a dense, trailing ground cover. Old stems become woody while new stems root as they touch the ground. Leaves are small, fleshy, and bright green. Tiny, white, star-shaped flowers bloom in summer. Suitable for erosion control. Taller than the species.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms an upright, multi-branching mound. Green leaves are small, oval and fragrant. Upright stems carry large two-lipped flowers in raspberry-red. Blooms from spring through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.
A hybrid shade-loving perennial with an upright and clumping form and dark green, silver-spotted leaves. Produces a profusion of pink flowers in spring. Attracts pollinators.
An herbaceous perennial prized for large and fragrant, double flowers in cream and soft pink. Lush and dark green, attractively divided foliage.

A perennial that forms showy flowers amongst tufts of grassy gray-green foliage. Double flowers feature fringed, fruity pink petals with dark red centers. Blooms emit a spicy fragrance. Attracts bees and butterflies. Makes a good cut flower. Flowers are edible.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a multi-branching mound. Green leaves are slender and fragrant. Upright stems carry two-lipped flowers in bright red. Blooms from summer through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

A semi-deciduous perennial that spreads by rhizomes. Dark green leaves are large, toothed and arranged in low-growing clumps. Red flower clusters bloom on thick stems in spring. Foliage turns red in fall. Used as a groundcover.

commonName: Red Creeping Thyme, Red Mother of Thyme
description: A shrubby evergreen perennial that forms a creeping ground cover. Tiny leaves are oval, aromatic and dark green. Foliage tinges bronze in cool weather. Abundant, dainty, pink-red flowers bloom in spring and summer. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.

An evergreen perennial that forms compact cushions of burgundy-tinted, grass-like leaf blades. From spring to early summer, upright stems bear poofy flower heads in rosy pink. Tolerates alkaline and limestone soils.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a subshrub with multi-branching stems. Leaves are slender, dark green, and sticky. Flared, tubular flowers are bright red. Spring to fall blooms attract butterflies and other pollinators. California native.
A fragrant perennial with narrow, blue-green leaves and loose clusters of star-shaped, pink-red flowers. Long blooming period. Attracts butterflies. Does well in poor soils.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, dark gray-green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in rosy red on 2 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.

A shade-friendly perennial that spreads by rhizomes and self-sowing. Velvety, clover-like foliage is dark green with bright ruby-violet undersides. Leaves divide into three heart-shaped leaflets. Cupped, pinkish-white flowers bloom in spring and fall. Native to coastal forests of the Pacific Northwest from Washington to California.

A shade-friendly perennial that spreads by rhizomes and self-sowing. Velvety, clover-like foliage is dark green with bright ruby-violet undersides. Leaves divide into three heart-shaped leaflets. Cupped, pinkish-white flowers bloom in spring and fall. Native to coastal forests of the Pacific Northwest from Washington to California.

A perennial with a compact, upright habit, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of nodding, bell-shaped flowers are lavender blue. Reblooms in waves through summer. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A perennial with a compact, upright habit, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of nodding, bell-shaped flowers are magenta pink. Reblooms in waves through summer. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A perennial with a compact, upright habit, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of nodding, bell-shaped flowers are bright violet with white throats. Reblooms in waves through summer. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A perennial with a compact, upright habit, multi-branching from the base. Green leaves are lance-shaped and oppositely arranged. Spikes of nodding, bell-shaped flowers are deep pink. Reblooms in waves through summer. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A low-growing perennial with bright green, softly textured foliage. Leaves are very finely divided and aromatic. Flowers are dainty and white with yellow centers. Tea can be made from this plant, but the familiar chamomile tea is actually made from Matricaria recutita.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, dark gray-green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in dark red on 2 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.

A perennial that forms a self-sowing clump. Silver-gray leaves are felt-textured and spear-shaped. Blooms from late spring into early summer with dazzling magenta, five-petaled flowers. Attracts butterflies.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact clump. Gray-green leaves are crinkled, egg-shaped and fragrant. Upright stalks carry spikes of two-lipped flowers in rosy pink with burgundy calyxes. Blooms in summer. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.
Heat and drought tolerant perennial with tall and airy flower clusters in white to deep pink.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a spreading carpet. Highly fragrant, silky, short-spurred flowers are violet-blue with small white eyes. Blooms in spring. Beneficial for butterflies and birds. Leaves are heart-shaped and dark green. Flowers are edible. Historic medicinal qualities.

A mounding, semi-evergreen perennial groundcover with deeply cut green leaves. Violet-blue, white-eyed flowers bloom from late spring into fall and feed bees and butterflies. Sterile flowers do not set seed, helping extend the bloom season. Use along borders, walls, or in masses. Leaves may turn reddish in cool fall weather; afternoon shade suits hot climates.

A self-sowing perennial flower. Leaves are gray, lobed, rough, and woolly. Long-stemmed daisy-like flowers typically display dark composite centers surrounded by a ring of contrasting yellow. Petals are ruby red.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, dull green leaves turn blackish-purple in fall. New growth comes in ruby red. Chartreuse-green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop red stems in spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a vigorously trailing ground cover. Rich magenta-pink flowers are dainty and saucer-shaped. Long bloom cycle lasts from spring through fall. Soft grayish green leaves are deeply lobed.

An evergreen perennial with a robust, mounding form. Leaves are furry, gray-green and strongly fragrant of mint. Pinkish-purple, two-lipped flowers are arranged in large, showy globes. Blooms from spring into early summer. Attracts butterflies, bees and hummingbirds. California native. Requires soil with good drainage. Does well on slopes.
A shrubby perennial with fine, feathery, aromatic, gray-green foliage. Lavender-blue flowers appear in tall, airy, branched stalks. Blooms in summer. Attracts bees and butterflies.

A perennial, clumping herbaceous plant with ferny aromatic foliage and flat-topped flower clusters held above the leaves. Long-season bloom supports bees, butterflies, and beneficial insects, and the stems are useful fresh or dried. It is a dependable low-water perennial for sunny borders with well-drained soil.

A woody evergreen perennial that forms a shrubby mound. Green leaves are slender and rough-textured. Daisy-like flowers are lavender-blue with yellow centers. Long bloom season from spring to fall. Attracts butterflies. Native to South Africa.

A tender deciduous perennial that spreads by rhizomes and self-seeding to form an upright mat. In summer, forked, square stems carry rounded clusters of dainty, purple flowers. Attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Leaves are dark green, lance-shaped, and have coarsely toothed edges. Leaf texture is rough like sandpaper. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.
A trailing evergreen groundcover with green, moss-like foliage and small, white, 5-petaled flowers.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in bright green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in rosy red.

commonName: Santa Barbara Daisy, Mexican Daisy, Fleabane
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a trailing, mounding groundcover. Little daisy-like flowers bloom nearly year-round, opening up to 1 inch across. Flowers are white and pink with yellow button-centers. Medium to dark green leaves are spoon to lance-shaped.

commonName: Santa Barbara Mexican Bush Sage, Velvet Sage
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a slowly spreading mound, more compact than the species. Dark gray-green leaves are lance-shaped, white and hairy below, and aromatic. Long, sweeping stalks carry two-lipped, bright purple flowers held in fuzzy, deep purple calyxes. Blooms from spring through fall in mild climates. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to Mexico.
An herbaceous perennial prized for very fragrant, large and double, pale rosy pink flowers. Lush and dark green, attractively divided foliage.

A compact and trailing perennial with narrow and toothed, bright green foliage. Distinctive, fan shaped flowers almost constantly available on terminal spikes throughout bloom period. Available in a range of floral colors. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

An evergreen perennial that forms a creeping clump with upright, unbranched stems. Leaves are bright green, slender and sticky. Flared, tubular flowers are scarlet-red and velvety. Spring through fall blooms attract hummingbirds and other pollinators. Grows in damp locations and along stream beds in the wild. California native.

A perennial that forms a trailing, cascading ground cover. Silvery-green foliage is soft, fine and needle-like. Vibrant scarlet red flowers are shaped like birds' beaks. Blooms in spring and summer. Good in hanging pots.

A perennial that forms showy flowers amongst tufts of grassy gray-green foliage. Double flowers feature fringed, rosy red petals. Blooms emit a spicy fragrance. Attracts bees and butterflies. Makes a good cut flower. Flowers are edible.

A moss-like perennial that forms a carpet of tiny, yellow-green leaves. Small white flowers dot the foliage in spring. Good for use along pathways or between stepping stones. Can tolerate moderate foot traffic. Tolerates less sun than Irish Moss.

commonName: Sea Breeuze Seaside Daisy, Beach Aster
description: An evergreen perennial with a low, mounding habit. Aster-like flowers bloom from spring to summer, opening up to 3 inches across. Threadlike petals appear in lavender-pink. Yellow button-centers attract all sorts of pollinators. Medium to dark gray-green leaves are spoon to lance-shaped. Native to coastal California and Oregon.

An evergreen, spreading perennial groundcover with low rosettes of narrow green foliage. Lavender daisy-like flowers with yellow centers rise on slender stems over a long bloom season, supporting bees, butterflies, and other pollinators. This variety was introduced by Cornflower Farms from an open-pollinated seedling off the difficult to propagate Erigeron glaucus 'Wayne Roderick' parent. This California native hybrid offers a similar landscape effect with g

An evergreen perennial with a low, mounding habit. Aster-like flowers bloom from spring to summer, opening up to 1 inch across. Threadlike petals appear in shades of white, lavender-blue, and pink. Yellow button-centers attract all sorts of pollinators. Medium to dark gray-green leaves are spoon to lance-shaped. Native to coastal California and Oregon.
Perennial with colorful daisy-like flowers with brown and yellow centers. Evergreen foliage is dark green with woolly undersides. Available in a range of flower colors.

A semi-deciduous, clumping herbaceous perennial with dark green, lobed basal foliage and tall, wiry flower stems. Single, saucer-shaped pink flowers with yellow stamens bloom from late summer into fall. Useful for borders, woodland edges, pollinator plantings, and cut flowers. Performs best with rich, well-drained soil and consistent moisture.
