An herbaceous perennial with a cascading, trailing growth habit. Flowers are star-shaped and appear in shades of blue, purple, pink and white. Blooms from late spring through summer. Foliage is medium green. Forms a small, showy groundcover. Attracts hummingbirds.

A tender perennial that forms a dense, upright mound. Abundant blooms spring thru fall. Flowers close at night. Foliage is bright green, narrowly oval and slightly toothed. 'Serenity Bronze' has soft bronzy-orange petals that radiate pink from the center. 'Serenity Dark Purple' has deep magenta-purple flowers. 'Serenity Pink' has white petals that blush pink at their tips. 'Serenity Red' has velvety, burgundy red petals. 'Serenity White' has pure white petals. 'Serenity Yellow' has lemon yellow petals. 'Serenity Sunshine Beauty' has apricot orange and yellow petals.

White petals washed with lavender surround dark centers on this mounding, tender perennial. The daisy-like flowers open in bright light above clean green leaves and feed bees through cool seasons. Use it at border fronts, in containers, or as seasonal groundcover. Sun, open soil, and even moisture maintain bloom; light shearing renews the mound.
An herbaceous perennial prized for very fragrant, large and double, pale rosy pink flowers. Lush and dark green, attractively divided foliage.
A woodland perennial groundcover with large, heart-shaped, deep-green leaves. Blue springtime flowers look similar to forget-me-nots. Can tolerate full shade.

commonName: Sierra Salmon California Fuchsia, Hummingbird Trumpet
description: An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a mounding habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers appear in salmon-orange. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, linear, and gray-green. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

botanicalName: Salvia x jamensis 'Sierra de San Antonio'
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a compact mound. Mid-green leaves are slender, shiny and fragrant. Tall stalks carry two-lipped, bi-colored flowers in yellow and peachy pink. Blooms from summer to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

commonName: Silky Gold Blood Flower, Silky Gold Indian Butterfly Weed
description: An evergreen perennial shrub, often grown as an annual. Rich green leaves are long, elliptical, and arranged in opposite pairs. Tiny star-shaped flowers grow in clusters of orange and yellow. Attracts many beneficial insects, especially the Monarch butterfly caterpillar.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Flowers and linear, silvery-white foliage are aromatic. Profuse, violet flower heads are topped by purple, flag-like bracts. Blooms in spring, later than 'Anouk', and reblooms in favorable conditions. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. Good resistance to foliar disease.

A dense, spreading woody perennial shrub with aromatic, finely divided, silver-green foliage. Leaves are similar to Senecio cineraria (Dusty Miller), but hardier. Native to Asia and naturalized to North America.

A South African ground cover that forms a slowly-spreading carpet. Dark green leaves are very narrow and cupped, prominently revealing silvery-white undersides. Somewhat inconspicuous yellow daisy-like flowers appear in summer. Tolerates a decent amount of foot traffic.

A perennial groundcover that forms a fast-growing, trailing carpet. Foliage is dense, silvery and spoon-shaped. Daisy-like flowers are lavender-pink with yellow centers. Blooms from late spring into fall. Attracts butterflies. Tolerant of clay, heat, coastal conditions, and drought. California native.

A perennial that forms a dense mat of mounding rosettes. Velvet-soft leaves are silver-green and tongue-shaped with serrated edges. Infrequent purple two-lipped flowers arise in spike-like clusters in late spring.

commonName: Silver Falls, Ponyfoot, Silver Nickel Vine, Silver Dichondra
description: A creeping, cascading perennial groundcover with oustanding silver foliage. Prostrate stems root as they grow, trailing up to 6 feet wide. Good in a hanging basket. Native to the Southwest.
Heat and drought tolerant perennial. Tall and airy stems with pink buds that open to clear white flowers. Leaves are narrow, pointed, and medium green with pale yellow edges. Does not set seed.
A woodland perennial groundcover with white and light green leaves that are large and heart-shaped. Blue to pink springtime flowers look similar to forget-me-nots. Can tolerate full shade.
A winter-blooming, clumping evergreen perennial with bold and serrated, large and leathery leaves in silvery-green. Clusters of cup-shaped, nodding flowers in lime-green.
A mounding woody perennial shrub with aromatic, finely divided, silver-green foliage. Dies back in winter. Native to Japan.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in dark silvery purple-green with darker veins. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white.
A perennial with a mounding habit. White daisy-like flowers bloom with highly unique, spoon-like petals from spring thru fall. Flowers close at night. Foliage is bright green and narrowly oval.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, gray-green leaves have variegated white margins. Yellow-cream, red-eyed inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A shrubby evergreen perennial that forms an upright, mounding ground cover. Tiny leaves are oval, highly aromatic and green with variegated silver markings. Edible leaves are lemon-flavored. Dainty pale-lavender flowers bloom in early summer. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers in deep rosy-pink. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated margins.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with lovely cup-shaped, nodding flowers in deep red. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated margins.

A perennial groundcover that spreads aggresively by rhizomes. Foliage is deep green and slender. Luminous pink flowers are large, fragrant, silky, and cupped. Blooms in abundance from spring into summer. Native to western North America. Often dormant at the peaks of summer and winter.

An herbaceous perennial featuring tall and airy, wand-like flower clusters in maroon to pink. Narrow and lance-shaped, maroon-tinged foliage. Valued for long blooming season, especially if occasionally sheared.

An evergreen shrub with a spreading, mat-forming growth habit. Foliage is finely lobed, woolly, and gray-green. Vibrant golden-yellow, daisy-like flowers bloom from spring to fall. Attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Native to California.
Shade-loving perennial with deep green leaves spotted in silvery-white. Nodding clusters of bright white funnel-shaped flowers typically age to shades of blush pink.

A low-water perennial with a rounded form, taller than the species. Gray-green leaves are soft and aromatic. Leaves are small, ovate and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of lavender-blue flowers bloom spring to fall. Attracts pollinators.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in light green marbled with white. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in deep pink.
Perennial with narrow and leathery dark green foliage, with large profuse flattened flower clusters in white.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a compact clump. Gray-green leaves are crinkled, egg-shaped and fragrant. Upright stalks carry spikes of two-lipped flowers in white. Blooms in summer. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.
A perennial groundcover with silver-gray leaves and masses of small, white flowers in the summer.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a compact patch of coarse, green leaves. Large, single flowers are bright white with yellow centers. Abundant summer blooms rise above the foliage on rigid stalks. Good cut flower. Attracts butterflies.

A low-water perennial with a compact, mounding form. Gray green foliage is soft and aromatic. Leaves are small, ovate and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of pure white flowers bloom spring to fall. Attracts pollinators.

Small white flowers spill over the edges of this tender, spreading perennial above fine green leaves. The long cool-season display softens containers, walls, and the front of moist borders, while small insects visit the blooms. Use it where stems can trail freely. Sun or filtered light, rich soil, and even moisture maintain a full curtain.
Perennial with narrow and leathery dark green foliage, with large profuse flattened flower clusters.
An herbaceous perennial with a compact form, featuring tall and airy, wand-like flower clusters in white. Narrow and lance-shaped foliage.

Bright flowers rise above a compact, upright clump of green leaves on sturdy stems. Daisy-like blooms come in yellow, orange, pink, red, white, and blended shades from late spring through summer. Strong branching supports heavy flower cover, while dry seed heads feed finches. Use in borders, mass plantings, pollinator gardens, or cut-flower beds.

A perennial, clumping herbaceous plant with ferny aromatic foliage and flat-topped flower clusters held above the leaves. Long-season bloom supports bees, butterflies, and beneficial insects, and the stems are useful fresh or dried. It is a dependable low-water perennial for sunny borders with well-drained soil.

A shrubby perennial forming dense mounds of fuzzy and silvery-gray, rounded to heart-shaped foliage. Clusters of showy deep burgundy flowers. Can be grown as annuals or houseplants outside of hardiness zones.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in variable color from red to pale peach. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white.

White butterfly-like flowers dance on thin stems above this clumping, herbaceous perennial. The compact green mound blooms for months and feeds bees without hiding nearby plants. Use it in sunny borders, meadow edges, or large containers. Open soil, good drainage, and a light trim after the first flush encourage a fresh second display.

commonName: Spindrift Santa Barbara Daisy, Mexican Daisy, Fleabane
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a compact mound. Aster-like flowers bloom nearly year-round, opening up to 1 inch across. Threadlike petals appear in white and pink. Yellow button-centers attract all sorts of pollinators. Medium to dark green leaves are spoon to lance-shaped.
A colorful perennial with pinwheel-like flowers in brick red. Valued for very long blooming period.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed leaves in bright green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in scarlet red.

A compact, evergreen perennial with tight mounds of narrow, grass-like green leaves. Rounded bright pink flower clusters rise on wiry stems in spring, often with repeat bloom in mild conditions. Useful for edging, rock gardens, containers, and coastal plantings. Performs best with well-drained soil and moderate to low irrigation.
A perennial grass with that forms a spreading carpet of coarse, dark green leaf blades. Tolerates heavy foot traffic. Often used for lawns. Tough root system can spread aggressively.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a mounding ground cover. Cream, pink-tinted flowers are dainty, saucer-shaped and clustered above the foliage on forked stems. Blooms from early spring into summer. Mid-green leaves are fancifully lobed. Similar to G. x c. 'Biokovo'.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with broadly heart-shaped, corrugated, golden leaves with irregular dark green margins. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. Resists slugs.
An evergreen shrub. Tubular bright pink flowers flare into frilly star-shaped tips. Leaves are medium green. Attracts pollinators.
A perennial that forms a rosette of large, bright green basal leaves. Branched stalks carry rounded, airy flower clusters in bicolor white and purple. Ideal for seaside conditions.

An evergreen perennial that forms a trailing carpet. Flowers are 5-petaled pinwheels of periwinkle-blue. Springtime blooms are tucked into the variegated white-edged, dark green foliage. Leaves are thick, elliptic, and smaller than V. major.

commonName: Sticky Monkey Flower, Shrubby Monkey Flower
description: A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a sub-shrub of upright, unbranched stems. Summer dormant in hot, dry climates. Leaves are slender, dark green, and sticky. Lobed, funnel-shaped flowers are light golden orange. Spring to fall blooms attract butterflies and other pollinators. California native.
An herbaceous woodland perennial with broadly heart-shaped, corrugated, bright golden leaves. Thin spikes carry clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. Resists slugs.

A self-sowing perennial that attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Low-growing leaves are ferny, dark gray-green, and aromatic. Flat-topped flower umbels grow in a variety of colors, including shades of white, cream, yellow, orange, pink, lilac, and red on 1 - 2 foot tall stems. Tolerant of drought, wind, and heat.
A shrubby perennial native to the Western US and Northern Mexico. Forms an upright and arching mound of gray-green foliage and striking, white tubular flowers. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.
A low and spreading perennial with colorful daisy-like flowers with red to burnt orange petals edged in yellow, with bright yellow centers. Narrow, deep green foliage. Tough and low-maintenance.
A showy perennial groundcover with bright yellow, four-petaled flowers and fuzzy, gray-blue-green foliage. Attracts butterflies, hummingbirds and moths. Native to the southwestern United States.
A perennial forming compact mounds of rounded, multi-lobed leathery leaves in orange, that mature to a pale yellow. Wiry stems carry small and nodding bell-shaped flowers in white.

A summer-blooming perennial with aromatic, medium green foliage. Whorled flowers grow on vertical spikes in a range of colors. Anise-scented leaves make a delicious herbal tea. Great selection for pollinator gardens. Attracts hummingbirds, butterflies, bees. 'Blue' has sky blue to lavender blue flowers. 'Orange' has light apricot to medium orange flowers. 'Red' has rich red flowers. 'Violet' has lavender to light violet flowers. 'White' has golden yellow buds that open to pure white flowers. 'Yellow' has tangerine orange to yellow flowers.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild climates. Deep blue-purple flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. Very large, plump flower spikes bloom from late spring into summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.

A hybrid perennial shrub that forms an upright bush or hedge when planted en masse. Evergreen in mild winters. Light purple-blue flowers and bright mint-green foliage are sweetly aromatic. Flower spikes bloom on long, tall stems in summer. Linear leaves are smooth at the tips and toothed near the bases. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

An herbaceous perennial with an upright, airy growth habit. From midsummer into fall, tall forked stems carry rounded clusters of vivid pinkish-purple flowers. Attracts butterflies and other pollinators. Foliage is sparse, creating a see-through effect. Leaves are dark green, lance-shaped, and have serrated edges. Self-sows.
A perennial forming compact mounds of maple-like, blue-green leaves with burgundy centers. Thin upright stalks carry wands of airy flower clusters in soft pink. Hybrid between Heuchera and Tiarella.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender, gray-green leaves are variegated with thick white margins. Creamy-yellow, green-eyed inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

commonName: Terra Seca Black Sage, Honey Sage
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a wide, dense mound. Gray-green leaves are linear, textured and aromatic. Long stems carry tiered whorls of two-lipped flowers in light lavender-white. Blooms from early spring into summer. Attracts pollinators, beneficial insects, birds and wildlife. Native to California. Tolerates more shade and water than the species.

A perennial, clumping herbaceous plant with ferny aromatic foliage and flat-topped flower clusters held above the leaves. Long-season bloom supports bees, butterflies, and beneficial insects, and the stems are useful fresh or dried. It is a dependable low-water perennial for sunny borders with well-drained soil.
An herbaceous perennial with an upright, mounding growth habit and abundant, petunia-like flowers in shades of yellow, peach and red. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.

A perennial with dense foliage, tuberous roots, and umbels of showy, undulating, cup-like flowers. Flower coloration is golden yellow to peachy rouge. Brown markings channel pollinators to prominent, pollen-coated anthers. A superb cut flower.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact, upright bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild climates. Bright violet-blue flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are intensely aromatic. Profuse, plump flower spikes bloom in summer with potential to repeat bloom. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.

A perennial that forms showy flowers amongst mats of grassy blue-gray foliage. Double flowers feature notched, pink petals. Blooms emit a spicy fragrance. Attracts butterflies and bees. Makes a good cut flower. Flowers are edible.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, compact bush. Slender, deep green leaves turn burgundy in fall. Lime-green, red-eyed inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms cluster atop reddish stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

An annual that forms a trailing mound. Rosy pink blooms from late spring into fall attract butterflies and other pollinators. Excellent powdery mildew resistance. Can be grown as an annual in all zones.
Perennial with small and ruffled rose-like flowers in golden tangerine orange. Mounding foliage is an attractive, lush green.
Colorful daisy-like flowers with brown and yellow centers, evergreen dark green foliage with woolly undersides.

commonName: Tricolor Oyster Plant, Tricolor Boat Lily, Tricolor Moses in a Cradle
description: A tender evergreen, clumping herbaceous perennial with a compact, upright habit. Strap-like leaves are striped green, cream, and pink with purple undersides, providing year-round foliage contrast in frost-protected plantings and interiorscapes. Small white flowers are held in boat-shaped bracts near the leaf bases. Performs well in well-drained potting media and is useful for containers, shaded patios, and indoor plantings.

A summer-blooming perennial with aromatic, gray-green foliage and whorled flowers, which grow on vertical spikes in shades of dark pink to purple-red. Sweetly-scented leaves make a delicious herbal tea. Great selection for pollinator gardens; attracts hummingbirds, butterflies and bees.

A perennial shrub that forms a compact bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Rich purple flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are aromatic. dense flower spikes bloom in summer. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies. English lavender is used for essential oil and culinary recipes, among many other uses.

commonName: U.C. Hybrid California Fuchsia, Hummingbird Trumpet
description: An herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with an upright habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers appear in scarlet red. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, linear to oval, and gray-green. Native to California, the West, and northern Mexico.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a compact clump. Dark green leaves are aromatic, small and slender. Upright stalks carry spikes of two-lipped flowers in bright purple-pink. Blooms from mid-summer through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

An easy-to-grow perennial. Large, butter yellow to creamy white flowers with a dark red eye, rise above a mound of narrowly lobed leaves on naked stems. Dead-head regularly to extend a long blooming season. Attracts pollinators. Cold hardy and excellent disease resistance.

A shrubby perennial with heart to kidney-shaped, velvety and aromatic foliage. Leaves have crinkled and toothed margins, and circular color bands in lime green and burgundy. Loose and rounded clusters of showy orange-red flowers. Can be grown as annuals or houseplants outside of hardiness zones.

commonName: Variegated Big Leaf Periwinkle, Creeping Myrtle
description: An evergreen perennial that forms an aggresively spreading mound. Flowers are 5-petaled pinwheels of periwinkle-purple. Springtime blooms are tucked into the variegated, white-edged, deep green foliage. Leaves are thick, heart-shaped, and larger than V. minor. Difficult to contain.

A broadleaf perennial groundcover that forms a dense, fast-spreading mat. Variegated leaflets of light green with toothed edges of white illuminate shady areas. Warm weather brings forth flat-topped clusters of small, white flowers that poke out above the foliage. Can tolerate full shade. Dormant in winter.
Groundcover with round, scalloped leaves that are variegated bright green and white. Small blue flowers in spring and summer.

An evergreen perennial that forms a trailing carpet. Flowers are 5-petaled pinwheels of periwinkle-blue. Springtime blooms are tucked into the variegated creamy-edged, deep green foliage. Leaves are thick, elliptic, and smaller than V. major.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a creeping ground cover by rooting at its nodes. It can quickly and aggressively spread when sited in its prime growing conditions. Opposite pairs of scallop-edged, heart-shaped leaves are dark green with bold silvery-white variegation. Upright clusters of bright yellow, hooded flowers cover the foliage in late spring.
A winter-blooming, woodland perennial with elegant cup-shaped, nodding semi-double flowers in pink. Handsome and leathery, palmate foliage with serrated margins.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a tight, compact mound. Mid-green leaves are egg-shaped, shiny and fragrant. Tall stalks carry abundant two-lipped flowers in bright fuchsia pink, dark purple, or pure white. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects. Tolerates humidity.

botanicalName: Mimulus aurantiacus x 'Vibrant Red', Diplacus 'Vibrant Red'
description: A semi-evergreen perennial that forms a sub-shrub of upright, unbranched stems. Summer dormant in hot, dry climates. Leaves are slender, dark green, and sticky. Lobed, funnel-shaped flowers are scarlet red. Spring to fall blooms attract butterflies and other pollinators. California native.

A moisture-loving woodland perennial with a compact, clump-forming growth habit. Erect, plume-like flowers bloom in late summer to display light, airy clusters. Fern-like foliage is divided into leaflets with finely serrated edges. Attracts butterflies. 'Visions in Pink' has soft pink flowers and bluish-green foliage. 'Visions in Purple' has soft purple flowers and deep green foliage. 'Visions in Red' has deep red flowers and dark green foliage. 'Visions in White' has off-white flowers and deep bronzy-green foliage.

A low-water perennial with a mounding, cascading form. Gray-green foliage is soft and aromatic. Leaves are small, ovate and toothed. Airy, billowing stalks of bright lavender-blue flowers bloom spring to fall. Attracts pollinators.

commonName: Wasatch Fire Hummingbird Trumpet, California Fuchsia
description: A low growing herbaceous semi-evergreen shrub with a mounding habit. Spreads by rhizomes. Trumpet-shaped flowers appear in fiery red-orange. Blooms in summer and fall. Pollinated by hummingbirds. Leaves are felty, linear to oval, and gray-green. More compact than the species.

A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a fountain-shaped clump. Dark gray green leaves are aromatic, toothed and slender. Upright stalks carry spikes of white, two-lipped flowers held in fuzzy, purple calyxes. Blooms from mid-summer through fall. Attracts pollinators and beneficial insects.

An evergreen to semi-evergreen, upright shrub with dark green leaves and maroon stems. Long magenta-pink tubular flowers bloom from spring through fall and draw hummingbirds. Use as a bold border plant, flowering screen, container accent, or pollinator feature. It performs well in rich, well-drained soil with regular moisture and shelter from hard frost.

A self-sowing, ornamental perennial known for its captivating flowers that nod and sway in the wind. Flowers are bright red and yellow with sweet, nectar-filled spurs and yellow stamens. Leaves are lacy and fresh green. Beneficial to many birds, butterflies, and other pollinators. Native to woodland areas of the Pacific Coast.
Heat and drought tolerant perennial with tall and airy flower clusters in white to deep pink.

A semi-deciduous, clumping herbaceous perennial with dark green basal foliage and tall, branching flower stems. Semi-double white flowers with ruffled petals and yellow stamens bloom from late summer into fall. Useful for borders, woodland edges, pollinator plantings, and cut flowers. Performs best with rich, well-drained soil and consistent moisture.

A semi-evergreen shrub with a mounding growth habit. Gray-green leaves are quilted, toothed, and very fragrant. Tall stalks carry elaborate whorls of two-lipped flowers in deep blue-lavender. Heaviest blooms in spring and summer. Attracts all sorts of pollinators and beneficial insects. Native to California.
A perennial selected for hanging baskets or as a small-scale groundcover. Leaves are small, toothed, and medium to light green. Flowers are dainty, five-petaled and white with yellow centers.

An herbaceous perennial that forms a mounding ground cover. Spreads by runners. White flowers are dainty and saucer-shaped. Long bloom cycle lasts from spring through fall. Dark green leaves are deeply lobed. Foliage turns deep red in fall.

This spreading, semi-evergreen California native shrub bears huge white crepe-like flowers with gold centers. Blue-gray leaves form tall thickets, and bees visit the summer bloom. Use it to cover sunny banks or fill broad dry beds. Deep, well-drained soil supports strong roots. Underground stems spread far, and the milky sap may bother skin.

A clump-forming woodland perennial with dangling, white, heart-shaped flowers. Pale green foliage is larger than other varieties and is similar in appearance to carrot tops. Blooms in cool weather. Attracts hummingbirds.

An evergreen perennial that forms compact cushions of green, grass-like leaf blades. From spring to early summer, upright stems bear poofy flower heads in white. Tolerates alkaline and limestone soils.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, mounding groundcover. Dark green leaves are small, oval, and scalloped on the edges. Large, saucer-shaped flowers are white with light pink veins. Attracts pollinators. Blooms from late spring through late summer. Can tolerate light foot traffic.

A shrubby evergreen perennial that forms a slowly creeping groundcover. Tiny leaves are oval and bright green. Dainty white flowers bloom in early spring. Attracts pollinators. Tolerates light foot traffic.

commonName: White False Heather, Mexican Heather, Hawaiian Heather
description: A compact and tidy evergreen shrub. Profusely re-blooming flowers are small, star-shaped and white. Leaves are small, glossy and lance-shaped. Stems are reddish-brown. Attracts pollinators.

A perennial tuber that forms a large, dramatic clump. Leaves are broad, arrow-shaped, and glossy with prominent veins. Coloration is deep green with variegated white spots. Spring and summer-blooming flowers are elegant, cone-shaped, and fragrant. Creamy-white, petal-like spathes surround a yellow spadix of tiny true flowers.

A moisture-loving woodland perennial with a clump-forming growth habit. Erect, plume-like flowers bloom into light, airy clusters of white. Fern-like foliage is divided into deep green leaflets with finely serrated edges. Attracts butterflies.

A sterile-hybrid perennial shrub that forms a mounding bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. White flowers and linear, gray-green foliage are intensely aromatic. Flower spikes bloom on very long stems in summer, good for drying. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.
A perennial ground cover that forms a dense, creeping mat. Bright green leaves are small, narrow, and toothed. White, tubular, two-lipped flowers bloom in late spring. Evergreen in mild climates.

commonName: White Mischief Mexican Bush Sage, Velvet Sage
description: A semi-evergreen shrub that forms a robust, spreading mound. Dark gray-green leaves are lance-shaped, white and hairy below, and aromatic. Long, sweeping stalks carry fuzzy, two-lipped flowers in white. Blooms from fall through spring in mild climates. Attracts hummingbirds, other pollinators, and beneficial insects.

commonName: White Nancy Dead Nettle, Yellow Archangel
description: A perennial mat-forming groundcover that likes shade. Variegated foliage is silver-white with fine green edges. Scalloped, quilted, heart-shaped leaves are arranged in opposite pairs on square stems. Short upright stalks carry hooded white flowers throughout summer.

An herbaceous perennial with a cascading, trailing growth habit. Flowers are white and star-shaped. Blooms from late spring through summer. Foliage is medium green. Forms a small, showy groundcover. Attracts hummingbirds.

A low, spreading semi-evergreen perennial groundcover selected as a durable, low-water turf alternative. Dense green foliage spreads by stolons to create a tight, weed-suppressing mat, with small white flowers appearing through the warm season for pollinator support. This sterile selection is useful for commercial landscapes, parkways, utility areas, slopes, and low-use lawn replacements where reduced mowing and lower irrigation are priorities. Performs well in a range of soils, including sandy loam and clay loam, with best establishment from consistent early irrigation followed by low to moderate water once rooted.
An evergreen perennial forming a carpet of dense and rounded large flower clusters in pure white. Narrow and shiny, dark green leaves. May be semi-evergreen in colder winter climates.

A perennial groundcover for shady, woodland areas. Dark, glossy, heart-shaped leaves are 2 - 7 inches across. Grows well under redwoods. Native to the Pacific Northwest. Drought tolerant once established. Can tolerate full shade.

A semi-evergreen perennial with clumping, fibrous roots and lobed, glossy green foliage. Upright, wiry stems carry single, saucer-shaped flowers. Petal-like sepals are bicolored white and violet-blue. Stamens are golden-yellow. Blooms from late summer through late fall. Flowers provide nutrient-rich pollen for butterflies and bees. Spent flowers form white, cottony seedheads. Creeping underground roots will naturalize plantings over time.

commonName: Winnifred (Winifred) Gilman Cleveland Sage, California Blue Sage
description: An evergreen shrub that forms a compact, dense mound. Gray-green leaves are small, almost linear, and intensely fragrant. Dark maroon stalks carry tiered whorls of two-lipped, dark violet-blue flowers that emerge from red buds. Blooms in late spring and summer. Attracts native hummingbirds, other pollinators, and beneficial insects. Native to California.

A perennial shrub that forms a robust bush or hedge. Evergreen in mild winters. Spring-summer flowers and linear, silver-green foliage are aromatic. Profuse, dark purple flower heads are topped by purple-blue, flag-like bracts. Blooms earlier than other L. stoechas varieties. Attracts birds, bees and butterflies.

An evergreen perennial that spreads by rhizomes. Variegated, dark green, red-edged leaves are large, waxy and arranged in low-growing clumps. Pink, rose, or purple flower clusters bloom on thick stems in winter through spring.
An evergreen perennial forming a compact mound of rounded, multi-lobed, ruffled leaves in lime green. Wiry stems carry small nodding bell-shaped flowers in white.
A perennial with a compact, mounding growth habit. Masses of fragrant, four-petaled flowers bloom in bright lilac-purple from late winter to spring. Long, narrow leaves are rich green.

A semi-deciduous perennial that spreads by rhizomes. Dark green leaves are large, heart-shaped, toothed and arranged in low-growing clumps. Dark pinky-red flower clusters bloom on thick stems in spring. Foliage turns red in fall. Used as a groundcover.

A perennial ground cover that spreads quickly from a central crown via extra long, above-ground runners. Glossy, mid-green leaves are three-lobed, rounded and toothed. Flowers are white, five-petaled, and bloom in spring. Blossoms are followed by small, flavorful strawberry-fruits. Native to regions with a Mediterranean-like climate near the California coast. Does well in understory and dry shade.

An evergreen perennial that forms a low, upright bush. Slender leaves are blue-green. Bright yellow-green inflorescences display showy bracts that cup tiny true flowers. Blooms in large, broad clusters atop stems throughout spring. Attracts butterflies. All plant parts contain a toxic milky sap.

A deciduous perennial with a variable growth habit, often grown as an annual. Leaves are bright green, rounded and toothed. Two-lipped, tubular flowers are bright-yellow with purple spots on the lower lips. Spring through summer blooms attract hummingbirds and other pollinators. Grows in damp locations and along stream beds in the wild. California native.

A perennial with a robust, clumping habit. Leaves are needle-like and bright green. Above the foliage, tubular, lemon yellow flowers nod at a right angle on their upright stems. Blooms from late spring to mid-summer. Attractive to hummingbirds and other pollinators. Southwestern native.

A perennial that forms a small, trailing ground cover. Spreads by above-ground runners. Minty green leaves are aromatic, egg-shaped to heart-shaped and scallop-edged. Edible leaves have medicinal qualities and are used in herbal teas. Small white flowers bloom in summer. Native to the West, including California.

A compact, clumping, herbaceous perennial with a fine-textured, airy habit. Narrow, threadlike green foliage forms a rounded mound topped by bright golden-yellow, daisy-like flowers from late spring into summer. Useful in mass plantings, borders, pollinator gardens, and meadow-style plantings; benefits from well-drained soil and occasional shearing to encourage rebloom. .
An evergreen perennial bulb that forms clumps of grassy, bright green leaves. White, lily-like flowers peak out from the tops of the foliage. Blooms in late summer and fall.

A tender, mounding perennial often grown as an annual. Velvety burgundy leaves pair with bright yellow flowers from spring through summer. Native from southern Mexico to western Panama, it is sterile and noninvasive. Its low form works in beds, pots, and window boxes.

A tender perennial that forms an upright mound. Daisy-like flowers are vibrantly multi-colored with tones of purple, pink, copper and orange. Abundant blooms spring thru fall. Flowers close at night. Foliage is bright green, narrowly oval and slightly toothed.

This shrubby perennial is a type of common geranium known for its kidney-shaped leaves, typically with scalloped edges and variegated in dark green or burgundy. Tall, rounded clusters of showy flowers vary in color by cultivar. Well branched and heat-resistant.

This deciduous floribunda rose grows with a bushy form and bears orange-blend flowers with yellow and pink tones. Rose beds gain structure when it is used in groups. A light spicy scent marks each flower cycle through the warm season. Flowers appear across the leafy form, not only on a few stems.

commonName: All My Loving Hybrid Tea Rose
description: On this upright, deciduous hybrid tea rose, clear pink flowers create the main display. Late spring starts a long bloom season with a light tea scent. The plant gives ordered beds a clear, upright structure. Containers add another practical design option. It fits cutting rows, formal designs, and mixed plantings.

A deciduous climbing rose develops a vigorous form and carries pink flowers. Repeated bloom brings a strong spicy clove scent from late spring through fall. Foliage fills the trained frame after each round of bloom. It brings bloom above narrow planting beds. The climbing form can frame entries, walls, and outdoor rooms.

Bushy in form, this deciduous floribunda rose carries lavender flowers brushed with red tones. The full plant gives a broad show instead of a narrow one. Choose it for low hedges, repeated border groups, or large containers. A strong citrus and rose scent comes with repeat bloom from late spring into fall.

On this bushy, deciduous floribunda rose, clear yellow flowers create the main display. A light rose scent comes with repeat bloom from late spring into fall. Its blooms suit fresh cutting. Between flowers, dense green foliage keeps the bed filled. Place it where a low hedge or strong border group is needed.

Warm apricot flowers give this tall, upright, deciduous grandiflora rose its main seasonal display. A moderate fruity scent marks each flower cycle through the warm season. The blooms are useful for indoor cutting. Leafy growth supports the height through the season. Its height suits flowering screens, formal rose beds, and bold accents.

Low and spreading in form, this deciduous groundcover rose carries warm apricot flowers. Through the warm months, new flowers open with a light scent. Leafy growth helps close gaps along walks and walls. Its low form softens paths and hard edges. Use it in broad drifts for low color and weed-shading cover.

commonName: Apricots N' Cream Hybrid Tea Rose
description: On this upright, deciduous hybrid tea rose, apricot-blend flowers with cream-white tones create the main display. Ordered designs benefit from its upright garden form. Late spring starts a long bloom season with a moderate fruity scent. It fits container plans as well. Use it in cutting beds, formal layouts, or mixed borders.

This deciduous climbing rose grows with a vigorous form and bears apricot-blend flowers with yellow tones. Leafy growth keeps the trained structure full. Cut stems work well indoors. Repeated bloom brings a strong fruity scent from late spring through fall. Guide the canes over strong supports for height, shade, and seasonal color.

An arching, deciduous rugosa shrub rose carries clear pink flowers. Its species is native to sandy coasts of northeast Asia. The fall hips add food and color. Plant it where flowers and showy hips can support a natural design. Repeated bloom brings a strong clove-like rose scent from late spring through fall.

This deciduous hybrid tea rose grows with an upright form and bears clear pink flowers. Use it in cutting beds, formal borders, or as a focal shrub. Green leaves hold a clean garden look after each bloom cycle. A strong damask rose scent comes with repeat bloom from late spring into fall.

Rich red flowers open across this upright, deciduous hybrid tea rose. Use the flowers in fresh arrangements. Between flower waves, green foliage keeps the planting neat. It works well in cutting rows, formal designs, and mixed plantings. The flowers rebloom through the warm season and carry a light rose scent.

commonName: Blanc Double de Coubert Beach Rose, Japanese Rose
description: An arching, deciduous rugosa shrub rose carries clean white flowers. The plant suits wildlife plantings, native-style borders, and informal screens. Red hips feed birds and extend interest into fall and winter. It comes from sandy coasts of northeast Asia. Flowers and hips support wildlife. Warm-season flower cycles carry a strong clove-like rose scent.

This upright, deciduous hybrid tea rose produces soft lavender flowers. Through the warm months, new flowers open with a strong sweet rose scent. Entry beds gain height and flowers from the long stems. Green foliage gives the bed a neat finish through the season. Flowers keep the design useful for many months.

Clear pink flowers appear on this rounded, deciduous shrub rose. Borders stay colorful for much of the season. Through the warm months, new flowers open with a light apple scent. Its shrub form stays useful even between the main flower waves. The full habit fits foundation beds, loose screens, and broad borders.

This deciduous hybrid tea rose grows with an upright form and bears warm apricot flowers. Ordered designs benefit from its upright garden form. The plant is also useful in large pots. Late spring starts a long bloom season with a strong tea scent. Cutting gardens and ordered beds make practical settings.

A deciduous floribunda rose with a bushy habit produces bright pink flowers painted over cream. Through the warm months, new flowers open with a light honey scent. Its repeat flowers keep the planting colorful. The leafy plant stays full between rounds of bloom. Mass planting creates a steady display beside paved areas.

A deciduous floribunda rose develops a bushy form and carries rich purple flowers. Through the warm months, new flowers open with a strong rose scent. Dense green foliage keeps the planting full between bloom cycles. The bloom season stays useful for months. Rose beds gain structure when it is used in groups.

A deciduous hybrid tea rose develops an upright form and carries coppery orange flowers. Flowers return in waves, each with a strong fruity scent. A leafy green backdrop remains between bloom cycles. It also works in roomy containers. Place it where a strong flower accent is needed in beds or borders.

On this bushy, deciduous floribunda rose, purple flowers brushed with red and cream-white tones create the main display. Mass it in borders, low hedges, or broad color drifts.
