A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in bronzy-green with pink and red stripes.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in bronzy-green with salmon-pink and red stripes.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in bronzy-green with pink to cream margins.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in salmon-pink fading to pale yellow, bronzy-green leaf margins.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in dark pink to cream, with dark green edges.

commonName: Rancho White Lily of the Nile
description: An evergreen perennial that forms fountainlike tufts of lush, strappy foliage. Tall, sturdy stalks explode into white clusters of funnel-shaped flowers. Attractive to butterflies and other pollinators. Does well in a container.
An evergreen perennial with fuzzy stems and flowers. Tubular flowers are curved at the tips like kangaroo paws, burgundy red in color. Smooth, sword-like leaves grow in fan-like clumps.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in bronzy-purple to red-brown.

An evergreen perennial that forms a fountain of arching, swordlike leaves. Coloration is matte burgundy. At maturity, it forms a multi-trunked palm-like shrub or tree. Fragrant flower clusters bloom in late spring.

commonName: Red Star Dracaena Palm, Red Grass Palm
description: An evergreen perennial that forms a fountain of arching, swordlike leaves. Coloration is bronzy burgundy-red. At maturity, it forms a multi-trunked palm-like shrub or tree. Fragrant flower clusters bloom in late spring.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms basal clumps of coarse, grass-like foliage. From late spring to fall, torch-like clusters of tubular, coral-red to golden-yellow flowers bloom atop tall, bare stalks. Attracts hummingbirds.
An evergreen perennial with fuzzy stems and flowers. Tubular flowers are curved at the tips like kangaroo paws, green and red in color. Smooth, sword-like leaves grow in fan-like clumps.

An evergreen perennial that forms a fountain of arching, swordlike leaves. Coloration is nearly black. At maturity, it forms a multi-trunked palm-like shrub or tree. Pale purple, fragrant flower clusters bloom in late spring.

commonName: Rocky Point Dwarf Blue Eyed Grass
description: A summer-deciduous perennial with a dwarf height and a vigrous, clumping growth habit. Grassy leaves are flattened, broad and bluish-green. Abundant flowers bloom from midwinter through spring on branched stalks above the foliage. Flowers are small, six-petaled, trumpet-shaped and bright violet-blue with yellow eyes. Self-sows. Native to California.
A perennial that forms grassy tufts of lush, dark green foliage. Tall spikes of small, deep violet flowers are followed by metallic fruits. Blooms in late summer-early fall. Likes shade.
An herbaceous perennial forming clumps of arching and slender, bright green leaves. Tall leafless stems produce deep wine red flowers with yellow-green throats. Reblooming.

A compact, evergreen clumping perennial with upright, strappy green foliage and strong flowering stems. Fuzzy, tubular ruby-red flowers are held at and above the foliage from spring into summer, attracting hummingbirds and supporting cut-flower use. This selection is noted for compact growth, improved vigor, and improved disease tolerance. Best performance comes with full sun, well-drained soil, and moderate irrigation during active growth.

A perennial with grassy semi-evergreen foliage. Green leaves are strap-like with parallel-venation. Reblooming mid season flowers cluster on smooth stems. 6" lily-like blooms open daily. Flowers are purple with darker eyezones and yellow throats.

A South African perennial that forms a fan-like clump of arching, bright green leaves. Terminal clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers appear in yellow with yellow stamens. Flowers are followed by small, ornamental yellow fruit. Can be grown indoors.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in rich green with bronze-maroon stripes.
An evergreen perennial with slender, arching, strappy leaf blades of silver-green. Female plants display greenish flower clusters that are followed by purple-black fruit. Preferes acidic, humus soil.

A perennial that forms arching, grassy tufts which spread vigorously by rhizomes. Variegated leaf blades are dark green with silvery-white stripes. Short spikes of small, light purple-white flowers are followed by metallic, black fruits. Blooms in late summer-early fall. Likes shade.

A perennial bulb that forms clumps of grassy foliage. Leaves are blue-green with variegated white edges. Tall, rounded clusters of fragrant, small, purple flowers bloom in spring. Flowers and foliage smell of garlic when crushed. Leaves are edible. Attracts pollinators.

An evergreen perennial that forms clumps of grass-like foliage. Strappy, arching leaf blades are variegated gray green with cream colored margins. Loose clusters of pale violet star-shaped flowers are followed by lustrous purple fruits.

A perennial that forms grassy tufts of lush leaf blades. Variegated foliage is dark green with yellow to white edges. Leaves fade to white-green or yellow-green, depending on sun exposure. Spikes of small lilac flowers are followed by metallic black fruits. Blooms in late summer-early fall. Likes shade.
Perennial with grass-like slender foliage, slender stalks carry beardless flowers.

A perennial bulb that forms clumps of grassy, blue-green foliage. Tall, rounded clusters of fragrant, small, purple flowers bloom in spring. Flowers and foliage smell of garlic when crushed. Leaves are edible. Attracts pollinators.

A perennial with grassy deciduous foliage. Green leaves are strap-like with parallel-venation. Reblooming early-mid season flowers cluster on smooth stems. 3", fragrant, lily-like blooms open daily. Flowers are golden yellow with ruffled edges.

commonName: Storm Cloud Lily of the Nile
description: An evergreen to semi-evergreen, clumping strappy-leaf perennial with dense basal foliage. Rounded umbels of tubular flowers rise on clean stems in summer, bringing structure and pollinator value to borders, mass plantings, and containers. It is dependable in well-drained soil and handles coastal conditions well.

commonName: Striped Cast-Iron Plant, Variegated Cast-Iron Plant
description: An evergreen perennial with a clumping growth habit. White-striped leaves are sturdy, broad, and glossy with distinct parallel veins. Withstands neglect, deep shade, and indoors.

commonName: Summer Gold Lily of the Nile
description: An evergreen perennial that forms fountainlike tufts of lush, strappy foliage variegated with bold golden margins. Tall, sturdy stalks explode into pale to dark lavender-blue clusters of funnel-shaped flowers. Attractive to butterflies and other pollinators. Does well in a container.

A perennial with grassy deciduous foliage. Green leaves are strap-like with parallel-venation. Mid season flowers cluster on smooth stems. 5.5" lily-like blooms open daily. Flowers are light purple with chartreuse throats.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in bronzy-olive green, pink stripes and fine red margins.

An evergreen perennial that forms clumps of grass-like foliage. Strappy, arching leaf blades are deep green with red bases, becoming more vivid in cool weather. Loose clusters of pale blue, star-shaped flowers are followed by lustrous purple fruits.

An upright, evergreen clumping perennial with strap-like dark green foliage and tall flower stems. Fuzzy, tubular red-orange flowers with yellow tones rise above the foliage in spring and summer, attracting hummingbirds and providing cut-flower stems. Performs best with well-drained sandy or gritty soil and low-phosphorus spring feeding.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of narrow and wavy-edged, evergreen leaves in olive green with reddish bronze margins.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in olive green with creamy-yellow margins, flushed pink in cooler weather. Slightly larger version than P. 'Tiny Tiger'.

An evergreen perennial that forms a fountain of arching, swordlike leaves. Coloration is variegated gray-green with straw-yellow margins. At maturity, it forms a multi-trunked palm-like shrub or tree. Fragrant flower clusters bloom in late spring.
A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in green with cream and red margins, flushed in rose-pink in cool weather.

commonName: Variegated Fortnight Lily, African Iris, Wild Iris
description: An evergreen perennial that forms neat clumps of flat, sword-shaped leaves with creamy white variegation. Stiff stalks carry iris-like flowers with pale violet inner petals and white outer petals spotted in white. Valued for a long bloom period from spring to fall.

A perennial that forms loose, grassy tufts of lush leaf blades. Variegated foliage is dark green with light yellow edges. Color ages to solid green in the second season. Tall spikes of small violet flowers are followed by metallic purple fruits. Blooms in late summer-early fall. Likes shade.

A perennial bulb that forms clumps of grassy foliage. Variegated leaves are blue-green with white stripes. Tall, rounded clusters of fragrant, purple flowers bloom in spring. Flowers and foliage smell of garlic when crushed. Leaves are edible. Attracts pollinators.

An evergreen perennial that forms clumps of grass-like foliage. Strappy, arching leaf blades are variegated gray green with creamy white margins. Loose clusters of pale blue star-shaped flowers are followed by lustrous purple fruits.

An evergreen to semi-evergreen, clumping strappy-leaf perennial with dense basal foliage. Rounded umbels of tubular flowers rise on clean stems in summer, bringing structure and pollinator value to borders, mass plantings, and containers. It is dependable in well-drained soil and handles coastal conditions well.

commonName: White Peter Pan Dwarf Lily of the Nile
description: A dwarf evergreen perennial that forms fountainlike tufts of lush, strappy foliage. Tall, sturdy stalks explode into clusters of bridal-white flowers. Attractive to butterflies and other pollinators. Does well in a container.

An evergreen, clumping grass-like perennial with broad gray-green leaves striped in clean white. Small blue spring flowers rise above the foliage, followed by bright blue berries. This Australian selection adds light to shaded beds, mass plantings, and containers. It handles frost well and grows best in fertile, well-drained soil with room to spread.
A perennial bulb that forms clumps of grassy, gray-green foliage. Tall, rounded clusters of fragrant, small, white flowers bloom in spring. Attracts pollinators.

commonName: Wings of Gold New uzealand Flax
description: A dramatic perennial forming clumps of strappy, evergreen leaves in olive green with yellow margins.

A South African perennial that forms a fan-like clump of arching, bright green leaves. Terminal clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers appear in bright creamy yellow with yellow stamens. Flowers are followed by small, ornamental red fruit.

A semi-evergreen perennial that forms basal clumps of coarse, grass-like foliage. From late summer to fall, torch-like clusters of tubular, golden-orange flowers bloom atop tall, bare stalks. Attracts hummingbirds.

commonName: Yellow Eyed Grass, Golden Eyed Grass
description: A semi-evergreen perennial with an upright, clumping growth habit. Grassy leaves are flattened and dull green. Flowers bloom from late spring to early summer on branched stalks above the foliage. Flowers are small, six-petaled, trumpet-shaped and bright yellow. Self-sows. Native to California.

An upright, evergreen clumping perennial with sword-like green foliage and tall, branched flower stems. Fuzzy yellow tubular flowers with red stems rise above the foliage from spring into fall and attract hummingbirds. Useful in borders, containers, mass plantings, and cut-flower programs. Performs best with well-drained soil and low-phosphorus spring feeding.

commonName: Yellow Striped Butterfly Iris, Wild Iris, Fairy Iris, Fortnight Lily
description: An evergreen perennial that forms neat clumps of flat, sword-shaped leaves with yellow variegation. Stiff stalks carry large iris-like flowers with white outer petals and violet inner petals. Valued for a long bloom period from spring to fall.
Dramatic evergreen perennial with sword-like green striped, bright yellow leaves that present in a fan-shape.
A rhizomatous bulb with large, beautifully veined, burgundy-black leaves and spikes of large, bright red flowers. A remarkable tropical ornamental.

A fast-growing shrub or small tree with woody bark. Leaves are medium green and broadly egg shaped. Flowers are akin to large, drooping, white trumpets that emit a strong fragrance, especially in the evening. Growth habit stays compact. Native to the Andes.

A tropical perennial with a fountain-shaped growth habit. Leathery, blue-green leaves are broad, up to 4 feet long and resemble banana leaves. Large bird-like flowers display grayish heads, golden-orange combs, and royal blue beaks. Blooms from fall to spring. Commonly grown indoors.
A tropical evergreen shrub featuring large and showy, funnel-shaped, hot red flowers with prominent stamen. Glossy, deep green leaves. Grows much larger to 20 - 30 feet high and wide in Hawaii.
A tropical evergreen shrub featuring large and showy, funnel-shaped, double yellow flowers with prominent stamen. Glossy, deep green leaves. Grows much larger to 20 - 30 feet high and wide in Hawaii.
A tropical evergreen shrub featuring large and showy, funnel-shaped, yellow flowers with prominent stamen. Glossy, deep green leaves. Grows much larger to 20 - 30 feet high and wide in Hawaii.

A hybrid series bred to thrive in cooler summer climates, as well as the sub-tropical and tropical zones to which they are native. This rhizomatous bulb retains a compact, well-branched habit with large, lush leaves. Long-lasting flowers bloom from early summer to first frost. Colors and size vary by cultivar.

A tender evergreen, large upright shrub with bold foliage and huge pendent golden-yellow trumpet flowers. Strong evening fragrance and repeated warm-season bloom make it useful near patios and protected entries. Provide rich, well-drained soil, regular irrigation, and room for its fast seasonal growth.

A tropical evergreen shrub featuring large and showy, funnel-shaped, golden yellow flowers with red eyes and prominent stamen. Glossy, deep green leaves. Grows much larger to 20 - 30 feet high and wide in Hawaii.

No two shoots look alike on this bold, herbaceous perennial. Green and bronze-striped leaves frame flowers that may be red, spotted yellow, or split between both colors. Use it for tropical rhythm near pools, entries, or water features. Rich soil and steady moisture build tall stems; spent stalks can be cut at the base.

A tender evergreen, large upright shrub with broad green leaves and fully double, pendent white trumpet flowers. Fragrant blooms are produced in flushes through warm weather, creating a lush tropical effect for courtyards and protected borders. It performs best in fertile, well-drained soil with regular moisture.

A fast-growing shrub or small tree with woody bark. Leaves are green and broadly egg shaped. Flowers are akin to large, drooping, salmon-pink trumpets that emit a strong fragrance, especially in the evening. Native to the Andes.

commonName: Giant Bird of Paradise, White Bird of Paradise
description: A tropical perennial with a tree-like, fountain-shaped growth habit. Leathery, blue-green leaves are broad, up to 6 feet long and resemble banana leaves. Large bird-like flowers display grayish-purple heads, white combs, and blue beaks. Blooms in fall and winter. Commonly grown indoors.
A tropical evergreen shrub featuring large and showy, funnel-shaped, rich yellow flowers with prominent stamen. Glossy, deep green leaves. Grows much larger to 20 - 30 feet high and wide in Hawaii.
A rhizomatous bulb with large, beautifully veined, lime green leaves and spikes of large, bright red flowers. A remarkable tropical ornamental.
A tropical evergreen shrub with thick and sturdy stems supporting glossy, dark green, and deeply cut leaves up to 4 feet long.

A tropical evergreen shrub featuring large and showy, funnel-shaped, virbant deep pink flowers with prominent stamen. Glossy, deep green leaves. Grows much larger to 20 - 30 feet high and wide in Hawaii.
A rhizomatous, tropical perennial with large and leathery, blue-green leaves. Spikes of large and showy flowers with red petals edged in yellow.

A fast-growing shrub or small tree with woody bark. Leaves are green and broadly egg shaped. Flowers are akin to large, drooping, rosy-pink trumpets that emit a strong fragrance, especially in the evening. Native to the Andes. Natural growth habit is more treelike than other species.

A stately tropical perennial that resembles a banana plant with no edible fruit. Glossy, rich green leaves are tinged with red and accented with wine-red midribs. Leaves are large, reaching 10 - 20 feet long and 2 - 4 feet wide. Inconspicuous white flowers appear on mature plants in summer. Tolerates neither wind, nor frost. May be grown in a pot and moved indoors to survive winters. Native to Africa.
A rhizomatous bulb with large, beautifully veined, striped yellow-green leaves and spikes of large, bright orange flowers. A remarkable tropical ornamental.
Tropical evergreen shrub with large and showy funnel shaped flowers with a prominent stamen.
A tropical evergreen shrub featuring large and showy, funnel-shaped flowers with prominent stamen. Each flower is exceptionally large, with scarlet red petals. Glossy, deep green leaves.
A rhizomatous bulb with large, beautifully veined, chocolate brown leaves and spikes of large, bright scarlet flowers. A remarkable tropical ornamental.
A rhizomatous bulb with large, beautifully veined leaves striped in green, yellow, orange and pink. Large flowers grow in spikes of bright orange. A remarkable tropical ornamental.
A rhizomatous bulb with large, beautifully veined, striped yellow-green leaves and spikes of large, bright yellow-orange flowers. A remarkable tropical ornamental.
A rhizomatous bulb with large, beautifully veined, striped yellow-green leaves and spikes of large, bright orange flowers. A remarkable tropical ornamental.

An evergreen, clumping tropical perennial with broad yellow-variegated leaves on cane-like stems. Shell-like white flowers with yellow and pink markings may appear in warm, protected sites. It brings bold foliage to shaded patios, containers, and mild-climate screens with rich soil and regular moisture.
Tropical evergreen shrub with large and showy funnel shaped flowers with a prominent stamen. Hawaii
A tropical evergreen shrub with thick and sturdy stems supporting glossy, dark green, and deeply cut leaves up to 18 inches long. Smaller and bushier than species.
Tropical perennial with large glossy leaves and spikes of large and showy flowers.

A deciduous vine with twining, woody stems that are adaptable to training. Much less vigorous than other cultivars. Medium green leaves are pinnately divided into lengthy, narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. During leaf-out, marvelous, cascading flower chains bloom in violet. Fragrant flowers are labiate with a delicate, fluffy quality. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods.

A semi-evergreen vine with a spreading habit that forms a ground cover. Can be trained to climb with support. Leaves are glossy and deep green. White, pinwheel-shaped flowers have long, slender petals with purple undersides. Fragrant. Blooms in summer. Attracts pollinators.

A tender evergreen, vigorous woody vine with thorny stems and vivid magenta-pink bracts surrounding small white flowers. The long warm-season display is effective on walls, arbors, banks, and large containers. Best color comes with heat, excellent drainage, and restrained irrigation after establishment.

A shrubby evergreen vine that displays clusters of showy blushing-orange bracts, surrounding tiny true flowers. Variegated cream and green leaves are oval to heart-shaped. Long thorns arm the branches.

commonName: Blue Dawn Morning Glory, Blue Dawn Flower
description: A fast-growing perennial vine with funnel-shaped flowers in vibrant violet-blue. Dark green, heart-shaped or three-lobed leaves.

A vigorous deciduous vine with twining, woody stems that are adaptable to training. Medium green leaves are pinnately divided into lengthy, narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. Throughout summer, marvelous, cascading flower chains bloom and rebloom in lavender-blue. Fragrant flowers are labiate with a delicate, fluffy quality. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods. Hardiest wisteria variety.

A vigorous and fast-growing semi-deciduous vine which attaches itself by suction disks at the end of clinging tendrils. Glossy, dark green leaves are variable in shape but usually have 3 pointed lobes, turning bright red to purple in the fall. Dark blue-black berries are attractive to birds.

An evergreen vine with vigorous, twining stems that mound freely or climb with support. Leaves are slender and rich green. Bright yellow, orchid-like flowers bloom and rebloom in late spring, summer, and fall. Winged fruit resembles a tan butterfly. Native to Mexico and Baja California.

A deciduous, twining vine with heart-shaped green leaves and unusual maroon pipe-shaped flowers in late winter to spring. This California native is the larval host for pipevine swallowtail butterflies and fits woodland edges, fences, and trellises. Performs best with well-drained soil, light shade, and occasional summer water.

A tender evergreen, vigorous woody vine with bright golden yellow bracts that age to warm apricot tones. Thorny stems can be trained on walls, fences, or large trellises for intense summer color. It performs best in warm exposures with excellent drainage and lean conditions once established.

An evergeen, shrubby vine with long and pendulous clusters of purple-pink, sweat pea-like flowers looking like small Wisteria blooms. Narrower, dark green foliage than species and a longer blooming period.

A nonclimbing deciduous vine with trailing, wiry stems. Large, saucer-shaped flowers rebloom throughout the seasons. Petals are deep crimson and have a velvety texture. Stamens are extra showy. Feathery, spherical seed heads remain after petals drop. Leaflets are rich green and more or less heart-shaped. Beneficial for hummingbirds and butterflies.
An evergreen vine with shiny, light green leaves and yellow trumpet-shaped flowers.

A deciduous vine with twining, woody stems that are adaptable to training. Medium green leaves are pinnately divided into narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. Very early before leaf-out, marvelous, cascading flower chains bloom in light and dark purple. Highly fragrant flowers are labiate with a fluffy, delicate quality. Clusters are more stout than those of W. floribunda. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods.

botanicalName: Dolichandra unguis-cati, Macfadyena unguis-cati, Bignonia tweediana
description: A semi-evergreen vine with self-clinging stems that easily attach to most surfaces. Freely forms a mounding ground cover. Showy, spring flowers are yellow, trumpet-shaped, and lobed. Pairs of oval, glossy, green leaflets are centered by a forked, claw-like tendril. Used in herbal medicine. Can spread invasively.

A deciduous vine with twining, woody stems that are adaptable to training. Medium green leaves are pinnately divided into narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. Before leaf-out, marvelous, cascading flower chains bloom in violet-blue. Fragrant flowers are labiate with a fluffy, delicate quality. Clusters are more stout than those of W. floribunda. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods.
A fast-growing, deciduous vine with rounded heart-shaped foliage. Mature plants develop large and white, lacecap flower clusters.

A deciduous vine with twining, woody stems, adaptable to training. Medium green leaves are pinnately divided into narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. Before leaf-out, cascading flower chains bloom in pearly purple. Fragrant flowers are labiate with a fluffy, delicate quality. Clusters are more stout than those of W. floribunda. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods.

A tropical evergreen vine with a vigorous, self-clinging habit, able to climb most surfaces with aerial rootlets. Young leaves are heart-shaped, delicate, and light green. Mature leaves are larger, elliptic, leathery, and dark green. Popular as an indoor plant. Inedible, pear-shaped fruits sporadically develop on outdoor plants. Root system spreads invasively.

A vigorous deciduous vine with twining, woody stems that are adaptable to training. Medium green leaves are pinnately divided into lengthy, narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. Foliage turns yellow in fall. During leaf-out, marvelous, cascading flower chains bloom in pearly lavender and dark violet. Fragrant flowers are double and labiate with a fluffy, delicate quality. Clusters are larger and more abundant than those of W. sinensis. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods.

An evergeen vine with three to five-lobed, small and dull, dark green leaves with prominent paler veining. Rounded greenish-white flower clusters followed by small black berries. Most often used as a groundcover.

An evergreen vine with wiry, climbing tendrils. Spring flowers are fragrant and star-shaped. Petals are creamy white and have a velvety texture. Stamens are extra showy. Leaves are dark green, narrow, and leathery. Beneficial for hummingbirds and butterflies.

A vigorous evergreen vine with fast climbing stems. Requires support. Foliage is glossy, dark-green and heart-shaped. Yellow and white flowers are long, tubular, flared, and fragrant. Blooms from spring thru fall. Attracts pollinators and hummingbirds. Flowers and leaves are larger than other honeysuckles. Stems become woody with age.

An evergeen vine with three to five-lobed, small and dull, dark green leaves irregularily variegated in gray and cream. Rounded greenish-white flower clusters followed by small black berries. Most often used as a groundcover.

A vining shrub with fast climbing, twining stems. Does best with support, though may be kept tidy with pruning. Foliage is blue-green and oval. Stems are reddish. Pink buds blossom to reveal golden-yellow interiors. Flowers are clustered and fragrant. Blooms from spring to fall. Attracts pollinators and hummingbirds. Semi-evergreen in warmer climates. A more vigorous variety.

A vigorous evergreen vine with clusters of small and flared tubular flowers in golden yellow with reddish brown markings. Twining stems are covered in foliage divided into narrowly oval, glossy, rich green leaflets. Leaves are bronzy when first emerging.

A vigorous and fast-growing semi-deciduous vine which attaches itself by suction disks at the end of clinging tendrils. Large and glossy, dark green leaves are variable in shape but usually have 3 pointed lobes, turning burgundy in the fall. Dark blue-black berries are attractive to birds.

An evergeen vine with three to five-lobed, smaller and delicate, dark green leaves. Rounded greenish-white flower clusters followed by small black berries. Most often used as a groundcover. Denser growth and less vigorous than the species.

A vigorous vine with sprawling, twining stems. Forms a ground cover, or train on a structure. Foliage is rich green and oval. White and yellow flowers are two-lipped, tubular and fragrant. Blooms from summer into fall. Attracts pollinators and hummingbirds. Semi-evergreen in warmer climates.
An evergeen, shrubby vine with long and pendulous clusters of purple-pink, sweet pea-like flowers looking like small Wisteria blooms. Narrow, dark green foliage.

Cream-white bracts blush pink across this evergreen, arching vine or shrub during repeated warm-season bloom. Small true flowers sit inside the showy bracts and feed insects. Train it on walls, fences, or large trellises for a soft two-tone screen. Strong sun and fast drainage improve color; sturdy support and gloves help manage thorny stems.

A tender evergreen, vigorous woody vine with clean white papery bracts around small true flowers. The luminous display is useful against dark walls, pergolas, and warm courtyards. Heat, good drainage, and limited established irrigation promote heavy flowering and compact growth.
Semi-evergreen vine commonly used as a bank cover, oval rich green foliage and clusters of fragrant tubular flowers. Considered invasive in the Eastern US.

A tender evergreen, compact woody shrub-vine with deep red bracts and a more restrained habit than many forms. It works well in containers, slopes, low screens, and espaliered plantings. Strong flowering is encouraged by warm exposure, good drainage, and lean post-establishment care.
An evergreen climbing vine with long-blooming, trumpet-shaped flowers of lavender purple. Foliage is dense, glossy, and dark green.

An evergreen twining vine that climbs well with support. Broad leaves are glossy, dark green and oblong. Strongly fragrant flowers are small, flared, funnel shaped and white. Clustered flowers bloom in spring and summer.

An evergreen, shrubby groundcover with long clusters of purple, sweet pea-like flowers looking like small Wisteria blooms. Narrow, dark green foliage. Creeping groundcover form, but will climb up support if allowed to.
A shrubby evergreen vine that displays clusters of tiny true flowers surrounded by showy petal-like bracts in hot pink. Bright green leaves are oval to heart-shaped. Long thorns arm the branches.

A tender perennial vine with twining stems that climb with provided support. Without support, it forms a ground cover. Triangular leaves are gray-green. Showy, tubular to flared flowers are bright orange. Blooms from spring to fall.

A tender evergreen, vigorous woody vine with warm orange to coppery bracts over a long bloom season. It brings strong color to walls, arbors, and large-scale slope plantings. It thrives in heat and reflected light with excellent drainage and reduced irrigation once established.
An evergreen vine with clusters of funnel-shaped flowers in pink with dark reddish-pink throats. Twining stems are covered in foliage divided into glossy and rich green, oval leaflets.

A deciduous vine with wiry, climbing tendrils. Large, saucer-shaped flowers rebloom throughout the seasons. Velvety petals are vibrant pink with a pale pink central stripe. Stamens are extra showy and yellow. Feathery, spherical seed heads remain after petals drop. Leaflets are medium green and more or less heart-shaped. Beneficial for hummingbirds and butterflies.

A decidous woody vine with rich green, palmate leaves that divide into five oval leaflets. Dangling clusters of pink flowers produce long, purple seed pods with an edible white pulp that ripens in fall. Fruits more reliably when cross-pollinated with another cultivar. Provide trellis for climbing. Can tolerate full shade.

An evergreen vine with a spreading, cascading habit. Train as a climbing vine with support. Rich green foliage divides into many leaflets. Blush-white, star-shaped flowers bloom from pink buds in large clusters at branch tips. Very fragrant. Blooms from late winter into summer. Attracts pollinators.

A semi-evergreen twining vine with a shrubby habit that climbs vigorously with support. Slender leaves are dark green. From spring to fall, clusters of star-shaped flowers bloom in bluish-white with yellow centers. Most floriferous in spring. Fruits ripen in fall. All parts are toxic.

A tender evergreen, vigorous woody vine with thorny stems and intense purple bracts surrounding small white flowers. It is well suited to walls, pergolas, slopes, and large containers where heat and reflected light are available. Excellent drainage and lean post-establishment care encourage heavy bloom.
A shrubby climbing vine that displays clouds of vividly violet bracts surrounding tiny true flowers. Medium green leaves are oval to heart-shaped.
A shrubby evergreen vine that displays clusters of showy deep magenta bracts surrounding tiny true flowers. Medium green leaves are oval to heart-shaped. Long thorns arm the branches.

A vigorously spreading vine with twining stems. Forms a sprawling ground cover, or train on a structure. Oval foliage is burgundy-green. Purple-red flowers with white-yellow centers are two-lipped and fragrant. Blooms in spring and summer. Attracts pollinators and hummingbirds. Semi-evergreen in warmer climates.
A vigorous, evergreen to semi-evergreen vine with large and showy, intricate flowers in pure white. Glossy, deep green foliage.

A deciduous clinging vine that attaches itself to surfaces by suction disks called holdfasts. Forms a dense screen or groundcover. Bright green, palmate foliage turns a deep red color in fall. Smaller and slower growing than P. quinquefolia.

A tender evergreen, compact woody shrub-vine with green-and-cream variegated foliage and raspberry-pink bracts. The foliage gives year-round contrast even between bloom cycles, making it useful in containers and warm entries. Best variegation and flowering occur with heat, drainage, and careful irrigation.

commonName: Red Trumpet Vine, Scarlet Trumpet Vine
botanicalName: DistictIs buccinatoria, Bignonia cherere, Amphilophium buccinatorium
description: A vigorous evergreen vine that can climb nearly any surface via branching tendrils and disks. Leaves are medium green and wavy-edged. Flowers are bright orange-red and trumpet shaped. Blooms in spring and summer. Attracts hummingbirds.

A deciduous vine with vigorously spreading, climbing tendrils. Broad, lobed leaves turn from green to yellow to brilliant red in fall. Bark is exfoliating and cinnamon-brown. Inconspicuous spring flowers emit a pleasant fragrance and attract bees. Small, edible grapes attract birds and other wildlife. Adaptable with pruning. Hybrid of European grape and California native.

An evergreen vine with clusters of funnel-shaped flowers in pink with purple throats. Twining stems are covered in foliage divided into glossy and rich green, oval leaflets. A heavier blooming variety with fragrant flowers.

A tender evergreen, compact woody shrub-vine with bracts that open gold and mature to rosy pink. The low, spreading habit suits containers, banks, and foreground color plantings in warm exposures. Excellent drainage and moderate-to-low established irrigation support dense growth and bloom.

A vigorous deciduous vine with twining, woody stems that are adaptable to training. Medium green leaves are pinnately divided into lengthy, narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. Foliage turns yellow in fall. During leaf-out, marvelous, cascading flower chains bloom in rich violet. Fragrant flowers are labiate with a fluffy, delicate quality. Clusters are larger and more abundant than those of W. sinensis. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods.

A vigorous evergreen vine that can climb almost any surface with branching tendrils and disks. Leaves are medium green and wavy-edged. Flowers are light purple to bright purple-pink. Attracts hummingbirds. A member of the Bignonia family.

A tender evergreen, vigorous woody vine with saturated red bracts produced heavily through warm weather. Fast growth covers walls, arbors, and fences where a bold, drought-tolerant color mass is needed. It performs best with heat, strong light, good drainage, and limited established water.

A woody deciduous vine with rich green, palmate leaves that divide into five oval leaflets. Dangling clusters of white flowers produce long, purple seed pods with an edible white pulp that ripens in fall. Fruits more reliably when cross-pollinated with another cultivar. Provide trellis for climbing. Can tolerate full shade.

A deciduous clinging vine that attaches itself to surfaces by suction disks called holdfasts. Forms a dense screen or groundcover. Foliage is bronze-green, purple-tinged and silver-veined with red undersides. The palmate leaves turns a rich red color in fall. Showy clusters of small, blue-black berries in fall.

commonName: Star Jasmine, Confederate Jasmine, Maile Haole
description: An evergreen groundcover with twining stems. If trained as a vine, it can grow 20 - 30 feet high. Distinctively fragrant flowers are small, white, and pinwheel-shaped. Leaves are elliptic, dark green, and glossy.

A hybrid evergreen vine with vigorous, twining stems. Leaves are oval, glossy and dark green. Large flowers have pale pink petals that flare out from tubular, deeper pink throats. Long, abundant bloom cycle throughout summer. Disease resistant.

A hybrid evergreen vine with twining stems and a compact habit. Leaves are oval, glossy and dark green. Showy flowers have crimson-red petals that flare out from tubular throats. Long, abundant bloom cycle throughout summer. Disease resistant.

commonName: Sun Parasol Stars And Stripes Mandevilla
botanicalName: Mandevilla Sun Parasol Stars And Stripes
description: A hybrid evergreen vine with twining stems and a compact habit. Leaves are oval, glossy and dark green. Showy flowers have bright red, white streaked petals that flare out from tubular throats. Long, abundant bloom cycle throughout summer. Disease resistant.

A hybrid evergreen vine with vigorous, twining stems. Leaves are oval, glossy and dark green. Large flowers have bright white petals that flare out from tubular, yellow throats. Long, abundant bloom cycle throughout summer. Disease resistant.

commonName: Sunny Susy Series Black-Eyed Susan Vine
description: A tender perennial vine with twining stems that climb with provided support. Triangular leaves are medium green. Showy, saucer-shaped flowers are rich orange with dark burgundy throats. Blooms from spring to fall. 'Sunny Susy Brownie' has deep red flowers with dark throats. 'Sunny Susy Orange' has tangerine-orange flowers with dark throats. 'Sunny Susy Red Orange' has blood-orange flowers with dark throats.

A deciduous or semi-evergreen vine with wiry, climbing tendrils. Flowers are fragrant and star-shaped. Petals are creamy white with a velvety texture. Feathery, spherical seed heads remain after petals drop. Leaflets are deep green and more or less heart-shaped. Beneficial for hummingbirds and butterflies.
A vigorous evergreen vine that can climb nearly any surface via branching tendrils and disks. Leaves are shiny and dark green. Flowers are bright orange-red and trumpet shaped. Attracts hummingbirds.
A shrubby evergreen vine that displays clusters of showy pinky-red bracts, which surround tiny true flowers. Deep green leaves are oval to heart-shaped. Long thorns arm the branches.

A tender evergreen, upright woody shrub with stiff vertical stems and purple-pink bracts clustered near branch tips. The narrow, self-supporting habit gives a different look from vining types and suits entries, containers, and desert-style plantings. It thrives in heat and sharply drained soil.

A deciduous vine with wiry, climbing tendrils. Large, open flowers are lightly fragrant like vanilla. Blooms in spring and fall. Petals are white and have a velvety texture. Stamens are purple and extra showy. Feathery, spherical seed heads remain after petals drop. Leaflets are medium green and more or less heart-shaped. Attracts hummingbirds and butterflies.

An evergreen vine with clusters of funnel-shaped flowers in pale pink with dark pink throats. Twining stems are covered in foliage divided into oval, glossy leaflets in rich green with irregular creamy variegation.

A tropical evergreen vine with a vigorous, self-clinging habit, able to climb most surfaces with aerial rootlets. Young leaves are heart-shaped, delicate, and variegated dark green with irregular white edges. Mature leaves are larger, elliptic, leathery, and also variegated. Popular as an indoor plant. Inedible, pear-shaped fruits sporadically develop on outdoor plants. Root system spreads invasively.

A vigorous and fast-growing semi-deciduous vine which attaches itself by suction disks at the end of clinging tendrils. Smaller, glossy dark green leaves are variable in shape but usually have 3 pointed lobes, turning right red and purple in the fall. Dark blue-black berries are attractive to birds. Less rampant growth than species.

A deciduous vine which attaches itself by suction disks at the end of clinging tendrils. Palmate leaves emerge bronzy purple and mature to satiny green, eventually turning brilliant crimson to burgundy in the fall. Dark blue-black berries are attractive to birds.
An evergreen vine with clusters of white, funnel-shaped flowers. Twining stems are covered in foliage divided into glossy and rich green, oval leaflets.

A decidous woody vine with rich green, palmate, oval leaflets. Dangling clusters of white flowers produce long, purple seed pods with an edible white pulp that ripens in fall. Fruits more reliably when cross-pollinated with another cultivar. Provide trellis for climbing. Can tolerate full shade.

A vigorous deciduous vine with twining, woody stems that are adaptable to training. Medium green leaves are pinnately divided into lengthy, narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. During leaf-out, marvelous, cascading, extra lengthy flower chains bloom in clean white. Fragrant flowers are labiate with a fluffy, delicate quality. Clusters are larger and more abundant than those of W. sinensis. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods.
An evergeen, shrubby vine with long and pendulous clusters of pure white, sweat pea-like flowers looking like small Wisteria blooms. Narrow, dark green foliage.

A vigorous deciduous vine with twining, woody stems that are adaptable to training. Downy, medium green leaves are pinnately divided into narrow-tipped, egg-shaped leaflets. During leaf-out, marvelous, cascading, extra stout flower chains bloom in white. Fragrant flowers are labiate with a fluffy, delicate quality. Attracts bees, butterflies and hummingbirds. Flowers are followed by drooping, velvety, green fruits that look like pea pods.
A shrubby evergreen vine that displays clusters of showy white bracts, which surround tiny true flowers. Variegated green and white leaves are oval to heart-shaped. Long thorns arm the branches.
